style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">input</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">type</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"text"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"form-0-title"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">id</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"id_form-0-title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>But with ArticleFormset(prefix='article') that becomes:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">label</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">for</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"id_article-0-title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>Title:</</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">label</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">input</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">type</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"text"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"article-0-title"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">id</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"id_article-0-title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This is useful if you want to <a href="index.html#page_364">use more than one formset in a view</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using a formset in views and templates</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Formsets have the following attributes and methods associated with rendering:</p> <p>BaseFormSet.<b>renderer</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Specifies the <a href="index.html#page_1550">renderer</a> to use for the formset. Defaults to the renderer specified by the <a href="index.html#page_1915"><i>FORM_RENDERER</i></a> setting.</p> <p>BaseFormSet.<b>template_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The name of the template rendered if the formset is cast into a string, e.g. via print(formset) or in a template via {{ formset }}.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">By default, a property returning the value of the renderer’s <a href="index.html#page_1551"><i>formset_template_name</i>. </a>You may set it as a string template name in order to override that for a particular formset class.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This template will be used to render the formset’s management form, and then each form in the formset</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">as per the template defined by the form’s <a href="index.html#page_1497"><i>template_name</i></a>.</p> <p>BaseFormSet.<b>template_name_div</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The name of the template used when calling <a href="index.html#page_362"><i>as_div()</i></a>. By default this is "django/forms/formsets/ div.html". This template renders the formset’s management form and then each form in the formset</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">as per the form’s <a href="index.html#page_1499"><i>as_div()</i></a> method.</p> <p>BaseFormSet.<b>template_name_p</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The name of the template used when calling <a href="index.html#page_362"><i>as_p()</i></a>. By default this is "django/forms/formsets/p. html" . This template renders the formset’s management form and then each form in the formset as</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">per the form’s <a href="index.html#page_1499"><i>as_p()</i></a> method.</p> <p id="page_362"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>BaseFormSet.<b>template_name_table</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The name of the template used when calling <a href="index.html#page_362"><i>as_table()</i></a>. By default this is "django/forms/formsets/ table.html" . This template renders the formset’s management form and then each form in the formset</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">as per the form’s <a href="index.html#page_1501"><i>as_table()</i></a> method.</p> <p>BaseFormSet.<b>template_name_ul</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The name of the template used when calling <a href="index.html#page_362"><i>as_ul()</i></a>. By default this is "django/forms/formsets/ ul.html". This template renders the formset’s management form and then each form in the formset</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">as per the form’s <a href="index.html#page_1500"><i>as_ul()</i></a> method.</p> <p>BaseFormSet.<b>get_context</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns the context for rendering a formset in a template.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The available context is:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• formset : The instance of the formset.</p> <p>BaseFormSet.<b>render</b>(template_name=None, context=None, renderer=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The render method is called by __str__ as well as the <a href="index.html#page_362"><i>as_div()</i>, <i>as_p()</i>, <i>as_ul()</i></a>, and <a href="index.html#page_362"><i>as_table()</i></a> methods. All arguments are optional and will default to:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• template_name: <a href="index.html#page_361"><i>template_name</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• context: Value returned by <a href="index.html#page_362"><i>get_context()</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• renderer: Value returned by <a href="index.html#page_361"><i>renderer</i></a></p> <p>BaseFormSet.<b>as_div</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Renders the formset with the <a href="index.html#page_361"><i>template_name_div</i></a> template.</p> <p>BaseFormSet.<b>as_p</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Renders the formset with the <a href="index.html#page_361"><i>template_name_p</i></a> template.</p> <p>BaseFormSet.<b>as_table</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Renders the formset with the <a href="index.html#page_361"><i>template_name_table</i></a> template.</p> <p>BaseFormSet.<b>as_ul</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Renders the formset with the <a href="index.html#page_362"><i>template_name_ul</i></a> template.</p> <p>Using a formset inside a view is not very different from using a regular Form class. The only thing you will want to be aware of is making sure to use the management form inside the template. Let’s look at a sample view:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.forms</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">formset_factory</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.shortcuts</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">render</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.forms</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ArticleForm</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_363" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">method</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span </p> <p>However there’s a slight shortcut for the above by letting the formset itself deal with the management form:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">method</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"post"</span><span style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">formset</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">table</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span This renders the formset</p> <p>using the template specified by the <a href="index.html#page_361"><i>template_name</i></a> attribute. Similar to forms, by default the formset will be rendered as_div, with other helper methods of as_p, as_ul, and as_table being available. The rendering of</p> <p>the formset can be customized by specifying the template_name attribute, or more generally by <a href="index.html#page_1554">overriding</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1554">the default template</a>.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_364"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Manually rendered can_delete and can_order</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you manually render fields in the template, you can render can_delete to order (can_order=True), it is possible to render it with {{ form. ORDER }}.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using more than one formset in a view</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You are able to use more than one formset in a view if you like. Formsets borrow much of its behavior from forms. With that said you are able to use prefix to prefix formset form field names with a given value to allow more than one formset to be sent to a view without name clashing. Let’s take a look at how this might be accomplished:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.forms</span> <span article_formset,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"book_formset"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: book_formset,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You would then render the formsets as normal. It is important to point out that you need to pass prefix on both the POST and non-POST cases so that it is rendered and processed correctly.</p> <p>Each formset’s <a href="index.html#page_361">prefix</a> replaces the default form prefix that’s added to each field’s name and id HTML at-tributes.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Creating forms from models</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>ModelForm</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class ModelForm</b></p> <p>If you’re building a database-driven app, chances are you’ll have forms that map closely to Django models. For instance, you might have a BlogComment model, and you want to create a form that lets people submit comments. In this case, it would be redundant to define the field types in your form, because you’ve already defined the fields in your model.</p> <p>For this reason, Django provides a helper class that lets you create a Form class from a Django model.</p> <p>For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.forms</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelForm</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Article</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"># Create the form class.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ArticleForm</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(ModelForm):</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Meta</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">model</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Article</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"pub_date"</span><span </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"># Creating a form to change an existing article.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">article</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Article</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(pk</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">article)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Field types</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The generated Form class will have a form field for every model field specified, in the order specified in the fields attribute.</p> <p>Each model field has a corresponding default form field. For example, a CharField on a model is represented as a CharField on a form. A model ManyToManyField is represented as a MultipleChoiceField. Here is the full list of conversions:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Model field Form field</p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_1626"><i>AutoField</i></a> Not represented in the form</p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_1627"><i>BigAutoField</i></a> Not represented in the form</p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_1627"><i>BigIntegerField</i></a> <a href="index.html#page_1534"><i>IntegerField</i></a> with min_value set to -9223372036854775808 and max_value set to href="index.html#page_1627"><i>BooleanField</i></a> <a href="index.html#page_1525"><i>BooleanField</i></a> , or <a href="index.html#page_1536"><i>NullBooleanField</i></a> if null=True.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_1628"><i>CharField</i></a> <a href="index.html#page_1526"><i>CharField</i></a> with max_length set to the model field’s max_length and <a style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_1630"><i>DecimalField</i></a> <a href="index.html#page_1528"><i>DecimalField</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_1631"><i>DurationField</i></a> <a href="index.html#page_1529"><i>DurationField</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_1631"><i>EmailField</i></a> <a style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_1635"><i>FilePathField</i></a> <a href="index.html#page_1530"><i>FilePathField</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a <p style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_1649"><i>ManyToManyField</i></a> <a href="index.html#page_1545"><i>ModelMultipleChoiceField</i></a> (see below)</p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right">Table 1 – continued from previous page</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Model field Form field</p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_1641"><i>SmallAutoField</i></a> Not represented in the form</p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_1641"><i>SmallIntegerField</i></a> <a href="index.html#page_1534"><i>IntegerField</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_1642"><i>TextField</i></a> <a href="index.html#page_1526"><i>CharField</i></a> with widget=forms.Textarea</p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_1642"><i>TimeField</i></a> <a href="index.html#page_1537"><i>TimeField</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_1642"><i>URLField</i></a> <a href="index.html#page_1539"><i>URLField</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_1643"><i>UUIDField</i></a> <a href="index.html#page_1539"><i>UUIDField</i></a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>As you might expect, the ForeignKey and ManyToManyField model field types are special cases:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• ForeignKey is represented by django.forms.ModelChoiceField, which is a ChoiceField whose</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">choices are a model QuerySet.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• ManyToManyField is represented by django.forms.ModelMultipleChoiceField, which is a</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">MultipleChoiceField whose choices are a model QuerySet.</p> <p>In addition, each generated form field has attributes set as follows:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• If the model field has blank=True, then required is set to False on the form field. Otherwise,</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">required=True.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The form field’s label is set to the verbose_name of the model field, with the first character capitalized.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The form field’s help_text is set to the help_text of the model field.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• If the model field has choices set, then the form field’s widget will be set to Select, with choices coming</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">from the model field’s choices. The choices will normally include the blank choice which is selected by default. If the field is required, this forces the user to make a selection. The blank choice will not be included if the model field has blank=False and an explicit default value (the default value will be initially selected instead).</p> <p>Finally, note that you can override the form field used for a given model field. See <a href="index.html#page_374">Overriding the default</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_374">fields</a> below.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>A full example</b></p> <p style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>BookForm</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(forms</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Form):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">forms</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">100</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">authors</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">forms</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelMultipleChoiceField(queryset</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">all())</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Validation on a ModelForm</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>There are two main steps involved in validating a ModelForm:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. <a href="index.html#page_1574">Validating the form</a></p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. <a href="index.html#page_1692">Validating the model instance</a></p> <p>Just like normal form validation, model form validation is triggered implicitly when calling <a href="index.html#page_1488"><i>is_valid()</i></a> or</p> <p>accessing the <a href="index.html#page_1489"><i>errors</i></a> attribute and explicitly when calling full_clean(), although you will typically not use the latter method in practice.</p> <p>Model validation (<a href="index.html#page_1693"><i>Model.full_clean()</i></a>) is triggered from within the form validation step, right after the form’s clean() method is called.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: The cleaning process modifies the model instance passed to the ModelForm constructor in</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">various ways. For instance, any date fields on the model are converted into actual date objects. Failed</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">validation may leave the underlying model instance in an inconsistent state and therefore it’s not rec-</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">ommended to reuse it.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Overriding the clean() method</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can override the clean() method on a model form to provide additional validation in the same way you can on a normal form.</p> <p>A model form instance attached to a model object will contain an instance attribute that gives its methods access to that specific model instance.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: The ModelForm.clean() method sets a flag that makes the <a href="index.html#page_1692">model validation</a></p> <p style="margin-left:1em">step validate the uniqueness of model fields that are marked as unique, unique_together or</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">unique_for_date|month|year.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">If you would like to override the clean() method and maintain this validation, you must call the parent</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">class’s clean() method.</p> <p id="page_370"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Interaction with model validation</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>As part of the validation process, ModelForm will call the clean() method of each field on your model that has a corresponding field on your form. If you have excluded any model fields, validation will not be run on</p> <p>those fields. See the <a href="index.html#page_1574">form validation</a> documentation for more on how field cleaning and validation work.</p> <p>The model’s clean() method will be called before any uniqueness checks are made. See <a href="index.html#page_1692">Validating objects</a> for more information on the model’s clean() hook.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Considerations regarding model’s error_messages</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Error messages defined at the <a href="index.html#page_1523"><i>form field</i></a> level or at the <a href="index.html#page_374">form Meta</a> level always take precedence over the</p> <p>error messages defined at the <a href="index.html#page_1624"><i>model field</i></a> level.</p> <p>Error messages defined on <a href="index.html#page_1624"><i>model fields</i></a> are only used when the ValidationError is raised during the <a href="index.html#page_1692">model</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1692">validation</a> step and no corresponding error messages are defined at the form level.</p> <p>You can override the error messages from NON_FIELD_ERRORS raised by model validation by adding the</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1473"><i>NON_FIELD_ERRORS</i></a> key to the error_messages dictionary of the ModelForm’s inner Meta class:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.core.exceptions</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">NON_FIELD_ERRORS</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.forms</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelForm</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ArticleForm</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(ModelForm):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Meta</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">error_messages</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">NON_FIELD_ERRORS: {</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"unique_together"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"%(model_name)s's %(field_labels)s are not unique."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>The save() method</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Every ModelForm also has a save() method. This method creates and saves a database object from the data bound to the form. A subclass of ModelForm can accept an existing model instance as the keyword argument instance; if this is supplied, save() will update that instance. If it’s not supplied, save() will create a new instance of the specified model:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Article</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.forms</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ArticleForm</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"># Create a form instance from POST data.</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_371" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">f</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ArticleForm(request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">POST)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"># Save a new Article object from the form's data.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">new_article</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">f</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"># Create a form to edit an existing Article, but use</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"># POST data to populate the form.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Article</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(pk</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">f</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ArticleForm(request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">POST, instance</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">f</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note that if the form <a href="index.html#page_369">hasn’t been validated, </a>calling save() will do so by checking form.errors. A ValueError will be raised if the data in the form doesn’t validate – i.e., if form.errors evaluates to True.</p> <p>If an optional field doesn’t appear in the form’s data, the resulting model instance uses the model field</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1623"><i>default</i>, </a>if there is one, for that field. This behavior doesn’t apply to fields that use <a href="index.html#page_1568"><i>CheckboxInput</i></a>,</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1571"><i>CheckboxSelectMultiple</i>, </a>or <a href="index.html#page_1569"><i>SelectMultiple</i></a> (or any custom widget whose <a href="index.html#page_1560"><i>value_omitted_from_data()</i></a> method always returns False) since an unchecked checkbox and unselected <select multiple> don’t ap-pear in the data of an HTML form submission. Use a custom form field or widget if you’re designing an API and want the default fallback behavior for a field that uses one of these widgets.</p> <p>This save() method accepts an optional commit keyword argument, which accepts either True or False. If you call save() with commit=False, then it will return an object that hasn’t yet been saved to the database. In this case, it’s up to you to call save() on the resulting model instance. This is useful if you want to do</p> <p>custom processing on the object before saving it, or if you want to use one of the specialized <a href="index.html#page_1699">model saving</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1699">options</a>. commit is True by default.</p> <p>Another side effect of using commit=False is seen when your model has a many-to-many relation with an-other model. If your model has a many-to-many relation and you specify commit=False when you save a form, Django cannot immediately save the form data for the many-to-many relation. This is because it isn’t possible to save many-to-many data for an instance until the instance exists in the database.</p> <p>To work around this problem, every time you save a form using commit=False, Django adds a save_m2m() method to your ModelForm subclass. After you’ve manually saved the instance produced by the form, you can invoke save_m2m() to save the many-to-many form data. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"># Create a form instance with POST data.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">f</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">AuthorForm(request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">POST)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"># Create, but don't save the new author instance.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">new_author</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">f</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save(commit</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=False</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"># Modify the author in some way.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">new_author</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">some_field</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"some_value"</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_372"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"># Save the new instance.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">new_author</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"># Now, save the many-to-many data for the form.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">f</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save_m2m()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Calling save_m2m() is only required if you use save(commit=False). When you use a save() on a form, all data – including many-to-many data – is saved without the need for any additional method calls. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"># Create a form instance with POST data.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">f</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">AuthorForm(request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">POST, instance</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"># Create and save the new author instance. There's no need to do anything else.</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">new_author</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">f</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Other than the save() and save_m2m() methods, a ModelForm works exactly the same way as any other forms form. For example, the is_valid() method is used to check for validity, the is_multipart() method is used to determine whether a form requires multipart file upload (and hence whether request.FILES must</p> <p>be passed to the form), etc. See <a href="index.html#page_1514">Binding uploaded files to a form</a> for more information.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Selecting the fields to use</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>It is strongly recommended that you explicitly set all fields that should be edited in the form using the fields attribute. Failure to do so can easily lead to security problems when a form unexpectedly allows a user to set certain fields, especially when new fields are added to a model. Depending on how the form is rendered, the problem may not even be visible on the web page.</p> <p>The alternative approach would be to include all fields automatically, or remove only some. This fundamen-</p> <p>tal approach is known to be much less secure and has led to serious exploits on major websites (e.g. <a href="https://github.blog/2012-03-04-public-key-security-vulnerability-and-mitigation/">GitHub</a>).</p> <p>There are, however, two shortcuts available for cases where you can guarantee these security concerns do not apply to you:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. Set the fields attribute to the special value '__all__' to indicate that all fields in the model should</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">be used. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.forms</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelForm</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AuthorForm</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(ModelForm):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Meta</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_373" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">model</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"__all__"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. Set the exclude attribute of the ModelForm’s inner Meta class to a list of fields to be excluded from the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">form.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>PartialAuthorForm</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(ModelForm):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Meta</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">model</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">exclude</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Since the Author model has the 3 fields name, title and birth_date, this will result in the fields name and birth_date being present on the form.</p> <p>If either of these are used, the order the fields appear in the form will be the order the fields are defined in the model, with ManyToManyField instances appearing last.</p> <p>In addition, Django applies the following rule: if you set editable=False on the model field, any form created from the model via ModelForm will not include that field.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: Any fields not included in a form by the above logic will not be set by the form’s save() method. Also, if you manually add the excluded fields back to the form, they will not be initialized from the model instance.</p> <p>Django will prevent any attempt to save an incomplete model, so if the model does not allow the missing fields to be empty, and does not provide a default value for the missing fields, any attempt to save() a ModelForm with missing fields will fail. To avoid this failure, you must instantiate your model with initial values for the missing, but required fields:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">author</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author(title</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Mr"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">PartialAuthorForm(request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">POST, instance</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">author)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Alternatively, you can use save(commit=False) and manually set any extra required fields:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">PartialAuthorForm(request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">POST)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">author</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save(commit</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=False</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">author</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Mr"</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">author</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>See the <a href="index.html#page_370">section on saving forms</a> for more details on using save(commit=False).</p> <p id="page_374"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Overriding the default fields</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The default field types, as described in the <a href="index.html#page_366">Field types</a> table above, are sensible defaults. If you have a DateField in your model, chances are you’d want that to be represented as a DateField in your form. But ModelForm gives you the flexibility of changing the form field for a given model.</p> <p>To specify a custom widget for a field, use the widgets attribute of the inner Meta class. This should be a dictionary mapping field names to widget classes or instances.</p> <p>For example, if you want the CharField for the name attribute of Author to be represented by a <textarea> instead of its default <input type="text">, you can override the field’s widget:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.forms</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelForm, Textarea</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AuthorForm</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(ModelForm):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Meta</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"birth_date"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">widgets</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: Textarea(attrs</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"cols"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span dictionary accepts either widget instances (e.g., Textarea(...)) or classes (e.g., Textarea). Note that the widgets dictionary is ignored for a model field with a non-empty choices attribute. In this case, you must override the form field to use a different widget.</p> <p>Similarly, you can specify the labels, help_texts and error_messages attributes of the inner Meta class if you want to you can do this by declaratively specifying fields like you would in a regular Form.</p> <p>If you want to specify a field’s validators, you can do so by defining the field declaratively and setting style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: When you explicitly instantiate a form field like this, it is important to understand how ModelForm and regular Form are related.</p> <p>ModelForm is a regular Form which can automatically generate certain fields. The fields that are automatically generated depend on the content of the Meta class and on which fields have already been defined declaratively. Basically, ModelForm will only generate fields that are missing from the form, or in other words, fields that weren’t defined declaratively.</p> <p>Fields defined declaratively are left as-is, therefore any customizations made to Meta attributes such as widgets, labels, help_texts, or error_messages are ignored; these only apply to fields that are generated automatically.</p> <p>Similarly, fields defined declaratively do not draw their attributes like max_length or required from the corresponding model. If you want to maintain the behavior specified in the model, you must set the relevant arguments explicitly when declaring the form field.</p> <p>For example, if the Article model looks like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Article</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">200</span><span custom validation for headline, while keeping the blank and help_text values as specified, you might define ArticleForm like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span id="page_377" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span contents of the corresponding model field. When they are not compatible, you will get a ValueError as no implicit conversion takes place.</p> <p>See the <a href="index.html#page_1517">form field documentation</a> for more information on fields and their arguments.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Enabling localization of fields</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>By default, the fields in a ModelForm will not localize their data. To enable localization for fields, you can use the localized_fields attribute on the Meta class.</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.forms</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelForm</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AuthorForm</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(ModelForm):</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Meta</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">model</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">localized_fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">'birth_date'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If localized_fields is set to the special value '__all__', all fields will be localized.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Form inheritance</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>As with basic forms, you can extend and reuse ModelForms by inheriting them. This is useful if you need to declare extra fields or extra methods on a parent class for use in a number of forms derived from models. For example, using the previous ArticleForm class:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>EnhancedArticleForm</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(ArticleForm):</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>clean_pub_date</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This creates a form that behaves identically to ArticleForm, except there’s some extra validation and clean-ing for the pub_date field.</p> <p>You can also subclass the parent’s Meta inner class if you want to change the Meta.fields or Meta.exclude lists:</p> <p id="page_378"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>RestrictedArticleForm</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(EnhancedArticleForm):</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Meta</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(ArticleForm</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Meta):</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">exclude</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"body"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This adds the extra method from the EnhancedArticleForm and modifies the original ArticleForm.Meta to remove one field.</p> <p>There are a couple of things to note, however.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Normal Python name resolution rules apply. If you have multiple base classes that declare a Meta inner</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">class, only the first one will be used. This means the child’s Meta, if it exists, otherwise the Meta of the first parent, etc.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• It’s possible to inherit from both Form and ModelForm simultaneously, however, you must ensure that</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">ModelForm appears first in the MRO. This is because these classes rely on different metaclasses and a class can only have one metaclass.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• It’s possible to declaratively remove a Field inherited from a parent class by setting the name to be</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">None on the subclass.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">You can only use this technique to opt out from a field defined declaratively by a parent class; it won’t prevent the ModelForm metaclass from generating a default field. To opt-out from default fields, see</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_372">Selecting the fields to use</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Providing initial values</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>As with regular forms, it’s possible to specify initial data for forms by specifying an initial parameter when instantiating the form. Initial values provided this way will override both initial values from the form field and values from an attached model instance. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">article</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Article</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(pk</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">article</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">headline</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">'My headline'</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ArticleForm(initial</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"headline"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Initial headline"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">}, instance</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">article)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">form[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"headline"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">value()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">'Initial headline'</span></p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_379" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>ModelForm factory function</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can create forms from a given model using the standalone function <a href="index.html#page_1548"><i>modelform_factory()</i>, </a>instead of using a class definition. This may be more convenient if you do not have many customizations to make:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.forms</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">modelform_factory</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Book</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">BookForm</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">modelform_factory(Book, fields</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"author"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">])</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This can also be used to make modifications to existing forms, for example by specifying the widgets to be used for a given field:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.forms</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Textarea</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Form</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">modelform_factory(Book, form</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">BookForm, widgets</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: Textarea()})</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The fields to include can be specified using the fields and exclude keyword arguments, or the corresponding</p> <p>attributes on the ModelForm inner Meta class. Please see the ModelForm <a href="index.html#page_372">Selecting the fields to use</a> documen-tation.</p> <p><i>. . .</i> or enable localization for specific fields:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Form</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">modelform_factory(Author, form</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">AuthorForm, localized_fields</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"birth_date"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">])</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Model formsets</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> models.<b>BaseModelFormSet</b></p> <p>Like <a href="index.html#page_344">regular formsets, </a>Django provides a couple of enhanced formset classes to make working with Django models more convenient. Let’s reuse the Author model from above:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.forms</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">modelformset_factory</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">AuthorFormSet</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">modelformset_factory(Author, fields</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">])</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Using fields restricts the formset to use only the given fields. Alternatively, you can take an “opt-out” approach, specifying which fields to exclude:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">AuthorFormSet</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">modelformset_factory(Author, exclude</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"birth_date"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">])</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This will create a formset that is capable of working with the data associated with the Author model. It works just like a regular formset:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">formset</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">AuthorFormSet()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">print</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(formset)</span></p> <p href="index.html#page_1549"><i>modelformset_factory()</i></a> uses <a href="index.html#page_1550"><i>formset_factory()</i></a> to generate formsets. This means that a model formset is an extension of a basic formset that knows how to interact with a particular model.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: When using <a href="index.html#page_136">multi-table inheritance</a>, forms generated by a formset factory will contain a parent link field (by default <parent_model_name>_ptr) instead of an id field.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Changing the queryset</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>By default, when you create a formset from a model, the formset will use a queryset that includes all objects in the model (e.g., Author.objects.all()). You can override this behavior by using the queryset argument:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">formset</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"O"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">))</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Alternatively, you can create a subclass that sets self.queryset in __init__:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.forms</span> <span Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">AuthorFormSet</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">modelformset_factory(</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author, fields</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span the model, you can specify an empty QuerySet:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">AuthorFormSet(queryset</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">none())</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Changing the form</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>By default, when you use modelformset_factory, a model form will be created using <a href="index.html#page_1548"><i>modelform_factory()</i></a>. Often, it can be useful to specify a custom model form. For example, you can create a custom model form that has custom validation:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AuthorForm</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(forms</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelForm):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Meta</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">model</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>clean_name</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># custom validation for the name field</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Then, pass your model form to the factory function:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">AuthorFormSet</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">modelformset_factory(Author, form</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">AuthorForm)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>It is not always necessary to define a custom model form. The modelformset_factory function has several arguments which are passed through to modelform_factory, which are described below.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Specifying widgets to use in the form with widgets</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Using the widgets parameter, you can specify a dictionary of values to customize the ModelForm’s widget class for a particular field. This works the same way as the widgets dictionary on the inner Meta class of a ModelForm works:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">AuthorFormSet</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">modelformset_factory(</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">widgets</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: Textarea(attrs</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"cols"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">80</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"rows"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">20</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">})},</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p id="page_382"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Enabling localization for fields with localized_fields</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Using the localized_fields parameter, you can enable localization for fields in the form.</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">AuthorFormSet</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">modelformset_factory(</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author, fields</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">'name'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'title'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'birth_date'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">localized_fields</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">'birth_date'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">])</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If localized_fields is set to the special value '__all__', all fields will be localized.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Providing initial values</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>As with regular formsets, it’s possible to <a href="index.html#page_345">specify initial data</a> for forms in the formset by specifying an initial</p> <p>parameter when instantiating the model formset class returned by <a href="index.html#page_1549"><i>modelformset_factory()</i></a>. However, with model formsets, the initial values only apply to extra forms, those that aren’t attached to an existing model instance. If the length of initial exceeds the number of extra forms, the excess initial data is ignored. If the extra forms with initial data aren’t changed by the user, they won’t be validated or saved.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Saving objects in the formset</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>As with a ModelForm, you can save the data as a model object. This is done with the formset’s save() method:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"># Create a formset instance with POST data.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">formset</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">AuthorFormSet(request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">POST)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"># Assuming all is valid, save the data.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">instances</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">formset</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The save() method returns the instances that have been saved to the database. If a given instance’s data didn’t change in the bound data, the instance won’t be saved to the database and won’t be included in the return value (instances, in the above example).</p> <p>When fields are missing from the form (for example because they have been excluded), these fields will not be set by the save() method. You can find more information about this restriction, which also holds for</p> <p>regular ModelForms, in <a href="index.html#page_372">Selecting the fields to use</a>.</p> <p>Pass commit=False to return the unsaved model instances:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"># don't save to the database</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">instances</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">formset</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save(commit</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=False</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">instance</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">instances:</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># do something with instance</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">instance</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span></p> <p id="page_383" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This gives you the ability to attach data to the instances before saving them to the database. If your form-set contains a ManyToManyField, you’ll also need to call formset.save_m2m() to ensure the many-to-many relationships are saved properly.</p> <p>After calling save(), your model formset will have three new attributes containing the formset’s changes:</p> <p>models.BaseModelFormSet.<b>changed_objects</b></p> <p>models.BaseModelFormSet.<b>deleted_objects</b></p> </p> <p>A max_num value of None (the default) puts a high limit on the number of forms displayed (1000). In practice this is equivalent to no limit.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Preventing new objects creation</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Using the edit_only parameter, you can prevent creation of any new objects:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">AuthorFormSet</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">modelformset_factory(</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">fields</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">edit_only</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Here, the formset will only edit existing Author instances. No other objects will be created or edited.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using a model formset in a view</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Model formsets are very similar to formsets. Let’s say we want to present a formset to edit Author model instances:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.forms</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">modelformset_factory</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.shortcuts</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">render</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>manage_authors</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">AuthorFormSet</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">modelformset_factory(Author, fields</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">method</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"POST"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">formset</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">AuthorFormSet(request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">POST, request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">FILES)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span something.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>else</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">formset</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">AuthorFormSet()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">render(request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"manage_authors.html"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, {</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"formset"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: formset})</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>As you can see, the view logic of a model formset isn’t drastically different than that of a “normal” formset. The only difference is that we call formset.save() to save the data into the database. (This was described</p> <p>above, in <a href="index.html#page_382">Saving objects in the formset</a>.)</p> <p id="page_385" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Overriding clean() on a ModelFormSet</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Just like with ModelForms, by default the clean() method of a ModelFormSet will validate that none of the items in the formset violate the unique constraints on your model (either unique, unique_together or unique_for_date|month|year). If you want to override the clean() method on a ModelFormSet and maintain this validation, you must call the parent class’s clean method:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.forms</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">BaseModelFormSet</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyModelFormSet</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(BaseModelFormSet):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>clean</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">clean()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># example custom validation across forms in the formset</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">forms:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># your custom formset validation</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Also note that by the time you reach this step, individual model instances have already been created for each Form. Modifying a value in form.cleaned_data is not sufficient to affect the saved value. If you wish to modify a value in ModelFormSet.clean() you must modify form.instance:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.forms</span> <span <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">forms:</span></p> <p style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">cleaned_data[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># update the instance value.</i></span></p> <p
