style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using the formset in the template</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>There are three ways to render a formset in a Django template.</p> <p>First, you can let the formset do most of the work:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">method</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Second, you can manually render the formset, but let the form deal with itself:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">method</span><span style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">formset</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When you manually render the forms yourself, be sure to render the management form as shown above. See</p> <p>the <a href="index.html#page_348">management form documentation</a>.</p> <p>Third, you can manually render each field:</p> <p id="page_387" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span> <span <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span> <span <span style="font-size:0.87em">form.age</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Notice how we need to explicitly render {{ form.id }}. This ensures that the model formset, in the POST case, will work correctly. (This example assumes a primary key named id. If you’ve explicitly defined your own primary key that isn’t called id, make sure it gets rendered.)</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Inline formsets</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> models.<b>BaseInlineFormSet</b></p> <p>Inline formsets is a small abstraction layer on top of model formsets. These simplify the case of working with related objects via a foreign key. Suppose you have these two models:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">100</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Book</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ForeignKey(Author, on_delete</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">100</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p id="page_388"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you want to create a formset that allows you to edit books belonging to a particular author, you could do this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span <span style="font-size:0.87em">inlineformset_factory(Author, Book, fields</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Mike Royko"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">BookFormSet(instance</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">author)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>BookFormSet’s <a href="index.html#page_361">prefix</a> is 'book_set' (<model name>_set ). If Book’s ForeignKey to Author has a</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1647"><i>related_name</i></a>, that’s used instead.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: <a href="index.html#page_1550"><i>inlineformset_factory()</i></a> uses <a href="index.html#page_1549"><i>modelformset_factory()</i></a> and marks can_delete=True.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>See also:</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_364">Manually rendered can_delete and can_order.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Overriding methods on an InlineFormSet</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When overriding methods on InlineFormSet, you should subclass <a href="index.html#page_387"><i>BaseInlineFormSet</i></a> rather than</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_379"><i>BaseModelFormSet</i>.</a></p> <p>For example, if you want to override clean():</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.forms</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">BaseInlineFormSet</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>CustomInlineFormSet</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(BaseInlineFormSet):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>clean</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">clean()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># example custom validation across forms in the formset</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">forms:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># your custom formset validation</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>See also <a href="index.html#page_385">Overriding clean() on a ModelFormSet</a>.</p> <p>Then when you create your inline formset, pass in the optional argument formset:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.forms</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">inlineformset_factory</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">BookFormSet</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">inlineformset_factory(</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author, Book, fields</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">], formset</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CustomInlineFormSet</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">author</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Mike Royko"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">formset</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">BookFormSet(instance</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">author)</span></p> <p id="page_389" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>More than one foreign key to the same model</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If your model contains more than one foreign key to the same model, you’ll need to resolve the ambiguity manually using fk_name. For example, consider the following model:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Friendship</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">to_friend</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ForeignKey(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">Friend,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">on_delete</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CASCADE,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">related_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"friends"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">length_in_months</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">IntegerField()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To resolve this, you can use fk_name to <a href="index.html#page_1550"><i>inlineformset_factory()</i>:</a></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">FriendshipFormSet</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">inlineformset_factory(</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Friend, Friendship, fk_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"from_friend"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, fields</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"to_friend"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"length_in_months"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using an inline formset in a view</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You may want to provide a view that allows a user to edit the related objects of a model. Here’s how you can do that:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>manage_books</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request, author_id):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">author</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(pk</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">author_id)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">BookInlineFormSet</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">inlineformset_factory(Author, Book, fields</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">])</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">method</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"POST"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">formset</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">BookInlineFormSet(request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">POST, request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">FILES, instance</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">author)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">formset</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">is_valid():</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">formset</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Do something. Should generally end with a redirect. For example:</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponseRedirect(author</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_absolute_url())</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>else</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">formset</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">BookInlineFormSet(instance</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">author)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">render(request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"manage_books.html"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, {</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"formset"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: formset})</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Notice how we pass instance in both the POST and GET cases.</p> <p id="page_390"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Specifying widgets to use in the inline form</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>inlineformset_factory uses modelformset_factory and passes most of its arguments to modelformset_factory. This means you can use the widgets parameter in much the same way as</p> <p>passing it to modelformset_factory. See <a href="index.html#page_381">Specifying widgets to use in the form with widgets</a> above.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Form Assets (the Media class)</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Rendering an attractive and easy-to-use web form requires more than just HTML - it also requires CSS stylesheets, and if you want to use fancy widgets, you may also need to include some JavaScript on each page. The exact combination of CSS and JavaScript that is required for any given page will depend upon the widgets that are in use on that page.</p> <p>This is where asset definitions come in. Django allows you to associate different files – like stylesheets and scripts – with the forms and widgets that require those assets. For example, if you want to use a calendar to render DateFields, you can define a custom Calendar widget. This widget can then be associated with the CSS and JavaScript that is required to render the calendar. When the Calendar widget is used on a form, Django is able to identify the CSS and JavaScript files that are required, and provide the list of file names in a form suitable for inclusion on your web page.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Assets and Django Admin</p> <p>The Django Admin application defines a number of customized widgets for calendars, filtered selections, and so on. These widgets define asset requirements, and the Django Admin uses the custom widgets in place of the Django defaults. The Admin templates will only include those files that are required to render the widgets on any given page.</p> <p>If you like the widgets that the Django Admin application uses, feel free to use them in your own application! They’re all stored in django.contrib.admin.widgets.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Which JavaScript toolkit?</p> <p>Many JavaScript toolkits exist, and many of them include widgets (such as calendar widgets) that can be used to enhance your application. Django has deliberately avoided blessing any one JavaScript toolkit. Each toolkit has its own relative strengths and weaknesses - use whichever toolkit suits your requirements. Django is able to integrate with any JavaScript toolkit.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_391" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Assets as a static definition</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The easiest way to define assets is as a static definition. Using this method, the declaration is an inner Media class. The properties of the inner class define the requirements.</p> <p>Here’s an example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">forms</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>CalendarWidget</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(forms</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">TextInput):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Media</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">css</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"all"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"pretty.css"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">js</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"animations.js"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"actions.js"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This code defines a CalendarWidget, which will be based on TextInput. Every time the CalendarWidget is used on a form, that form will be directed to include the CSS file pretty.css, and the JavaScript files animations.js and actions.js.</p> <p>This static definition is converted at runtime into a widget property named media. The list of assets for a CalendarWidget instance can be retrieved through this property:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">w</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">CalendarWidget()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">print</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(w</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">media)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><link href="https://static.example.com/pretty.css" media="all" rel="stylesheet"></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><script src="https://static.example.com/animations.js"></script></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><script src="https://static.example.com/actions.js"></script></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Here’s a list of all possible Media options. There are no required options.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>css</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A dictionary describing the CSS files required for various forms of output media.</p> <p>The values in the dictionary should be a tuple/list of file names. See <a href="index.html#page_394">the section on paths</a> for details of how to specify paths to these files.</p> <p>The keys in the dictionary are the output media types. These are the same types accepted by CSS files in media declarations: ‘all’, ‘aural’, ‘braille’, ‘embossed’, ‘handheld’, ‘print’, ‘projection’, ‘screen’, ‘tty’ and ‘tv’. If you need to have different stylesheets for different media types, provide a list of CSS files for each output medium. The following example would provide two CSS options – one for the screen, and one for print:</p> <p id="page_392"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Media</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">css</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"screen"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"pretty.css"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"print"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"newspaper.css"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If a group of CSS files are appropriate for multiple output media types, the dictionary key can be a comma separated list of output media types. In the following example, TV’s and projectors will have the same media requirements:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Media</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">css</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"screen"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"pretty.css"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"tv,projector"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"lo_res.css"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"print"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"newspaper.css"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If this last CSS definition were to be rendered, it would become the following HTML:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">link</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">href</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"animations.js"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"actions.js"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>OtherWidget</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(forms</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">w1</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">CalendarWidget()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">w2</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">OtherWidget()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">print</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(w1</span><span rel="stylesheet"></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><script src="https://static.example.com/animations.js"></script></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><script src="https://static.example.com/actions.js"></script></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><script src="https://static.example.com/whizbang.js"></script></span></p> <p id="page_397" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Order of assets</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The order in which assets are inserted into the DOM is often important. For example, you may have a script that depends on jQuery. Therefore, combining Media objects attempts to preserve the relative order in which assets are defined in each Media class.</p> <p>For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>CalendarWidget</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(forms</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">TextInput):</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Media</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">js</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"jQuery.js"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"calendar.js"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"noConflict.js"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>TimeWidget</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(forms</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">TextInput):</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Media</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">js</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"jQuery.js"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"time.js"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"noConflict.js"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">w1</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">CalendarWidget()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">w2</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">TimeWidget()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">print</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(w1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">media</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>+</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">w2</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">media)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><script src="https://static.example.com/jQuery.js"></script></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><script src="https://static.example.com/calendar.js"></script></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><script src="https://static.example.com/time.js"></script></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><script src="https://static.example.com/noConflict.js"></script></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Combining Media objects with assets in a conflicting order results in a MediaOrderConflictWarning.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Media on Forms</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Widgets aren’t the only objects that can have media definitions – forms can also define media. The rules for media definitions on forms are the same as the rules for widgets: declarations can be static or dynamic; path and inheritance rules for those declarations are exactly the same.</p> <p>Regardless of whether you define a media declaration, all Form objects have a media property. The default value for this property is the result of adding the media definitions for all widgets that are part of the form:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">forms</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ContactForm</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(forms</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Form):</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">date</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">DateField(widget</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CalendarWidget)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">40</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, widget</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">OtherWidget)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">f</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ContactForm()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">f</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">media</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_398"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><link href="https://static.example.com/pretty.css" media="all" rel="stylesheet"></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><script src="https://static.example.com/animations.js"></script></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><script src="https://static.example.com/actions.js"></script></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><script src="https://static.example.com/whizbang.js"></script></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you want to associate additional assets with a form – for example, CSS for form layout – add a Media declaration to the form:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ContactForm</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(forms</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Form):</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">date</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">DateField(widget</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CalendarWidget)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">40</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, widget</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">OtherWidget)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Media</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">css</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"all"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"layout.css"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">f</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ContactForm()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">f</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">media</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><link href="https://static.example.com/pretty.css" media="all" rel="stylesheet"></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><link href="https://static.example.com/layout.css" media="all" rel="stylesheet"></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><script src="https://static.example.com/animations.js"></script></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><script src="https://static.example.com/actions.js"></script></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><script src="https://static.example.com/whizbang.js"></script></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>See also:</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1487">The Forms Reference</a></p> <p style="text-align:center">Covers the full API reference, including form fields, form widgets, and form and field validation.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.47em"><b>3.5 Templates</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Being a web framework, Django needs a convenient way to generate HTML dynamically. The most common approach relies on templates. A template contains the static parts of the desired HTML output as well as some special syntax describing how dynamic content will be inserted. For a hands-on example of creating</p> <p>HTML pages with templates, see <a href="index.html#page_42">Tutorial 3.</a></p> <p>A Django project can be configured with one or several template engines (or even zero if you don’t use tem-plates). Django ships built-in backends for its own template system, creatively called the Django template</p> <p>language (DTL), and for the popular alternative <a href="https://jinja.palletsprojects.com/">Jinja2. </a>Backends for other template languages may be</p> <p>available from third-parties. You can also write your own custom backend, see <a href="index.html#page_814">Custom template backend</a></p> <p>Django defines a standard API for loading and rendering templates regardless of the backend. Loading con-sists of finding the template for a given identifier and preprocessing it, usually compiling it to an in-memory</p> <p id="page_399" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>representation. Rendering means interpolating the template with context data and returning the resulting string.</p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_1965">Django template language</a> is Django’s own template system. Until Django 1.8 it was the only built-in option available. It’s a good template library even though it’s fairly opinionated and sports a few idiosyn-crasies. If you don’t have a pressing reason to choose another backend, you should use the DTL, especially if you’re writing a pluggable application and you intend to distribute templates. Django’s contrib apps that include templates, like <a href="index.html#page_1017">django.contrib.admin, </a>use the DTL.</p> <p>For historical reasons, both the generic support for template engines and the implementation of the Django template language live in the django.template namespace.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: The template system isn’t safe against untrusted template authors. For example, a site</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">shouldn’t allow its users to provide their own templates, since template authors can do things like per-</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">form XSS attacks and access properties of template variables that may contain sensitive information.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.5.1 The Django template language</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Syntax</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>About this section</p> <p>This is an overview of the Django template language’s syntax. For details see the <a href="index.html#page_1965">language syntax reference</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A Django template is a text document or a Python string marked-up using the Django template language. Some constructs are recognized and interpreted by the template engine. The main ones are variables and tags.</p> <p>A template is rendered with a context. Rendering replaces variables with their values, which are looked up in the context, and executes tags. Everything else is output as is.</p> <p>The syntax of the Django template language involves four constructs.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Variables</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A variable outputs a value from the context, which is a dict-like object mapping keys to values.</p> <p>Variables are surrounded by {{ and }} like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">My first name is</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">first_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">. My last name is</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">last_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>With a context of {'first_name': 'John', 'last_name': 'Doe'}, this template renders to:</p> <p id="page_400"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">My first name is John. My last name is Doe.</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Dictionary lookup, attribute lookup and list-index lookups are implemented with a dot notation:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">my_dict.key</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">my_object.attribute</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">my_list.0</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If a variable resolves to a callable, the template system will call it with no arguments and use its result instead of the callable.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Tags</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Tags provide arbitrary logic in the rendering process.</p> <p>This definition is deliberately vague. For example, a tag can output content, serve as a control structure e.g. an “if” statement or a “for” loop, grab content from a database, or even enable access to other template tags.</p> <p>Tags are surrounded by {% and %} like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>csrf_token</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Most tags accept arguments:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>cycle</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'odd' 'even'</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Some tags require beginning and ending tags:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">user.is_authenticated</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Hello,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">user.username</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endif</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A <a href="index.html#page_1979">reference of built-in tags</a> is available as well as <a href="index.html#page_825">instructions for writing custom tags</a><a href="index.html#page_825">.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Filters</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Filters transform the values of variables and tag arguments.</p> <p>They look like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>title</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>With a context of {'django': 'the web framework for perfectionists with deadlines'}, this tem-plate renders to:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">The Web Framework For Perfectionists With Deadlines</span></p> <p id="page_401" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Some filters take an argument:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">my_date</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>date</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:"Y-m-d"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A <a href="index.html#page_2004">reference of built-in filters</a> is available as well as <a href="index.html#page_819">instructions for writing custom filters</a><a href="index.html#page_819">.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Comments</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Comments look like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i>{# this won't be rendered #}</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A <a href="index.html#page_1980"><i>{% comment %}</i></a> tag provides multi-line comments.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Components</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>About this section</p> <p>This is an overview of the Django template language’s APIs. For details see the <a href="index.html#page_2030">API reference</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Engine</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><a href="index.html#page_2031"><i>django.template.Engine</i></a> encapsulates an instance of the Django template system. The main reason for</p> <p>instantiating an <a href="index.html#page_2031"><i>Engine</i></a> directly is to use the Django template language outside of a Django project.</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_407"><i>django.template.backends.django.DjangoTemplates</i></a> is a thin wrapper adapting <a href="index.html#page_2031"><i>django.template.</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_2031"><i>Engine</i></a> to Django’s template backend API.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Template</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><a href="index.html#page_2033"><i>django.template.Template</i></a> represents a compiled template. Templates are obtained with <a href="index.html#page_2033"><i>Engine.</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_2033"><i>get_template()</i></a> or <a href="index.html#page_2033"><i>Engine.from_string()</i>.</a></p> <p>Likewise django.template.backends.django.Template is a thin wrapper adapting <a href="index.html#page_2033"><i>django.template.</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_2033"><i>Template</i></a> to the common template API.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_402"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Context</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><a href="index.html#page_2034"><i>django.template.Context</i></a> holds some metadata in addition to the context data. It is passed to <a href="index.html#page_2034"><i>Template.</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_2034"><i>render()</i></a> for rendering a template.</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_2042"><i>django.template.RequestContext</i></a> is a subclass of <a href="index.html#page_2034"><i>Context</i></a> that stores the current <a href="index.html#page_1859"><i>HttpRequest</i></a> and runs template context processors.</p> <p>The common API doesn’t have an equivalent concept. Context data is passed in a plain <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict">dict</a> and the current</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1859"><i>HttpRequest</i></a> is passed separately if needed.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Loaders</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Template loaders are responsible for locating templates, loading them, and returning <a href="index.html#page_2033"><i>Template</i></a> objects.</p> <p>Django provides several <a href="index.html#page_2047">built-in template loaders</a> and supports <a href="index.html#page_2050">custom template loaders</a><a href="index.html#page_2050">.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Context processors</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Context processors are functions that receive the current <a href="index.html#page_1859"><i>HttpRequest</i></a> as an argument and return a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict">dict</a> of data to be added to the rendering context.</p> <p>Their main use is to add common data shared by all templates to the context without repeating code in every view.</p> <p>Django provides many <a href="index.html#page_2043">built-in context processors, </a>and you can implement your own additional context processors, too.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.5.2 Support for template engines</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Configuration</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Templates engines are configured with the <a href="index.html#page_1932"><i>TEMPLATES</i></a> setting. It’s a list of configurations, one for each engine.</p> <p>The default value is empty. The settings.py generated by the <a href="index.html#page_1456"><i>startproject</i></a> command defines a more useful value:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">TEMPLATES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"BACKEND"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.template.backends.django.DjangoTemplates"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"DIRS"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"APP_DIRS"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"OPTIONS"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ... some options here ...</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_403" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1932"><i>BACKEND</i></a> is a dotted Python path to a template engine class implementing Django’s template backend API.</p> <p>The built-in backends are <a href="index.html#page_407"><i>django.template.backends.django.DjangoTemplates</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_408"><i>django.template.</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_408"><i>backends.jinja2.Jinja2</i></a>.</p> <p>Since most engines load templates from files, the top-level configuration for each engine contains two common settings:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>DIRS</i></a> defines a list of directories where the engine should look for template source files, in search order.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>APP_DIRS</i></a> tells whether the engine should look for templates inside installed applications. Each backend</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">defines a conventional name for the subdirectory inside applications where its templates should be stored.</p> <p>While uncommon, it’s possible to configure several instances of the same backend with different options. In</p> <p>that case you should define a unique <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>NAME</i></a> for each engine.</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>OPTIONS</i></a> contains backend-specific settings.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Usage</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The django.template.loader module defines two functions to load templates.</p> <p><b>get_template</b>(template_name, using=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This function loads the template with the given name and returns a Template object.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The exact type of the return value depends on the backend that loaded the template. Each backend has its own Template class.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">get_template() tries each template engine in order until one succeeds. If the template cannot be</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">found, it raises <a href="index.html#page_403"><i>TemplateDoesNotExist</i></a>. If the template is found but contains invalid syntax, it raises</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_404"><i>TemplateSyntaxError</i></a> .</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">How templates are searched and loaded depends on each engine’s backend and configuration.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you want to restrict the search to a particular template engine, pass the engine’s <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>NAME</i></a> in the using argument.</p> <p><b>select_template</b>(template_name_list, using=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">select_template() is just like get_template(), except it takes a list of template names. It tries each name in order and returns the first template that exists.</p> <p>If loading a template fails, the following two exceptions, defined in django.template, may be raised:</p> <p id="page_404"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>exception TemplateDoesNotExist</b>(msg, tried=None, backend=None, chain=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This exception is raised when a template cannot be found. It accepts the following optional arguments</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">for populating the <a href="index.html#page_815">template postmortem</a> on the debug page:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>backend</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The template backend instance from which the exception originated.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>tried</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A list of sources that were tried when finding the template. This is formatted as a list of tuples</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">containing (origin, status), where origin is an <a href="index.html#page_817">origin-like</a> object and status is a string with the reason the template wasn’t found.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>chain</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A list of intermediate <a href="index.html#page_403"><i>TemplateDoesNotExist</i></a> exceptions raised when trying to load a template.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">This is used by functions, such as <a href="index.html#page_403"><i>get_template()</i></a>, that try to load a given template from multiple engines.</p> <p><b>exception TemplateSyntaxError</b>( msg)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This exception is raised when a template was found but contains errors.</p> <p>Template objects returned by get_template() and select_template() must provide a render() method with the following signature:</p> <p>Template.<b>render</b>(context=None, request=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Renders this template with a given context.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If context is provided, it must be a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict">dict. </a>If it isn’t provided, the engine will render the template with an empty context.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If request is provided, it must be an <a href="index.html#page_1859"><i>HttpRequest</i>. </a>Then the engine must make it, as well as the CSRF token, available in the template. How this is achieved is up to each backend.</p> <p>Here’s an example of the search algorithm. For this example the <a href="index.html#page_1932"><i>TEMPLATES</i></a> setting is:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">TEMPLATES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"BACKEND"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.template.backends.django.DjangoTemplates"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"DIRS"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/home/html/example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/home/html/default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"BACKEND"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.template.backends.jinja2.Jinja2"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"DIRS"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/home/html/jinja2"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_405" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you call get_template('story_detail.html'), here are the files Django will look for, in order:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• /home/html/example.com/story_detail.html ('django' engine)</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• /home/html/default/story_detail.html ('django' engine)</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• /home/html/jinja2/story_detail.html ('jinja2' engine)</p> <p>If you call select_template(['story_253_detail.html', 'story_detail.html']), here’s what Django will look for:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• /home/html/example.com/story_253_detail.html ('django' engine)</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• /home/html/default/story_253_detail.html ('django' engine)</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• /home/html/jinja2/story_253_detail.html ('jinja2' engine)</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• /home/html/example.com/story_detail.html ('django' engine)</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• /home/html/default/story_detail.html ('django' engine)</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• /home/html/jinja2/story_detail.html ('jinja2' engine)</p> <p>When Django finds a template that exists, it stops looking.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Use <b>django.template.loader.select_template()</b> for more flexibility</p> <p>You can use <a href="index.html#page_403"><i>select_template()</i></a> for flexible template loading. For example, if you’ve written a news story and want some stories to have custom templates, use something like select_template(['story_%s_detail. html' % story.id, 'story_detail.html']). That’ll allow you to use a custom template for an individual story, with a fallback template for stories that don’t have custom templates.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>It’s possible – and preferable – to organize templates in subdirectories inside each directory containing tem-plates. The convention is to make a subdirectory for each Django app, with subdirectories within those subdirectories as needed.</p> <p>Do this for your own sanity. Storing all templates in the root level of a single directory gets messy.</p> <p>To load a template that’s within a subdirectory, use a slash, like so:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_template(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"news/story_detail.html"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Using the same <a href="index.html#page_1932"><i>TEMPLATES</i></a> option as above, this will attempt to load the following templates:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• /home/html/example.com/news/story_detail.html ('django' engine)</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• /home/html/default/news/story_detail.html ('django' engine)</p> <p id="page_406"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• /home/html/jinja2/news/story_detail.html ('jinja2' engine)</p> <p>In addition, to cut down on the repetitive nature of loading and rendering templates, Django provides a shortcut function which automates the process.</p> <p><b>render_to_string</b>( template_name, context=None, request=None, using=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">render_to_string() loads a template like <a href="index.html#page_403"><i>get_template()</i></a> and calls its render() method immedi-ately. It takes the following arguments.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>template_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The name of the template to load and render. If it’s a list of template names, Django uses</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_403"><i>select_template()</i></a> instead of <a href="index.html#page_403"><i>get_template()</i></a> to find the template.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>context</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict">dict</a> to be used as the template’s context for rendering.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>request</b></p> <p style="text-align:center">An optional <a href="index.html#page_1859"><i>HttpRequest</i></a> that will be available during the template’s rendering process.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>using</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">An optional template engine <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>NAME</i></a> . The search for the template will be restricted to that engine.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Usage example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.template.loader</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">render_to_string</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">rendered</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">render_to_string(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"my_template.html"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, {</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"foo"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"bar"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">})</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>See also the <a href="index.html#page_297"><i>render()</i></a> shortcut which calls <a href="index.html#page_406"><i>render_to_string()</i></a> and feeds the result into an <a href="index.html#page_1871"><i>HttpResponse</i></a> suitable for returning from a view.</p> <p>Finally, you can use configured engines directly:</p> <p><b>engines</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Template engines are available in django.template.engines:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.template</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">engines</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">django_engine</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">engines[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"django"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django_engine</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">from_string(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Hello {{ name }}!"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The lookup key — 'django' in this example — is the engine’s <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>NAME</i></a> .</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_407" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Built-in backends</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class DjangoTemplates</b></p> <p>Set <a href="index.html#page_1932"><i>BACKEND</i></a> to 'django.template.backends.django.DjangoTemplates' to configure a Django template engine.</p> <p>When <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>APP_DIRS</i></a> is True, DjangoTemplates engines look for templates in the templates subdirectory of in-stalled applications. This generic name was kept for backwards-compatibility.</p> <p>DjangoTemplates engines accept the following <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>OPTIONS</i></a>:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'autoescape': a boolean that controls whether HTML autoescaping is enabled.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">It defaults to True.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em">Warning: Only set it to False if you’re rendering non-HTML templates!</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'context_processors': a list of dotted Python paths to callables that are used to populate the context</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">when a template is rendered with a request. These callables take a request object as their argument</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">and return a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict">dict</a> of items to be merged into the context.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">It defaults to an empty list.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">See <a href="index.html#page_2042"><i>RequestContext</i></a> for more information.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'debug': a boolean that turns on/off template debug mode. If it is True, the fancy error page will</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">display a detailed report for any exception raised during template rendering. This report contains the relevant snippet of the template with the appropriate line highlighted.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">It defaults to the value of the <a href="index.html#page_1907"><i>DEBUG</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'loaders': a list of dotted Python paths to template loader classes. Each Loader class knows how to</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">import templates from a particular source. Optionally, a tuple can be used instead of a string. The first item in the tuple should be the Loader class name, and subsequent items are passed to the Loader during initialization.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The default depends on the values of <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>DIRS</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>APP_DIRS</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">See <a href="index.html#page_2047">Loader types</a> for details.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'string_if_invalid': the output, as a string, that the template system should use for invalid (e.g.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">misspelled) variables.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">It defaults to an empty string.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">See <a href="index.html#page_2037">How invalid variables are handled</a> for details.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'file_charset': the charset used to read template files on disk.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">It defaults to 'utf-8'.</p> <p id="page_408"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'libraries': A dictionary of labels and dotted Python paths of template tag modules to register with</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">the template engine. This can be used to add new libraries or provide alternate labels for existing ones. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">OPTIONS</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"libraries"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"myapp_tags"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"path.to.myapp.tags"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"admin.urls"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.contrib.admin.templatetags.admin_urls"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Libraries can be loaded by passing the corresponding dictionary key to the <a href="index.html#page_1993"><i>{% load %}</i></a> tag.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'builtins': A list of dotted Python paths of template tag modules to add to <a href="index.html#page_1979">built-ins. </a>For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">OPTIONS</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"builtins"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"myapp.builtins"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Tags and filters from built-in libraries can be used without first calling the <a href="index.html#page_1993"><i>{% load %}</i></a> tag.</p> <p><b>class Jinja2</b></p> <p>Requires <a href="https://jinja.palletsprojects.com/">Jinja2</a> to be installed:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">$</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">python -m pip install Jinja2</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Set <a href="index.html#page_1932"><i>BACKEND</i></a> to 'django.template.backends.jinja2.Jinja2' to configure a <a href="https://jinja.palletsprojects.com/">Jinja2</a> engine.</p> <p>When <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>APP_DIRS</i></a> is True, Jinja2 engines look for templates in the jinja2 subdirectory of installed applica-tions.</p> <p>The most important entry in <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>OPTIONS</i></a> is 'environment'. It’s a dotted Python path to a callable returning a Jinja2 environment. It defaults to 'jinja2.Environment'. Django invokes that callable and passes other options as keyword arguments. Furthermore, Django adds defaults that differ from Jinja2’s for a few options:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'autoescape': True</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'loader': a loader configured for <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>DIRS</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>APP_DIRS</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'auto_reload': settings.DEBUG</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'undefined': DebugUndefined if settings.DEBUG else Undefined</p> <p>Jinja2 engines also accept the following <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>OPTIONS</i></a>:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'context_processors': a list of dotted Python paths to callables that are used to populate the context</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">when a template is rendered with a request. These callables take a request object as their argument</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">and return a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict">dict</a> of items to be merged into the context.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">It defaults to an empty list.</p> <p id="page_409" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Using context processors with Jinja2 templates is discouraged.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Context processors are useful with Django templates because Django templates don’t support calling functions with arguments. Since Jinja2 doesn’t have that limitation, it’s recommended to put the func-tion that you would use as a context processor in the global variables available to the template using jinja2.Environment as described below. You can then call that function in the template:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">function</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>(</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>)</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Some Django templates context processors return a fixed value. For Jinja2 templates, this layer of indirection isn’t necessary since you can add constants directly in jinja2.Environment.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The original use case for adding context processors for Jinja2 involved:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– Making an expensive computation that depends on the request.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– Needing the result in every template.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– Using the result multiple times in each template.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Unless all of these conditions are met, passing a function to the template is more in line with the design of Jinja2.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The default configuration is purposefully kept to a minimum. If a template is rendered with a request (e.g.</p> <p>when using <a href="index.html#page_297"><i>render()</i>), </a>the Jinja2 backend adds the globals request, csrf_input, and csrf_token to the context. Apart from that, this backend doesn’t create a Django-flavored environment. It doesn’t know about Django filters and tags. In order to use Django-specific APIs, you must configure them into the environment.</p> <p>For example, you can create myproject/jinja2.py with this content:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.templatetags.static</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">static</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.urls</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">reverse</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">jinja2</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Environment</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>environment</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">options):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">env</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Environment(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">options)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">env</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">globals</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">update(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"static"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: static,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"url"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: reverse,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">env</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>and set the 'environment' option to 'myproject.jinja2.environment'.</p> <p id="page_410"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Then you could use the following constructs in Jinja2 templates:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">img</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">src</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">static</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>(</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">'path/to/company-logo.png'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>)</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">alt</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Company Logo"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">href</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">url</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>(</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">'admin:index'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>)</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>Administration</</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The concepts of tags and filters exist both in the Django template language and in Jinja2 but they’re used differently. Since Jinja2 supports passing arguments to callables in templates, many features that require a template tag or filter in Django templates can be achieved by calling a function in Jinja2 templates, as shown in the example above. Jinja2’s global namespace removes the need for template context processors. The Django template language doesn’t have an equivalent of Jinja2 tests.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.47em"><b>3.6 Class-based views</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A view is a callable which takes a request and returns a response. This can be more than just a function, and Django provides an example of some classes which can be used as views. These allow you to structure your views and reuse code by harnessing inheritance and mixins. There are also some generic views for tasks which we’ll get to later, but you may want to design your own structure of reusable views which suits your use case.
