prevents users who aren’t logged in from accessing the form. If you omit that, you’ll</p> <p>need to handle unauthorized users in <a href="index.html#page_989"><i>form_valid()</i>.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Content negotiation example</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Here is an example showing how you might go about implementing a form that works with an API-based workflow as well as ‘normal’ form POSTs:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.http</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">JsonResponse</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.views.generic.edit</span> <span style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">accepted_type</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span href="index.html#page_1866"><i>HttpRequest.get_preferred_type()</i></a> method was added.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.6.4 Using mixins with class-based views</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Caution: This is an advanced topic. A working knowledge of <a href="index.html#page_410">Django’s class-based views</a> is advised</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">before exploring these techniques.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django’s built-in class-based views provide a lot of functionality, but some of it you may want to use sepa-rately. For instance, you may want to write a view that renders a template to make the HTTP response, but</p> <p>you can’t use <a href="index.html#page_952"><i>TemplateView</i></a>; perhaps you need to render a template only on POST, with GET doing something</p> <p>else entirely. While you could use <a href="index.html#page_2054"><i>TemplateResponse</i></a> directly, this will likely result in duplicate code.</p> <p>For this reason, Django also provides a number of mixins that provide more discrete functionality. Template</p> <p>rendering, for instance, is encapsulated in the <a href="index.html#page_979"><i>TemplateResponseMixin</i></a>. The Django reference documenta-</p> <p>tion contains <a href="index.html#page_978">full documentation of all the mixins.</a></p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_432"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Context and template responses</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Two central mixins are provided that help in providing a consistent interface to working with templates in class-based views.</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_979"><i><b>TemplateResponseMixin</b></i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Every built in view which returns a <a href="index.html#page_2054"><i>TemplateResponse</i></a> will call the <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>render_to_response()</i></a> method that TemplateResponseMixin provides. Most of the time this will be called for you (for instance, it</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">is called by the get() method implemented by both <a href="index.html#page_952"><i>TemplateView</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_955"><i>DetailView</i></a>); similarly, it’s unlikely that you’ll need to override it, although if you want your response to return something not</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">rendered via a Django template then you’ll want to do it. For an example of this, see the <a href="index.html#page_442">JSONRespon-</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_442">seMixin example</a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">render_to_response() itself calls <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>get_template_names()</i></a>, which by default will look up</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_979"><i>template_name</i></a> on the class-based view; two other mixins (<a href="index.html#page_982"><i>SingleObjectTemplateResponseMixin</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">and <a href="index.html#page_986"><i>MultipleObjectTemplateResponseMixin</i></a>) override this to provide more flexible defaults when dealing with actual objects.</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_978"><i><b>ContextMixin</b></i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Every built in view which needs context data, such as for rendering a template (including</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">TemplateResponseMixin above), should call <a href="index.html#page_978"><i>get_context_data()</i></a> passing any data they want to en-sure is in there as keyword arguments. get_context_data() returns a dictionary; in ContextMixin it returns its keyword arguments, but it is common to override this to add more members to the dictio-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">nary. You can also use the <a href="index.html#page_978"><i>extra_context</i></a> attribute.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Building up Django’s generic class-based views</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Let’s look at how two of Django’s generic class-based views are built out of mixins providing discrete func-</p> <p>tionality. We’ll consider <a href="index.html#page_955"><i>DetailView</i></a>, which renders a “detail” view of an object, and <a href="index.html#page_957"><i>ListView</i></a>, which will render a list of objects, typically from a queryset, and optionally paginate them. This will introduce us to four mixins which between them provide useful functionality when working with either a single Django object, or multiple objects.</p> <p>There are also mixins involved in the generic edit views (<a href="index.html#page_959"><i>FormView</i></a>, and the model-specific views <a href="index.html#page_961"><i>CreateView</i></a>,</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_962"><i>UpdateView</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_964"><i>DeleteView</i></a>), and in the date-based generic views. These are covered in the <a href="index.html#page_978">mixin reference</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_978">documentation</a>.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_433" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>DetailView: working with a single Django object</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To show the detail of an object, we basically need to do two things: we need to look up the object and then</p> <p>we need to make a <a href="index.html#page_2054"><i>TemplateResponse</i></a> with a suitable template, and that object as context.</p> <p>To get the object, <a href="index.html#page_955"><i>DetailView</i></a> relies on <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>SingleObjectMixin</i></a>, which provides a <a href="index.html#page_981"><i>get_object()</i></a> method that figures out the object based on the URL of the request (it looks for pk and slug keyword arguments as</p> <p>declared in the URLConf, and looks the object up either from the <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>model</i></a> attribute on the view, or the <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>queryset</i></a></p> <p>attribute if that’s provided). SingleObjectMixin also overrides <a href="index.html#page_978"><i>get_context_data()</i></a>, which is used across all Django’s built in class-based views to supply context data for template renders.</p> <p>To then make a <a href="index.html#page_2054"><i>TemplateResponse</i></a>, <a href="index.html#page_997"><i>DetailView</i></a> uses <a href="index.html#page_982"><i>SingleObjectTemplateResponseMixin</i></a>, which ex-</p> <p>tends <a href="index.html#page_979"><i>TemplateResponseMixin</i></a>, overriding <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>get_template_names()</i></a> as discussed above. It actually provides a fairly sophisticated set of options, but the main one that most people are going to use is <app_label>/</p> <p><model_name>_detail.html. The _detail part can be changed by setting <a href="index.html#page_982"><i>template_name_suffix</i></a> on a</p> <p>subclass to something else. (For instance, the <a href="index.html#page_425">generic edit views</a> use _form for create and update views, and _confirm_delete for delete views.)</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>ListView: working with many Django objects</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Lists of objects follow roughly the same pattern: we need a (possibly paginated) list of objects, typically a</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1709"><i>QuerySet</i>, </a>and then we need to make a <a href="index.html#page_2054"><i>TemplateResponse</i></a> with a suitable template using that list of objects.</p> <p>To get the objects, <a href="index.html#page_957"><i>ListView</i></a> uses <a href="index.html#page_983"><i>MultipleObjectMixin</i></a>, which provides both <a href="index.html#page_984"><i>get_queryset()</i></a> and</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_985"><i>paginate_queryset()</i></a>. Unlike with <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>SingleObjectMixin</i></a>, there’s no need to key off parts of the URL to</p> <p>figure out the queryset to work with, so the default uses the <a href="index.html#page_984"><i>queryset</i></a> or <a href="index.html#page_983"><i>model</i></a> attribute on the view class.</p> <p>A common reason to override <a href="index.html#page_984"><i>get_queryset()</i></a> here would be to dynamically vary the objects, such as de-pending on the current user or to exclude posts in the future for a blog.</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_983"><i>MultipleObjectMixin</i></a> also overrides <a href="index.html#page_978"><i>get_context_data()</i></a> to include appropriate context variables for pag-ination (providing dummies if pagination is disabled). It relies on object_list being passed in as a keyword</p> <p>argument, which <a href="index.html#page_998"><i>ListView</i></a> arranges for it.</p> <p>To make a <a href="index.html#page_2054"><i>TemplateResponse</i></a>, <a href="index.html#page_998"><i>ListView</i></a> then uses <a href="index.html#page_986"><i>MultipleObjectTemplateResponseMixin</i></a>; as with</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_982"><i>SingleObjectTemplateResponseMixin</i></a> above, this overrides get_template_names() to provide <a href="index.html#page_986"><i>a range</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_986"><i>of options</i></a>, with the most commonly-used being <app_label>/<model_name>_list.html, with the _list</p> <p>part again being taken from the <a href="index.html#page_986"><i>template_name_suffix</i></a> attribute. (The date based generic views use suffixes such as _archive, _archive_year and so on to use different templates for the various specialized date-based list views.)</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_434"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using Django’s class-based view mixins</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Now we’ve seen how Django’s generic class-based views use the provided mixins, let’s look at other ways we can combine them. We’re still going to be combining them with either built-in class-based views, or other generic class-based views, but there are a range of rarer problems you can solve than are provided for by Django out of the box.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: Not all mixins can be used together, and not all generic class based views can be used with</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">all other mixins. Here we present a few examples that do work; if you want to bring together other</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">functionality then you’ll have to consider interactions between attributes and methods that overlap</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">between the different classes you’re using, and how <a href="https://www.python.org/download/releases/2.3/mro/">method resolution order</a> will affect which versions</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">of the methods will be called in what order.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">The reference documentation for Django’s <a href="index.html#page_949">class-based views</a> and <a href="index.html#page_978">class-based view mixins</a> will help you</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">in understanding which attributes and methods are likely to cause conflict between different classes and</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">mixins.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">If in doubt, it’s often better to back off and base your work on <a href="index.html#page_996"><i>View</i></a> or <a href="index.html#page_996"><i>TemplateView</i></a>, perhaps with</p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_980"><i>SingleObjectMixin</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_983"><i>MultipleObjectMixin</i></a>. Although you will probably end up writing more code,</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">it is more likely to be clearly understandable to someone else coming to it later, and with fewer interac-</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">tions to worry about you will save yourself some thinking. (Of course, you can always dip into Django’s</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">implementation of the generic class-based views for inspiration on how to tackle problems.)</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using SingleObjectMixin with View</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If we want to write a class-based view that responds only to POST, we’ll subclass <a href="index.html#page_950"><i>View</i></a> and write a post() method in the subclass. However if we want our processing to work on a particular object, identified from</p> <p>the URL, we’ll want the functionality provided by <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>SingleObjectMixin</i></a>.</p> <p>We’ll demonstrate this with the Author model we used in the <a href="index.html#page_417">generic class-based views introduction</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">Listing 22: views.py</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"""Records the current user's interest in an author."""</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">model</span> <span <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>post</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>*</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">args,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if not</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span interest in a key-value store rather than in a relational database,</p> <p>so we’ve left that bit out. The only bit of the view that needs to worry about using <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>SingleObjectMixin</i></a> is where we want to look up the author we’re interested in, which it does with a call to self.get_object(). Everything else is taken care of for us by the mixin.</p> <p>We can hook this into our URLs easily enough:</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_436"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">Listing 23: urls.py</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.urls</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">path</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">books.views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">RecordInterestView</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"author/<int:pk>/interest/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">RecordInterestView</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">as_view(),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"author-interest"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note the pk named group, which <a href="index.html#page_981"><i>get_object()</i></a> uses to look up the Author instance. You could also use a</p> <p>slug, or any of the other features of <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>SingleObjectMixin</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using SingleObjectMixin with ListView</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><a href="index.html#page_957"><i>ListView</i></a> provides built-in pagination, but you might want to paginate a list of objects that are all linked (by a foreign key) to another object. In our publishing example, you might want to paginate through all the books by a particular publisher.</p> <p>One way to do this is to combine <a href="index.html#page_998"><i>ListView</i></a> with <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>SingleObjectMixin</i></a>, so that the queryset for the paginated list of books can hang off the publisher found as the single object. In order to do this, we need to have two different querysets:</p> <p><b>Book</b> queryset for use by <a href="index.html#page_957"><i><b>ListView</b></i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Since we have access to the Publisher whose books we want to list, we override get_queryset() and</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">use the Publisher’s <a href="index.html#page_172">reverse foreign key manager.</a></p> <p><b>Publisher</b> queryset for use in <a href="index.html#page_981"><i><b>get_object()</b></i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">We’ll rely on the default implementation of get_object() to fetch the correct Publisher object. How-ever, we need to explicitly pass a queryset argument because otherwise the default implementation of get_object() would call get_queryset() which we have overridden to return Book objects instead of Publisher ones.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: We have to think carefully about get_context_data(). Since both <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>SingleObjectMixin</i></a> and</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_998"><i>ListView</i></a> will put things in the context data under the value of context_object_name if it’s set, we’ll in-</p> <p>stead explicitly ensure the Publisher is in the context data. <a href="index.html#page_998"><i>ListView</i></a> will add in the suitable page_obj and paginator for us providing we remember to call super().</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Now we can write a new PublisherDetailView:</p> <p id="page_437" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.views.generic</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ListView</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.views.generic.detail</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">SingleObjectMixin</span></p> <p><span style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">context</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">object</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">book_set</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">all()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Notice how we set self.object within get() so we can use it again later in get_context_data() and</p> <p>get_queryset(). If you don’t set template_name, the template will default to the normal <a href="index.html#page_998"><i>ListView</i></a> choice,</p> <p>which in this case would be "books/book_list.html" because it’s a list of books; <a href="index.html#page_998"><i>ListView</i></a> knows nothing</p> <p>about <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>SingleObjectMixin</i></a>, so it doesn’t have any clue this view is anything to do with a Publisher.</p> <p>The paginate_by is deliberately small in the example so you don’t have to create lots of books to see the pagination working! Here’s the template you’d want to use:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>extends</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"base.html"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>block</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">content</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">publisher.name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">h2</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ol</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">book</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">page_obj</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">book.title</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endif</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">span</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">class</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"current"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">Page</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">page_obj.number</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">of</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">paginator.num_pages</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">span</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">page_obj.has_next</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">href</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"?page=</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">page_obj.next_page_number</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>next</</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endif</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">span</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">div</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endblock</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Avoid anything more complex</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Generally you can use <a href="index.html#page_979"><i>TemplateResponseMixin</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>SingleObjectMixin</i></a> when you need their functionality.</p> <p>As shown above, with a bit of care you can even combine SingleObjectMixin with <a href="index.html#page_957"><i>ListView</i></a>. However things get increasingly complex as you try to do so, and a good rule of thumb is:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Hint: Each of your views should use only mixins or views from one of the groups of generic class-based</p> <p>views: <a href="index.html#page_417">detail, list</a>, <a href="index.html#page_425">editing</a> and date. For example it’s fine to combine <a href="index.html#page_996"><i>TemplateView</i></a> (built in view) with</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_983"><i>MultipleObjectMixin</i></a> (generic list), but you’re likely to have problems combining SingleObjectMixin (generic detail) with MultipleObjectMixin (generic list).</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To show what happens when you try to get more sophisticated, we show an example that sacrifices read-ability and maintainability when there is a simpler solution. First, let’s look at a naive attempt to combine</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_955"><i>DetailView</i></a> with <a href="index.html#page_987"><i>FormMixin</i></a> to enable us to POST a Django <a href="index.html#page_1487"><i>Form</i></a> to the same URL as we’re displaying an</p> <p>object using <a href="index.html#page_997"><i>DetailView</i></a> .</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using FormMixin with DetailView</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Think back to our earlier example of using <a href="index.html#page_996"><i>View</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>SingleObjectMixin</i></a> together. We were recording a user’s interest in a particular author; say now that we want to let them leave a message saying why they like them. Again, let’s assume we’re not going to store this in a relational database but instead in something more esoteric that we won’t worry about here.</p> <p>At this point it’s natural to reach for a <a href="index.html#page_1487"><i>Form</i></a> to encapsulate the information sent from the user’s browser to</p> <p>Django. Say also that we’re heavily invested in <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer">REST</a>, so we want to use the same URL for displaying the author as for capturing the message from the user. Let’s rewrite our AuthorDetailView to do that.</p> <p>We’ll keep the GET handling from <a href="index.html#page_997"><i>DetailView</i></a>, although we’ll have to add a <a href="index.html#page_1487"><i>Form</i></a> into the context data so</p> <p id="page_439" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>we can render it in the template. We’ll also want to pull in form processing from <a href="index.html#page_987"><i>FormMixin</i></a>, and write a bit of code so that on POST the form gets called appropriately.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: We use <a href="index.html#page_987"><i>FormMixin</i></a> and implement post() ourselves rather than try to mix <a href="index.html#page_997"><i>DetailView</i></a> with <a href="index.html#page_999"><i>FormView</i></a> (which provides a suitable post() already) because both of the views implement get(), and things would get much more confusing.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Our new AuthorDetailView looks like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># CAUTION: you almost certainly do not want form.cleaned_data['message']</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span provides somewhere to redirect to, which gets used in the default implementation of form_valid(). We have to provide our own post() as noted earlier.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>A better solution</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The number of subtle interactions between <a href="index.html#page_987"><i>FormMixin</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_997"><i>DetailView</i></a> is already testing our ability to man-age things. It’s unlikely you’d want to write this kind of class yourself.</p> <p>In this case, you could write the post() method yourself, keeping <a href="index.html#page_997"><i>DetailView</i></a> as the only generic function-</p> <p>ality, although writing <a href="index.html#page_1487"><i>Form</i></a> handling code involves a lot of duplication.</p> <p>Alternatively, it would still be less work than the above approach to have a separate view for processing the</p> <p>form, which could use <a href="index.html#page_959"><i>FormView</i></a> distinct from <a href="index.html#page_997"><i>DetailView</i></a> without concerns.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>An alternative better solution</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>What we’re really trying to do here is to use two different class based views from the same URL. So why not</p> <p>do just that? We have a very clear division here: GET requests should get the <a href="index.html#page_997"><i>DetailView</i></a> (with the <a href="index.html#page_1487"><i>Form</i></a></p> <p>added to the context data), and POST requests should get the <a href="index.html#page_999"><i>FormView</i></a>. Let’s set up those views first.</p> <p>The AuthorDetailView view is almost the same as <a href="index.html#page_424">when we first introduced AuthorDetailView; </a>we have to write our own get_context_data() to make the AuthorInterestForm available to the template. We’ll skip the get_object() override from before for clarity:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">forms</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.views.generic</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">DetailView</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">books.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AuthorInterestForm</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(forms</span><span <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">context[</span><span <a href="index.html#page_999"><i>FormView</i></a>, but we have to bring in <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>SingleObjectMixin</i></a> so we can find the author we’re talking about, and we have to remember to set template_name to ensure that form errors will render the same template as AuthorDetailView is using on GET:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.urls</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">reverse</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.views.generic</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">FormView</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.views.generic.detail</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">SingleObjectMixin</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AuthorInterestFormView</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(SingleObjectMixin, FormView):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">form_class</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">AuthorInterestForm</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">model</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>post</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>*</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">args,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if not</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">object</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_object()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">post(request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>*</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">args,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get_success_url</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">reverse(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"author-detail"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, kwargs</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span in a new AuthorView view. We already know that calling <a href="index.html#page_950"><i>as_view()</i></a> on a class-based view gives us something that behaves exactly like a function based view, so we can do that at the point we choose between the two subviews.</p> <p>You can pass through keyword arguments to <a href="index.html#page_950"><i>as_view()</i></a> in the same way you would in your URLconf, such as if you wanted the AuthorInterestFormView behavior to also appear at another URL but using a different template:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">View</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AuthorView</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(View):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>*</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">args,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span
