For example, to set a User-Agent header:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">client</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Client(headers</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"user-agent"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"curl/7.79.1"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">})</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">query_params allows you to specify the default query string that will be set on every request.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Arbitrary keyword arguments in **defaults set WSGI <a href="https://peps.python.org/pep-3333/#environ-variables">environ variables. </a>For example, to set the script name:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">client</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Client(SCRIPT_NAME</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/app/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Note: Keyword arguments starting with a HTTP_ prefix are set as headers, but the headers parameter should be preferred for readability.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The values from the headers, query_params, and extra keyword arguments passed to <a href="index.html#page_478"><i>get()</i>,</a> <a href="index.html#page_479"><i>post()</i></a>, etc. have precedence over the defaults passed to the class constructor.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The enforce_csrf_checks argument can be used to test CSRF protection (see above).</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The raise_request_exception argument allows controlling whether or not exceptions raised during the request should also be raised in the test. Defaults to True.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The json_encoder argument allows setting a custom JSON encoder for the JSON serialization that’s</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">described in <a href="index.html#page_479"><i>post()</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The query_params argument was added.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Once you have a Client instance, you can call any of the following methods:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get</b>(path, data=None, follow=False, secure=False, *, headers=None, query_params=None, **extra)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Makes a GET request on the provided path and returns a Response object, which is documented below.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The key-value pairs in the query_params dictionary are used to set query strings. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">c</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Client()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">c</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/customers/details/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, query_params</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"fred"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"age"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">7</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">})</span></p> <p id="page_479" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><i>. . .</i> will result in the evaluation of a GET request equivalent to:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">/customers/details/?name=fred&age=7</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">It is also possible to pass these parameters into the data parameter. However, query_params is preferred as it works for any HTTP method.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The headers parameter can be used to specify headers to be sent in the request. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">c</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Client()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">c</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"/customers/details/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">query_params</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"fred"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"age"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">7</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">headers</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"accept"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"application/json"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><i>. . .</i> will send the HTTP header HTTP_ACCEPT to the details view, which is a good way to test code</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">paths that use the <a href="index.html#page_1867"><i>django.http.HttpRequest.accepts()</i></a> method.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Arbitrary keyword arguments set WSGI <a href="https://peps.python.org/pep-3333/#environ-variables">environ variables</a>. For example, headers to set the script name:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">c</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Client()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">c</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, SCRIPT_NAME</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/app/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If you already have the GET arguments in URL-encoded form, you can use that encoding instead of using the data argument. For example, the previous GET request could also be posed as:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">c</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Client()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">c</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/customers/details/?name=fred&age=7"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If you provide a URL with both an encoded GET data and either a query_params or data argument these arguments will take precedence.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If you set follow to True the client will follow any redirects and a redirect_chain attribute will be set in the response object containing tuples of the intermediate urls and status codes.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If you had a URL /redirect_me/ that redirected to /next/, that redirected to /final/, this is what you’d see:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">c</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/redirect_me/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, follow</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">redirect_chain</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">[('http://testserver/next/', 302), ('http://testserver/final/', 302)]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If you set secure to True the client will emulate an HTTPS request.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The query_params argument was added.</p> <p id="page_480"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center"><b>post</b>(path, data=None, content_type=MULTIPART_CONTENT, follow=False, secure=False, *,</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">headers=None, query_params=None, **extra)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Makes a POST request on the provided path and returns a Response object, which is documented below.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The key-value pairs in the data dictionary are used to submit POST data. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">c</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Client()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">c</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">post(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/login/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, {</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"fred"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"passwd"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"secret"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">})</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><i>. . .</i> will result in the evaluation of a POST request to this URL:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">/login/</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><i>. . .</i> with this POST data:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name=fred&passwd=secret</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If you provide content_type as <i>application/json</i>, the data is serialized using <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html#json.dumps">json.dumps()</a> if</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">it’s a dict, list, or tuple. Serialization is performed with <a href="index.html#page_737"><i>DjangoJSONEncoder</i></a> by default, and can</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">be overridden by providing a json_encoder argument to <a href="index.html#page_478"><i>Client</i>. </a>This serialization also happens</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">for <a href="index.html#page_482"><i>put()</i>, <i>patch()</i></a>, and <a href="index.html#page_482"><i>delete()</i></a> requests.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If you provide any other content_type (e.g. <i>text/xml</i> for an XML payload), the contents of data are sent as-is in the POST request, using content_type in the HTTP Content-Type header.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If you don’t provide a value for content_type, the values in data will be transmitted with a content type of <i>multipart/form-data</i>. In this case, the key-value pairs in data will be encoded as a multipart message and used to create the POST data payload.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">To submit multiple values for a given key – for example, to specify the selections for a <select multiple> – provide the values as a list or tuple for the required key. For example, this value of data would submit three selected values for the field named choices:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"choices"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"a"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"b"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"d"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Submitting files is a special case. To POST a file, you need only provide the file field name as a key, and a file handle to the file you wish to upload as a value. For example, if your form has fields</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">name and attachment, the latter a <a href="index.html#page_1530"><i>FileField</i></a>:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">c</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Client()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>with</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">open</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"wishlist.doc"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"rb"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">fp:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">c</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">post(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/customers/wishes/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, {</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"fred"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"attachment"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: fp})</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">You may also provide any file-like object (e.g., <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/io.html#io.StringIO">StringIO</a> or <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/io.html#io.BytesIO">BytesIO</a>) as a file handle.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If you’re uploading to an <a href="index.html#page_1638"><i>ImageField</i></a>, the object needs a name attribute that passes the</p> <p id="page_481" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_2098"><i>validate_image_file_extension</i></a> validator. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">io</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">BytesIO</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">img</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">BytesIO(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">b"GIF89a\x01\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00!\xf9\x04\x01\x00\x00\x00"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">b"\x00,\x00\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x00\x02\x01\x00\x00"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">img</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"myimage.gif"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Note that if you wish to use the same file handle for multiple post() calls then you will need to manually reset the file pointer between posts. The easiest way to do this is to manually close the file after it has been provided to post(), as demonstrated above.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">You should also ensure that the file is opened in a way that allows the data to be read. If your file contains binary data such as an image, this means you will need to open the file in rb (read binary) mode.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The headers, query_params, and extra parameters acts the same as for <a href="index.html#page_478"><i>Client.get()</i>.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If the URL you request with a POST contains encoded parameters, these parameters will be made available in the request.GET data. For example, if you were to make the request:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">c</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">post(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"/login/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, {</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"fred"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"passwd"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"secret"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">}, query_params</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"visitor"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"true"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><i>. . .</i> the view handling this request could interrogate request.POST to retrieve the username and password, and could interrogate request.GET to determine if the user was a visitor.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If you set follow to True the client will follow any redirects and a redirect_chain attribute will be set in the response object containing tuples of the intermediate urls and status codes.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If you set secure to True the client will emulate an HTTPS request.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The query_params argument was added.</p> <p style="text-align:center"><b>head</b>(path, data=None, follow=False, secure=False, *, headers=None, query_params=None,</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">**extra)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Makes a HEAD request on the provided path and returns a Response object. This method works</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">just like <a href="index.html#page_478"><i>Client.get()</i></a>, including the follow, secure, headers, query_params, and extra param-eters, except it does not return a message body.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The query_params argument was added.</p> <p style="text-align:center"><b>options</b>(path, data='', content_type='application/octet-stream', follow=False, secure=False, *,</p> <p style="margin-left:6em">headers=None, query_params=None, **extra)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Makes an OPTIONS request on the provided path and returns a Response object. Useful for testing RESTful interfaces.</p> <p id="page_482"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">When data is provided, it is used as the request body, and a Content-Type header is set to content_type.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The follow, secure, headers, query_params, and extra parameters act the same as for <a href="index.html#page_478"><i>Client.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_478"><i>get()</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The query_params argument was added.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>put</b>(path, data='', content_type='application/octet-stream', follow=False, secure=False, *,</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">headers=None, query_params=None, **extra)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Makes a PUT request on the provided path and returns a Response object. Useful for testing RESTful interfaces.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">When data is provided, it is used as the request body, and a Content-Type header is set to content_type.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The follow, secure, headers, query_params, and extra parameters act the same as for <a href="index.html#page_478"><i>Client.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_478"><i>get()</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The query_params argument was added.</p> <p style="text-align:center"><b>patch</b>( path, data='', content_type='application/octet-stream', follow=False, secure=False, *,</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">headers=None, query_params=None, **extra)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Makes a PATCH request on the provided path and returns a Response object. Useful for testing RESTful interfaces.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The follow, secure, headers, query_params, and extra parameters act the same as for <a href="index.html#page_478"><i>Client.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_478"><i>get()</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The query_params argument was added.</p> <p style="text-align:center"><b>delete</b>(path, data='', content_type='application/octet-stream', follow=False, secure=False, *,</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">headers=None, query_params=None, **extra)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Makes a DELETE request on the provided path and returns a Response object. Useful for testing RESTful interfaces.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">When data is provided, it is used as the request body, and a Content-Type header is set to content_type.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The follow, secure, headers, query_params, and extra parameters act the same as for <a href="index.html#page_478"><i>Client.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_478"><i>get()</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The query_params argument was added.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>trace</b>( path, follow=False, secure=False, *, headers=None, query_params=None, **extra)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Makes a TRACE request on the provided path and returns a Response object. Useful for simulat-ing diagnostic probes.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Unlike the other request methods, data is not provided as a keyword parameter in order to comply</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">with <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110.html#section-9.3.8">RFC 9110#section-9.3.8, </a>which mandates that TRACE requests must not have a body.</p> <p id="page_483" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The follow, secure, headers, query_params, and extra parameters act the same as for <a href="index.html#page_478"><i>Client.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_478"><i>get()</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The query_params argument was added.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>login</b>( **credentials)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>alogin</b>(**credentials)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Asynchronous version: alogin()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If your site uses Django’s <a href="index.html#page_530">authentication system</a> and you deal with logging in users, you can use the test client’s login() method to simulate the effect of a user logging into the site.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">After you call this method, the test client will have all the cookies and session data required to pass any login-based tests that may form part of a view.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The format of the credentials argument depends on which <a href="index.html#page_576">authentication backend</a> you’re using</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">(which is configured by your <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS</i></a> setting). If you’re using the standard authentication backend provided by Django (ModelBackend), credentials should be the user’s username and password, provided as keyword arguments:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">c</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Client()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">c</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">login(username</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"fred"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, password</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"secret"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"># Now you can access a view that's only available to logged-in users.</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If you’re using a different authentication backend, this method may require different credentials. It requires whichever credentials are required by your backend’s authenticate() method.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">login() returns True if it the credentials were accepted and login was successful.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Finally, you’ll need to remember to create user accounts before you can use this method. As we explained above, the test runner is executed using a test database, which contains no users by default. As a result, user accounts that are valid on your production site will not work under test conditions. You’ll need to create users as part of the test suite – either manually (using the Django model API) or with a test fixture. Remember that if you want your test user to have a password, you can’t set the user’s password by setting the password attribute directly – you must use the</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_1104"><i>set_password()</i></a> function to store a correctly hashed password. Alternatively, you can use the</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_1106"><i>create_user()</i></a> helper method to create a new user with a correctly hashed password.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>force_login</b>(user, backend=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>aforce_login</b>( user, backend=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Asynchronous version: aforce_login()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If your site uses Django’s <a href="index.html#page_530">authentication system</a>, you can use the force_login() method to sim-</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">ulate the effect of a user logging into the site. Use this method instead of <a href="index.html#page_483"><i>login()</i></a> when a test requires a user be logged in and the details of how a user logged in aren’t important.</p> <p id="page_484"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Unlike login(), this method skips the authentication and verification steps: inactive users</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_1102">(<i>is_active=False</i>) </a>are permitted to login and the user’s credentials don’t need to be provided.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The user will have its backend attribute set to the value of the backend argument (which should be a dotted Python path string), or to settings.AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS[0] if a value isn’t</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">provided. The <a href="index.html#page_532"><i>authenticate()</i></a> function called by <a href="index.html#page_483"><i>login()</i></a> normally annotates the user like this.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">This method is faster than login() since the expensive password hashing algorithms are bypassed.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Also, you can speed up login() by <a href="index.html#page_475">using a weaker hasher while testing</a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>logout</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>alogout</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Asynchronous version: alogout()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If your site uses Django’s <a href="index.html#page_530">authentication system, </a>the logout() method can be used to simulate the effect of a user logging out of your site.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">After you call this method, the test client will have all the cookies and session data cleared to</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">defaults. Subsequent requests will appear to come from an <a href="index.html#page_1107"><i>AnonymousUser</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Testing responses</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The get() and post() methods both return a Response object. This Response object is not the same as the HttpResponse object returned by Django views; the test response object has some additional data useful for test code to verify.</p> <p>Specifically, a Response object has the following attributes:</p> <p><b>class Response</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>client</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The test client that was used to make the request that resulted in the response.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>content</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The body of the response, as a bytestring. This is the final page content as rendered by the view, or any error message.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>context</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The template Context instance that was used to render the template that produced the response content.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If the rendered page used multiple templates, then context will be a list of Context objects, in the order in which they were rendered.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Regardless of the number of templates used during rendering, you can retrieve context values using the [] operator. For example, the context variable name could be retrieved using:</p> <p id="page_485" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">client</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/foo/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">context[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">'Arthur'</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Not using Django templates?</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">This attribute is only populated when using the <a href="index.html#page_407"><i>DjangoTemplates</i></a> backend. If you’re using an-</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">other template engine, <a href="index.html#page_2052"><i>context_data</i></a> may be a suitable alternative on responses with that at-tribute.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>exc_info</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A tuple of three values that provides information about the unhandled exception, if any, that occurred during the view.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The values are (type, value, traceback), the same as returned by Python’s <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/sys.html#sys.exc_info">sys.exc_info(). </a>Their meanings are:</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• type: The type of the exception.</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• value: The exception instance.</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• traceback: A traceback object which encapsulates the call stack at the point where the excep-</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">tion originally occurred.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If no exception occurred, then exc_info will be None.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>json</b>(**kwargs)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The body of the response, parsed as JSON. Extra keyword arguments are passed to <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/json.html#json.loads">json.loads()</a>. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">client</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/foo/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">json()[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">'Arthur'</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If the Content-Type header is not "application/json", then a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError">ValueError</a> will be raised when trying to parse the response.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>request</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The request data that stimulated the response.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>wsgi_request</b></p> <p style="text-align:center">The WSGIRequest instance generated by the test handler that generated the response.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>status_code</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The HTTP status of the response, as an integer. For a full list of defined codes, see the <a href="https://www.iana.org/assignments/http-status-codes/http-status-codes.xhtml">IANA status</a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="https://www.iana.org/assignments/http-status-codes/http-status-codes.xhtml">code registry</a>.</p> <p id="page_486"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>templates</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A list of Template instances used to render the final content, in the order they were rendered. For each template in the list, use template.name to get the template’s file name, if the template was loaded from a file. (The name is a string such as 'admin/index.html'.)</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Not using Django templates?</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">This attribute is only populated when using the <a href="index.html#page_407"><i>DjangoTemplates</i></a> backend. If you’re using an-</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">other template engine, <a href="index.html#page_2052"><i>template_name</i></a> may be a suitable alternative if you only need the name of the template used for rendering.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>resolver_match</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">An instance of <a href="index.html#page_2065"><i>ResolverMatch</i></a> for the response. You can use the <a href="index.html#page_2065"><i>func</i></a> attribute, for example, to verify the view that served the response:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># my_view here is a function based view.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertEqual(response</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">resolver_match</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">func, my_view)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Class-based views need to compare the view_class, as the</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># functions generated by as_view() won't be equal.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertIs(response</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">resolver_match</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">func</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">view_class, MyView)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If the given URL is not found, accessing this attribute will raise a <a href="index.html#page_1474"><i>Resolver404</i></a> exception.</p> <p>As with a normal response, you can also access the headers through <a href="index.html#page_1873"><i>HttpResponse.headers</i>. </a>For example, you could determine the content type of a response using response.headers['Content-Type'].</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Exceptions</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you point the test client at a view that raises an exception and Client.raise_request_exception is True, that exception will be visible in the test case. You can then use a standard try ... except block or</p> <p><a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.html#unittest.TestCase.assertRaises">assertRaises()</a> to test for exceptions.</p> <p>The only exceptions that are not visible to the test client are <a href="index.html#page_285"><i>Http404</i></a>, <a href="index.html#page_1472"><i>PermissionDenied</i></a>, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#SystemExit">SystemExit</a><a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#SystemExit">, </a>and</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1471"><i>SuspiciousOperation</i></a>. Django catches these exceptions internally and converts them into the appropriate HTTP response codes. In these cases, you can check response.status_code in your test.</p> <p>If Client.raise_request_exception is False, the test client will return a 500 response as would be re-</p> <p>turned to a browser. The response has the attribute <a href="index.html#page_485"><i>exc_info</i></a> to provide information about the unhandled exception.</p> <p id="page_487" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Persistent state</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The test client is stateful. If a response returns a cookie, then that cookie will be stored in the test client and sent with all subsequent get() and post() requests.</p> <p>Expiration policies for these cookies are not followed. If you want a cookie to expire, either delete it manually or create a new Client instance (which will effectively delete all cookies).</p> <p>A test client has attributes that store persistent state information. You can access these properties as part of a test condition.</p> <p>Client.<b>cookies</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A Python <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/http.cookies.html#http.cookies.SimpleCookie">SimpleCookie</a> object, containing the current values of all the client cookies. See the docu-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">mentation of the <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/http.cookies.html#module-http.cookies">http.cookies</a> module for more.</p> <p>Client.<b>session</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A dictionary-like object containing session information. See the <a href="index.html#page_311">session documentation</a> for full details.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">To modify the session and then save it, it must be stored in a variable first (because a new SessionStore is created every time this property is accessed):</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>test_something</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">session</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">client</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">session</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">session[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"somekey"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"test"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">session</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Client.<b>asession</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This is similar to the <a href="index.html#page_487"><i>session</i></a> attribute but it works in async contexts.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Setting the language</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When testing applications that support internationalization and localization, you might want to set the lan-</p> <p>guage for a test client request. The method for doing so depends on whether or not the <a href="index.html#page_1594"><i>LocaleMiddleware</i></a> is enabled.</p> <p>If the middleware is enabled, the language can be set by creating a cookie with a name of</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1919"><i>LANGUAGE_COOKIE_NAME</i></a> and a value of the language code:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.conf</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">settings</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>test_language_using_cookie</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">client</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">cookies</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">load({settings</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">LANGUAGE_COOKIE_NAME:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"fr"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">})</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">client</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertEqual(response</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">content,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">b"Bienvenue sur mon site."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p id="page_488"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>or by including the Accept-Language HTTP header in the request:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>test_language_using_header</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">client</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, headers</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"accept-language"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"fr"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">})</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertEqual(response</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">content,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">b"Bienvenue sur mon site."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: When using these methods, ensure to reset the active language at the end of each test:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>tearDown</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">translation</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">activate(settings</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">LANGUAGE_CODE)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>More details are in <a href="index.html#page_686">How Django discovers language preference</a>.</p> <p>If the middleware isn’t enabled, the active language may be set using <a href="index.html#page_2090"><i>translation.override()</i>:</a></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">translation</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>test_language_using_override</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>with</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">translation</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">override(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"fr"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">client</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertEqual(response</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">content,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">b"Bienvenue sur mon site."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>More details are in <a href="index.html#page_684">Explicitly setting the active language.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Example</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The following is a unit test using the test client:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">unittest</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.test</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Client</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>SimpleTest</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(unittest</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">TestCase):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>setUp</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Every test needs a client.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">client</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Client()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>test_details</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Issue a GET request.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">client</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/customer/details/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Check that the response is 200 OK.</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_489" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertEqual(response</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">status_code,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">200</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Check that the rendered context contains 5 customers.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertEqual(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">len</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(response</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">context[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"customers"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]),</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">5</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>See also:</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_515"><i>django.test.RequestFactory</i></a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Provided test case classes</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Normal Python unit test classes extend a base class of <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.html#unittest.TestCase">unittest.TestCase</a>. Django provides a few extensions of this base class:</p> <p style="text-align:center"><img src="index-489_1.png" alt="" width="551px" height="96px"/></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.93em"><i>standard library</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:10em"><span style="font-size:0.93em">TestCase</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.93em">unittest</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"><img src="index-489_2.png" alt="" width="551px" height="258px"/></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.93em">django.test</span></p> <p style="margin-left:9em"><span style="font-size:0.93em">SimpleTestCase</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:8em"><span style="font-size:0.93em">TransactionTestCase</span></p> <p><img src="index-489_3.png" alt="" width="207px" height="55px"/></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:10em"><span style="font-size:0.93em">TestCase</span> <span style="font-size:0.93em">LiveServerTestCase</span></p> <p><img src="index-489_4.png" alt="" width="207px" height="55px"/></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">Fig. 1: Hierarchy of Django unit testing classes</p> <p><img src="index-489_5.png" alt="" width="207px" height="55px"/></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can convert a normal <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.html#unittest.TestCase">unittest.TestCase</a> to any of the subclasses: change the base class of your test from unittest.TestCase to the subclass. All of the standard Python unit test functionality will be available, and it will be augmented with some useful additions as described in each section below.</p> <p><img src="index-489_6.png" alt="" width="207px" height="55px"/></p> <p><img src="index-489_7.png" alt="" width="207px" height="55px"/></p> <p><img src="index-489_8.png" alt="" width="183px" height="32px"/></p> <p><img src="index-489_9.png" alt="" width="183px" height="32px"/></p> <p><img src="index-489_10.png" alt="" width="183px" height="32px"/></p> <p><img src="index-489_11.png" alt="" width="183px" height="32px"/></p> <p><img src="index-489_12.png" alt="" width="183px" height="32px"/></p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_490"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>SimpleTestCase</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class SimpleTestCase</b></p> <p>A subclass of <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.html#unittest.TestCase">unittest.TestCase</a> that adds this functionality:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Some useful assertions like:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– Checking that a callable <a href="index.html#page_504"><i>raises a certain exception</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– Checking that a callable <a href="index.html#page_505"><i>triggers a certain warning</i>.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– Testing form field <a href="index.html#page_505"><i>rendering and error treatment</i>.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– Testing <a href="index.html#page_506"><i>HTML responses for the presence/lack of a given fragment</i>.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– Verifying that a template <a href="index.html#page_506"><i>has/hasn't been used to generate a given response content</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– Verifying that two <a href="index.html#page_507"><i>URLs</i></a> are equal.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– Verifying an HTTP <a href="index.html#page_507"><i>redirect</i></a> is performed by the app.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– Robustly testing two <a href="index.html#page_507"><i>HTML fragments</i></a> for equality/inequality or <a href="index.html#page_508"><i>containment</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– Robustly testing two <a href="index.html#page_508"><i>XML fragments</i></a> for equality/inequality.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– Robustly testing two <a href="index.html#page_509"><i>JSON fragments</i></a> for equality.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The ability to run tests with <a href="index.html#page_499">modified settings.</a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Using the <a href="index.html#495"><i>client </i></a><a href="index.html#page_478"><i>Client</i></a>.</p> <p>If your tests make any database queries, use subclasses <a href="index.html#page_491"><i>TransactionTestCase</i></a> or <a href="index.html#page_492"><i>TestCase</i></a><a href="index.html#page_492">.</a></p> <p>SimpleTestCase.<b>databases</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_490"><i>SimpleTestCase</i></a> disallows database queries by default. This helps to avoid executing write queries which will affect other tests since each SimpleTestCase test isn’t run in a transaction. If you aren’t concerned about this problem, you can disable this behavior by setting the databases class attribute to '__all__' on your test class.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: SimpleTestCase and its subclasses (e.g. TestCase, <i>. . .</i>) rely on setUpClass() and</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">tearDownClass() to perform some class-wide initialization (e.g. overriding settings). If you need to</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">override those methods, don’t forget to call the super implementation:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyTestCase</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(TestCase):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@classmethod</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>setUpClass</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">cls</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">setUpClass()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@classmethod</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>tearDownClass</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">cls</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p id="page_491" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">tearDownClass()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Be sure to account for Python’s behavior if an exception is raised during setUpClass(). If that happens,</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">neither the tests in the class nor tearDownClass() are run. In the case of <a href="index.html#page_492"><i>django.test.TestCase</i>, </a>this</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">will leak the transaction created in super() which results in various symptoms including a segmentation</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">fault on some platforms (reported on macOS). If you want to intentionally raise an exception such as</p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.html#unittest.SkipTest">unittest.SkipTest</a> in setUpClass(), be sure to do it before calling super() to avoid this.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>TransactionTestCase</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class TransactionTestCase</b></p> <p>TransactionTestCase inherits from <a href="index.html#page_490"><i>SimpleTestCase</i></a> to add some database-specific features:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Resetting the database to a known state at the beginning of each test to ease testing and using the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">ORM.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Database <a href="index.html#page_497"><i>fixtures</i>.</a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Test <a href="index.html#page_514">skipping based on database backend features</a>.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The remaining specialized <a href="index.html#page_509"><i>assert*</i></a> methods.</p> <p>Django’s <a href="index.html#page_492"><i>TestCase</i></a> class is a more commonly used subclass of TransactionTestCase that makes use of database transaction facilities to speed up the process of resetting the database to a known state at the begin-ning of each test. A consequence of this, however, is that some database behaviors cannot be tested within a Django TestCase class. For instance, you cannot test that a block of code is executing within a transaction, as is required when using <a href="index.html#page_1739"><i>select_for_update()</i></a>. In those cases, you should use TransactionTestCase.</p> <p>TransactionTestCase and TestCase are identical except for the manner in which the database is reset to a known state and the ability for test code to test the effects of commit and rollback:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• A TransactionTestCase resets the database after the test runs by truncating all tables. <span style="float:right">A</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">TransactionTestCase may call commit and rollback and observe the effects of these calls on the database.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• A TestCase, on the other hand, does not truncate tables after a test. Instead, it encloses the test code</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">in a database transaction that is rolled back at the end of the test. This guarantees that the rollback at the end of the test restores the database to its initial state.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: TestCase running on a database that does not support rollback (e.g. MySQL with the MyISAM</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">storage engine), and all instances of TransactionTestCase, will roll back at the end of the test by deleting</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">all data from the test database.</p> <p id="page_492"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Apps <a href="index.html#page_473">will not see their data reloaded</a>; if you need this functionality (for example, third-party apps should</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">enable this) you can set serialized_rollback = True inside the TestCase body.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>TestCase</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class TestCase</b></p> <p>This is the most common class to use for writing tests in Django. It inherits from <a href="index.html#page_491"><i>TransactionTestCase</i></a> (and</p> <p>by extension <a href="index.html#page_490"><i>SimpleTestCase</i></a>). If your Django application doesn’t use a database, use <a href="index.html#page_490"><i>SimpleTestCase</i></a>.</p> <p>The class:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Wraps the tests within two nested <a href="index.html#page_209"><i>atomic()</i></a> blocks: one for the whole class and one for each test.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Therefore, if you want to test some specific database transaction behavior, use <a href="index.html#page_491"><i>TransactionTestCase</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Checks deferrable database constraints at the end of each test.</p> <p>It also provides an additional method:</p> <p><b>classmethod</b> TestCase.<b>setUpTestData</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The class-level atomic block described above allows the creation of initial data at the class level, once for the whole TestCase. This technique allows for faster tests as compared to using setUp().</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.test</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">TestCase</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyTests</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(TestCase):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@classmethod</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>setUpTestData</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">cls</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Set up data for the whole TestCase</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">cls</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">foo</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Foo</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">create(bar</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Some test using self.foo</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Some other test using self.foo</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Note that if the tests are run on a database with no transaction support (for instance, MySQL with the MyISAM engine), setUpTestData() will be called before each test, negating the speed benefits.</p> <p id="page_493" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Objects assigned to class attributes in setUpTestData() must support creating deep copies with <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/copy.html#copy.deepcopy">copy.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/copy.html#copy.deepcopy">deepcopy()</a> in order to isolate them from alterations performed by each test methods.</p> <p><b>classmethod</b> TestCase.<b>captureOnCommitCallbacks</b>(using=DEFAULT_DB_ALIAS, execute=False)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns a context manager that captures <a href="index.html#page_213"><i>transaction.on_commit()</i></a> callbacks for the given database connection. It returns a list that contains, on exit of the context, the captured callback functions. From this list you can make assertions on the callbacks or call them to invoke their side effects, emulating a commit.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">using is the alias of the database connection to capture callbacks for.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If execute is True, all the callbacks will be called as the context manager exits, if no exception occurred. This emulates a commit after the wrapped block of code.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.core</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">mail</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.test</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">TestCase</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ContactTests</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(TestCase):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>test_post</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>with</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">captureOnCommitCallbacks(execute</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">callbacks:</span></p> <p style="font-size:0.87em">"message"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"I like your site"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertEqual(response</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">status_code,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertEqual(mail</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">outbox[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertEqual(mail</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">outbox[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">0</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">body,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"I like your site"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>LiveServerTestCase</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class LiveServerTestCase</b></p> <p>LiveServerTestCase does basically the same as <a href="index.html#page_491"><i>TransactionTestCase</i></a> with one extra feature: it launches a live Django server in the background on setup, and shuts it down on teardown. This allows the use of</p> <p>automated test clients other than the <a href="index.html#page_476">Django dummy client</a> such as, for example, the <a href="https://www.selenium.dev/">Selenium</a> client, to execute a series of functional tests inside a browser and simulate a real user’s actions.</p> <p>The live server listens on localhost and binds to port 0 which uses a free port assigned by the operating system. The server’s URL can be accessed with self.live_server_url during the tests.</p> <p id="page_494"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To demonstrate how to use LiveServerTestCase, let’s write a Selenium test. First of all, you need to install</p> <p>the <a href="https://pypi.org/project/selenium/">selenium</a> package:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">$</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">python -m pip install</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"selenium >= 4.8.0"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Then, add a LiveServerTestCase-based test to your app’s tests module (for example: myapp/tests.py). For</p> <p>this example, we’ll assume you’re using the <a href="index.html#page_1369"><i>staticfiles</i></a> app and want to have static files served during the execution of your tests similar to what we get at development time with DEBUG=True, i.e. without having to</p> <p>collect them using <a href="index.html#page_1370"><i>collectstatic</i>. </a>We’ll use the <a href="index.html#page_1378"><i>StaticLiveServerTestCase</i></a> subclass which provides that functionality. Replace it with django.test.LiveServerTestCase if you don’t need that.</p> <p>The code for this test may look as follows:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">selenium.webdriver.common.by</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"user-data.json"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="font-size:0.87em"><b>setUpClass</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">cls</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">setUpClass()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">cls</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">selenium</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">WebDriver()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">cls</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">selenium</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">implicitly_wait(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">10</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"secret"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span
