out</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">getvalue())</span></p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_514"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Skipping tests</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The unittest library provides the <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.html#unittest.skipIf">@skipIf</a> and <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.html#unittest.skipUnless">@skipUnless</a> decorators to allow you to skip tests if you know ahead of time that those tests are going to fail under certain conditions.</p> <p>For example, if your test requires a particular optional library in order to succeed, you could decorate the</p> <p>test case with <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.html#unittest.skipIf">@skipIf</a>. Then, the test runner will report that the test wasn’t executed and why, instead of failing the test or omitting the test altogether.</p> <p>To supplement these test skipping behaviors, Django provides two additional skip decorators. Instead of testing a generic boolean, these decorators check the capabilities of the database, and skip the test if the database doesn’t support a specific named feature.</p> <p>The decorators use a string identifier to describe database features. This string corresponds to attributes of</p> <p>the database connection features class. See <a href="https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/db/backends/base/features.py">django.db.backends.base.features.BaseDatabaseFeatures class</a> for a full list of database features that can be used as a basis for skipping tests.</p> <p><b>skipIfDBFeature</b>(*feature_name_strings)</p> <p>Skip the decorated test or TestCase if all of the named database features are supported.</p> <p>For example, the following test will not be executed if the database supports transactions (e.g., it would not run under PostgreSQL, but it would under MySQL with MyISAM tables):</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyTests</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(TestCase):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@skipIfDBFeature(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"supports_transactions"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>test_transaction_behavior</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ... conditional test code</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>pass</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>skipUnlessDBFeature</b>(*feature_name_strings)</p> <p>Skip the decorated test or TestCase if any of the named database features are not supported.</p> <p>For example, the following test will only be executed if the database supports transactions (e.g., it would run under PostgreSQL, but not under MySQL with MyISAM tables):</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyTests</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(TestCase):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@skipUnlessDBFeature(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"supports_transactions"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>test_transaction_behavior</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ... conditional test code</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>pass</b></span></p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_515" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.9.3 Advanced testing topics</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>The request factory</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class RequestFactory</b></p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_515"><i>RequestFactory</i></a> shares the same API as the test client. However, instead of behaving like a browser, the RequestFactory provides a way to generate a request instance that can be used as the first argument to any view. This means you can test a view function the same way as you would test any other function – as a black box, with exactly known inputs, testing for specific outputs.</p> <p>The API for the <a href="index.html#page_515"><i>RequestFactory</i></a> is a slightly restricted subset of the test client API:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• It only has access to the HTTP methods <a href="index.html#page_478"><i>get()</i></a>, <a href="index.html#page_479"><i>post()</i></a><a href="index.html#page_479">,</a> <a href="index.html#page_482"><i>put()</i></a>, <a href="index.html#page_482"><i>delete()</i></a><a href="index.html#page_482">,</a> <a href="index.html#page_481"><i>head()</i></a>, <a href="index.html#page_481"><i>options()</i></a><a href="index.html#page_481">, </a>and</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_482"><i>trace()</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• These methods accept all the same arguments except for follow. Since this is just a factory for pro-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">ducing requests, it’s up to you to handle the response.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• It does not support middleware. Session and authentication attributes must be supplied by the test</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">itself if required for the view to function properly.</p> <p>The query_params parameter was added.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Example</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The following is a unit test using the request factory:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.auth.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">AnonymousUser, User</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.test</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">RequestFactory, TestCase</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">.views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">MyView, my_view</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>SimpleTest</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(TestCase):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>setUp</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Every test needs access to the request factory.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">factory</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">RequestFactory()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">User</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">create_user(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">username</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"jacob"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, email</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"jacob@</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i>. . .</i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, password</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"top_secret"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>test_details</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Create an instance of a GET request.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">factory</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/customer/details"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_516"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Recall that middleware are not supported. You can simulate a</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># logged-in user by setting request.user manually.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Or you can simulate an anonymous user by setting request.user to</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># an AnonymousUser instance.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">AnonymousUser()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Test my_view() as if it were deployed at /customer/details</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">my_view(request)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Use this syntax for class-based views.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">MyView</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">as_view()(request)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertEqual(response</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">status_code,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">200</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>AsyncRequestFactory</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class AsyncRequestFactory</b></p> <p>RequestFactory creates WSGI-like requests. If you want to create ASGI-like requests, including having a correct ASGI scope, you can instead use django.test.AsyncRequestFactory.</p> <p>This class is directly API-compatible with RequestFactory, with the only difference being that it returns ASGIRequest instances rather than WSGIRequest instances. All of its methods are still synchronous callables.</p> <p>Arbitrary keyword arguments in defaults are added directly into the ASGI scope.</p> <p>The query_params parameter was added.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Testing class-based views</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>In order to test class-based views outside of the request/response cycle you must ensure that they are config-</p> <p>ured correctly, by calling <a href="index.html#page_951"><i>setup()</i></a> after instantiation.</p> <p>For example, assuming the following class-based view:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">Listing 24: views.py</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.views.generic</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">TemplateView</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>HomeView</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(TemplateView):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">template_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"myapp/home.html"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get_context_data</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs):</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_517" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"environment"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Production"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_context_data(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You may directly test the get_context_data() method by first instantiating the view, then passing a request to setup(), before proceeding with your test’s code:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">Listing 25: tests.py</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.test</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">RequestFactory, TestCase</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">.views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HomeView</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>HomePageTest</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(TestCase):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>test_environment_set_in_context</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">RequestFactory()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">view</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HomeView()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">view</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">setup(request)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">context</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">view</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_context_data()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertIn(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"environment"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, context)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Tests and multiple host names</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_1888"><i>ALLOWED_HOSTS</i></a> setting is validated when running tests. This allows the test client to differentiate be-tween internal and external URLs.</p> <p>Projects that support multitenancy or otherwise alter business logic based on the request’s host and use</p> <p>custom host names in tests must include those hosts in <a href="index.html#page_1888"><i>ALLOWED_HOSTS</i></a>.</p> <p>The first option to do so is to add the hosts to your settings file. For example, the test suite for docs.djangoproject.com includes the following:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.test</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">TestCase</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>SearchFormTestCase</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(TestCase):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>test_empty_get</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">client</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/en/dev/search/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">headers</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"host"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"docs.djangoproject.dev:8000"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertEqual(response</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">status_code,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">200</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>and the settings file includes a list of the domains supported by the project:</p> <p id="page_518"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">ALLOWED_HOSTS</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"www.djangoproject.dev"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"docs.djangoproject.dev"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Another option is to add the required hosts to <a href="index.html#page_1888"><i>ALLOWED_HOSTS</i></a> using <a href="index.html#page_500"><i>override_settings()</i></a> or</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_500"><i>modify_settings()</i></a>. This option may be preferable in standalone apps that can’t package their own settings file or for projects where the list of domains is not static (e.g., subdomains for multitenancy). For example, you could write a test for the domain http://otherserver/ as follows:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.test</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">TestCase, override_settings</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MultiDomainTestCase</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(TestCase):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@override_settings(ALLOWED_HOSTS</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"otherserver"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">])</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>test_other_domain</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">client</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"http://otherserver/foo/bar/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Disabling <a href="index.html#page_1888"><i>ALLOWED_HOSTS</i></a> checking (ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['*']) when running tests prevents the test client from raising a helpful error message if you follow a redirect to an external URL.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Tests and multiple databases</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Testing primary/replica configurations</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you’re testing a multiple database configuration with primary/replica (referred to as master/slave by some databases) replication, this strategy of creating test databases poses a problem. When the test databases are created, there won’t be any replication, and as a result, data created on the primary won’t be seen on the replica.</p> <p>To compensate for this, Django allows you to define that a database is a test mirror. Consider the following (simplified) example database configuration:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">DATABASES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"ENGINE"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.db.backends.mysql"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"NAME"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"myproject"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"HOST"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"dbprimary"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ... plus some other settings</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"replica"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"ENGINE"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.db.backends.mysql"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"NAME"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"myproject"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"HOST"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"dbreplica"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"TEST"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"MIRROR"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_519" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ... plus some other settings</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>In this setup, we have two database servers: dbprimary, described by the database alias default, and dbreplica described by the alias replica. As you might expect, dbreplica has been configured by the database administrator as a read replica of dbprimary, so in normal activity, any write to default will ap-pear on replica.</p> <p>If Django created two independent test databases, this would break any tests that expected replication to</p> <p>occur. However, the replica database has been configured as a test mirror (using the <a href="index.html#page_1901"><i>MIRROR</i></a> test setting), indicating that under testing, replica should be treated as a mirror of default.</p> <p>When the test environment is configured, a test version of replica will not be created. Instead the connection to replica will be redirected to point at default. As a result, writes to default will appear on replica – but because they are actually the same database, not because there is data replication between the two databases.</p> <p>As this depends on transactions, the tests must use <a href="index.html#page_491"><i>TransactionTestCase</i></a> instead of <a href="index.html#page_492"><i>TestCase</i></a><a href="index.html#page_492">.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Controlling creation order for test databases</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>By default, Django will assume all databases depend on the default database and therefore always create the default database first. However, no guarantees are made on the creation order of any other databases in your test setup.</p> <p>If your database configuration requires a specific creation order, you can specify the dependencies that exist</p> <p>using the <a href="index.html#page_1901"><i>DEPENDENCIES</i></a> test setting. Consider the following (simplified) example database configuration:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">DATABASES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ... db settings</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"TEST"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"DEPENDENCIES"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"diamonds"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"diamonds"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ... db settings</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"TEST"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"DEPENDENCIES"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"clubs"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ... db settings</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_520"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"TEST"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"DEPENDENCIES"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"diamonds"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"spades"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ... db settings</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"TEST"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"DEPENDENCIES"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"diamonds"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"hearts"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"hearts"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ... db settings</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"TEST"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"DEPENDENCIES"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"diamonds"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"clubs"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Under this configuration, the diamonds database will be created first, as it is the only database alias without dependencies. The default and clubs alias will be created next (although the order of creation of this pair is not guaranteed), then hearts, and finally spades.</p> <p>If there are any circular dependencies in the <a href="index.html#page_1901"><i>DEPENDENCIES</i></a> definition, an <a href="index.html#page_1472"><i>ImproperlyConfigured</i></a> exception will be raised.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Advanced features of TransactionTestCase</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>TransactionTestCase.<b>available_apps</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em">Warning: This attribute is a private API. It may be changed or removed without a deprecation period in the future, for instance to accommodate changes in application loading.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">It’s used to optimize Django’s own test suite, which contains hundreds of models but no relations between models in different applications.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">By default, available_apps is set to None. After each test, Django calls <a href="index.html#page_1439"><i>flush</i></a> to reset the database</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">state. This empties all tables and emits the <a href="index.html#page_1961"><i>post_migrate</i></a> signal, which recreates one content type and four permissions for each model. This operation gets expensive proportionally to the number of models.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Setting available_apps to a list of applications instructs Django to behave as if only the models from these applications were available. The behavior of TransactionTestCase changes as follows:</p> <p id="page_521" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_1961"><i>post_migrate</i></a> is fired before each test to create the content types and permissions for each model</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">in available apps, in case they’re missing.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• After each test, Django empties only tables corresponding to models in available apps. However,</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">at the database level, truncation may cascade to related models in unavailable apps. Furthermore</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_1961"><i>post_migrate</i></a> isn’t fired; it will be fired by the next TransactionTestCase, after the correct set of applications is selected.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Since the database isn’t fully flushed, if a test creates instances of models not included in available_apps, they will leak and they may cause unrelated tests to fail. Be careful with tests that use sessions; the default session engine stores them in the database.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Since <a href="index.html#page_1961"><i>post_migrate</i></a> isn’t emitted after flushing the database, its state after a TransactionTestCase</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">isn’t the same as after a TestCase: it’s missing the rows created by listeners to <a href="index.html#page_1961"><i>post_migrate</i></a>. Consid-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">ering the <a href="index.html#page_473">order in which tests are executed, </a>this isn’t an issue, provided either all TransactionTestCase in a given test suite declare available_apps, or none of them.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">available_apps is mandatory in Django’s own test suite.</p> <p>TransactionTestCase.<b>reset_sequences</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Setting reset_sequences = True on a TransactionTestCase will make sure sequences are always reset before the test run:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>TestsThatDependsOnPrimaryKeySequences</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(TransactionTestCase):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">reset_sequences</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>= True</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>test_animal_pk</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">lion</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Animal</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">create(name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"lion"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, sound</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"roar"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># lion.pk is guaranteed to always be 1</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertEqual(lion</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">pk,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Unless you are explicitly testing primary keys sequence numbers, it is recommended that you do not hard code primary key values in tests.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Using reset_sequences = True will slow down the test, since the primary key reset is a relatively expensive database operation.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Enforce running test classes sequentially</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you have test classes that cannot be run in parallel (e.g. because they share a common resource), you can use django.test.testcases.SerializeMixin to run them sequentially. This mixin uses a filesystem lockfile.</p> <p>For example, you can use __file__ to determine that all test classes in the same file that inherit from SerializeMixin will run sequentially:</p> <p id="page_522"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">os</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.test</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">TestCase</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.test.testcases</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">SerializeMixin</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertFalse(os</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">path</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">exists(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">))</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using the Django test runner to test reusable applications</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you are writing a <a href="index.html#page_88">reusable application</a> you may want to use the Django test runner to run your own test suite and thus benefit from the Django testing infrastructure.</p> <p>A common practice is a tests directory next to the application code, with the following structure:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">runtests.py</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">polls/</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">__init__.py</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">models.py</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">tests/</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">__init__.py</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">models.py</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">test_settings.py</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">tests.py</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Let’s take a look inside a couple of those files:</p> <p id="page_523" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">Listing 26: runtests.py</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i>#!/usr/bin/env python</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">os</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">sys</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_runner(settings)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">test_runner</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">TestRunner()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">failures</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span
