style="font-size:0.87em">"app.can_deliver_pizzas"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">))</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">True</span></p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_537" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Authentication in web requests</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django uses <a href="index.html#page_311">sessions</a> and middleware to hook the authentication system into <a href="index.html#page_1859"><i>request objects</i></a>.</p> <p>These provide a <a href="index.html#page_1863"><i>request.user</i></a> attribute and a <a href="index.html#page_1864"><i>request.auser</i></a> async method on every request which rep-resents the current user. If the current user has not logged in, this attribute will be set to an instance of</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1107"><i>AnonymousUser</i></a> , otherwise it will be an instance of <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>User</i></a>.</p> <p>You can tell them apart with <a href="index.html#page_1103"><i>is_authenticated</i></a>, like so:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">is_authenticated:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Do something for authenticated users.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>else</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Do something for anonymous users.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Or in an asynchronous view:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>= await</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">auser()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">is_authenticated:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Do something for authenticated users.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>else</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Do something for anonymous users.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>How to log a user in</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you have an authenticated user you want to attach to the current session - this is done with a <a href="index.html#page_537"><i>login()</i></a> function.</p> <p><b>login</b>(request, user, backend=None)</p> <p><b>alogin</b>(request, user, backend=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Asynchronous version: alogin()</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">To log a user in, from a view, use <a href="index.html#page_537"><i>login()</i></a>. It takes an <a href="index.html#page_1859"><i>HttpRequest</i></a> object and a <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>User</i></a> object. <a href="index.html#page_537"><i>login()</i></a> saves the user’s ID in the session, using Django’s session framework.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Note that any data set during the anonymous session is retained in the session after a user logs in.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This example shows how you might use both <a href="index.html#page_532"><i>authenticate()</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_537"><i>login()</i></a><a href="index.html#page_537">:</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.auth</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">authenticate, login</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_538"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">username</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">POST[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"username"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">password</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">POST[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"password"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">authenticate(request, username</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">username, password</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">password)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>is not None</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">login(request, user)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Redirect to a success page.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>else</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Return an 'invalid login' error message.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Selecting the authentication backend</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When a user logs in, the user’s ID and the backend that was used for authentication are saved in the user’s</p> <p>session. This allows the same <a href="index.html#page_576">authentication backend</a> to fetch the user’s details on a future request. The authentication backend to save in the session is selected as follows:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. Use the value of the optional backend argument, if provided.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. Use the value of the user.backend attribute, if present. This allows pairing <a href="index.html#page_532"><i>authenticate()</i></a> and</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_537"><i>login()</i></a>: <a href="index.html#page_532"><i>authenticate()</i></a> sets the user.backend attribute on the user object it returns.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">3. Use the backend in <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS</i></a> , if there is only one.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">4. Otherwise, raise an exception.</p> <p>In cases 1 and 2, the value of the backend argument or the user.backend attribute should be a dotted import</p> <p>path string (like that found in <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS</i></a> ), not the actual backend class.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>How to log a user out</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>logout</b>(request)</p> <p><b>alogout</b>(request)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Asynchronous version: alogout()</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">To log out a user who has been logged in via <a href="index.html#page_537"><i>django.contrib.auth.login()</i></a>, use <a href="index.html#page_538"><i>django.contrib.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_538"><i>auth.logout()</i></a> within your view. It takes an <a href="index.html#page_1859"><i>HttpRequest</i></a> object and has no return value. Example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.auth</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">logout</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_539" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>logout_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">logout(request)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Redirect to a success page.</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Note that <a href="index.html#page_538"><i>logout()</i></a> doesn’t throw any errors if the user wasn’t logged in.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">When you call <a href="index.html#page_538"><i>logout()</i></a>, the session data for the current request is completely cleaned out. All existing data is removed. This is to prevent another person from using the same web browser to log in and have access to the previous user’s session data. If you want to put anything into the session that will</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">be available to the user immediately after logging out, do that after calling <a href="index.html#page_538"><i>django.contrib.auth.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_538"><i>logout()</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Limiting access to logged-in users</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>The raw way</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The raw way to limit access to pages is to check <a href="index.html#page_1103"><i>request.user.is_authenticated</i></a> and either redirect to a login page:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.conf</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">settings</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.shortcuts</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">redirect</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if not</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">is_authenticated:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">redirect(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">f"{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">settings</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">LOGIN_URL</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">}?next={</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">path</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">}"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><i>. . .</i>or display an error message:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.shortcuts</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">render</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if not</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">is_authenticated:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">render(request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"myapp/login_error.html"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_540"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>The login_required decorator</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>login_required</b>(redirect_field_name='next', login_url=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">As a shortcut, you can use the convenient <a href="index.html#page_540"><i>login_required()</i></a> decorator:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.auth.decorators</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">login_required</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@login_required</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_540"><i>login_required()</i></a> does the following:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• If the user isn’t logged in, redirect to <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>settings.LOGIN_URL</i></a>, passing the current absolute path in</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">the query string. Example: /accounts/login/?next=/polls/3/.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• If the user is logged in, execute the view normally. The view code is free to assume the user is</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">logged in.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">By default, the path that the user should be redirected to upon successful authentication is stored in a query string parameter called "next". If you would prefer to use a different name for this parameter,</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_540"><i>login_required()</i></a> takes an optional redirect_field_name parameter:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.auth.decorators</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">login_required</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@login_required(redirect_field_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"my_redirect_field"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Note that if you provide a value to redirect_field_name, you will most likely need to customize your login template as well, since the template context variable which stores the redirect path will use the value of redirect_field_name as its key rather than "next" (the default).</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_540"><i>login_required()</i></a> also takes an optional login_url parameter. Example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.auth.decorators</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">login_required</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@login_required(login_url</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/accounts/login/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Note that if you don’t specify the login_url parameter, you’ll need to ensure that the <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>settings.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>LOGIN_URL</i></a> and your login view are properly associated. For example, using the defaults, add the fol-lowing lines to your URLconf:</p> <p id="page_541" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.auth</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">auth_views</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"accounts/login/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, auth_views</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">LoginView</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">as_view()),</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>settings.LOGIN_URL</i></a> also accepts view function names and <a href="index.html#page_278">named URL patterns</a>. This allows you to freely remap your login view within your URLconf without having to update the setting.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: The login_required decorator does NOT check the is_active flag on a user, but the default</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS</i></a> reject inactive users.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>See also:</p> <p>If you are writing custom views for Django’s admin (or need the same authorization check that the built-in</p> <p>views use), you may find the <a href="index.html#page_1101"><i>django.contrib.admin.views.decorators.staff_member_required()</i></a> dec-orator a useful alternative to login_required().</p> <p>Support for wrapping asynchronous view functions was added.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>The LoginRequiredMixin mixin</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When using <a href="index.html#page_410">class-based views, </a>you can achieve the same behavior as with login_required by using the LoginRequiredMixin. This mixin should be at the leftmost position in the inheritance list.</p> <p><b>class LoginRequiredMixin</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If a view is using this mixin, all requests by non-authenticated users will be redirected to the login page</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">or shown an HTTP 403 Forbidden error, depending on the <a href="index.html#page_546"><i>raise_exception</i></a> parameter.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">You can set any of the parameters of <a href="index.html#page_546"><i>AccessMixin</i></a> to customize the handling of unauthorized users:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.auth.mixins</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">LoginRequiredMixin</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyView</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(LoginRequiredMixin, View):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">login_url</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"/login/"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">redirect_field_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"redirect_to"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: Just as the login_required decorator, this mixin does NOT check the is_active flag on a user, but</p> <p>the default <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS</i></a> reject inactive users.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_542"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>The login_not_required decorator</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When <a href="index.html#page_1599"><i>LoginRequiredMiddleware</i></a> is installed, all views require authentication by default. Some views, such as the login view, may need to disable this behavior.</p> <p><b>login_not_required</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Allows unauthenticated requests to this view when <a href="index.html#page_1599"><i>LoginRequiredMiddleware</i></a> is installed.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Limiting access to logged-in users that pass a test</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To limit access based on certain permissions or some other test, you’d do essentially the same thing as de-scribed in the previous section.</p> <p>You can run your test on <a href="index.html#page_1863"><i>request.user</i></a> in the view directly. For example, this view checks to make sure the user has an email in the desired domain and if not, redirects to the login page:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.shortcuts</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">redirect</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if not</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">email</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">endswith(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">redirect(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/login/?next=%s"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">path)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>user_passes_test</b>( test_func, login_url=None, redirect_field_name='next')</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">As a shortcut, you can use the convenient user_passes_test decorator which performs a redirect when the callable returns False:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.auth.decorators</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">user_passes_test</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>email_check</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(user):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">email</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">endswith(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@user_passes_test(email_check)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_542"><i>user_passes_test()</i></a> takes a required argument: a callable that takes a <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>User</i></a> object and returns True</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">if the user is allowed to view the page. Note that <a href="index.html#page_542"><i>user_passes_test()</i></a> does not automatically check</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">that the <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>User</i></a> is not anonymous.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_542"><i>user_passes_test()</i></a> takes two optional arguments:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>login_url</b></p> <p id="page_543" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Lets you specify the URL that users who don’t pass the test will be redirected to. It may be a login</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">page and defaults to <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>settings.LOGIN_URL</i></a> if you don’t specify one.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>redirect_field_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Same as for <a href="index.html#page_540"><i>login_required()</i>. </a>Setting it to None removes it from the URL, which you may want to do if you are redirecting users that don’t pass the test to a non-login page where there’s no “next page”.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@user_passes_test(email_check, login_url</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/login/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Support for wrapping asynchronous view functions and using asynchronous test callables was added.</p> <p><b>class UserPassesTestMixin</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">When using <a href="index.html#page_410">class-based views</a>, you can use the UserPassesTestMixin to do this.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>test_func</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">You have to override the test_func() method of the class to provide the test that is performed.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Furthermore, you can set any of the parameters of <a href="index.html#page_546"><i>AccessMixin</i></a> to customize the handling of unauthorized users:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.auth.mixins</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">UserPassesTestMixin</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyView</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(UserPassesTestMixin, View):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>test_func</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">email</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">endswith(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_test_func</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">You can also override the get_test_func() method to have the mixin use a differently named</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">function for its checks (instead of <a href="index.html#page_543"><i>test_func()</i>).</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Stacking <b>UserPassesTestMixin</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Due to the way UserPassesTestMixin is implemented, you cannot stack them in your inheritance list. The following does NOT work:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>TestMixin1</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(UserPassesTestMixin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>test_func</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">email</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">endswith(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>TestMixin2</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(UserPassesTestMixin):</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_544"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>test_func</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">username</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">startswith(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"django"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyView</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(TestMixin1, TestMixin2, View):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If TestMixin1 would call super() and take that result into account, TestMixin1 wouldn’t work stan-dalone anymore.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>The permission_required decorator</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>permission_required</b>(perm, login_url=None, raise_exception=False)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">It’s a relatively common task to check whether a user has a particular permission. For that reason,</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Django provides a shortcut for that case: the <a href="index.html#page_544"><i>permission_required()</i></a> decorator:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.auth.decorators</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">permission_required</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@permission_required(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"polls.add_choice"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Just like the <a href="index.html#page_1105"><i>has_perm()</i></a> method, permission names take the form "<app label>.<permission codename>" (i.e. polls.add_choice for a permission on a model in the polls application).</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The decorator may also take an iterable of permissions, in which case the user must have all of the permissions in order to access the view.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Note that <a href="index.html#page_544"><i>permission_required()</i></a> also takes an optional login_url parameter:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.auth.decorators</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">permission_required</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@permission_required(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"polls.add_choice"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, login_url</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/loginpage/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">As in the <a href="index.html#page_540"><i>login_required()</i></a> decorator, login_url defaults to <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>settings.LOGIN_URL</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If the raise_exception parameter is given, the decorator will raise <a href="index.html#page_1472"><i>PermissionDenied</i>, </a>prompting <a href="index.html#page_2101">the</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_2101">403 (HTTP Forbidden) view</a> instead of redirecting to the login page.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you want to use raise_exception but also give your users a chance to login first, you can add the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_540"><i>login_required()</i></a> decorator:</p> <p id="page_545" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.auth.decorators</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">login_required, permission_required</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@login_required</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@permission_required(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"polls.add_choice"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, raise_exception</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This also avoids a redirect loop when <a href="index.html#page_549"><i>LoginView</i></a>’s redirect_authenticated_user=True and the logged-in user doesn’t have all of the required permissions.</p> <p>Support for wrapping asynchronous view functions was added.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>The PermissionRequiredMixin mixin</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To apply permission checks to <a href="index.html#page_949">class-based views, </a>you can use the PermissionRequiredMixin:</p> <p><b>class PermissionRequiredMixin</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This mixin, just like the permission_required decorator, checks whether the user accessing a view has all given permissions. You should specify the permission (or an iterable of permissions) using the permission_required parameter:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.auth.mixins</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">PermissionRequiredMixin</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyView</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(PermissionRequiredMixin, View):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">permission_required</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"polls.add_choice"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Or multiple of permissions:</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">permission_required</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"polls.view_choice"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"polls.change_choice"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">You can set any of the parameters of <a href="index.html#page_546"><i>AccessMixin</i></a> to customize the handling of unauthorized users.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">You may also override these methods:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_permission_required</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns an iterable of permission names used by the mixin. Defaults to the permission_required attribute, converted to a tuple if necessary.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>has_permission</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns a boolean denoting whether the current user has permission to execute the decorated view.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">By default, this returns the result of calling <a href="index.html#page_1105"><i>has_perms()</i></a> with the list of permissions returned by</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_545"><i>get_permission_required()</i></a>.</p> <p id="page_546"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Redirecting unauthorized requests in class-based views</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To ease the handling of access restrictions in <a href="index.html#page_949">class-based views, </a>the AccessMixin can be used to configure the behavior of a view when access is denied. Authenticated users are denied access with an HTTP 403 Forbidden response. Anonymous users are redirected to the login page or shown an HTTP 403 Forbidden</p> <p>response, depending on the <a href="index.html#page_546"><i>raise_exception</i></a> attribute.</p> <p><b>class AccessMixin</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>login_url</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Default return value for <a href="index.html#page_546"><i>get_login_url()</i>. </a>Defaults to None in which case <a href="index.html#page_546"><i>get_login_url()</i></a> falls</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">back to <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>settings.LOGIN_URL</i>.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>permission_denied_message</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Default return value for <a href="index.html#page_546"><i>get_permission_denied_message()</i></a>. Defaults to an empty string.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>redirect_field_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Default return value for <a href="index.html#page_546"><i>get_redirect_field_name()</i>. </a>Defaults to "next".</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>raise_exception</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If this attribute is set to True, a <a href="index.html#page_1472"><i>PermissionDenied</i></a> exception is raised when the conditions are not met. When False (the default), anonymous users are redirected to the login page.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_login_url</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns the URL that users who don’t pass the test will be redirected to. Returns <a href="index.html#page_546"><i>login_url</i></a> if</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">set, or <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>settings.LOGIN_URL</i></a> otherwise.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_permission_denied_message</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">When <a href="index.html#page_546"><i>raise_exception</i></a> is True, this method can be used to control the error message passed to</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">the error handler for display to the user. Returns the <a href="index.html#page_546"><i>permission_denied_message</i></a> attribute by default.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_redirect_field_name</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns the name of the query parameter that will contain the URL the user should be redirected to after a successful login. If you set this to None, a query parameter won’t be added. Returns the</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_546"><i>redirect_field_name</i></a> attribute by default.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>handle_no_permission</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Depending on the value of raise_exception, the method either raises a <a href="index.html#page_1472"><i>PermissionDenied</i></a> ex-ception or redirects the user to the login_url, optionally including the redirect_field_name if it is set.</p> <p id="page_547" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Session invalidation on password change</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If your <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>AUTH_USER_MODEL</i></a> inherits from <a href="index.html#page_587"><i>AbstractBaseUser</i></a> or implements its own</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_589"><i>get_session_auth_hash()</i></a> method, authenticated sessions will include the hash returned by this function.</p> <p>In the <a href="index.html#page_587"><i>AbstractBaseUser</i></a> case, this is an HMAC of the password field. Django verifies that the hash in the session for each request matches the one that’s computed during the request. This allows a user to log out all of their sessions by changing their password.</p> <p>The default password change views included with Django, <a href="index.html#page_552"><i>PasswordChangeView</i></a> and the</p> <p>user_change_password view in the <a href="index.html#page_598"><i>django.contrib.auth</i></a> admin, update the session with the new password hash so that a user changing their own password won’t log themselves out. If you have a custom</p> <p>password change view and wish to have similar behavior, use the <a href="index.html#page_547"><i>update_session_auth_hash()</i></a> function.</p> <p><b>update_session_auth_hash</b>(request, user)</p> <p><b>aupdate_session_auth_hash</b>(request, user)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Asynchronous version: aupdate_session_auth_hash()</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This function takes the current request and the updated user object from which the new session hash will be derived and updates the session hash appropriately. It also rotates the session key so that a stolen session cookie will be invalidated.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Example usage:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.auth</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">update_session_auth_hash</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>password_change</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">method</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"POST"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">PasswordChangeForm(user</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user, data</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">POST)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">is_valid():</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">update_session_auth_hash(request, form</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>else</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: Since <a href="index.html#page_589"><i>get_session_auth_hash()</i></a> is based on <a href="index.html#page_1925"><i>SECRET_KEY</i></a> , secret key values must be rotated to avoid</p> <p>invalidating existing sessions when updating your site to use a new secret. See <a href="index.html#page_1926"><i>SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS</i></a> for details.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_548"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Authentication Views</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django provides several views that you can use for handling login, logout, and password management. These</p> <p>make use of the <a href="index.html#page_557">stock auth forms</a> but you can pass in your own forms as well.</p> <p>Django provides no default template for the authentication views. You should create your own templates for</p> <p>the views you want to use. The template context is documented in each view, see <a href="index.html#page_549">All authentication views.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using the views</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>There are different methods to implement these views in your project. The easiest way is to include the provided URLconf in django.contrib.auth.urls in your own URLconf, for example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"accounts/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, include(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.contrib.auth.urls"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This will include the following URL patterns:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">accounts/login/ [name='login']</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">accounts/logout/ [name='logout']</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">accounts/password_change/ [name='password_change']</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">accounts/password_change/done/ [name='password_change_done']</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">accounts/password_reset/ [name='password_reset']</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">accounts/password_reset/done/ [name='password_reset_done']</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">accounts/reset/<uidb64>/<token>/ [name='password_reset_confirm']</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">accounts/reset/done/ [name='password_reset_complete']</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The views provide a URL name for easier reference. See <a href="index.html#page_266">the URL documentation</a> for details on using named URL patterns.</p> <p>If you want more control over your URLs, you can reference a specific view in your URLconf:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.auth</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">auth_views</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"change-password/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, auth_views</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">PasswordChangeView</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">as_view()),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The views have optional arguments you can use to alter the behavior of the view. For example, if you want to change the template name a view uses, you can provide the template_name argument. A way to do this is to provide keyword arguments in the URLconf, these will be passed on to the view. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_549" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"change-password/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">auth_views</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">PasswordChangeView</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">as_view(template_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"change-password.html"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>All views are <a href="index.html#page_410">class-based</a>, which allows you to easily customize them by subclassing.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>All authentication views</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This is a list with all the views django.contrib.auth provides. For implementation details see <a href="index.html#page_548">Using the</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_548">views.</a></p> <p><b>class LoginView</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">URL name: login</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">See <a href="index.html#page_266">the URL documentation</a> for details on using named URL patterns.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Methods and Attributes</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>template_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The name of a template to display for the view used to log the user in. Defaults to registration/ login.html .</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>next_page</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The URL to redirect to after login. Defaults to <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>LOGIN_REDIRECT_URL</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>redirect_field_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The name of a GET field containing the URL to redirect to after login. Defaults to next. Overrides</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">the <a href="index.html#page_550"><i>get_default_redirect_url()</i></a> URL if the given GET parameter is passed.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>authentication_form</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A callable (typically a form class) to use for authentication. Defaults to <a href="index.html#page_558"><i>AuthenticationForm</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>extra_context</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A dictionary of context data that will be added to the default context data passed to the template.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>redirect_authenticated_user</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A boolean that controls whether or not authenticated users accessing the login page will be redi-rected as if they had just successfully logged in. Defaults to False.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:5em">Warning: If you enable redirect_authenticated_user, other websites will be able to de-termine if their visitors are authenticated on your site by requesting redirect URLs to image</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">files on your website. To avoid this “<a href="https://robinlinus.github.io/socialmedia-leak/">social media fingerprinting” </a>information leakage, host all images and your favicon on a separate domain.</p> <p id="page_550"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:5em">Enabling redirect_authenticated_user can also result in a redirect loop when using the</p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><a href="index.html#page_544"><i>permission_required()</i></a> decorator unless the raise_exception parameter is used.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>success_url_allowed_hosts</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#set">set</a> of hosts, in addition to <a href="index.html#page_1864"><i>request.get_host()</i></a><a href="index.html#page_1864">, </a>that are safe for redirecting after login. De-</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">faults to an empty <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#set">set.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_default_redirect_url</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns the URL to redirect to after login. The default implementation resolves and returns</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_549"><i>next_page</i></a> if set, or <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>LOGIN_REDIRECT_URL</i></a> otherwise.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Here’s what LoginView does:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• If called via GET, it displays a login form that POSTs to the same URL. More on this in a bit.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• If called via POST with user submitted credentials, it tries to log the user in. If login is successful,</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">the view redirects to the URL specified in next. If next isn’t provided, it redirects to <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>settings.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>LOGIN_REDIRECT_URL</i></a> (which defaults to /accounts/profile/). If login isn’t successful, it redis-plays the login form.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">It’s your responsibility to provide the html for the login template , called registration/login.html by default. This template gets passed four template context variables:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• form: A <a href="index.html#page_1487"><i>Form</i></a> object representing the <a href="index.html#page_558"><i>AuthenticationForm</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• next: The URL to redirect to after successful login. This may contain a query string, too.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• site: The current <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i></a>, according to the <a href="index.html#page_1945"><i>SITE_ID</i></a> setting. If you don’t have the site framework</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">installed, this will be set to an instance of <a href="index.html#page_1368"><i>RequestSite</i>, </a>which derives the site name and domain</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">from the current <a href="index.html#page_1859"><i>HttpRequest</i>.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• site_name: An alias for site.name. If you don’t have the site framework installed, this will be</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">set to the value of <a href="index.html#page_1861"><i>request.META['SERVER_NAME']</i>. </a>For more on sites, see <a href="index.html#page_1360">The “sites” framework</a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you’d prefer not to call the template registration/login.html, you can pass the template_name parameter via the extra arguments to the as_view method in your URLconf. For example, this URL-conf line would use myapp/login.html instead:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"accounts/login/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, auth_views</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">LoginView</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">as_view(template_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"myapp/login.html"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)),</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">You can also specify the name of the GET field which contains the URL to redirect to after login using redirect_field_name. By default, the field is called next.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Here’s a sample registration/login.html template you can use as a starting point. This form must accept a request keyword argument in its __init__() method and provide a get_user() method which returns the authenticated user object (this method is only ever called after successful form validation).</p> <p><b>class LogoutView</b></p> <p id="page_552"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Logs a user out on POST requests.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">URL name: logout</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Attributes:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>next_page</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The URL to redirect to after logout. If you don’t have the site framework installed, this will be</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">set to the value of <a href="index.html#page_1861"><i>request.META['SERVER_NAME']</i>. </a>For more on sites, see <a href="index.html#page_1360">The “sites” framework</a>.</p> <p><b>logout_then_login</b>(request, login_url=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Logs a user out on POST requests, then redirects to the login page.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">URL name: No default URL provided</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Optional arguments:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• login_url: The URL of the login page to redirect to. Defaults to <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>settings.LOGIN_URL</i></a> if not</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">supplied.</p> <p><b>class PasswordChangeView</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">URL name: password_change</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Allows a user to change their password.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Attributes:</p> <p id="page_553" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>template_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The full name of a template to use for displaying the password change form. Defaults to <a href="index.html#page_559"><i>PasswordChangeForm</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>extra_context</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A dictionary of context data that will be added to the default context data passed to the template.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Template context:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• form: The password change form (see form_class above).</p> <p><b>class PasswordChangeDoneView</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">URL name: password_change_done</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The page shown after a user has changed their password.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Attributes:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>template_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The full name of a template to use. Defaults to registration/password_change_done.html if not supplied.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>extra_context</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A dictionary of context data that will be added to the default context data passed to the template.</p> <p><b>class PasswordResetView</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">URL name: password_reset</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Allows a user to reset their password by generating a one-time use link that can be used to reset the password, and sending that link to the user’s registered email address.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This view will send an email if the following conditions are met:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• The email address provided exists in the system.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• The requested user is active (User.is_active is True).</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• The requested user has a usable password. Users flagged with an unusable password (see</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_1104"><i>set_unusable_password()</i> ) </a>aren’t allowed to request a password reset to prevent misuse when using an external authentication source like LDAP.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If any of these conditions are not met, no email will be sent, but the user won’t receive any error mes-sage either. This prevents information leaking to potential attackers. If you want to provide an error</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">message in this case, you can subclass <a href="index.html#page_559"><i>PasswordResetForm</i></a> and use the form_class attribute.</p> <p id="page_554"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Note: Be aware that sending an email costs extra time, hence you may be vulnerable to an email address enumeration timing attack due to a difference between the duration of a reset request for an existing email address and the duration of a reset request for a nonexistent email address. To reduce</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">the overhead, you can use a 3rd party package that allows to send emails asynchronously, e.g. <a href="https://pypi.org/project/django-mailer/">django-</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="https://pypi.org/project/django-mailer/">mailer</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Attributes:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>template_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The full name of a template to use for displaying the password reset form. Defaults to registration/password_reset_form.html if not supplied.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>form_class</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Form that will be used to get the email of the user to reset the password for. Defaults to</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_559"><i>PasswordResetForm</i></a> .</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>email_template_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The full name of a template to use for generating the email with the reset password link. Defaults to registration/password_reset_email.html if not supplied.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>subject_template_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The full name of a template to use for the subject of the email with the reset password link. De-faults to registration/password_reset_subject.txt if not supplied.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>token_generator</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Instance of the class to check the one time link. This will default to default_token_generator, it’s an instance of django.contrib.auth.tokens.PasswordResetTokenGenerator.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>success_url</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The URL to redirect to after a successful password reset request. <span style="float:right">Defaults to</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">'password_reset_done'.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>from_email</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A valid email address. By default Django uses the <a href="index.html#page_1910"><i>DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL</i>.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>extra_context</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A dictionary of context data that will be added to the default context data passed to the template.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>html_email_template_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The full name of a template to use for generating a <i>text/html</i> multipart email with the password reset link. By default, HTML email is not sent.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>extra_email_context</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A dictionary of context data that will be available in the email template. It can be used to override default template context values listed below e.g. domain.</p> <p id="page_555" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Template context:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• form: The form (see form_class above) for resetting the user’s password.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Email template context:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• email: An alias for user.email</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• user: The current <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>User</i></a>, according to the email form field. Only active users are able to reset their</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">passwords (User.is_active is True).</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• site_name: An alias for site.name. If you don’t have the site framework installed, this will be</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">set to the value of <a href="index.html#page_1861"><i>request.META['SERVER_NAME']</i>. </a>For more on sites, see <a href="index.html#page_1360">The “sites” framework</a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• domain: An alias for site.domain. If you don’t have the site framework installed, this will be set</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">to the value of request.get_host().</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• protocol: http or https</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• uid: The user’s primary key encoded in base 64.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• token: Token to check that the reset link is valid.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Sample registration/password_reset_email.html (email body template):</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">Someone asked for password reset for email</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">email</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.
