style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"fields"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"email"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"date_of_birth"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"password1"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"password2"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">search_fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"email"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">ordering</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"email"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter_horizontal</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Now register the new UserAdmin...</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">register(MyUser, UserAdmin)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ... and, since we're not using Django's built-in permissions,</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># unregister the Group model from admin.</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">unregister(Group)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Finally, specify the custom model as the default user model for your project using the <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>AUTH_USER_MODEL</i></a> setting in your settings.py:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">AUTH_USER_MODEL</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"customauth.MyUser"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Adding an async interface</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To optimize performance when called from an async context authentication, backends can implement async versions of each function -aget_user(user_id) and aauthenticate(request, **credentials). When an authentication backend extends BaseBackend and async versions of these functions are not provided, they</p> <p>will be automatically synthesized with sync_to_async. This has <a href="index.html#page_767">performance penalties</a>.</p> <p>While an async interface is optional, a synchronous interface is always required. There is no automatic synthesis for a synchronous interface if an async interface is implemented.</p> <p id="page_598"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django’s out-of-the-box authentication backends have native async support. If these native backends are extended take special care to make sure the async versions of modified functions are modified as well. Django comes with a user authentication system. It handles user accounts, groups, permissions and cookie-based user sessions. This section of the documentation explains how the default implementation works out of the box, as well as how to <a href="index.html#page_576">extend and customize</a> it to suit your project’s needs.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.10.4 Overview</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The Django authentication system handles both authentication and authorization. Briefly, authentication verifies a user is who they claim to be, and authorization determines what an authenticated user is allowed to do. Here the term authentication is used to refer to both tasks.</p> <p>The auth system consists of:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Users</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Permissions: Binary (yes/no) flags designating whether a user may perform a certain task.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Groups: A generic way of applying labels and permissions to more than one user.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• A configurable password hashing system</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Forms and view tools for logging in users, or restricting content</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• A pluggable backend system</p> <p>The authentication system in Django aims to be very generic and doesn’t provide some features commonly found in web authentication systems. Solutions for some of these common problems have been implemented in third-party packages:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Password strength checking</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Throttling of login attempts</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Authentication against third-parties (OAuth, for example)</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Object-level permissions</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.10.5 Installation</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Authentication support is bundled as a Django contrib module in django.contrib.auth. By default, the</p> <p>required configuration is already included in the settings.py generated by <a href="index.html#page_1456"><i>django-admin startproject</i></a>,</p> <p>these consist of two items listed in your <a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a> setting:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. 'django.contrib.auth' contains the core of the authentication framework, and its default models.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. 'django.contrib.contenttypes' is the Django <a href="index.html#page_1114">content type system</a>, which allows permissions to be</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">associated with models you create.</p> <p>and these items in your <a href="index.html#page_1923"><i>MIDDLEWARE</i></a> setting:</p> <p id="page_599" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. <a href="index.html#page_1599"><i>SessionMiddleware</i></a> manages <a href="index.html#page_311">sessions</a> across requests.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. <a href="index.html#page_1599"><i>AuthenticationMiddleware</i></a> associates users with requests using sessions.</p> <p>With these settings in place, running the command manage.py migrate creates the necessary database tables for auth related models and permissions for any models defined in your installed apps.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.10.6 Usage</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><a href="index.html#page_530">Using Django’s default implementation</a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_530">Working with User objects</a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_533">Permissions and authorization</a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_537">Authentication in web requests</a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_561">Managing users in the admin</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1102">API reference for the default implementation</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_576">Customizing Users and authentication</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_562">Password management in Django</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.47em"><b>3.11 Django’s cache framework</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A fundamental trade-off in dynamic websites is, well, they’re dynamic. Each time a user requests a page, the web server makes all sorts of calculations – from database queries to template rendering to business logic – to create the page that your site’s visitor sees. This is a lot more expensive, from a processing-overhead perspective, than your standard read-a-file-off-the-filesystem server arrangement.</p> <p>For most web applications, this overhead isn’t a big deal. Most web applications aren’t washingtonpost.com or slashdot.org; they’re small- to medium-sized sites with so-so traffic. But for medium- to high-traffic sites, it’s essential to cut as much overhead as possible.</p> <p>That’s where caching comes in.</p> <p>To cache something is to save the result of an expensive calculation so that you don’t have to perform the calculation next time. Here’s some pseudocode explaining how this would work for a dynamically generated web page:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">given a URL, try finding that page in the cache</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">if the page is in the cache:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">return the cached page</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">else:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">generate the page</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_600"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">save the generated page in the cache (for next time)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">return the generated page</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django comes with a robust cache system that lets you save dynamic pages so they don’t have to be calculated for each request. For convenience, Django offers different levels of cache granularity: You can cache the output of specific views, you can cache only the pieces that are difficult to produce, or you can cache your entire site.</p> <p>Django also works well with “downstream” caches, such as <a href="http://www.squid-cache.org/">Squid</a> and browser-based caches. These are the types of caches that you don’t directly control but to which you can provide hints (via HTTP headers) about which parts of your site should be cached, and how.</p> <p>See also:</p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_2110">Cache Framework design philosophy</a> explains a few of the design decisions of the framework.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.11.1 Setting up the cache</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The cache system requires a small amount of setup. Namely, you have to tell it where your cached data should live – whether in a database, on the filesystem or directly in memory. This is an important decision that affects your cache’s performance; yes, some cache types are faster than others.</p> <p>Your cache preference goes in the <a href="index.html#page_1889"><i>CACHES</i></a> setting in your settings file. Here’s an explanation of all available</p> <p>values for <a href="index.html#page_1889"><i>CACHES</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Memcached</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><a href="https://memcached.org/">Memcached</a> is an entirely memory-based cache server, originally developed to handle high loads at Live-Journal.com and subsequently open-sourced by Danga Interactive. It is used by sites such as Facebook and Wikipedia to reduce database access and dramatically increase site performance.</p> <p>Memcached runs as a daemon and is allotted a specified amount of RAM. All it does is provide a fast interface for adding, retrieving and deleting data in the cache. All data is stored directly in memory, so there’s no overhead of database or filesystem usage.</p> <p>After installing Memcached itself, you’ll need to install a Memcached binding. There are several Python</p> <p>Memcached bindings available; the two supported by Django are <a href="https://pypi.org/project/pylibmc/">pylibmc</a> and <a href="https://pypi.org/project/pymemcache/">pymemcache</a><a href="https://pypi.org/project/pymemcache/">.</a></p> <p>To use Memcached with Django:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Set <a href="index.html#page_1890"><i>BACKEND</i></a> to django.core.cache.backends.memcached.PyMemcacheCache or django.core.cache.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">backends.memcached.PyLibMCCache (depending on your chosen memcached binding)</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Set <a href="index.html#page_1891"><i>LOCATION</i></a> to ip:port values, where ip is the IP address of the Memcached daemon and port is the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">port on which Memcached is running, or to a unix:path value, where path is the path to a Memcached Unix socket file.</p> <p id="page_601" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>In this example, Memcached is running on localhost (127.0.0.1) port 11211, using the pymemcache binding:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">CACHES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"BACKEND"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.cache.backends.memcached.PyMemcacheCache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"LOCATION"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"127.0.0.1:11211"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>In this example, Memcached is available through a local Unix socket file /tmp/memcached.sock using the pymemcache binding:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">CACHES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"BACKEND"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.cache.backends.memcached.PyMemcacheCache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"LOCATION"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"unix:/tmp/memcached.sock"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>One excellent feature of Memcached is its ability to share a cache over multiple servers. This means you can run Memcached daemons on multiple machines, and the program will treat the group of machines as a single cache, without the need to duplicate cache values on each machine. To take advantage of this feature,</p> <p>include all server addresses in <a href="index.html#page_1891"><i>LOCATION</i></a> , either as a semicolon or comma delimited string, or as a list.</p> <p>In this example, the cache is shared over Memcached instances running on IP address 172.19.26.240 and 172.19.26.242, both on port 11211:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">CACHES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"BACKEND"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.cache.backends.memcached.PyMemcacheCache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"LOCATION"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"172.19.26.240:11211"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"172.19.26.242:11211"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>In the following example, the cache is shared over Memcached instances running on the IP addresses 172.19.26.240 (port 11211), 172.19.26.242 (port 11212), and 172.19.26.244 (port 11213):</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">CACHES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"BACKEND"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.cache.backends.memcached.PyMemcacheCache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"LOCATION"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"172.19.26.240:11211"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_602"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"172.19.26.242:11212"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"172.19.26.244:11213"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>By default, the PyMemcacheCache backend sets the following options (you can override them in your</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1891"><i>OPTIONS</i></a> ):</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">"OPTIONS"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"allow_unicode_keys"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default_noreply"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>False</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"serde"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: pymemcache</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">serde</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">pickle_serde,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A final point about Memcached is that memory-based caching has a disadvantage: because the cached data is stored in memory, the data will be lost if your server crashes. Clearly, memory isn’t intended for permanent data storage, so don’t rely on memory-based caching as your only data storage. Without a doubt, none of the Django caching backends should be used for permanent storage – they’re all intended to be solutions for caching, not storage – but we point this out here because memory-based caching is particularly temporary.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Redis</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><a href="https://redis.io/">Redis</a> is an in-memory database that can be used for caching. To begin you’ll need a Redis server running either locally or on a remote machine.</p> <p>After setting up the Redis server, you’ll need to install Python bindings for Redis. <a href="https://pypi.org/project/redis/">redis-py</a> is the binding</p> <p>supported natively by Django. Installing the <a href="https://pypi.org/project/hiredis/">hiredis-py</a> package is also recommended.</p> <p>To use Redis as your cache backend with Django:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Set <a href="index.html#page_1890"><i>BACKEND</i></a> to django.core.cache.backends.redis.RedisCache.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Set <a href="index.html#page_1891"><i>LOCATION</i></a> to the URL pointing to your Redis instance, using the appropriate scheme. See the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">redis-py docs for <a href="https://redis-py.readthedocs.io/en/stable/connections.html#redis.connection.ConnectionPool.from_url">details on the available schemes</a>.</p> <p>For example, if Redis is running on localhost (127.0.0.1) port 6379:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">CACHES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"BACKEND"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.cache.backends.redis.RedisCache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"LOCATION"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"redis://127.0.0.1:6379"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p id="page_603" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Often Redis servers are protected with authentication. In order to supply a username and password, add them in the LOCATION along with the URL:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">CACHES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"BACKEND"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.cache.backends.redis.RedisCache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"LOCATION"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"redis://username:password@127.0.0.1:6379"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you have multiple Redis servers set up in the replication mode, you can specify the servers either as a semi-colon or comma delimited string, or as a list. While using multiple servers, write operations are performed on the first server (leader). Read operations are performed on the other servers (replicas) chosen at random:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">CACHES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"BACKEND"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.cache.backends.redis.RedisCache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"LOCATION"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"redis://127.0.0.1:6379"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># leader</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"redis://127.0.0.1:6378"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># read-replica 1</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"redis://127.0.0.1:6377"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># read-replica 2</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Database caching</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django can store its cached data in your database. This works best if you’ve got a fast, well-indexed database server.</p> <p>To use a database table as your cache backend:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Set <a href="index.html#page_1890"><i>BACKEND</i></a> to django.core.cache.backends.db.DatabaseCache</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Set <a href="index.html#page_1891"><i>LOCATION</i></a> to tablename, the name of the database table. This name can be whatever you want, as</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">long as it’s a valid table name that’s not already being used in your database.</p> <p>In this example, the cache table’s name is my_cache_table:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">CACHES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"BACKEND"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.cache.backends.db.DatabaseCache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"LOCATION"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"my_cache_table"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p id="page_604"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Unlike other cache backends, the database cache does not support automatic culling of expired entries at the database level. Instead, expired cache entries are culled each time add(), set(), or touch() is called.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Creating the cache table</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Before using the database cache, you must create the cache table with this command:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">python manage.py createcachetable</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This creates a table in your database that is in the proper format that Django’s database-cache system ex-</p> <p>pects. The name of the table is taken from <a href="index.html#page_1891"><i>LOCATION</i></a> .</p> <p>If you are using multiple database caches, <a href="index.html#page_1436"><i>createcachetable</i></a> creates one table for each cache.</p> <p>If you are using multiple databases, <a href="index.html#page_1436"><i>createcachetable</i></a> observes the allow_migrate() method of your database routers (see below).</p> <p>Like <a href="index.html#page_1446"><i>migrate</i>,</a> <a href="index.html#page_1436"><i>createcachetable</i></a> won’t touch an existing table. It will only create missing tables.</p> <p>To print the SQL that would be run, rather than run it, use the <a href="index.html#page_1436"><i>createcachetable --dry-run</i></a> option.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Multiple databases</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you use database caching with multiple databases, you’ll also need to set up routing instructions for your database cache table. For the purposes of routing, the database cache table appears as a model named CacheEntry, in an application named django_cache. This model won’t appear in the models cache, but the model details can be used for routing purposes.</p> <p>For example, the following router would direct all cache read operations to cache_replica, and all write operations to cache_primary. The cache table will only be synchronized onto cache_primary:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>CacheRouter</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"""A router to control all database cache operations"""</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>db_for_read</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, model,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">hints):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"All cache read operations go to the replica"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">model</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">_meta</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">app_label</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django_cache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"cache_replica"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return None</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>db_for_write</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, model,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">hints):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"All cache write operations go to primary"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">model</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">_meta</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">app_label</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django_cache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"cache_primary"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return None</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_605" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>allow_migrate</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, db, app_label, model_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=None</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">hints):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Only install the cache model on primary"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">app_label</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django_cache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"cache_primary"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return None</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you don’t specify routing directions for the database cache model, the cache backend will use the default database.</p> <p>And if you don’t use the database cache backend, you don’t need to worry about providing routing instruc-tions for the database cache model.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Filesystem caching</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The file-based backend serializes and stores each cache value as a separate file. To use this backend set</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1890"><i>BACKEND</i></a> to "django.core.cache.backends.filebased.FileBasedCache" and <a href="index.html#page_1891"><i>LOCATION</i></a> to a suitable di-rectory. For example, to store cached data in /var/tmp/django_cache, use this setting:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">CACHES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"BACKEND"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.cache.backends.filebased.FileBasedCache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"LOCATION"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"/var/tmp/django_cache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you’re on Windows, put the drive letter at the beginning of the path, like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">CACHES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"BACKEND"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.cache.backends.filebased.FileBasedCache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"LOCATION"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"c:/foo/bar"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The directory path should be absolute – that is, it should start at the root of your filesystem. It doesn’t matter whether you put a slash at the end of the setting.</p> <p>Make sure the directory pointed-to by this setting either exists and is readable and writable, or that it can be created by the system user under which your web server runs. Continuing the above example, if your server runs as the user apache, make sure the directory /var/tmp/django_cache exists and is readable and writable by the user apache, or that it can be created by the user apache.</p> <p id="page_606"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: When the cache <a href="index.html#page_1891"><i>LOCATION</i></a> is contained within <a href="index.html#page_1922"><i>MEDIA_ROOT</i></a> , <a href="index.html#page_1945"><i>STATIC_ROOT</i></a> , or</p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_1947"><i>STATICFILES_FINDERS</i></a> , sensitive data may be exposed.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">An attacker who gains access to the cache file can not only falsify HTML content, which your site will</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">trust, but also remotely execute arbitrary code, as the data is serialized using <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/pickle.html#module-pickle">pickle</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: Filesystem caching may become slow when storing a large number of files. If you run into</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">this problem, consider using a different caching mechanism. You can also subclass <a href="https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/core/cache/backends/filebased.py">FileBasedCache</a> and</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">improve the culling strategy.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Local-memory caching</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This is the default cache if another is not specified in your settings file. If you want the speed advantages of in-memory caching but don’t have the capability of running Memcached, consider the local-memory cache</p> <p>backend. This cache is per-process (see below) and thread-safe. To use it, set <a href="index.html#page_1890"><i>BACKEND</i></a> to "django.core. cache.backends.locmem.LocMemCache". For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">CACHES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"BACKEND"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.cache.backends.locmem.LocMemCache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"LOCATION"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"unique-snowflake"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The cache <a href="index.html#page_1891"><i>LOCATION</i></a> is used to identify individual memory stores. If you only have one locmem cache, you</p> <p>can omit the <a href="index.html#page_1891"><i>LOCATION</i></a> ; however, if you have more than one local memory cache, you will need to assign a name to at least one of them in order to keep them separate.</p> <p>The cache uses a least-recently-used (LRU) culling strategy.</p> <p>Note that each process will have its own private cache instance, which means no cross-process caching is possible. This also means the local memory cache isn’t particularly memory-efficient, so it’s probably not a good choice for production environments. It’s nice for development.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_607" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Dummy caching (for development)</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Finally, Django comes with a “dummy” cache that doesn’t actually cache – it just implements the cache interface without doing anything.</p> <p>This is useful if you have a production site that uses heavy-duty caching in various places but a devel-opment/test environment where you don’t want to cache and don’t want to have to change your code to</p> <p>special-case the latter. To activate dummy caching, set <a href="index.html#page_1890"><i>BACKEND</i></a> like so:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">CACHES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"BACKEND"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.cache.backends.dummy.DummyCache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using a custom cache backend</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>While Django includes support for a number of cache backends out-of-the-box, sometimes you might want to use a customized cache backend. To use an external cache backend with Django, use the Python import</p> <p>path as the <a href="index.html#page_1890"><i>BACKEND</i></a> of the <a href="index.html#page_1889"><i>CACHES</i></a> setting, like so:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">CACHES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"BACKEND"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"path.to.backend"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you’re building your own backend, you can use the standard cache backends as reference implementations.</p> <p>You’ll find the code in the <a href="https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/core/cache/backends/">django/core/cache/backends/</a> directory of the Django source.</p> <p>Note: Without a really compelling reason, such as a host that doesn’t support them, you should stick to the cache backends included with Django. They’ve been well-tested and are well-documented.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Cache arguments</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Each cache backend can be given additional arguments to control caching behavior. These arguments are</p> <p>provided as additional keys in the <a href="index.html#page_1889"><i>CACHES</i></a> setting. Valid arguments are as follows:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1891"><i>TIMEOUT</i></a> : The default timeout, in seconds, to use for the cache. This argument defaults to 300 seconds</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">(5 minutes). You can set TIMEOUT to None so that, by default, cache keys never expire. A value of 0 causes keys to immediately expire (effectively “don’t cache”).</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1891"><i>OPTIONS</i></a>: Any options that should be passed to the cache backend. The list of valid options will vary</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">with each backend, and cache backends backed by a third-party library will pass their options directly to the underlying cache library.</p> <p id="page_608"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Cache backends that implement their own culling strategy (i.e., the locmem, filesystem and database backends) will honor the following options:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– MAX_ENTRIES: The maximum number of entries allowed in the cache before old values are deleted.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">This argument defaults to 300.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– CULL_FREQUENCY: The fraction of entries that are culled when MAX_ENTRIES is reached. The</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">actual ratio is 1 / CULL_FREQUENCY, so set CULL_FREQUENCY to 2 to cull half the entries when MAX_ENTRIES is reached. This argument should be an integer and defaults to 3.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A value of 0 for CULL_FREQUENCY means that the entire cache will be dumped when MAX_ENTRIES is reached. On some backends (database in particular) this makes culling much faster at the expense of more cache misses.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The Memcached and Redis backends pass the contents of <a href="index.html#page_1891"><i>OPTIONS</i></a> as keyword arguments to the client constructors, allowing for more advanced control of client behavior. For example usage, see below.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1890"><i>KEY_PREFIX</i></a> : A string that will be automatically included (prepended by default) to all cache keys used</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">by the Django server.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">See the <a href="index.html#page_618">cache documentation</a> for more information.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1891"><i>VERSION</i></a> : The default version number for cache keys generated by the Django server.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">See the <a href="index.html#page_619">cache documentation</a> for more information.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1890"><i>KEY_FUNCTION</i></a> A string containing a dotted path to a function that defines how to compose a prefix,</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">version and key into a final cache key.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">See the <a href="index.html#page_620">cache documentation</a> for more information.</p> <p>In this example, a filesystem backend is being configured with a timeout of 60 seconds, and a maximum capacity of 1000 items:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">CACHES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"BACKEND"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.cache.backends.filebased.FileBasedCache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"LOCATION"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"/var/tmp/django_cache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"TIMEOUT"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">60</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"OPTIONS"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"MAX_ENTRIES"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">1000</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Here’s an example configuration for a pylibmc based backend that enables the binary protocol, SASL au-thentication, and the ketama behavior mode:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">CACHES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"BACKEND"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.cache.backends.memcached.PyLibMCCache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_609" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"LOCATION"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"127.0.0.1:11211"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"OPTIONS"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"binary"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"username"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"user"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"behaviors"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"ketama"</span><span <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Here’s an example configuration for a pymemcache based backend that enables client pooling (which may improve performance by keeping clients connected), treats memcache/network errors as cache misses, and sets the TCP_NODELAY flag on the connection’s socket:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">CACHES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"max_pool_size"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">4</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"use_pooling"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Here’s an example configuration for a redis based backend that selects database 10 (by default Redis ships</p> <p>with 16 logical databases), and sets a custom <a href="https://github.com/redis/redis-py#connection-pools">connection pool class</a> (redis.ConnectionPool is used by de-fault):</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">CACHES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.cache.backends.redis.RedisCache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"LOCATION"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"redis://127.0.0.1:6379"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"OPTIONS"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"db"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"10"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"pool_class"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"redis.BlockingConnectionPool"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p id="page_610"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.11.2 The per-site cache</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Once the cache is set up, the simplest way to use caching is to cache your entire site. <span style="float:right">You’ll</span></p> <p>need to add 'django.middleware.cache.UpdateCacheMiddleware' and 'django.middleware.cache.</p> <p>FetchFromCacheMiddleware' to your <a href="index.html#page_1923"><i>MIDDLEWARE</i></a> setting, as in this example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">MIDDLEWARE</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.middleware.cache.UpdateCacheMiddleware"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.middleware.common.CommonMiddleware"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.middleware.cache.FetchFromCacheMiddleware"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: No, that’s not a typo: the “update” middleware must be first in the list, and the “fetch” middleware</p> <p>must be last. The details are a bit obscure, but see <a href="index.html#page_625">Order of MIDDLEWARE</a> below if you’d like the full story.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Then, add the following required settings to your Django settings file:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1892"><i>CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_ALIAS</i></a> – The cache alias to use for storage.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1892"><i>CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_SECONDS</i></a> – The integer number of seconds each page should be cached.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1892"><i>CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_KEY_PREFIX</i></a> – If the cache is shared across multiple sites using the same Django</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">installation, set this to the name of the site, or some other string that is unique to this Django instance, to prevent key collisions. Use an empty string if you don’t care.</p> <p>FetchFromCacheMiddleware caches GET and HEAD responses with status 200, where the request and re-sponse headers allow. Responses to requests for the same URL with different query parameters are consid-ered to be unique pages and are cached separately. This middleware expects that a HEAD request is answered with the same response headers as the corresponding GET request; in which case it can return a cached GET response for HEAD request.</p> <p>Additionally, UpdateCacheMiddleware automatically sets a few headers in each <a href="index.html#page_1871"><i>HttpResponse</i></a> which affect</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_621">downstream caches:</a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Sets the Expires header to the current date/time plus the defined <a href="index.html#page_1892"><i>CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_SECONDS</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Sets the Cache-Control header to give a max age for the page – again, from the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1892"><i>CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_SECONDS</i></a> setting.</p> <p>See <a href="index.html#page_303">Middleware</a> for more on middleware.</p> <p>If a view sets its own cache expiry time (i.e. it has a max-age section in its Cache-Control header) then the</p> <p>page will be cached until the expiry time, rather than <a href="index.html#page_1892"><i>CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_SECONDS</i></a> . Using the decorators</p> <p>in django.views.decorators.cache you can easily set a view’s expiry time (using the <a href="index.html#page_289"><i>cache_control()</i></a></p> <p>decorator) or disable caching for a view (using the <a href="index.html#page_289"><i>never_cache()</i></a> decorator). See the <a href="index.html#page_623">using other headers</a> section for more on these decorators.</p> <p id="page_611" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If <a href="index.html#page_1936"><i>USE_I18N</i></a> is set to True then the generated cache key will include the name of the active <a href="index.html#page_706">language</a> – see</p> <p>also <a href="index.html#page_686">How Django discovers language preference</a>). This allows you to easily cache multilingual sites without having to create the cache key yourself.</p> <p>Cache keys also include the <a href="index.html#page_695">current time zone</a> when <a href="index.html#page_1936"><i>USE_TZ</i></a> is set to True.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.11.3 The per-view cache</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>django.views.decorators.cache.<b>cache_page</b>(timeout, *, cache=None, key_prefix=None)</p> <p>A more granular way to use the caching framework is by caching the output of individual views. django. views.decorators.cache defines a cache_page decorator that will automatically cache the view’s response for you:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.views.decorators.cache</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">cache_page</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@cache_page(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">60</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>*</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">15</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>cache_page takes a single argument: the cache timeout, in seconds. In the above example, the result of the my_view() view will be cached for 15 minutes. (Note that we’ve written it as 60 * 15 for the purpose of readability. 60 * 15 will be evaluated to 900 – that is, 15 minutes multiplied by 60 seconds per minute.)</p> <p>The cache timeout set by cache_page takes precedence over the max-age directive from the Cache-Control header.</p> <p>The per-view cache, like the per-site cache, is keyed off of the URL. If multiple URLs point at the same view, each URL will be cached separately. Continuing the my_view example, if your URLconf looks like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"foo/<int:code>/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, my_view),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>then requests to /foo/1/ and /foo/23/ will be cached separately, as you may expect. But once a particular URL (e.g., /foo/23/) has been requested, subsequent requests to that URL will use the cache.</p> <p>cache_page can also take an optional keyword argument, cache, which directs the decorator to use a specific</p> <p>cache (from your <a href="index.html#page_1889"><i>CACHES</i></a> setting) when caching view results. By default, the default cache will be used, but you can specify any cache you want:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@cache_page(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">60</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>*</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">15</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, cache</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"special_cache"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can also override the cache prefix on a per-view basis. cache_page takes an optional keyword argument, <b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p id="page_612">key_prefix, which works in the same way as the <a href="index.html#page_1892"><i>CACHE_MIDDLEWARE_KEY_PREFIX</i></a> setting for the middle-ware. It can be used like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@cache_page(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">60</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>*</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">15</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, key_prefix</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"site1"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The key_prefix and cache arguments may be specified together. The key_prefix argument and the</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1890"><i>KEY_PREFIX</i></a> specified under <a href="index.html#page_1889"><i>CACHES</i></a> will be concatenated.</p> <p>Additionally, cache_page automatically sets Cache-Control and Expires headers in the response which</p> <p>affect <a href="index.html#page_621">downstream caches.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Specifying per-view cache in the URLconf</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The examples in the previous section have hard-coded the fact that the view is cached, because cache_page alters the my_view function in place. This approach couples your view to the cache system, which is not ideal for several reasons. For instance, you might want to reuse the view functions on another, cache-less site, or you might want to distribute the views to people who might want to use them without being cached. The solution to these problems is to specify the per-view cache in the URLconf rather than next to the view functions themselves.</p> <p>You can do so by wrapping the view function with cache_page when you refer to it in the URLconf. Here’s the old URLconf from earlier:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"foo/<int:code>/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, my_view),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Here’s the same thing, with my_view wrapped in cache_page:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.views.decorators.cache</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">cache_page</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"foo/<int:code>/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, cache_page(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">60</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>*</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">15</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)(my_view)),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.11.4 Template fragment caching</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you’re after even more control, you can also cache template fragments using the cache template tag. To give your template access to this tag, put {% load cache %} near the top of your template.</p> <p>The {% cache %} template tag caches the contents of the block for a given amount of time. It takes at least two arguments: the cache timeout, in seconds, and the name to give the cache fragment. The fragment is cached forever if timeout is None. The name will be taken as is, do not use a variable. For example:</p> <p id="page_613" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">cache</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>cache</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">500</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">sidebar</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">.. sidebar ..</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endcache</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Sometimes you might want to cache multiple copies of a fragment depending on some dynamic data that appears inside the fragment. For example, you might want a separate cached copy of the sidebar used in the previous example for every user of your site. Do this by passing one or more additional arguments, which may be variables with or without filters, to the {% cache %} template tag to uniquely identify the cache fragment:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">cache</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>cache</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">500</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">sidebar request.user.username</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">.. sidebar for logged in user ..</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endcache</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If <a href="index.html#page_1936"><i>USE_I18N</i></a> is set to True the per-site middleware cache will <a href="index.html#page_610">respect the active language</a>. For the cache</p> <p>template tag you could use one of the <a href="index.html#page_666">translation-specific variables</a> available in templates to achieve the same result:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">i18n</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">cache</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get_current_language as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">LANGUAGE_CODE</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>cache</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">600</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">welcome LANGUAGE_CODE</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>translate</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Welcome to example.com"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endcache</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The cache timeout can be a template variable, as long as the template variable resolves to an integer value. For example, if the template variable my_timeout is set to the value 600, then the following two examples are equivalent:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>cache</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">600</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">sidebar</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endcache</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>cache</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">my_timeout sidebar</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endcache</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This feature is useful in avoiding repetition in templates. You can set the timeout in a variable, in one place, and reuse that value.</p> <p>By default, the cache tag will try to use the cache called “template_fragments”. If no such cache exists, it will fall back to using the default cache. You may select an alternate cache backend to use with the using keyword argument, which must be the last argument to the tag.</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>cache</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">300</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">local-thing</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">using</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"localcache"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p id="page_614"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>It is considered an error to specify a cache name that is not configured.</p> <p>django.core.cache.utils.<b>make_template_fragment_key</b>(fragment_name, vary_on=None)</p> <p>If you want to obtain the cache key used for a cached fragment, you can use make_template_fragment_key. fragment_name is the same as second argument to the cache template tag; vary_on is a list of all additional arguments passed to the tag. This function can be useful for invalidating or overwriting a cached item, for example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.core.cache</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">cache</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.core.cache.utils</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">make_template_fragment_key</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"># cache key for {% cache 500 sidebar username %}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">key</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">make_template_fragment_key(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"sidebar"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, [username])</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">cache</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">delete(key)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># invalidates cached template fragment</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">True</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.11.5 The low-level cache API</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Sometimes, caching an entire rendered page doesn’t gain you very much and is, in fact, inconvenient overkill.</p> <p>Perhaps, for instance, your site includes a view whose results depend on several expensive queries, the results of which change at different intervals. In this case, it would not be ideal to use the full-page caching that the per-site or per-view cache strategies offer, because you wouldn’t want to cache the entire result (since some of the data changes often), but you’d still want to cache the results that rarely change.</p> <p>For cases like this, Django exposes a low-level cache API. You can use this API to store objects in the cache with any level of granularity you like. You can cache any Python object that can be pickled safely: strings, dictionaries, lists of model objects, and so forth. (Most common Python objects can be pickled; refer to the Python documentation for more information about pickling.)</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Accessing the cache</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>django.core.cache.<b>caches</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">You can access the caches configured in the <a href="index.html#page_1889"><i>CACHES</i></a> setting through a dict-like object: django.core. cache.caches . Repeated requests for the same alias in the same thread will return the same object.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.core.cache</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">caches</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">cache1</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">caches[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"myalias"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">cache2</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">caches[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"myalias"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">cache1</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>is</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">cache2</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">True</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If the named key does not exist, InvalidCacheBackendError will be raised.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">To provide thread-safety, a different instance of the cache backend will be returned for each thread.</p> <p id="page_615" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>django.core.cache.<b>cache</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">As a shortcut, the default cache is available as django.core.cache.cache:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.core.cache</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">cache</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This object is equivalent to caches['default'].</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Basic usage</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The basic interface is:</p> <p>cache.<b>set</b>( key, value, timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT, version=None)</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">cache</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">set(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"my_key"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"hello, world!"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">30</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>cache.<b>get</b>( key, default=None, version=None)</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">cache</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"my_key"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">'hello, world!'</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>key should be a str, and value can be any picklable Python object.</p> <p>The timeout argument is optional and defaults to the timeout argument of the appropriate backend in the</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1889"><i>CACHES</i></a> setting (explained above). It’s the number of seconds the value should be stored in the cache. Passing in None for timeout will cache the value forever. A timeout of 0 won’t cache the value.</p> <p>If the object doesn’t exist in the cache, cache.get() returns None:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Wait 30 seconds for 'my_key' to expire...</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">cache</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"my_key"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">None</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you need to determine whether the object exists in the cache and you have stored a literal value None, use a sentinel object as the default:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">sentinel</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">object</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">cache</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"my_key"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, sentinel)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>is</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">sentinel</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">False</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Wait 30 seconds for 'my_key' to expire...</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">cache</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"my_key"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, sentinel)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>is</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">sentinel</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">True</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>cache.get() can take a default argument.
