style="font-size:0.87em">"my_variable"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">42</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Then, create a multipart email instance.</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">msg</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">EmailMultiAlternatives(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Subject here"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">text_content,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"from@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"to@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">headers</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"List-Unsubscribe"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"<mailto:unsub@example.com>"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Lastly, attach the HTML content to the email instance and send.</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">msg</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">attach_alternative(html_content,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"text/html"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">msg</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">send()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Mail is sent using the SMTP host and port specified in the <a href="index.html#page_1911"><i>EMAIL_HOST</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1911"><i>EMAIL_PORT</i></a> settings. The</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1911"><i>EMAIL_HOST_USER</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1911"><i>EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD</i></a> settings, if set, are used to authenticate to the SMTP server,</p> <p>and the <a href="index.html#page_1912"><i>EMAIL_USE_TLS</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1912"><i>EMAIL_USE_SSL</i></a> settings control whether a secure connection is used.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: The character set of email sent with django.core.mail will be set to the value of your</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1909"><i>DEFAULT_CHARSET</i></a> setting.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_636"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.14.2</b></span> <span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>send_mail()</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>send_mail</b>( subject, message, from_email, recipient_list, fail_silently=False, auth_user=None,</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">auth_password=None, connection=None, html_message=None)</p> <p>In most cases, you can send email using django.core.mail.send_mail().</p> <p>The subject, message, from_email and recipient_list parameters are required.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• subject: A string.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• message: A string.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• from_email: A string. If None, Django will use the value of the <a href="index.html#page_1910"><i>DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• recipient_list: A list of strings, each an email address. Each member of recipient_list will see</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">the other recipients in the “To:” field of the email message.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• fail_silently: A boolean. When it’s False, send_mail() will raise an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/smtplib.html#smtplib.SMTPException">smtplib.SMTPException</a> if</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">an error occurs. See the <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/smtplib.html#module-smtplib">smtplib</a> docs for a list of possible exceptions, all of which are subclasses of</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/smtplib.html#smtplib.SMTPException">SMTPException</a>.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• auth_user: The optional username to use to authenticate to the SMTP server. If this isn’t provided,</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Django will use the value of the <a href="index.html#page_1911"><i>EMAIL_HOST_USER</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• auth_password: The optional password to use to authenticate to the SMTP server. If this isn’t provided,</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Django will use the value of the <a href="index.html#page_1911"><i>EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• connection: The optional email backend to use to send the mail. If unspecified, an instance of the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">default backend will be used. See the documentation on <a href="index.html#page_644">Email backends</a> for more details.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• html_message: If html_message is provided, the resulting email will be a <i>multipart/alternative</i></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">email with message as the <i>text/plain</i> content type and html_message as the <i>text/html</i> content type.</p> <p>The return value will be the number of successfully delivered messages (which can be 0 or 1 since it can only send one message).</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.14.3</b></span> <span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>send_mass_mail()</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>send_mass_mail</b>(datatuple, fail_silently=False, auth_user=None, auth_password=None,</p> <p style="margin-left:6em">connection=None)</p> <p>django.core.mail.send_mass_mail() is intended to handle mass emailing.</p> <p>datatuple is a tuple in which each element is in this format:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">(subject, message, from_email, recipient_list)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>fail_silently, auth_user and auth_password have the same functions as in <a href="index.html#page_636"><i>send_mail()</i></a>.</p> <p id="page_637" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Each separate element of datatuple results in a separate email message. As in <a href="index.html#page_636"><i>send_mail()</i></a>, recipients in the same recipient_list will all see the other addresses in the email messages’ “To:” field.</p> <p>For example, the following code would send two different messages to two different sets of recipients; how-ever, only one connection to the mail server would be opened:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">message1</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Subject here"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Here is the message"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"from@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"first@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"other@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">message2</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Another Subject"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Here is another message"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"from@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"second@test.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">send_mass_mail((message1, message2), fail_silently</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=False</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The return value will be the number of successfully delivered messages.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>send_mass_mail() vs. send_mail()</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The main difference between <a href="index.html#page_636"><i>send_mass_mail()</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_636"><i>send_mail()</i></a> is that <a href="index.html#page_636"><i>send_mail()</i></a> opens a connection</p> <p>to the mail server each time it’s executed, while <a href="index.html#page_636"><i>send_mass_mail()</i></a> uses a single connection for all of its</p> <p>messages. This makes <a href="index.html#page_636"><i>send_mass_mail()</i></a> slightly more efficient.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.14.4</b></span> <span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>mail_admins()</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>mail_admins</b>(subject, message, fail_silently=False, connection=None, html_message=None)</p> <p>django.core.mail.mail_admins() is a shortcut for sending an email to the site admins, as defined in the</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1888"><i>ADMINS</i></a> setting.</p> <p>mail_admins() prefixes the subject with the value of the <a href="index.html#page_1912"><i>EMAIL_SUBJECT_PREFIX</i></a> setting, which is "[Django] " by default.</p> <p>The “From:” header of the email will be the value of the <a href="index.html#page_1930"><i>SERVER_EMAIL</i></a> setting.</p> <p>This method exists for convenience and readability.</p> <p>If html_message is provided, the resulting email will be a <i>multipart/alternative</i> email with message as the <i>text/plain</i> content type and html_message as the <i>text/html</i> content type.</p> <p id="page_638"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.14.5</b></span> <span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>mail_managers()</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>mail_managers</b>(subject, message, fail_silently=False, connection=None, html_message=None)</p> <p>django.core.mail.mail_managers() is just like mail_admins(), except it sends an email to the site man-</p> <p>agers, as defined in the <a href="index.html#page_1922"><i>MANAGERS</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.14.6 Examples</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This sends a single email to <a href="mailto:john@example.com">john@example.com</a> and <a href="mailto:jane@example.com">jane@example.com</a>, with them both appearing in the “To:”:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">send_mail(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Subject"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Message."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"from@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"john@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"jane@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This sends a message to <a href="mailto:john@example.com">john@example.com</a> and <a href="mailto:jane@example.com">jane@example.com</a><a href="mailto:jane@example.com">, </a>with them both receiving a separate email:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">datatuple</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Subject"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Message."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"from@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"john@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]),</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Subject"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Message."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"from@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"jane@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">send_mass_mail(datatuple)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.14.7 Preventing header injection</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><a href="http://www.nyphp.org/phundamentals/8_Preventing-Email-Header-Injection.html">Header injection</a> is a security exploit in which an attacker inserts extra email headers to control the “To:” and “From:” in email messages that your scripts generate.</p> <p>The Django email functions outlined above all protect against header injection by forbidding newlines in header values. If any subject, from_email or recipient_list contains a newline (in either Unix, Windows</p> <p>or Mac style), the email function (e.g. <a href="index.html#page_636"><i>send_mail()</i>) </a>will raise django.core.mail.BadHeaderError (a sub-class of ValueError) and, hence, will not send the email. It’s your responsibility to validate all data before passing it to the email functions.</p> <p>If a message contains headers at the start of the string, the headers will be printed as the first bit of the email message.</p> <p>Here’s an example view that takes a subject, message and from_email from the request’s POST data, sends</p> <p>that to <a href="mailto:admin@example.com">admin@example.com</a> and redirects to “/contact/thanks/” when it’s done:</p> <p id="page_639" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.core.mail</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">BadHeaderError, send_mail</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.http</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse, HttpResponseRedirect</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>send_email</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">subject</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">POST</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"subject"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">""</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">message</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">POST</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"message"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">""</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">from_email</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">POST</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"from_email"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">""</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">subject</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>and</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">message</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>and</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">from_email:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>try</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">send_mail(subject, message, from_email, [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"admin@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">])</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>except</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">BadHeaderError:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Invalid header found."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponseRedirect(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/contact/thanks/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>else</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># In reality we'd use a form class</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># to get proper validation errors.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Make sure all fields are entered and valid."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.14.8 The</b></span> <span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>EmailMessage</b></span> <span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>class</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django’s <a href="index.html#page_636"><i>send_mail()</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_636"><i>send_mass_mail()</i></a> functions are actually thin wrappers that make use of the</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_640"><i>EmailMessage</i></a> class.</p> <p>Not all features of the <a href="index.html#page_640"><i>EmailMessage</i></a> class are available through the <a href="index.html#page_636"><i>send_mail()</i></a> and related wrapper func-tions. If you wish to use advanced features, such as BCC’ed recipients, file attachments, or multi-part email,</p> <p>you’ll need to create <a href="index.html#page_640"><i>EmailMessage</i></a> instances directly.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: This is a design feature. <a href="index.html#page_636"><i>send_mail()</i></a> and related functions were originally the only interface Django provided. However, the list of parameters they accepted was slowly growing over time. It made sense to move to a more object-oriented design for email messages and retain the original functions only for backwards compatibility.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><a href="index.html#page_640"><i>EmailMessage</i></a> is responsible for creating the email message itself. The <a href="index.html#page_644">email backend</a> is then responsible for sending the email.</p> <p>For convenience, <a href="index.html#page_640"><i>EmailMessage</i></a> provides a send() method for sending a single email. If you need to send</p> <p>multiple messages, the email backend API <a href="index.html#page_647">provides an alternative</a>.</p> <p id="page_640"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>EmailMessage Objects</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class EmailMessage</b></p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_640"><i>EmailMessage</i></a> class is initialized with the following parameters (in the given order, if positional argu-ments are used). All parameters are optional and can be set at any time prior to calling the send() method.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• subject: The subject line of the email.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• body: The body text. This should be a plain text message.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• from_email: The sender’s address. Both fred@example.com and "Fred" <fred@example.com> forms</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">are legal. If omitted, the <a href="index.html#page_1910"><i>DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL</i></a> setting is used.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• to: A list or tuple of recipient addresses.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• bcc: A list or tuple of addresses used in the “Bcc” header when sending the email.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• connection: An <a href="index.html#page_644">email backend</a> instance. Use this parameter if you are sending the EmailMessage via</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">send() and you want to use the same connection for multiple messages. If omitted, a new connection</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">is created when send() is called. This parameter is ignored when using <a href="index.html#page_647">send_messages().</a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• attachments: A list of attachments to put on the message. These can be instances of <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/email.mime.html#email.mime.base.MIMEBase">MIMEBase</a> or</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_642"><i>EmailAttachment</i></a>, or a tuple with attributes (filename, content, mimetype).</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Support for <a href="index.html#page_642"><i>EmailAttachment</i></a> items of attachments were added.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• headers: A dictionary of extra headers to put on the message. The keys are the header name, values</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">are the header values. It’s up to the caller to ensure header names and values are in the correct format for an email message. The corresponding attribute is extra_headers.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• cc: A list or tuple of recipient addresses used in the “Cc” header when sending the email.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• reply_to: A list or tuple of recipient addresses used in the “Reply-To” header when sending the email.</p> <p>For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.core.mail</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">EmailMessage</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">email</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">EmailMessage(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Hello"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Body goes here"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"from@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"to1@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"to2@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"bcc@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">reply_to</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"another@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">headers</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Message-ID"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"foo"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The class has the following methods:</p> <p id="page_641" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• send(fail_silently=False) sends the message. If a connection was specified when the email was</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">constructed, that connection will be used. Otherwise, an instance of the default backend will be instan-tiated and used. If the keyword argument fail_silently is True, exceptions raised while sending the message will be quashed. An empty list of recipients will not raise an exception. It will return 1 if the message was sent successfully, otherwise 0.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• message() constructs a django.core.mail.SafeMIMEText object (a subclass of Python’s <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/email.mime.html#email.mime.text.MIMEText">MIMEText</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">class) or a django.core.mail.SafeMIMEMultipart object holding the message to be sent. If you ever</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">need to extend the <a href="index.html#page_640"><i>EmailMessage</i></a> class, you’ll probably want to override this method to put the content you want into the MIME object.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• recipients() returns a list of all the recipients of the message, whether they’re recorded in the to, cc</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">or bcc attributes. This is another method you might need to override when subclassing, because the SMTP server needs to be told the full list of recipients when the message is sent. If you add another way to specify recipients in your class, they need to be returned from this method as well.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• attach() creates a new file attachment and adds it to the message. There are two ways to call attach():</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– You can pass it a single argument that is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/email.mime.html#email.mime.base.MIMEBase">MIMEBase</a> instance. This will be inserted directly into</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">the resulting message.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– Alternatively, you can pass attach() three arguments: filename, content and mimetype.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">filename is the name of the file attachment as it will appear in the email, content is the data that will be contained inside the attachment and mimetype is the optional MIME type for the at-tachment. If you omit mimetype, the MIME content type will be guessed from the filename of the attachment.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">message</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">attach(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"design.png"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, img_data,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"image/png"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If you specify a mimetype of <i>message/rfc822</i>, it will also accept <a href="index.html#page_640"><i>django.core.mail.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_640"><i>EmailMessage</i></a> and <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/email.compat32-message.html#email.message.Message">email.message.Message</a><a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/email.compat32-message.html#email.message.Message">.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">For a mimetype starting with <i>text/</i>, content is expected to be a string. Binary data will be decoded using UTF-8, and if that fails, the MIME type will be changed to <i>application/octet-stream</i> and the data will be attached unchanged.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">In addition, <i>message/rfc822</i> attachments will no longer be base64-encoded in violation of <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2046.html#section-5.2.1">RFC</a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2046.html#section-5.2.1">2046#section-5.2.1, </a>which can cause issues with displaying the attachments in <a href="https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=651197">Evolution</a> and</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=333880">Thunderbird.</a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• attach_file() creates a new attachment using a file from your filesystem. Call it with the path of the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">file to attach and, optionally, the MIME type to use for the attachment. If the MIME type is omitted, it will be guessed from the filename. You can use it like this:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">message</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">attach_file(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/images/weather_map.png"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p id="page_642"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For MIME types starting with <i>text/</i>, binary data is handled as in attach().</p> <p><b>class EmailAttachment</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A named tuple to store attachments to an email.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The named tuple has the following indexes:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• filename</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• content</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• mimetype</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Sending alternative content types</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Sending multiple content versions</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>It can be useful to include multiple versions of the content in an email; the classic example is to send both text and HTML versions of a message. With Django’s email library, you can do this using the</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_642"><i>EmailMultiAlternatives</i></a> class.</p> <p><b>class EmailMultiAlternatives</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A subclass of <a href="index.html#page_640"><i>EmailMessage</i></a> that allows additional versions of the message body in the email via the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_642"><i>attach_alternative()</i></a> method. This directly inherits all methods (including the class initialization)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">from <a href="index.html#page_640"><i>EmailMessage</i>.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>alternatives</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A list of <a href="index.html#page_643"><i>EmailAlternative</i></a> named tuples. This is particularly useful in tests:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertEqual(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">len</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(msg</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">alternatives),</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertEqual(msg</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">alternatives[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">0</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">content, html_content)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertEqual(msg</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">alternatives[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">0</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">mimetype,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"text/html"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Alternatives should only be added using the <a href="index.html#page_642"><i>attach_alternative()</i></a> method, or passed to the constructor.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">In older versions, alternatives was a list of regular tuples, as opposed to <a href="index.html#page_643"><i>EmailAlternative</i></a> named tuples.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>attach_alternative</b>( content, mimetype)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Attach an alternative representation of the message body in the email.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">For example, to send a text and HTML combination, you could write:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.core.mail</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">EmailMultiAlternatives</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">subject</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"hello"</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_643" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">from_email</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"from@example.com"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">to</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"<p>This is an <strong>important</strong> message.</p>"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">msg</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">EmailMultiAlternatives(subject, text_content, from_email, [to])</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">msg</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">attach_alternative(html_content,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"text/html"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">msg</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">send()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>body_contains</b>(text)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns a boolean indicating whether the provided text is contained in the email body and in all attached MIME type text/* alternatives.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">This can be useful when testing emails. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>test_contains_email_content</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">subject</span> <span
