style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertIs(msg</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">body_contains(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"I am content"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertIs(msg</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">body_contains(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"<p>I am content.</p>"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>False</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class EmailAlternative</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A named tuple to store alternative versions of email content.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The named tuple has the following indexes:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• content</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• mimetype</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Updating the default content type</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>By default, the MIME type of the body parameter in an <a href="index.html#page_640"><i>EmailMessage</i></a> is "text/plain". It is good practice to leave this alone, because it guarantees that any recipient will be able to read the email, regardless of their mail client. However, if you are confident that your recipients can handle an alternative content type, you</p> <p>can use the content_subtype attribute on the <a href="index.html#page_640"><i>EmailMessage</i></a> class to change the main content type. The major type will always be "text", but you can change the subtype. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">msg</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">EmailMessage(subject, html_content, from_email, [to])</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">msg</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">content_subtype</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"html"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Main content is now text/html</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">msg</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">send()</span></p> <p id="page_644"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.14.9 Email backends</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The actual sending of an email is handled by the email backend.</p> <p>The email backend class has the following methods:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• open() instantiates a long-lived email-sending connection.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• close() closes the current email-sending connection.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• send_messages(email_messages) sends a list of <a href="index.html#page_640"><i>EmailMessage</i></a> objects. If the connection is not open,</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">this call will implicitly open the connection, and close the connection afterward. If the connection is already open, it will be left open after mail has been sent.</p> <p>It can also be used as a context manager, which will automatically call open() and close() as needed:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.core</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">mail</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>with</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">mail</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_connection()</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">connection:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">mail</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">EmailMessage(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">subject1,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">body1,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">from1,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">[to1],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">connection</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">connection,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">send()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">mail</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">EmailMessage(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">subject2,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">body2,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">from2,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">[to2],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">connection</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">connection,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">send()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Obtaining an instance of an email backend</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_644"><i>get_connection()</i></a> function in django.core.mail returns an instance of the email backend that you can use.</p> <p><b>get_connection</b>(backend=None, fail_silently=False, *args, **kwargs)</p> <p>By default, a call to get_connection() will return an instance of the email backend specified in</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1911"><i>EMAIL_BACKEND</i></a> . If you specify the backend argument, an instance of that backend will be instantiated.</p> <p>The fail_silently argument controls how the backend should handle errors. If fail_silently is True, exceptions during the email sending process will be silently ignored.</p> <p>All other arguments are passed directly to the constructor of the email backend.</p> <p id="page_645" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django ships with several email sending backends. With the exception of the SMTP backend (which is the default), these backends are only useful during testing and development. If you have special email sending</p> <p>requirements, you can <a href="index.html#page_647">write your own email backend</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>SMTP backend</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> backends.smtp.<b>EmailBackend</b>(host=None, port=None, username=None, password=None,</p> <p style="text-align:right">use_tls=None, fail_silently=False, use_ssl=None, timeout=None, ssl_keyfile=None, ssl_certfile=None, **kwargs)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This is the default backend. Email will be sent through a SMTP server.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The value for each argument is retrieved from the matching setting if the argument is None:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• host: <a href="index.html#page_1911"><i>EMAIL_HOST</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• port: <a href="index.html#page_1911"><i>EMAIL_PORT</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• username: <a href="index.html#page_1911"><i>EMAIL_HOST_USER</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• password: <a href="index.html#page_1911"><i>EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• use_tls: <a href="index.html#page_1912"><i>EMAIL_USE_TLS</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• use_ssl: <a href="index.html#page_1912"><i>EMAIL_USE_SSL</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• timeout: <a href="index.html#page_1913"><i>EMAIL_TIMEOUT</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• ssl_keyfile: <a href="index.html#page_1913"><i>EMAIL_SSL_KEYFILE</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• ssl_certfile: <a href="index.html#page_1912"><i>EMAIL_SSL_CERTFILE</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The SMTP backend is the default configuration inherited by Django. If you want to specify it explicitly, put the following in your settings:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">EMAIL_BACKEND</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.mail.backends.smtp.EmailBackend"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If unspecified, the default timeout will be the one provided by <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/socket.html#socket.getdefaulttimeout">socket.getdefaulttimeout(), </a>which defaults to None (no timeout).</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Console backend</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Instead of sending out real emails the console backend just writes the emails that would be sent to the stan-dard output. By default, the console backend writes to stdout. You can use a different stream-like object by providing the stream keyword argument when constructing the connection.</p> <p>To specify this backend, put the following in your settings:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">EMAIL_BACKEND</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.mail.backends.console.EmailBackend"</span></p> <p id="page_646"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This backend is not intended for use in production – it is provided as a convenience that can be used during development.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>File backend</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The file backend writes emails to a file. A new file is created for each new session that is opened on this</p> <p>backend. The directory to which the files are written is either taken from the <a href="index.html#page_1911"><i>EMAIL_FILE_PATH</i></a> setting or</p> <p>from the file_path keyword when creating a connection with <a href="index.html#page_644"><i>get_connection()</i></a>.</p> <p>To specify this backend, put the following in your settings:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">EMAIL_BACKEND</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.mail.backends.filebased.EmailBackend"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">EMAIL_FILE_PATH</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"/tmp/app-messages"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># change this to a proper location</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This backend is not intended for use in production – it is provided as a convenience that can be used during development.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>In-memory backend</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The 'locmem' backend stores messages in a special attribute of the django.core.mail module. The outbox</p> <p>attribute is created when the first message is sent. It’s a list with an <a href="index.html#page_640"><i>EmailMessage</i></a> instance for each message that would be sent.</p> <p>To specify this backend, put the following in your settings:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">EMAIL_BACKEND</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.mail.backends.locmem.EmailBackend"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This backend is not intended for use in production – it is provided as a convenience that can be used during development and testing.</p> <p>Django’s test runner <a href="index.html#page_512">automatically uses this backend for testing.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Dummy backend</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>As the name suggests the dummy backend does nothing with your messages. To specify this backend, put the following in your settings:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">EMAIL_BACKEND</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.core.mail.backends.dummy.EmailBackend"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This backend is not intended for use in production – it is provided as a convenience that can be used during development.</p> <p id="page_647" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Defining a custom email backend</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you need to change how emails are sent you can write your own email backend. The <a href="index.html#page_1911"><i>EMAIL_BACKEND</i></a> setting in your settings file is then the Python import path for your backend class.</p> <p>Custom email backends should subclass BaseEmailBackend that is located in the django.core.mail. backends.base module. A custom email backend must implement the send_messages(email_messages)</p> <p>method. This method receives a list of <a href="index.html#page_640"><i>EmailMessage</i></a> instances and returns the number of successfully de-livered messages. If your backend has any concept of a persistent session or connection, you should also implement the open() and close() methods. Refer to smtp.EmailBackend for a reference implementation.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Sending multiple emails</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Establishing and closing an SMTP connection (or any other network connection, for that matter) is an ex-pensive process. If you have a lot of emails to send, it makes sense to reuse an SMTP connection, rather than creating and destroying a connection every time you want to send an email.</p> <p>There are two ways you tell an email backend to reuse a connection.</p> <p>Firstly, you can use the send_messages() method on a connection. This takes a list of <a href="index.html#page_640"><i>EmailMessage</i></a> (or</p> <p>subclass) instances, and sends them all using that single connection. As a consequence, any <a href="index.html#page_640"><i>connection</i></a> set on an individual message is ignored.</p> <p>For example, if you have a function called get_notification_email() that returns a list of <a href="index.html#page_640"><i>EmailMessage</i></a> objects representing some periodic email you wish to send out, you could send these emails using a single call to send_messages:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.core</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">mail</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">connection</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">mail</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_connection()</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Use default email connection</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">get_notification_email()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">connection</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">send_messages(messages)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>In this example, the call to send_messages() opens a connection on the backend, sends the list of messages, and then closes the connection again.</p> <p>The second approach is to use the open() and close() methods on the email backend to manually control the connection. send_messages() will not manually open or close the connection if it is already open, so if you manually open the connection, you can control when it is closed. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.core</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">mail</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">connection</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">mail</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_connection()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Manually open the connection</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">connection</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">open()</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_648"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Construct an email message that uses the connection</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">email1</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">mail</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">EmailMessage(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Hello"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Body goes here"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"from@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"to1@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">connection</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">connection,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">email1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">send()</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Send the email</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Construct two more messages</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">email2</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">mail</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">EmailMessage(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Hello"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Body goes here"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"from@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"to2@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">email3</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">mail</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">EmailMessage(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Hello"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Body goes here"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"from@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"to3@example.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Send the two emails in a single call -</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">connection</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">send_messages([email2, email3])</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># The connection was already open so send_messages() doesn't close it.</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># We need to manually close the connection.</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">connection</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">close()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.14.10 Configuring email for development</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>There are times when you do not want Django to send emails at all. For example, while developing a website, you probably don’t want to send out thousands of emails – but you may want to validate that emails will be sent to the right people under the right conditions, and that those emails will contain the correct content.</p> <p>The easiest way to configure email for local development is to use the <a href="index.html#page_645">console</a> email backend. This backend redirects all email to stdout, allowing you to inspect the content of mail.</p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_646">file</a> email backend can also be useful during development – this backend dumps the contents of every SMTP connection to a file that can be inspected at your leisure.</p> <p>Another approach is to use a “dumb” SMTP server that receives the emails locally and displays them to the</p> <p id="page_649" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>terminal, but does not actually send anything. The <a href="https://pypi.org/project/aiosmtpd/">aiosmtpd</a> package provides a way to accomplish this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">python -m pip install aiosmtpd</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">python -m aiosmtpd -n -l localhost:8025</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This command will start a minimal SMTP server listening on port 8025 of localhost. This server prints to stan-</p> <p>dard output all email headers and the email body. You then only need to set the <a href="index.html#page_1911"><i>EMAIL_HOST</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1911"><i>EMAIL_PORT</i></a></p> <p>accordingly. For a more detailed discussion of SMTP server options, see the documentation of the <a href="https://aiosmtpd.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">aiosmtpd</a> module.</p> <p>For information about unit-testing the sending of emails in your application, see the <a href="index.html#page_512">Email services</a> section of the testing documentation.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.47em"><b>3.15 Internationalization and localization</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.15.1 Translation</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Overview</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>In order to make a Django project translatable, you have to add a minimal number of hooks to your Python</p> <p>code and templates. These hooks are called <a href="index.html#page_707">translation strings. </a>They tell Django: “This text should be translated into the end user’s language, if a translation for this text is available in that language.” It’s your responsibility to mark translatable strings; the system can only translate strings it knows about.</p> <p>Django then provides utilities to extract the translation strings into a <a href="index.html#page_707">message file. </a>This file is a convenient way for translators to provide the equivalent of the translation strings in the target language. Once the translators have filled in the message file, it must be compiled. This process relies on the GNU gettext toolset.</p> <p>Once this is done, Django takes care of translating web apps on the fly in each available language, according to users’ language preferences.</p> <p>Django’s internationalization hooks are on by default, and that means there’s a bit of i18n-related overhead in certain places of the framework. If you don’t use internationalization, you should take the two seconds to</p> <p>set <a href="index.html#page_1936"><i>USE_I18N = False</i></a> in your settings file. Then Django will make some optimizations so as not to load the internationalization machinery.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: Make sure you’ve activated translation for your project (the fastest way is to check if <a href="index.html#page_1923"><i>MIDDLEWARE</i></a></p> <p>includes <a href="index.html#page_1594"><i>django.middleware.locale.LocaleMiddleware</i></a>). If you haven’t yet, see <a href="index.html#page_686">How Django discovers</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_686">language preference</a>.</p> <p id="page_650"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Internationalization: in Python code</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Standard translation</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Specify a translation string by using the function <a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>gettext()</i></a>. It’s convention to import this as a shorter alias, _, to save typing.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: Python’s standard library gettext module installs _() into the global namespace, as an alias for gettext(). In Django, we have chosen not to follow this practice, for a couple of reasons:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. Sometimes, you should use <a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>gettext_lazy()</i></a> as the default translation method for a particular file.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Without _() in the global namespace, the developer has to think about which is the most appropriate translation function.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. The underscore character (_) is used to represent “the previous result” in Python’s interactive shell and</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">doctest tests. Installing a global _() function causes interference. Explicitly importing gettext() as _() avoids this problem.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>What functions may be aliased as <b>_</b>?</p> <p>Because of how xgettext (used by <a href="index.html#page_1442"><i>makemessages</i></a>) works, only functions that take a single string argument can be imported as _:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>gettext()</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>gettext_lazy()</i></a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>In this example, the text "Welcome to my site." is marked as a translation string:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.http</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">gettext</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">_</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">output</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">_(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Welcome to my site."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse(output)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You could code this without using the alias. This example is identical to the previous one:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.http</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">gettext</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_651" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">output</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">gettext(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Welcome to my site."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse(output)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Translation works on computed values. This example is identical to the previous two:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">words</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Welcome"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"to"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"my"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"site."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">output</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">_(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">" "</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">join(words))</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse(output)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Translation works on variables. Again, here’s an identical example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">sentence</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Welcome to my site."</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">output</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">_(sentence)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse(output)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>(The caveat with using variables or computed values, as in the previous two examples, is that Django’s</p> <p>translation-string-detecting utility, <a href="index.html#page_1442"><i>django-admin makemessages</i>, </a>won’t be able to find these strings. More</p> <p>on <a href="index.html#page_1442"><i>makemessages</i></a> later.)</p> <p>The strings you pass to _() or gettext() can take placeholders, specified with Python’s standard named-string interpolation syntax. Example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request, m, d):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">output</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">_(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Today is %(month)s %(day)s."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"month"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: m,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"day"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: d}</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse(output)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This technique lets language-specific translations reorder the placeholder text. For example, an En-glish translation may be "Today is November 26.", while a Spanish translation may be "Hoy es 26 de noviembre." – with the month and the day placeholders swapped.</p> <p>For this reason, you should use named-string interpolation (e.g., %(day)s) instead of positional interpola-tion (e.g., %s or %d) whenever you have more than a single parameter. If you used positional interpolation, translations wouldn’t be able to reorder placeholder text.</p> <p>Since string extraction is done by the xgettext command, only syntaxes supported by gettext are supported</p> <p>by Django. In particular, Python <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/reference/lexical_analysis.html#f-strings">f-strings</a> are not yet supported by xgettext, and JavaScript template strings need gettext 0.21+.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_652"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Comments for translators</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you would like to give translators hints about a translatable string, you can add a comment prefixed with the Translators keyword on the line preceding the string, e.g.:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Translators: This message appears on the home page only</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">output</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">gettext(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Welcome to my site."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The comment will then appear in the resulting .po file associated with the translatable construct located below it and should also be displayed by most translation tools.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: Just for completeness, this is the corresponding fragment of the resulting .po file:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i>#. Translators: This message appears on the home page only</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># path/to/python/file.py:123</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">msgid</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Welcome to my site."</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">msgstr</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">""</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This also works in templates. See <a href="index.html#page_664">Comments for translators in templates</a> for more details.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Marking strings as no-op</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Use the function <a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>django.utils.translation.gettext_noop()</i></a> to mark a string as a translation string with-out translating it. The string is later translated from a variable.</p> <p>Use this if you have constant strings that should be stored in the source language because they are exchanged over systems or users – such as strings in a database – but should be translated at the last possible point in time, such as when the string is presented to the user.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Pluralization</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Use the function <a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>django.utils.translation.ngettext()</i></a> to specify pluralized messages.</p> <p>ngettext() takes three arguments: the singular translation string, the plural translation string and the number of objects.</p> <p>This function is useful when you need your Django application to be localizable to languages where the</p> <p>number and complexity of <a href="https://www.gnu.org/software/gettext/manual/gettext.html#Plural-forms">plural forms</a> is greater than the two forms used in English (‘object’ for the singular and ‘objects’ for all the cases where count is different from one, irrespective of its value.)</p> <p>For example:</p> <p id="page_653" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.http</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ngettext</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>hello_world</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request, count):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">page</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ngettext(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"there is %(count)d object"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"there are %(count)d objects"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">count,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"count"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: count,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse(page)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>In this example the number of objects is passed to the translation languages as the count variable.</p> <p>Note that pluralization is complicated and works differently in each language. Comparing count to 1 isn’t always the correct rule. This code looks sophisticated, but will produce incorrect results for some languages:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ngettext</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Report</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">count</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Report</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">count()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">count</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Report</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">_meta</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">verbose_name</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>else</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Report</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">_meta</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">verbose_name_plural</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">text</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ngettext(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"There is %(count)d %(name)s available."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"There are %(count)d %(name)s available."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">count,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"count"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: count,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: name}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Don’t try to implement your own singular-or-plural logic; it won’t be correct. In a case like this, consider something like the following:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">text</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ngettext(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"There is %(count)d %(name)s object available."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"There are %(count)d %(name)s objects available."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">count,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"count"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: count,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: Report</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">_meta</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">verbose_name,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p id="page_654"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: When using ngettext(), make sure you use a single name for every extrapolated variable included in the literal. In the examples above, note how we used the name Python variable in both translation strings. This example, besides being incorrect in some languages as noted above, would fail:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">text</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ngettext(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"There is %(count)d %(name)s available."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"There are %(count)d %(plural_name)s available."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">count,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"count"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: Report</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">count(),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: Report</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">_meta</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">verbose_name,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"plural_name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: Report</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">_meta</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">verbose_name_plural,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You would get an error when running <a href="index.html#page_1435"><i>django-admin compilemessages</i></a>:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">a format specification for argument 'name', as in 'msgstr[0]', doesn't exist in 'msgid'</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Contextual markers</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Sometimes words have several meanings, such as "May" in English, which refers to a month name and to a</p> <p>verb. To enable translators to translate these words correctly in different contexts, you can use the <a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>django.</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>utils.translation.pgettext()</i></a> function, or the <a href="index.html#page_2090"><i>django.utils.translation.npgettext()</i></a> function if the string needs pluralization. Both take a context string as the first variable.</p> <p>In the resulting .po file, the string will then appear as often as there are different contextual markers for the same string (the context will appear on the msgctxt line), allowing the translator to give a different translation for each of them.</p> <p>For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">pgettext</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">month</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">pgettext(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"month name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"May"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>or:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">pgettext_lazy</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyThing</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Model):</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_655" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">help_text</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">pgettext_lazy(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"help text for MyThing model"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"This is the help text"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>will appear in the .po file as:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">msgctxt</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"month name"</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">msgid</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"May"</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">msgstr</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">""</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Contextual markers are also supported by the <a href="index.html#page_660"><i>translate</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_661"><i>blocktranslate</i></a> template tags.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Lazy translation</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Use the lazy versions of translation functions in <a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>django.utils.translation</i></a> (easily recognizable by the lazy suffix in their names) to translate strings lazily – when the value is accessed rather than when they’re called.</p> <p>These functions store a lazy reference to the string – not the actual translation. The translation itself will be done when the string is used in a string context, such as in template rendering.</p> <p>This is essential when calls to these functions are located in code paths that are executed at module load time.</p> <p>This is something that can easily happen when defining models, forms and model forms, because Django implements these such that their fields are actually class-level attributes. For that reason, make sure to use lazy translations in the following cases:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Model fields and relationships verbose_name and help_text option values</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>For example, to translate the help text of the name field in the following model, do the following:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">gettext_lazy</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">_</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyThing</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Model):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(help_text</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">_(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"This is the help text"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">))</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can mark names of <a href="index.html#page_1643"><i>ForeignKey</i></a>, <a href="index.html#page_1649"><i>ManyToManyField</i></a> or <a href="index.html#page_1652"><i>OneToOneField</i></a> relationship as translatable by</p> <p>using their <a href="index.html#page_1687"><i>verbose_name</i></a> options:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyThing</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Model):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">kind</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ForeignKey(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">ThingKind,</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_656"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">on_delete</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CASCADE,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">related_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"kinds"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">verbose_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">_(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"kind"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Just like you would do in <a href="index.html#page_1687"><i>verbose_name</i></a> you should provide a lowercase verbose name text for the relation as Django will automatically titlecase it when required.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Model verbose names values</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>It is recommended to always provide explicit <a href="index.html#page_1687"><i>verbose_name</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1687"><i>verbose_name_plural</i></a> options rather than relying on the fallback English-centric and somewhat naïve determination of verbose names Django performs by looking at the model’s class name:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">gettext_lazy</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">_</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyThing</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Model):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(_(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">), help_text</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">_(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"This is the help text"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">))</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Meta</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">verbose_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span
