style="font-size:0.87em">verbose_name_plural</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">_(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"my things"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Model methods description argument to the @display decorator</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>For model methods, you can provide translations to Django and the admin site with the description argu-</p> <p>ment to the <a href="index.html#page_1100"><i>display()</i></a> decorator:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">gettext_lazy</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">_</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyThing</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Model):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">kind</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ForeignKey(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">ThingKind,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">on_delete</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CASCADE,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">related_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"kinds"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">verbose_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">_(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"kind"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_657" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">display(description</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">_(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Is it a mouse?"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">))</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>is_mouse</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">kind</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">type</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">MOUSE_TYPE</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Working with lazy translation objects</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The result of a gettext_lazy() call can be used wherever you would use a string (a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str">str</a> object) in other Django code, but it may not work with arbitrary Python code. For example, the following won’t work because</p> <p>the <a href="https://pypi.org/project/requests/">requests</a> library doesn’t handle gettext_lazy objects:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">body</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">gettext_lazy(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"I \u2764 Django"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># (Unicode :heart:)</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">requests</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">post(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"https://example.com/send"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, data</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"body"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: body})</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can avoid such problems by casting gettext_lazy() objects to text strings before passing them to non-Django code:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">requests</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">post(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"https://example.com/send"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, data</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"body"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">str</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(body)})</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you don’t like the long gettext_lazy name, you can alias it as _ (underscore), like so:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">gettext_lazy</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">_</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyThing</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Model):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(help_text</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">_(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"This is the help text"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">))</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Using gettext_lazy() and ngettext_lazy() to mark strings in models and utility functions is a common operation. When you’re working with these objects elsewhere in your code, you should ensure that you don’t accidentally convert them to strings, because they should be converted as late as possible (so that the correct locale is in effect). This necessitates the use of the helper function described next.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Lazy translations and plural</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When using lazy translation for a plural string (n[p]gettext_lazy), you generally don’t know the number argument at the time of the string definition. Therefore, you are authorized to pass a key name instead of an integer as the number argument. Then number will be looked up in the dictionary under that key during string interpolation. Here’s example:</p> <p id="page_658"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">forms</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.core.exceptions</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ValidationError</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ngettext_lazy</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyForm</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(forms</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Form):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">error_message</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ngettext_lazy(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"You only provided %(num)d argument"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"You only provided %(num)d arguments"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"num"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>clean</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">error:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>raise</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ValidationError(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">error_message</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"num"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: number})</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If the string contains exactly one unnamed placeholder, you can interpolate directly with the number argu-ment:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyForm</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(forms</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Form):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">error_message</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ngettext_lazy(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"You provided %d argument"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"You provided %d arguments"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>clean</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">error:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>raise</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ValidationError(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">error_message</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">number)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Formatting strings: format_lazy()</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Python’s <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str.format">str.format()</a> method will not work when either the format_string or any of the arguments to</p> <p><a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str.format">str.format()</a> contains lazy translation objects. Instead, you can use <a href="index.html#page_2087"><i>django.utils.text.format_lazy()</i></a>, which creates a lazy object that runs the str.format() method only when the result is included in a string. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.text</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">format_lazy</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">gettext_lazy</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">gettext_lazy(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"John Lennon"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_659" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">instrument</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">gettext_lazy(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"guitar"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">result</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">format_lazy(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"{name}: {instrument}"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">name, instrument</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">instrument)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>In this case, the lazy translations in result will only be converted to strings when result itself is used in a string (usually at template rendering time).</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Other uses of lazy in delayed translations</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>For any other case where you would like to delay the translation, but have to pass the translatable string as argument to another function, you can wrap this function inside a lazy call yourself. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.functional</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">lazy</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">gettext_lazy</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">_</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>to_lower</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(string):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">string</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">lower()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">to_lower_lazy</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">lazy(to_lower,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">str</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>And then later:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">lazy_string</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">to_lower_lazy(_(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"My STRING!"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">))</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Localized names of languages</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>get_language_info</b>(lang_code)</p> <p>The get_language_info() function provides detailed information about languages:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">activate, get_language_info</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">activate(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"fr"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">get_language_info(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"de"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">print</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(li[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">], li[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name_local"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">], li[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name_translated"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">], li[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"bidi"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">])</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">German Deutsch Allemand False</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The name, name_local, and name_translated attributes of the dictionary contain the name of the language in English, in the language itself, and in your current active language respectively. The bidi attribute is True only for bi-directional languages.</p> <p>The source of the language information is the django.conf.locale module. Similar access to this informa-tion is available for template code. See below.</p> <p id="page_660"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Internationalization: in template code</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Translations in <a href="index.html#page_1965">Django templates</a> uses two template tags and a slightly different syntax than in Python code. To give your template access to these tags, put {% load i18n %} toward the top of your template. As with all template tags, this tag needs to be loaded in all templates which use translations, even those templates that extend from other templates which have already loaded the i18n tag.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: Translated strings will not be escaped when rendered in a template. This allows you to include</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">HTML in translations, for example for emphasis, but potentially dangerous characters (e.g. ") will also</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">be rendered unchanged.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>translate template tag</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The {% translate %} template tag translates either a constant string (enclosed in single or double quotes) or variable content:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>translate</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"This is the title."</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>translate</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myvar</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If the noop option is present, variable lookup still takes place but the translation is skipped. This is useful when “stubbing out” content that will require translation in the future:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>translate</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"myvar"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">noop</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Internally, inline translations use a <a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>gettext()</i></a> call.</p> <p>In case a template var (myvar above) is passed to the tag, the tag will first resolve such variable to a string at run-time and then look up that string in the message catalogs.</p> <p>It’s not possible to mix a template variable inside a string within {% translate %}. If your translations</p> <p>require strings with variables (placeholders), use <a href="index.html#page_661"><i>{% blocktranslate %}</i></a> instead.</p> <p>If you’d like to retrieve a translated string without displaying it, you can use the following syntax:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>translate</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"This is the title"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">the_title</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">the_title</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">meta</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"description"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">content</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">the_title</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>In practice you’ll use this to get a string you can use in multiple places in a template or so you can use the output as an argument for other template tags or filters:</p> <p id="page_661" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>translate</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"starting point"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">start</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>translate</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"end point"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">end</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>translate</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"La Grande Boucle"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>blocktranslate</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">' homepage</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.47em"><i>→</i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endif</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endfor</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">p</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>{% translate %} also supports <a
