style="font-size:0.87em">activate(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"nl"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">reverse(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"news:index"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">'/nl/news/'</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: <a href="index.html#page_674"><i>i18n_patterns()</i></a> is only allowed in a root URLconf. Using it within an included URLconf</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">will throw an <a href="index.html#page_1472"><i>ImproperlyConfigured</i></a> exception.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: <span style="float:right">Ensure that you don’t have non-prefixed URL patterns that might collide with an</span></p> <p style="margin-left:1em">automatically-added language prefix.</p> <p id="page_676"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Translating URL patterns</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>URL patterns can also be marked translatable using the <a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>gettext_lazy()</i></a> function. Example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.conf.urls.i18n</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">i18n_patterns</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.urls</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">include, path</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">gettext_lazy</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">_</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">about</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">about_views</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">news</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">news_views</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">sitemaps.views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">sitemap</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"sitemap.xml"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, sitemap, name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"sitemap-xml"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">news_patterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">""</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, news_views</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">index, name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"index"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(_(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"category/<slug:slug>/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">), news_views</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">category, name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"category"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"<slug:slug>/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, news_views</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">details, name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"detail"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"news"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>+=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">i18n_patterns(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(_(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"about/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">), about_views</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">main, name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"about"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(_(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"news/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">), include(news_patterns, namespace</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"news"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>After you’ve created the translations, the <a href="index.html#page_2063"><i>reverse()</i></a> function will return the URL in the active language. Example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.urls</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">reverse</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">activate</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">activate(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"en"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">reverse(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"news:category"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, kwargs</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"slug"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"recent"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">})</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">'/en/news/category/recent/'</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">activate(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"nl"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">reverse(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"news:category"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, kwargs</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"slug"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"recent"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">})</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">'/nl/nieuws/categorie/recent/'</span></p> <p id="page_677" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: In most cases, it’s best to use translated URLs only within a language code prefixed block</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">of patterns (using <a href="index.html#page_674"><i>i18n_patterns()</i></a>), to avoid the possibility that a carelessly translated URL causes a</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">collision with a non-translated URL pattern.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Reversing in templates</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If localized URLs get reversed in templates they always use the current language. To link to a URL in another</p> <p>language use the <a href="index.html#page_665"><i>language</i></a> template tag. It enables the given language in the enclosed template section:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">i18n</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get_available_languages as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">languages</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>translate</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"View this category in:"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">lang_code</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>,</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">lang_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">languages</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>language</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">lang_code</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">href</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>url</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'category'</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">slug</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">category.slug</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">lang_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endlanguage</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endfor</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_665"><i>language</i></a> tag expects the language code as the only argument.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Localization: how to create language files</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Once the string literals of an application have been tagged for later translation, the translation themselves need to be written (or obtained). Here’s how that works.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Message files</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The first step is to create a <a href="index.html#page_707">message file</a> for a new language. A message file is a plain-text file, representing a single language, that contains all available translation strings and how they should be represented in the given language. Message files have a .po file extension.</p> <p>Django comes with a tool, <a href="index.html#page_1442"><i>django-admin makemessages</i></a>, that automates the creation and upkeep of these files.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Gettext utilities</p> <p>The makemessages command (and compilemessages discussed later) use commands from the GNU gettext toolset: xgettext, msgfmt, msgmerge and msguniq.</p> <p id="page_678"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The minimum version of the gettext utilities supported is 0.19.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To create or update a message file, run this command:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">django-admin makemessages -l de</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><i>. . .</i>where de is the <a href="index.html#page_706">locale name</a> for the message file you want to create. For example, pt_BR for Brazilian Portuguese, de_AT for Austrian German or id for Indonesian.</p> <p>The script should be run from one of two places:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The root directory of your Django project (the one that contains manage.py).</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The root directory of one of your Django apps.</p> <p>The script runs over your project source tree or your application source tree and pulls out all strings marked</p> <p>for translation (see <a href="index.html#page_688">How Django discovers translations</a> and be sure <a href="index.html#page_1921"><i>LOCALE_PATHS</i></a> is configured correctly). It creates (or updates) a message file in the directory locale/LANG/LC_MESSAGES. In the de example, the file will be locale/de/LC_MESSAGES/django.po.</p> <p>When you run makemessages from the root directory of your project, the extracted strings will be automat-ically distributed to the proper message files. That is, a string extracted from a file of an app containing a locale directory will go in a message file under that directory. A string extracted from a file of an app</p> <p>without any locale directory will either go in a message file under the directory listed first in <a href="index.html#page_1921"><i>LOCALE_PATHS</i></a></p> <p>or will generate an error if <a href="index.html#page_1921"><i>LOCALE_PATHS</i></a> is empty.</p> <p>By default <a href="index.html#page_1442"><i>django-admin makemessages</i></a> examines every file that has the .html, .txt or .py file extension. If</p> <p>you want to override that default, use the<a href="index.html#page_1442"><i>--extension</i></a> or-e option to specify the file extensions to examine:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">django-admin makemessages -l de -e txt</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Separate multiple extensions with commas and/or use-e or--extension multiple times:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">django-admin makemessages -l de -e html,txt -e xml</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: When <a href="index.html#page_681">creating message files from JavaScript source code</a> you need to use the special djangojs</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">domain, not-e js.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Using Jinja2 templates?</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1442"><i>makemessages</i></a> doesn’t understand the syntax of Jinja2 templates. To extract strings from a project contain-</p> <p>ing Jinja2 templates, use <a href="https://babel.pocoo.org/en/latest/messages.html#message-extraction">Message Extracting</a> from <a href="https://babel.pocoo.org/en/latest/">Babel</a> instead.</p> <p>Here’s an example babel.cfg configuration file:</p> <p id="page_679" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Extraction from Python source files</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>[python: **.py]</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Extraction from Jinja2 templates</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>[jinja2: **.jinja]</b></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">extensions</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">jinja2.ext.with_</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Make sure you list all extensions you’re using! Otherwise Babel won’t recognize the tags defined by these extensions and will ignore Jinja2 templates containing them entirely.</p> <p>Babel provides similar features to <a href="index.html#page_1442"><i>makemessages</i></a>, can replace it in general, and doesn’t depend on gettext.</p> <p>For more information, read its documentation about <a href="https://babel.pocoo.org/en/latest/messages.html">working with message catalogs</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>No gettext?</p> <p>If you don’t have the gettext utilities installed, <a href="index.html#page_1442"><i>makemessages</i></a> will create empty files. If that’s the case, either install the gettext utilities or copy the English message file (locale/en/LC_MESSAGES/django.po) if available and use it as a starting point, which is an empty translation file.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Working on Windows?</p> <p>If you’re using Windows and need to install the GNU gettext utilities so <a href="index.html#page_1442"><i>makemessages</i></a> works, see <a href="index.html#page_682">gettext on</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_682">Windows</a> for more information.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Each .po file contains a small bit of metadata, such as the translation maintainer’s contact information, but the bulk of the file is a list of messages – mappings between translation strings and the actual translated text for the particular language.</p> <p>For example, if your Django app contained a translation string for the text "Welcome to my site.", like so:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">_(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Welcome to my site."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><i>. . .</i>then <a href="index.html#page_1442"><i>django-admin makemessages</i></a> will have created a .po file containing the following snippet – a mes-sage:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>#: path/to/python/module.py:23</b></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">msgid</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Welcome to my site."</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">msgstr</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">""</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A quick explanation:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• msgid is the translation string, which appears in the source. Don’t change it.</p> <p id="page_680"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• msgstr is where you put the language-specific translation. It starts out empty, so it’s your responsibility</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">to change it. Make sure you keep the quotes around your translation.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• As a convenience, each message includes, in the form of a comment line prefixed with # and located</p> <p style="text-align:center">above the msgid line, the filename and line number from which the translation string was gleaned.</p> <p>Long messages are a special case. There, the first string directly after the msgstr (or msgid) is an empty string. Then the content itself will be written over the next few lines as one string per line. Those strings are directly concatenated. Don’t forget trailing spaces within the strings; otherwise, they’ll be tacked together without whitespace!</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Mind your charset</p> <p>Due to the way the gettext tools work internally and because we want to allow non-ASCII source strings in Django’s core and your applications, you must use UTF-8 as the encoding for your .po files (the default when .po files are created). This means that everybody will be using the same encoding, which is important when Django processes the .po files.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Fuzzy entries</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1442"><i>makemessages</i></a> sometimes generates translation entries marked as fuzzy, e.g. when translations are inferred</p> <p>from previously translated strings. By default, fuzzy entries are not processed by <a href="index.html#page_1435"><i>compilemessages</i>.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To reexamine all source code and templates for new translation strings and update all message files for all languages, run this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">django-admin makemessages -a</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Compiling message files</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>After you create your message file – and each time you make changes to it – you’ll need to compile it into a</p> <p>more efficient form, for use by gettext. Do this with the <a href="index.html#page_1435"><i>django-admin compilemessages</i></a> utility.</p> <p>This tool runs over all available .po files and creates .mo files, which are binary files optimized for use</p> <p>by gettext. In the same directory from which you ran <a href="index.html#page_1442"><i>django-admin makemessages</i>, </a>run <a href="index.html#page_1435"><i>django-admin</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1435"><i>compilemessages</i></a> like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">django-admin compilemessages</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>That’s it. Your translations are ready for use.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Working on Windows?</p> <p id="page_681" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you’re using Windows and need to install the GNU gettext utilities so <a href="index.html#page_1435"><i>django-admin compilemessages</i></a></p> <p>works see <a href="index.html#page_682">gettext on Windows</a> for more information.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>.po</b> files: Encoding and BOM usage.</p> <p>Django only supports .po files encoded in UTF-8 and without any BOM (Byte Order Mark) so if your text editor adds such marks to the beginning of files by default then you will need to reconfigure it.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Troubleshooting: gettext() incorrectly detects python-format in strings with percent signs</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>In some cases, such as strings with a percent sign followed by a space and a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#old-string-formatting">string conversion type</a> (e.g. _("10%</p> <p>interest")), <a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>gettext()</i></a> incorrectly flags strings with python-format.</p> <p>If you try to compile message files with incorrectly flagged strings, you’ll get an error message like number of format specifications in 'msgid' and 'msgstr' does not match or 'msgstr' is not a valid Python format string, unlike 'msgid'.</p> <p>To workaround this, you can escape percent signs by adding a second percent sign:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">gettext</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">_</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">output</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">_(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"10%% interest"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Or you can use no-python-format so that all percent signs are treated as literals:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># xgettext:no-python-format</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">output</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">_(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"10% interest"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Creating message files from JavaScript source code</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You create and update the message files the same way as the other Django message files – with the</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1442"><i>django-admin makemessages</i></a> tool. The only difference is you need to explicitly specify what in gettext parlance is known as a domain in this case the djangojs domain, by providing a-d djangojs parameter, like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">django-admin makemessages -d djangojs -l de</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This would create or update the message file for JavaScript for German. After updating message files, run</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1435"><i>django-admin compilemessages</i></a> the same way as you do with normal Django message files.</p> <p id="page_682"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>gettext on Windows</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This is only needed for people who either want to extract message IDs or compile message files (.po). Trans-lation work itself involves editing existing files of this type, but if you want to create your own message files,</p> <p>or want to test or compile a changed message file, download <a href="https://mlocati.github.io/articles/gettext-iconv-windows.html">a precompiled binary installer</a>.</p> <p>You may also use gettext binaries you have obtained elsewhere, so long as the xgettext --version com-mand works properly. Do not attempt to use Django translation utilities with a gettext package if the command xgettext --version entered at a Windows command prompt causes a popup window saying “xgettext.exe has generated errors and will be closed by Windows”.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Customizing the makemessages command</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you want to pass additional parameters to xgettext, you need to create a custom <a href="index.html#page_1442"><i>makemessages</i></a> command and override its xgettext_options attribute:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.core.management.commands</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Miscellaneous</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>The set_language redirect view</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>set_language</b>(request)</p> <p>As a convenience, Django comes with a view, <a href="index.html#page_683"><i>django.views.i18n.set_language()</i></a>, that sets a user’s lan-guage preference and redirects to a given URL or, by default, back to the previous page.</p> <p>Activate this view by adding the following line to your URLconf:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"i18n/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, include(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.conf.urls.i18n"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)),</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>(Note that this example makes the view available at /i18n/setlang/.)</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: Make sure that you don’t include the above URL within <a href="index.html#page_674"><i>i18n_patterns()</i></a>- it needs to be</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">language-independent itself to work correctly.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The view expects to be called via the POST method, with a language parameter set in request. If session support is enabled, the view saves the language choice in the user’s session. It also saves the language choice in a cookie that is named django_language by default. (The name can be changed through the</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1919"><i>LANGUAGE_COOKIE_NAME</i></a> setting.)</p> <p>After setting the language choice, Django looks for a next parameter in the POST or GET data. If that is found and Django considers it to be a safe URL (i.e. it doesn’t point to a different host and uses a safe scheme), a redirect to that URL will be performed. Otherwise, Django may fall back to redirecting the user to the URL from the Referer header or, if it is not set, to /, depending on the nature of the request:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• If the request accepts HTML content (based on its Accept HTTP header), the fallback will always be</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">performed.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• If the request doesn’t accept HTML, the fallback will be performed only if the next parameter was set.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Otherwise a 204 status code (No Content) will be returned.</p> <p>Here’s example HTML template code:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">i18n</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">action</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>url</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'set_language'</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">method</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"post"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>csrf_token</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">input</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"next"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">type</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"hidden"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">redirect_to</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">select</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"language"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get_available_languages as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">LANGUAGES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span
