</p> <p>In this example, Django looks up the URL of the page to which the user will be redirected in the redirect_to context variable.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Explicitly setting the active language</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You may want to set the active language for the current session explicitly. Perhaps a user’s language pref-</p> <p>erence is retrieved from another system, for example. You’ve already been introduced to <a href="index.html#page_2090"><i>django.utils.</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_2090"><i>translation.activate()</i>. </a>That applies to the current thread only. To persist the language for the entire</p> <p>session in a cookie, set the <a href="index.html#page_1919"><i>LANGUAGE_COOKIE_NAME</i></a> cookie on the response:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.conf</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">settings</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.http</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">translation</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">user_language</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"fr"</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">translation</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">activate(user_language)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">set_cookie(settings</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">LANGUAGE_COOKIE_NAME, user_language)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You would typically want to use both: <a href="index.html#page_2090"><i>django.utils.translation.activate()</i></a> changes the language for this thread, and setting the cookie makes this preference persist in future requests.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using translations outside views and templates</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>While Django provides a rich set of i18n tools for use in views and templates, it does not restrict the usage to Django-specific code. The Django translation mechanisms can be used to translate arbitrary texts to any language that is supported by Django (as long as an appropriate translation catalog exists, of course). You can load a translation catalog, activate it and translate text to language of your choice, but remember to switch back to original language, as activating a translation catalog is done on per-thread basis and such change will affect code running in the same thread.</p> <p>For example:</p> <p id="page_685" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">translation</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>welcome_translated</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(language):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">cur_language</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">translation</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_language()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>try</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">translation</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">activate(language)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">text</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">translation</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">gettext(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"welcome"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>finally</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">translation</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">activate(cur_language)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">text</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Calling this function with the value 'de' will give you "Willkommen", regardless of <a href="index.html#page_1918"><i>LANGUAGE_CODE</i></a> and language set by middleware.</p> <p>Functions of particular interest are <a href="index.html#page_2090"><i>django.utils.translation.get_language()</i></a> which returns the lan-</p> <p>guage used in the current thread, <a href="index.html#page_2090"><i>django.utils.translation.activate()</i></a> which activates a translation</p> <p>catalog for the current thread, and <a href="index.html#page_2090"><i>django.utils.translation.check_for_language()</i></a> which checks if the given language is supported by Django.</p> <p>To help write more concise code, there is also a context manager <a href="index.html#page_2090"><i>django.utils.translation.override()</i></a> that stores the current language on enter and restores it on exit. With it, the above example becomes:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">translation</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>welcome_translated</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(language):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>with</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">translation</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">override(language):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">translation</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">gettext(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"welcome"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Language cookie</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A number of settings can be used to adjust language cookie options:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1919"><i>LANGUAGE_COOKIE_NAME</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1919"><i>LANGUAGE_COOKIE_AGE</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1919"><i>LANGUAGE_COOKIE_DOMAIN</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1919"><i>LANGUAGE_COOKIE_HTTPONLY</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1919"><i>LANGUAGE_COOKIE_PATH</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1920"><i>LANGUAGE_COOKIE_SAMESITE</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1920"><i>LANGUAGE_COOKIE_SECURE</i></a></p> <p id="page_686"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Implementation notes</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Specialties of Django translation</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django’s translation machinery uses the standard gettext module that comes with Python. If you know gettext, you might note these specialties in the way Django does translation:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The string domain is django or djangojs. This string domain is used to differentiate between differ-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">ent programs that store their data in a common message-file library (usually /usr/share/locale/). The django domain is used for Python and template translation strings and is loaded into the global translation catalogs. The djangojs domain is only used for JavaScript translation catalogs to make sure that those are as small as possible.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Django doesn’t use xgettext alone. It uses Python wrappers around xgettext and msgfmt. This is</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">mostly for convenience.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>How Django discovers language preference</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Once you’ve prepared your translations – or, if you want to use the translations that come with Django – you’ll need to activate translation for your app.</p> <p>Behind the scenes, Django has a very flexible model of deciding which language should be used – installation-wide, for a particular user, or both.</p> <p>To set an installation-wide language preference, set <a href="index.html#page_1918"><i>LANGUAGE_CODE</i></a>. Django uses this language as the de-fault translation – the final attempt if no better matching translation is found through one of the methods employed by the locale middleware (see below).</p> <p>If all you want is to run Django with your native language all you need to do is set <a href="index.html#page_1918"><i>LANGUAGE_CODE</i></a> and make</p> <p>sure the corresponding <a href="index.html#page_707">message files</a> and their compiled versions (.mo) exist.</p> <p>If you want to let each individual user specify which language they prefer, then you also need to use the LocaleMiddleware. LocaleMiddleware enables language selection based on data from the request. It cus-tomizes content for each user.</p> <p>To use LocaleMiddleware, add 'django.middleware.locale.LocaleMiddleware' to your <a href="index.html#page_1923"><i>MIDDLEWARE</i></a> set-ting. Because middleware order matters, follow these guidelines:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Make sure it’s one of the first middleware installed.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• It should come after SessionMiddleware, because LocaleMiddleware makes use of session data. And</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">it should come before CommonMiddleware because CommonMiddleware needs an activated language in order to resolve the requested URL.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• If you use CacheMiddleware, put LocaleMiddleware after it.</p> <p>For example, your <a href="index.html#page_1923"><i>MIDDLEWARE</i></a> might look like this:</p> <p id="page_687" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">MIDDLEWARE</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.contrib.sessions.middleware.SessionMiddleware"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.middleware.locale.LocaleMiddleware"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.middleware.common.CommonMiddleware"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>(For more on middleware, see the <a href="index.html#page_303">middleware documentation.)</a></p> <p>LocaleMiddleware tries to determine the user’s language preference by following this algorithm:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• First, it looks for the language prefix in the requested URL. This is only performed when you are using</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">the i18n_patterns function in your root URLconf. See <a href="index.html#page_674">Internationalization: in URL patterns</a> for more information about the language prefix and how to internationalize URL patterns.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Failing that, it looks for a cookie.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The name of the cookie used is set by the <a href="index.html#page_1919"><i>LANGUAGE_COOKIE_NAME</i></a> setting. (The default name is django_language.)</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Failing that, it looks at the Accept-Language HTTP header. This header is sent by your browser and</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">tells the server which language(s) you prefer, in order by priority. Django tries each language in the header until it finds one with available translations.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Failing that, it uses the global <a href="index.html#page_1918"><i>LANGUAGE_CODE</i></a> setting.</p> <p>Notes:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• In each of these places, the language preference is expected to be in the standard <a href="index.html#page_706">language format, </a>as</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">a string. For example, Brazilian Portuguese is pt-br.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• If a base language is available but the sublanguage specified is not, Django uses the base language. For</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">example, if a user specifies de-at (Austrian German) but Django only has de available, Django uses de.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Only languages listed in the <a href="index.html#page_1920"><i>LANGUAGES</i></a> setting can be selected. If you want to restrict the language se-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">lection to a subset of provided languages (because your application doesn’t provide all those languages),</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">set <a href="index.html#page_1920"><i>LANGUAGES</i></a> to a list of languages. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">LANGUAGES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"de"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, _(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"German"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"en"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, _(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"English"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This example restricts languages that are available for automatic selection to German and English (and any sublanguage, like de-ch or en-us).</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• If you define a custom <a href="index.html#page_1920"><i>LANGUAGES</i></a> setting, as explained in the previous bullet, you can mark the lan-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">guage names as translation strings – but use <a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>gettext_lazy()</i></a> instead of <a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>gettext()</i></a> to avoid a circular import.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Here’s a sample settings file:</p> <p id="page_688"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">gettext_lazy</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">_</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">LANGUAGES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"de"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, _(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"German"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"en"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, _(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"English"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Once LocaleMiddleware determines the user’s preference, it makes this preference available as request.</p> <p>LANGUAGE_CODE for each <a href="index.html#page_1859"><i>HttpRequest</i>. </a>Feel free to read this value in your view code. Here’s an example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.http</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>hello_world</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request, count):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">LANGUAGE_CODE</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"de-at"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"You prefer to read Austrian German."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>else</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"You prefer to read another language."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note that, with static (middleware-less) translation, the language is in settings.LANGUAGE_CODE, while with dynamic (middleware) translation, it’s in request.LANGUAGE_CODE.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>How Django discovers translations</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>At runtime, Django builds an in-memory unified catalog of literals-translations. To achieve this it looks for translations by following this algorithm regarding the order in which it examines the different file paths to</p> <p>load the compiled <a href="index.html#page_707">message files</a> (.mo) and the precedence of multiple translations for the same literal:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. The directories listed in <a href="index.html#page_1921"><i>LOCALE_PATHS</i></a> have the highest precedence, with the ones appearing first hav-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">ing higher precedence than the ones appearing later.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. Then, it looks for and uses if it exists a locale directory in each of the installed apps listed in</p> <p style="text-align:center"><a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a> . The ones appearing first have higher precedence than the ones appearing later.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">3. Finally, the Django-provided base translation in <a href="https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/conf/locale">django/conf/locale</a> is used as a fallback.</p> <p>See also:</p> <p>The translations for literals included in JavaScript assets are looked up following a similar but not identical</p> <p>algorithm. See <a href="index.html#page_667"><i>JavaScriptCatalog</i></a> for more details.</p> <p>You can also put <a href="index.html#page_692">custom format files</a> in the <a href="index.html#page_1921"><i>LOCALE_PATHS</i></a> directories if you also set <a href="index.html#page_1916"><i>FORMAT_MODULE_PATH</i></a> .</p> <p>In all cases the name of the directory containing the translation is expected to be named using <a href="index.html#page_706">locale name</a> no-tation. E.g. de, pt_BR, es_AR, etc. Untranslated strings for territorial language variants use the translations of the generic language. For example, untranslated pt_BR strings use pt translations.</p> <p id="page_689" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This way, you can write applications that include their own translations, and you can override base transla-tions in your project. Or, you can build a big project out of several apps and put all translations into one big common message file specific to the project you are composing. The choice is yours.</p> <p>All message file repositories are structured the same way. They are:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• All paths listed in <a href="index.html#page_1921"><i>LOCALE_PATHS</i></a> in your settings file are searched for <language>/LC_MESSAGES/</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">django.(po|mo)</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• $APPPATH/locale/<language>/LC_MESSAGES/django.(po|mo)</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• $PYTHONPATH/django/conf/locale/<language>/LC_MESSAGES/django.(po|mo)</p> <p>To create message files, you use the <a href="index.html#page_1442"><i>django-admin makemessages</i></a> tool. And you use <a href="index.html#page_1435"><i>django-admin</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1435"><i>compilemessages</i></a> to produce the binary .mo files that are used by gettext.</p> <p>You can also run <a href="index.html#page_1435"><i>django-admin compilemessages --settings=path.to.settings</i></a> to make the compiler</p> <p>process all the directories in your <a href="index.html#page_1921"><i>LOCALE_PATHS</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using a non-English base language</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django makes the general assumption that the original strings in a translatable project are written in English. You can choose another language, but you must be aware of certain limitations:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• gettext only provides two plural forms for the original messages, so you will also need to provide a</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">translation for the base language to include all plural forms if the plural rules for the base language are different from English.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• When an English variant is activated and English strings are missing, the fallback language will not be</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">the <a href="index.html#page_1918"><i>LANGUAGE_CODE</i></a> of the project, but the original strings. For example, an English user visiting a site</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">with <a href="index.html#page_1918"><i>LANGUAGE_CODE</i></a> set to Spanish and original strings written in Russian will see Russian text rather than Spanish.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.15.2 Format localization</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Overview</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django’s formatting system is capable of displaying dates, times and numbers in templates using the format</p> <p>specified for the current <a href="index.html#page_706">locale</a>. It also handles localized input in forms.</p> <p>Two users accessing the same content may see dates, times and numbers formatted in different ways, de-pending on the formats for their current locale.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: <span style="float:right">To enable number formatting with thousand separators, it is necessary to set <b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p id="page_690"><a href="index.html#page_1936"><i>USE_THOUSAND_SEPARATOR = True</i></a> in your settings file. Alternatively, you could use <a href="index.html#page_1284"><i>intcomma</i></a> to for-mat numbers in your template.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: There is a related <a href="index.html#page_1936"><i>USE_I18N</i></a> setting that controls if Django should activate translation. See <a href="index.html#page_649">Translation</a> for more details.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Locale aware input in forms</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When formatting is enabled, Django can use localized formats when parsing dates, times and numbers in forms. That means it tries different formats for different locales when guessing the format used by the user when inputting data on forms.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: Django uses different formats for displaying data to those it uses for parsing data. Most notably, the formats for parsing dates can’t use the %a (abbreviated weekday name), %A (full weekday name), %b (abbreviated month name), %B (full month name), or %p (AM/PM).</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To enable a form field to localize input and output data use its localize argument:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>CashRegisterForm</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(forms</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Form):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">product</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">forms</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">revenue</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">forms</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">DecimalField(max_digits</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">4</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, decimal_places</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">2</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, localize</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Controlling localization in templates</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django tries to use a locale specific format whenever it outputs a value in a template.</p> <p>However, it may not always be appropriate to use localized values – for example, if you’re outputting JavaScript or XML that is designed to be machine-readable, you will always want unlocalized values. You may also want to use localization in selected templates, rather than using localization everywhere.</p> <p>To allow for fine control over the use of localization, Django provides the l10n template library that contains the following tags and filters.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_691" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Template tags</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>localize</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Enables or disables localization of template variables in the contained block.</p> <p>To activate or deactivate localization for a template block, use:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">l10n</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>localize</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">on</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endlocalize</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>localize</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">off</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endlocalize</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When localization is disabled, the <a href="index.html#page_1950">localization settings</a> formats are applied.</p> <p>See <a href="index.html#page_691"><i>localize</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_692"><i>unlocalize</i></a> for template filters that will do the same job on a per-variable basis.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Template filters</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>localize</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Forces localization of a single value.</p> <p>For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">l10n</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>localize</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To disable localization on a single value, use <a href="index.html#page_692"><i>unlocalize</i></a>. To control localization over a large section of a</p> <p>template, use the <a href="index.html#page_691"><i>localize</i></a> template tag.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_692"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>unlocalize</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Forces a single value to be printed without localization.</p> <p>For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">l10n</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>unlocalize</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To force localization of a single value, use <a href="index.html#page_691"><i>localize</i>. </a>To control localization over a large section of a template,</p> <p>use the <a href="index.html#page_691"><i>localize</i></a> template tag.</p> <p>Returns a string representation for numbers (int, float, or Decimal) with the <a href="index.html#page_1950">localization settings</a> formats applied.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Creating custom format files</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django provides format definitions for many locales, but sometimes you might want to create your own, because a format file doesn’t exist for your locale, or because you want to overwrite some of the values.</p> <p>To use custom formats, specify the path where you’ll place format files first. To do that, set your</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1916"><i>FORMAT_MODULE_PATH</i></a> setting to the package where format files will exist, for instance:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">FORMAT_MODULE_PATH</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"mysite.formats"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"some_app.formats"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Files are not placed directly in this directory, but in a directory named as the locale, and must be named formats.py. Be careful not to put sensitive information in these files as values inside can be exposed if you</p> <p>pass the string to django.utils.formats.get_format() (used by the <a href="index.html#page_2006"><i>date</i></a> template filter).</p> <p>To customize the English formats, a structure like this would be needed:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">mysite/</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">formats/</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">__init__.py</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">en/</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">__init__.py</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">formats.py</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>where formats.py contains custom format definitions. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">THOUSAND_SEPARATOR</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"\xa0"</span></p> <p id="page_693" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>to use a non-breaking space (Unicode 00A0) as a thousand separator, instead of the default for English, a comma.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Limitations of the provided locale formats</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Some locales use context-sensitive formats for numbers, which Django’s localization system cannot handle automatically.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Switzerland (German)</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The Swiss number formatting depends on the type of number that is being formatted. For monetary values, a comma is used as the thousand separator and a decimal point for the decimal separator. For all other num-bers, a comma is used as decimal separator and a space as thousand separator. The locale format provided by Django uses the generic separators, a comma for decimal and a space for thousand separators.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>3.15.3 Time zones</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Overview</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When support for time zones is enabled, Django stores datetime information in UTC in the database, uses time-zone-aware datetime objects internally, and converts them to the end user’s time zone in forms. Tem-</p> <p>plates will use the <a href="index.html#page_695">default time zone, </a>but this can be updated to the end user’s time zone through the use of</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_697">filters and tags.</a></p> <p>This is handy if your users live in more than one time zone and you want to display datetime information according to each user’s wall clock.</p> <p>Even if your website is available in only one time zone, it’s still good practice to store data in UTC in your database. The main reason is daylight saving time (DST). Many countries have a system of DST, where clocks are moved forward in spring and backward in autumn. If you’re working in local time, you’re likely to encounter errors twice a year, when the transitions happen. This probably doesn’t matter for your blog, but it’s a problem if you over bill or under bill your customers by one hour, twice a year, every year. The solution to this problem is to use UTC in the code and use local time only when interacting with end users.</p> <p>Time zone support is enabled by default. To disable it, set <a href="index.html#page_1936"><i>USE_TZ = False</i></a> in your settings file.</p> <p>Time zone support uses <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/zoneinfo.html#module-zoneinfo">zoneinfo, </a>which is part of the Python standard library from Python 3.9.</p> <p>If you’re wrestling with a particular problem, start with the <a href="index.html#page_702">time zone FAQ</a>.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_694"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Concepts</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Naive and aware datetime objects</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Python’s <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime">datetime.datetime</a> objects have a tzinfo attribute that can be used to store time zone informa-</p> <p>tion, represented as an instance of a subclass of <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.tzinfo">datetime.tzinfo</a>. When this attribute is set and describes an offset, a datetime object is aware. Otherwise, it’s naive.</p> <p>You can use <a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>is_aware()</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>is_naive()</i></a> to determine whether datetimes are aware or naive.</p> <p>When time zone support is disabled, Django uses naive datetime objects in local time. This is sufficient for many use cases. In this mode, to obtain the current time, you would write:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">now</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">now()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When time zone support is enabled (<a href="index.html#page_1936"><i>USE_TZ=True</i></a>), Django uses time-zone-aware datetime objects. If your code creates datetime objects, they should be aware too. In this mode, the example above becomes:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">timezone</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">now</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">timezone</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">now()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: Dealing with aware datetime objects isn’t always intuitive. For instance, the tzinfo argu-</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">ment of the standard datetime constructor doesn’t work reliably for time zones with DST. Using UTC</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">is generally safe; if you’re using other time zones, you should review the <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/zoneinfo.html#module-zoneinfo">zoneinfo</a> documentation care-</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">fully.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: Python’s <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.time">datetime.time</a> objects also feature a tzinfo attribute, and PostgreSQL has a matching time with time zone type. However, as PostgreSQL’s docs put it, this type “exhibits properties which lead to questionable usefulness”.</p> <p>Django only supports naive time objects and will raise an exception if you attempt to save an aware time object, as a timezone for a time with no associated date does not make sense.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_695" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Interpretation of naive datetime objects</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When <a href="index.html#page_1936"><i>USE_TZ</i></a> is True, Django still accepts naive datetime objects, in order to preserve backwards-compatibility. When the database layer receives one, it attempts to make it aware by interpreting it in</p> <p>the <a href="index.html#page_695">default time zone</a> and raises a warning.</p> <p>Unfortunately, during DST transitions, some datetimes don’t exist or are ambiguous. That’s why you should</p> <p>always create aware datetime objects when time zone support is enabled. (See the <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/zoneinfo.html#module-zoneinfo">Using ZoneInfo section</a></p> <p><a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/zoneinfo.html#module-zoneinfo">of the zoneinfo docs</a> for examples using the fold attribute to specify the offset that should apply to a datetime during a DST transition.)</p> <p>In practice, this is rarely an issue. Django gives you aware datetime objects in the models and forms, and</p> <p>most often, new datetime objects are created from existing ones through <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.timedelta">timedelta</a> arithmetic. The only</p> <p>datetime that’s often created in application code is the current time, and <a href="index.html#page_2088"><i>timezone.now()</i></a> automatically does the right thing.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Default time zone and current time zone</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The default time zone is the time zone defined by the <a href="index.html#page_1935"><i>TIME_ZONE</i></a> setting.</p> <p>The current time zone is the time zone that’s used for rendering.</p> <p>You should set the current time zone to the end user’s actual time zone with <a href="index.html#page_2088"><i>activate()</i></a>. Otherwise, the default time zone is used.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: As explained in the documentation of <a href="index.html#page_1935"><i>TIME_ZONE</i></a> , Django sets environment variables so that its process</p> <p>runs in the default time zone. This happens regardless of the value of <a href="index.html#page_1936"><i>USE_TZ</i></a> and of the current time zone.</p> <p>When <a href="index.html#page_1936"><i>USE_TZ</i></a> is True, this is useful to preserve backwards-compatibility with applications that still rely on</p> <p>local time. However, <a href="index.html#page_695">as explained above, </a>this isn’t entirely reliable, and you should always work with aware</p> <p>datetimes in UTC in your own code. For instance, use <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp">fromtimestamp()</a> and set the tz parameter to <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.timezone.utc">utc</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Selecting the current time zone</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The current time zone is the equivalent of the current <a href="index.html#page_706">locale</a> for translations. However, there’s no equivalent of the Accept-Language HTTP header that Django could use to determine the user’s time zone automatically.</p> <p>Instead, Django provides <a href="index.html#page_2088">time zone selection functions. </a>Use them to build the time zone selection logic that makes sense for you.</p> <p>Most websites that care about time zones ask users in which time zone they live and store this information in</p> <p>the user’s profile. For anonymous users, they use the time zone of their primary audience or UTC. <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/zoneinfo.html#zoneinfo.available_timezones">zoneinfo.</a></p> <p><a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/zoneinfo.html#zoneinfo.available_timezones">available_timezones()</a> provides a set of available timezones that you can use to build a map from likely locations to time zones.</p> <p id="page_696"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Here’s an example that stores the current timezone in the session. (It skips error handling entirely for the sake of simplicity.)</p> <p>Add the following middleware to <a href="index.html#page_1923"><i>MIDDLEWARE</i></a> :</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">zoneinfo</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">timezone</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>TimezoneMiddleware</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>__init__</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, get_response):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_response</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">get_response</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>__call__</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">tzname</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">session</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"django_timezone"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">tzname:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">timezone</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">activate(zoneinfo</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ZoneInfo(tzname))</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>else</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">timezone</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">deactivate()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_response(request)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Create a view that can set the current timezone:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.shortcuts</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">redirect, render</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Prepare a map of common locations to timezone choices you wish to offer.</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">common_timezones</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"London"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Europe/London"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Paris"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Europe/Paris"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"New York"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"America/New_York"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>set_timezone</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">method</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">session[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"django_timezone"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">redirect(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>else</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">render(request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"template.html"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, {</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"timezones"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: common_timezones})</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Include a form in template.html that will POST to this view:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">tz</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get_current_timezone as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">TIME_ZONE</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">action</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>url</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'set_timezone'</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">method</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"POST"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_697" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">select</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">city</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>,</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">tz</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">tz</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">TIME_ZONE</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">selected</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endif</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">city</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">option</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endfor</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">select</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">input</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">type</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"submit"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Set"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Time zone aware input in forms</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When you enable time zone support, Django interprets datetimes entered in forms in the <a href="index.html#page_695">current time zone</a> and returns aware datetime objects in cleaned_data.</p> <p>Converted datetimes that don’t exist or are ambiguous because they fall in a DST transition will be reported as invalid values.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Time zone aware output in templates</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When you enable time zone support, Django converts aware datetime objects to the <a href="index.html#page_695">current time zone</a> when</p> <p>they’re rendered in templates. This behaves very much like <a href="index.html#page_689">format localization</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: Django doesn’t convert naive datetime objects, because they could be ambiguous, and because</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">your code should never produce naive datetimes when time zone support is enabled. However, you can</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">force conversion with the template filters described below.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Conversion to local time isn’t always appropriate – you may be generating output for computers rather than for humans. The following filters and tags, provided by the tz template tag library, allow you to control the time zone conversions.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Template tags</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>localtime</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Enables or disables conversion of aware datetime objects to the current time zone in the contained block.</p> <p>This tag has exactly the same effects as the <a href="index.html#page_1936"><i>USE_TZ</i></a> setting as far as the template engine is concerned. It allows a more fine grained control of conversion.</p> <p>To activate or deactivate conversion for a template block, use:</p> <p id="page_698"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">tz</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>localtime</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">on</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endlocaltime</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>localtime</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">off</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endlocaltime</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: The value of <a href="index.html#page_1936"><i>USE_TZ</i></a> isn’t respected inside of a {% localtime %} block.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>timezone</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Sets or unsets the current time zone in the contained block. When the current time zone is unset, the default time zone applies.</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">tz</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>timezone</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Europe/Paris"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">Paris time:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endtimezone</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>timezone None</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">Server time:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endtimezone</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>get_current_timezone</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can get the name of the current time zone using the get_current_timezone tag:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get_current_timezone as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">TIME_ZONE</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Alternatively, you can activate the <a href="index.html#page_2045"><i>tz()</i></a> context processor and use the TIME_ZONE context variable.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_699" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Template filters</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>These filters accept both aware and naive datetimes. For conversion purposes, they assume that naive date-times are in the default time zone. They always return aware datetimes.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>localtime</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Forces conversion of a single value to the current time zone.</p> <p>For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">tz</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>localtime</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>utc</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Forces conversion of a single value to UTC.</p> <p>For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">tz</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>utc</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>timezone</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Forces conversion of a single value to an arbitrary timezone.</p> <p>The argument must be an instance of a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.tzinfo">tzinfo</a> subclass or a time zone name.</p> <p>For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">tz</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>timezone</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:"Europe/Paris"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_700"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Migration guide</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Here’s how to migrate a project that was started before Django supported time zones.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Database</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>PostgreSQL</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The PostgreSQL backend stores datetimes as timestamp with time zone. In practice, this means it converts datetimes from the connection’s time zone to UTC on storage, and from UTC to the connection’s time zone on retrieval.</p> <p>As a consequence, if you’re using PostgreSQL, you can switch between USE_TZ = False and USE_TZ = True</p> <p>freely. The database connection’s time zone will be set to <a href="index.html#page_1898"><i>DATABASE-TIME_ZONE</i></a> or UTC respectively, so that Django obtains correct datetimes in all cases. You don’t need to perform any data conversions.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Time zone settings</p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_1898"><i>time zone</i></a> configured for the connection in the <a href="index.html#page_1895"><i>DATABASES</i></a> setting is distinct from the general <a href="index.html#page_1935"><i>TIME_ZONE</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Other databases</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Other backends store datetimes without time zone information. If you switch from USE_TZ = False to USE_TZ = True, you must convert your data from local time to UTC – which isn’t deterministic if your local time has DST.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Code</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The first step is to add <a href="index.html#page_1936"><i>USE_TZ = True</i></a> to your settings file. At this point, things should mostly work. If you create naive datetime objects in your code, Django makes them aware when necessary.</p> <p>However, these conversions may fail around DST transitions, which means you aren’t getting the full benefits of time zone support yet. Also, you’re likely to run into a few problems because it’s impossible to compare a naive datetime with an aware datetime. Since Django now gives you aware datetimes, you’ll get exceptions wherever you compare a datetime that comes from a model or a form with a naive datetime that you’ve created in your code.</p> <p>So the second step is to refactor your code wherever you instantiate datetime objects to make them aware.</p> <p>This can be done incrementally. <a href="index.html#page_2088"><i>django.utils.timezone</i></a> defines some handy helpers for compatibility code:</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_2088"><i>now()</i></a>, <a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>is_aware()</i></a>, <a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>is_naive()</i></a>, <a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>make_aware()</i></a><a href="index.html#page_2089">, </a>and <a href="index.html#page_2089"><i>make_naive()</i></a><a href="index.html#page_2089">.</a></p> <p id="page_701" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Finally, in order to help you locate code that needs upgrading, Django raises a warning when you attempt to save a naive datetime to the database:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">RuntimeWarning: DateTimeField ModelName.field_name received a naive</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime (2012-01-01 00:00:00) while time zone support is active.</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>During development, you can turn such warnings into exceptions and get a traceback by adding the following to your settings file:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">warnings</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">warnings</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filterwarnings(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"error"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">r"DateTimeField .* received a naive datetime"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>RuntimeWarning</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">r"django\.db\.models\.fields"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Fixtures</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When serializing an aware datetime, the UTC offset is included, like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">"2011-09-01T13:20:30+03:00"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>While for a naive datetime, it isn’t:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">"2011-09-01T13:20:30"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>For models with <a href="index.html#page_1630"><i>DateTimeField</i></a>s, this difference makes it impossible to write a fixture that works both with and without time zone support.</p> <p>Fixtures generated with USE_TZ = False, or before Django 1.4, use the “naive” format. If your project con-</p> <p>tains such fixtures, after you enable time zone support, you’ll see <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#RuntimeWarning">RuntimeWarning</a>s when you load them. To get rid of the warnings, you must convert your fixtures to the “aware” format.</p> <p>You can regenerate fixtures with <a href="index.html#page_1441"><i>loaddata</i></a> then <a href="index.html#page_1438"><i>dumpdata</i></a>. Or, if they’re small enough, you can edit them to</p> <p>add the UTC offset that matches your <a href="index.html#page_1935"><i>TIME_ZONE</i></a> to each serialized datetime.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_702"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>FAQ</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Setup</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. I don’t need multiple time zones. Should I enable time zone support?</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Yes. When time zone support is enabled, Django uses a more accurate model of local time. This shields you from subtle and unreproducible bugs around daylight saving time (DST) transitions.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">When you enable time zone support, you’ll encounter some errors because you’re using naive datetimes where Django expects aware datetimes. Such errors show up when running tests. You’ll quickly learn how to avoid invalid operations.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">On the other hand, bugs caused by the lack of time zone support are much harder to prevent, diagnose and fix. Anything that involves scheduled tasks or datetime arithmetic is a candidate for subtle bugs that will bite you only once or twice a year.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For these reasons, time zone support is enabled by default in new projects, and you should keep it unless you have a very good reason not to.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. I’ve enabled time zone support. Am I safe?</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Maybe. You’re better protected from DST-related bugs, but you can still shoot yourself in the foot by carelessly turning naive datetimes into aware datetimes, and vice-versa.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If your application connects to other systems – for instance, if it queries a web service – make sure datetimes are properly specified. To transmit datetimes safely, their representation should include the UTC offset, or their values should be in UTC (or both!).</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Finally, our calendar system contains interesting edge cases. For example, you can’t always subtract one year directly from a given date:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> style="font-size:0.87em"><b>one_year_before</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(value):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Wrong example.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">year</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>-</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">one_year_before(datetime</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">2012</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">3</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">10</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">0</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">))</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime.datetime(2011, 3, 1, 10, 0)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">one_year_before(datetime</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">2012</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">2</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">29</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">10</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">0</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">))</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">Traceback (most recent call last):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i>...</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">ValueError</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: day is out of range for month</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">To implement such a function correctly, you must decide whether 2012-02-29 minus one year is 2011-02-28 or 2011-03-01, which depends on your business requirements.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">3. How do I interact with a database that stores datetimes in local time?</p> <p style="text-align:center">Set the <a href="index.html#page_1898"><i>TIME_ZONE</i></a> option to the appropriate time zone for this database in the <a href="index.html#page_1895"><i>DATABASES</i></a> setting.</p> <p id="page_703" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This is useful for connecting to a database that doesn’t support time zones and that isn’t managed by</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Django when <a href="index.html#page_1936"><i>USE_TZ</i></a> is True.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Troubleshooting</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. My application crashes with TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">datetimes – what’s wrong?</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Let’s reproduce this error by comparing a naive and an aware datetime:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">timezone</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">aware</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">timezone</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">now()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">naive</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">timezone</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">make_naive(aware)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">naive</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">aware</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">Traceback (most recent call last):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i>...</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">TypeError</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you encounter this error, most likely your code is comparing these two things:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• a datetime provided by Django – for instance, a value read from a form or a model field. Since</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">you enabled time zone support, it’s aware.</p> <p style="text-align:center">• a datetime generated by your code, which is naive (or you wouldn’t be reading this).</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Generally, the correct solution is to change your code to use an aware datetime instead.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you’re writing a pluggable application that’s expected to work independently of the value of <a href="index.html#page_1936"><i>USE_TZ</i></a>,</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">you may find <a href="index.html#page_2088"><i>django.utils.timezone.now()</i></a> useful. This function returns the current date and time as a naive datetime when USE_TZ = False and as an aware datetime when USE_TZ = True. You can</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">add or subtract <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.timedelta">datetime.timedelta</a> as needed.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. I see lots of RuntimeWarning: DateTimeField received a naive datetime <span style="float:right">(YYYY-MM-DD</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">HH:MM:SS) while time zone support is active – is that bad?</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">When time zone support is enabled, the database layer expects to receive only aware datetimes from your code. This warning occurs when it receives a naive datetime. This indicates that you haven’t</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">finished porting your code for time zone support. Please refer to the <a href="index.html#page_700">migration guide</a> for tips on this process.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">In the meantime, for backwards compatibility, the datetime is considered to be in the default time zone, which is generally what you expect.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">3. now.date() is yesterday! (or tomorrow)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you’ve always used naive datetimes, you probably believe that you can convert a datetime to a date</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">by calling its <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime.date">date()</a> method. You also consider that a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.date">date</a> is a lot like a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime">datetime</a>, except that it’s less accurate.</p> <p id="page_704"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">None of this is true in a time zone aware environment:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span
