style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">separator</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>!=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">","</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"separator"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">separator</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">name, path, args, kwargs</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>More complex examples are beyond the scope of this document, but remember - for any configuration of your Field instance, deconstruct() must return arguments that you can pass to __init__ to reconstruct that state.</p> <p>Pay extra attention if you set new default values for arguments in the Field superclass; you want to make sure they’re always included, rather than disappearing if they take on the old default value.</p> <p>In addition, try to avoid returning values as positional arguments; where possible, return values as keyword arguments for maximum future compatibility. If you change the names of things more often than their position in the constructor’s argument list, you might prefer positional, but bear in mind that people will be reconstructing your field from the serialized version for quite a while (possibly years), depending how long your migrations live for.</p> <p>You can see the results of deconstruction by looking in migrations that include the field, and you can test deconstruction in unit tests by deconstructing and reconstructing the field:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">name, path, args, kwargs</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">my_field_instance</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">deconstruct()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">new_instance</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">MyField(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>*</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">args,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">assertEqual(my_field_instance</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">some_attribute, new_instance</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">some_attribute)</span></p> <p id="page_783" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Field attributes not affecting database column definition</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can override Field.non_db_attrs to customize attributes of a field that don’t affect a column definition. It’s used during model migrations to detect no-op AlterField operations.</p> <p>For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>CommaSepField</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Field):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@property</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>non_db_attrs</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">non_db_attrs</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>+</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"separator"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Changing a custom field’s base class</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can’t change the base class of a custom field because Django won’t detect the change and make a mi-gration for it. For example, if you start with:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>CustomCharField</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>and then decide that you want to use TextField instead, you can’t change the subclass like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>CustomCharField</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">TextField):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Instead, you must create a new custom field class and update your models to reference it:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>CustomCharField</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>CustomTextField</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">TextField):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>As discussed in <a href="index.html#page_456">removing fields</a>, you must retain the original CustomCharField class as long as you have migrations that reference it.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Documenting your custom field</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>As always, you should document your field type, so users will know what it is. In addition to providing a docstring for it, which is useful for developers, you can also allow users of the admin app to see a short</p> <p>description of the field type via the <a href="index.html#page_1034">django.contrib.admindocs</a> application. To do this provide descriptive</p> <p>text in a <a href="index.html#page_1656"><i>description</i></a> class attribute of your custom field. In the above example, the description displayed by the admindocs application for a HandField will be ‘A hand of cards (bridge style)’.</p> <p>In the <a href="index.html#page_1034"><i>django.contrib.admindocs</i></a> display, the field description is interpolated with field.__dict__ which</p> <p>allows the description to incorporate arguments of the field. For example, the description for <a href="index.html#page_1628"><i>CharField</i></a> is:</p> <p id="page_784"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">description</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">_(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"String (up to %(max_length)s)"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Useful methods</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Once you’ve created your <a href="index.html#page_1656"><i>Field</i></a> subclass, you might consider overriding a few standard methods, depending on your field’s behavior. The list of methods below is in approximately decreasing order of importance, so start from the top.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Custom database types</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Say you’ve created a PostgreSQL custom type called mytype. You can subclass Field and implement the</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1657"><i>db_type()</i></a> method, like so:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MytypeField</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Field):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>db_type</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, connection):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"mytype"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Once you have MytypeField, you can use it in any model, just like any other Field type:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Person</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Model):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">80</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">something_else</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">MytypeField()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you aim to build a database-agnostic application, you should account for differences in database column types. For example, the date/time column type in PostgreSQL is called timestamp, while the same column in</p> <p>MySQL is called datetime. You can handle this in a <a href="index.html#page_1657"><i>db_type()</i></a> method by checking the connection.vendor attribute. Current built-in vendor names are: sqlite, postgresql, mysql, and oracle.</p> <p>For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyDateField</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Field):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>db_type</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, connection):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">connection</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">vendor</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"mysql"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"datetime"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>else</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"timestamp"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_1657"><i>db_type()</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1657"><i>rel_db_type()</i></a> methods are called by Django when the framework constructs the CREATE TABLE statements for your application – that is, when you first create your tables. The methods are also</p> <p id="page_785" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>called when constructing a WHERE clause that includes the model field – that is, when you retrieve data using QuerySet methods like get(), filter(), and exclude() and have the model field as an argument.</p> <p>Some database column types accept parameters, such as CHAR(25), where the parameter 25 represents the maximum column length. In cases like these, it’s more flexible if the parameter is specified in the model rather than being hard-coded in the db_type() method. For example, it wouldn’t make much sense to have a CharMaxlength25Field, shown here:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># This is a silly example of hard-coded parameters.</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>CharMaxlength25Field</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Field):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>db_type</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, connection):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"char(25)"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># In the model:</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyModel</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Model):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">my_field</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">CharMaxlength25Field()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The better way of doing this would be to make the parameter specifiable at run time – i.e., when the class is instantiated. To do that, implement Field.__init__(), like so:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># This is a much more flexible example.</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>BetterCharField</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Field):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>__init__</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, max_length,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>*</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">args,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">max_length</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">max_length</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>__init__</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>*</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">args,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>db_type</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, connection):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"char(%s)"</span> <span style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">my_field</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">BetterCharField(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">25</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Finally, if your column requires truly complex SQL setup, return None from <a href="index.html#page_1657"><i>db_type()</i>. </a>This will cause Django’s SQL creation code to skip over this field. You are then responsible for creating the column in the right table in some other way, but this gives you a way to tell Django to get out of the way.</p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_1657"><i>rel_db_type()</i></a> method is called by fields such as ForeignKey and OneToOneField that point to another field to determine their database column data types. For example, if you have an UnsignedAutoField, you also need the foreign keys that point to that field to use the same data type:</p> <p id="page_786"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># MySQL unsigned integer (range 0 to 4294967295).</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>UnsignedAutoField</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">AutoField):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"integer UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>rel_db_type</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, connection):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"integer UNSIGNED"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Converting values to Python objects</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If your custom <a href="index.html#page_1656"><i>Field</i></a> class deals with data structures that are more complex than strings, dates, integers, or</p> <p>floats, then you may need to override <a href="index.html#page_1657"><i>from_db_value()</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1658"><i>to_python()</i></a><a href="index.html#page_1658">.</a></p> <p>If present for the field subclass, from_db_value() will be called in all circumstances when the data is loaded</p> <p>from the database, including in aggregates and <a href="index.html#page_1716"><i>values()</i></a> calls.</p> <p>to_python() is called by deserialization and during the <a href="index.html#page_1693"><i>clean()</i></a> method used from forms.</p> <p>As a general rule, to_python() should deal gracefully with any of the following arguments:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• An instance of the correct type (e.g., Hand in our ongoing example).</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• A string</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• None (if the field allows null=True)</p> <p>In our HandField class, we’re storing the data as a VARCHAR field in the database, so we need to be able to process strings and None in the from_db_value(). </p> <p>Notice that we always return a Hand instance from these methods. That’s the Python object type we want to store in the model’s attribute.</p> <p>For to_python(), if anything goes wrong during value conversion, you should raise a <a href="index.html#page_1473"><i>ValidationError</i></a> exception.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Converting Python objects to query values</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Since using a database requires conversion in both ways, if you override <a href="index.html#page_1657"><i>from_db_value()</i></a> you also have to</p> <p>override <a href="index.html#page_1657"><i>get_prep_value()</i></a> to convert Python objects back to query values.</p> <p>For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>HandField</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Field):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get_prep_value</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, value):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">""</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">join(</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">""</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">join(l)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">l</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">north, value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">east, value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">south, value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">west)]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: If your custom field uses the CHAR, VARCHAR or TEXT types for MySQL, you must make sure that</p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_1657"><i>get_prep_value()</i></a> always returns a string type. MySQL performs flexible and unexpected matching</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">when a query is performed on these types and the provided value is an integer, which can cause queries</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">to include unexpected objects in their results. This problem cannot occur if you always return a string <b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p id="page_788" style="margin-left:1em">type from <a href="index.html#page_1657"><i>get_prep_value()</i>.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Converting query values to database values</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Some data types (for example, dates) need to be in a specific format before they can be used by a database</p> <p>backend. <a href="index.html#page_1657"><i>get_db_prep_value()</i></a> is the method where those conversions should be made. The specific connec-tion that will be used for the query is passed as the connection parameter. This allows you to use backend-specific conversion logic if it is required.</p> <p>For example, Django uses the following method for its <a href="index.html#page_1627"><i>BinaryField</i>:</a></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get_db_prep_value</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, value, connection, prepared</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=False</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_db_prep_value(value, connection, prepared)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>is not None</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">connection</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Database</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Binary(value)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>In case your custom field needs a special conversion when being saved that is not the same as the conversion</p> <p>used for normal query parameters, you can override <a href="index.html#page_1658"><i>get_db_prep_save()</i>.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Preprocessing values before saving</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you want to preprocess the value just before saving, you can use <a href="index.html#page_1658"><i>pre_save()</i></a>. For example, Django’s</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1630"><i>DateTimeField</i></a> uses this method to set the attribute correctly in the case of <a href="index.html#page_1628"><i>auto_now</i></a> or <a href="index.html#page_1629"><i>auto_now_add</i></a>.</p> <p>If you do override this method, you must return the value of the attribute at the end. You should also update the model’s attribute if you make any changes to the value so that code holding references to the model will always see the correct value.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Specifying the form field for a model field</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To customize the form field used by <a href="index.html#page_365"><i>ModelForm</i></a>, you can override <a href="index.html#page_1658"><i>formfield()</i></a><a href="index.html#page_1658">.</a></p> <p>The form field class can be specified via the form_class and choices_form_class arguments; the latter is</p> <p>used if the field has choices specified, the former otherwise. If these arguments are not provided, <a href="index.html#page_1526"><i>CharField</i></a></p> <p>or <a href="index.html#page_1538"><i>TypedChoiceField</i></a> will be used.</p> <p>All of the kwargs dictionary is passed directly to the form field’s __init__() method. Normally, all you need to do is set up a good default for the form_class (and maybe choices_form_class) argument and then delegate further handling to the parent class. This might require you to write a custom form field (and even</p> <p>a form widget). See the <a href="index.html#page_328">forms documentation</a> for information about this.</p> <p id="page_789" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you wish to exclude the field from the <a href="index.html#page_365"><i>ModelForm</i></a>, you can override the <a href="index.html#page_1658"><i>formfield()</i></a> method to return None.</p> <p>Continuing our ongoing example, we can write the <a href="index.html#page_1658"><i>formfield()</i></a> method as:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>HandField</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Field):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>formfield</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Exclude the field from the ModelForm when some condition is met.</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">some_condition</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">some_condition:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return None</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Set up some defaults while letting the caller override them.</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">defaults</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"form_class"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: MyFormField}</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">defaults</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">update(kwargs)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">formfield(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">defaults)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This assumes we’ve imported a MyFormField field class (which has its own default widget). This document doesn’t cover the details of writing custom form fields.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Emulating built-in field types</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you have created a <a href="index.html#page_1657"><i>db_type()</i></a> method, you don’t need to worry about <a href="index.html#page_1656"><i>get_internal_type()</i></a> – it won’t be used much. Sometimes, though, your database storage is similar in type to some other field, so you can use that other field’s logic to create the right column.</p> <p>For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>HandField</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Field):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get_internal_type</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"CharField"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>No matter which database backend we are using, this will mean that <a href="index.html#page_1446"><i>migrate</i></a> and other SQL commands create the right column type for storing a string.</p> <p>If <a href="index.html#page_1656"><i>get_internal_type()</i></a> returns a string that is not known to Django for the database backend you are using – that is, it doesn’t appear in django.db.backends.<db_name>.base.DatabaseWrapper.data_types</p> <p>– the string will still be used by the serializer, but the default <a href="index.html#page_1657"><i>db_type()</i></a> method will return None. See the</p> <p>documentation of <a href="index.html#page_1657"><i>db_type()</i></a> for reasons why this might be useful. Putting a descriptive string in as the type of the field for the serializer is a useful idea if you’re ever going to be using the serializer output in some other place, outside of Django.</p> <p id="page_790"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Converting field data for serialization</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To customize how the values are serialized by a serializer, you can override <a href="index.html#page_1658"><i>value_to_string()</i></a>. Using</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1658"><i>value_from_object()</i></a> is the best way to get the field’s value prior to serialization. For example, since HandField uses strings for its data storage anyway, we can reuse some existing conversion code:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>HandField</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Field):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>value_to_string</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, obj):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">value_from_object(obj)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_prep_value(value)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Some general advice</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Writing a custom field can be a tricky process, particularly if you’re doing complex conversions between your Python types and your database and serialization formats. Here are a couple of tips to make things go more smoothly:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. Look at the existing Django fields (in <a href="https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/db/models/fields/__init__.py">django/db/models/fields/__init__.py</a>) for inspiration. Try to find a</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">field that’s similar to what you want and extend it a little bit, instead of creating an entirely new field from scratch.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. Put a __str__() method on the class you’re wrapping up as a field. There are a lot of places where the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">default behavior of the field code is to call str() on the value. (In our examples in this document, value would be a Hand instance, not a HandField). So if your __str__() method automatically converts to the string form of your Python object, you can save yourself a lot of work.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Writing a FileField subclass</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>In addition to the above methods, fields that deal with files have a few other special requirements which must be taken into account. The majority of the mechanics provided by FileField, such as controlling database storage and retrieval, can remain unchanged, leaving subclasses to deal with the challenge of supporting a particular type of file.</p> <p>Django provides a File class, which is used as a proxy to the file’s contents and operations. This can be subclassed to customize how the file is accessed, and what methods are available. It lives at django.db.</p> <p>models.fields.files, and its default behavior is explained in the <a href="index.html#page_1476">file documentation.</a></p> <p>Once a subclass of File is created, the new FileField subclass must be told to use it. To do so, assign the new File subclass to the special attr_class attribute of the FileField subclass.</p> <p id="page_791" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>A few suggestions</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>In addition to the above details, there are a few guidelines which can greatly improve the efficiency and readability of the field’s code.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. The source for Django’s own ImageField (in <a href="https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/db/models/fields/files.py">django/db/models/fields/files.py</a>) is a great example of</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">how to subclass FileField to support a particular type of file, as it incorporates all of the techniques described above.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. Cache file attributes wherever possible. Since files may be stored in remote storage systems, retrieving</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">them may cost extra time, or even money, that isn’t always necessary. Once a file is retrieved to obtain some data about its content, cache as much of that data as possible to reduce the number of times the file must be retrieved on subsequent calls for that information.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>4.1.4 How to create database migrations</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This document explains how to structure and write database migrations for different scenarios you might</p> <p>encounter. For introductory material on migrations, see <a href="index.html#page_446">the topic guide.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Data migrations and multiple databases</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When using multiple databases, you may need to figure out whether or not to run a migration against a particular database. For example, you may want to only run a migration on a particular database.</p> <p>In order to do that you can check the database connection’s alias inside a RunPython operation by looking at the schema_editor.connection.alias attribute:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>forwards</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(apps, schema_editor):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">schema_editor</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">connection</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">alias</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>!=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Your migration code goes here</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Migration</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Migration):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">dependencies</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Dependencies to other migrations</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">operations</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">RunPython(forwards),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p id="page_792"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can also provide hints that will be passed to the <a href="index.html#page_223"><i>allow_migrate()</i></a> method of database routers as **hints:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">Listing 1: myapp/dbrouters.py</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyRouter</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>allow_migrate</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, db, app_label, model_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=None</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">hints):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"target_db"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">hints:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">hints[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"target_db"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return True</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Then, to leverage this in your migrations, do the following:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>forwards</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(apps, schema_editor):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Your migration code goes here</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Migration</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Migration):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">dependencies</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Dependencies to other migrations</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">operations</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">RunPython(forwards, hints</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"target_db"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">}),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If your RunPython or RunSQL operation only affects one model, it’s good practice to pass model_name as a hint to make it as transparent as possible to the router. This is especially important for reusable and third-party apps.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Migrations that add unique fields</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Applying a “plain” migration that adds a unique non-nullable field to a table with existing rows will raise an error because the value used to populate existing rows is generated only once, thus breaking the unique constraint.</p> <p>Therefore, the following steps should be taken. In this example, we’ll add a non-nullable <a href="index.html#page_1643"><i>UUIDField</i></a> with a default value. Modify the respective field according to your needs.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Add the field on your model with default=uuid.uuid4 and unique=True arguments (choose an ap-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">propriate default for the type of the field you’re adding).</p> <p id="page_793" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Run the <a href="index.html#page_1444"><i>makemigrations</i></a> command. This should generate a migration with an AddField operation.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Generate two empty migration files for the same app by running makemigrations myapp --empty</p> <p style="text-align:center">twice. We’ve renamed the migration files to give them meaningful names in the examples below.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Copy the AddField operation from the auto-generated migration (the first of the three new files) to the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">last migration, change AddField to AlterField, and add imports of uuid and models. For example:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">Listing 2: 0006_remove_uuid_null.py</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Generated by Django A.B on YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations, models</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">uuid</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Migration</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Migration):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">dependencies</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"myapp"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"0005_populate_uuid_values"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">operations</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">AlterField(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">model_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"mymodel"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"uuid"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">field</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">UUIDField(default</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">uuid</span><span style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Edit the first migration file. The generated migration class should look similar to this:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">Listing 3: 0004_add_uuid_field.py</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Migration</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Migration):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">dependencies</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"myapp"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"0003_auto_20150129_1705"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">operations</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">AddField(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">model_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"mymodel"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"uuid"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">field</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">UUIDField(default</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">uuid</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">uuid4, unique</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Change unique=True to null=True – this will create the intermediary null field and defer creating the unique constraint until we’ve populated unique values on all the rows.</p> <p id="page_794"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• In the first empty migration file, add a <a href="index.html#page_1609"><i>RunPython</i></a> or <a href="index.html#page_1607"><i>RunSQL</i></a> operation to generate a unique value (UUID</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">in the example) for each existing row. Also add an import of uuid. For example:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">Listing 4: 0005_populate_uuid_values.py</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Generated by Django A.B on YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">uuid</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>gen_uuid</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(apps, schema_editor):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">MyModel</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">apps</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_model(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"myapp"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"MyModel"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">row</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">MyModel</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">all():</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">row</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">uuid</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">uuid</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">uuid4()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">row</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save(update_fields</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"uuid"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">])</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Migration</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Migration):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">dependencies</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"myapp"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"0004_add_uuid_field"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">operations</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># omit reverse_code=... if you don't want the migration to be reversible.</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">RunPython(gen_uuid, reverse_code</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">RunPython</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">noop),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Now you can apply the migrations as usual with the <a href="index.html#page_1446"><i>migrate</i></a> command.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Note there is a race condition if you allow objects to be created while this migration is running. Objects created after the AddField and before RunPython will have their original uuid’s overwritten.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Non-atomic migrations</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>On databases that support DDL transactions (SQLite and PostgreSQL), migrations will run inside a transac-tion by default. For use cases such as performing data migrations on large tables, you may want to prevent a migration from running in a transaction by setting the atomic attribute to False:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Migration</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Migration):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">atomic</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>= False</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Within such a migration, all operations are run without a transaction. It’s possible to execute parts of the</p> <p id="page_795" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>migration inside a transaction using <a href="index.html#page_209"><i>atomic()</i></a> or by passing atomic=True to RunPython.</p> <p>Here’s an example of a non-atomic data migration that updates a large table in smaller batches:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">uuid</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations, transaction</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>gen_uuid</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(apps, schema_editor):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">MyModel</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">apps</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_model(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"myapp"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"MyModel"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>while</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">MyModel</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(uuid__isnull</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">exists():</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>with</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">transaction</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">atomic():</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">row</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">MyModel</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(uuid__isnull</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)[:</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1000</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">row</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">uuid</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">uuid</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">uuid4()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">row</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Migration</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Migration):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">atomic</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>= False</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">operations</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">RunPython(gen_uuid),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The atomic attribute doesn’t have an effect on databases that don’t support DDL transactions (e.g. MySQL,</p> <p>Oracle). (MySQL’s <a href="https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/en/atomic-ddl.html">atomic DDL statement support</a> refers to individual statements rather than multiple state-ments wrapped in a transaction that can be rolled back.)</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Controlling the order of migrations</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django determines the order in which migrations should be applied not by the filename of each migration, but by building a graph using two properties on the Migration class: dependencies and run_before.</p> <p>If you’ve used the <a href="index.html#page_1444"><i>makemigrations</i></a> command you’ve probably already seen dependencies in action because auto-created migrations have this defined as part of their creation process.</p> <p>The dependencies property is declared like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Migration</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Migration):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">dependencies</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"myapp"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"0123_the_previous_migration"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p id="page_796"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Usually this will be enough, but from time to time you may need to ensure that your migration runs be-fore other migrations. This is useful, for example, to make third-party apps’ migrations run after your</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>AUTH_USER_MODEL</i></a> replacement.</p> <p>To achieve this, place all migrations that should depend on yours in the run_before attribute on your Migration class:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Migration</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Migration):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">run_before</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"third_party_app"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"0001_do_awesome"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Prefer using dependencies over run_before when possible. You should only use run_before if it is unde-sirable or impractical to specify dependencies in the migration which you want to run after the one you are writing.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Migrating data between third-party apps</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can use a data migration to move data from one third-party application to another.</p> <p>If you plan to remove the old app later, you’ll need to set the dependencies property based on whether or not the old app is installed. Otherwise, you’ll have missing dependencies once you uninstall the old app.</p> <p>Similarly, you’ll need to catch <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#LookupError">LookupError</a> in the apps.get_model() call that retrieves models from the old app. This approach allows you to deploy your project anywhere without first installing and then uninstalling the old app.</p> <p>Here’s a sample migration:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">Listing 5: myapp/migrations/0124_move_old_app_to_new_app. py</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.apps</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">apps</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">global_apps</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>forwards</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(apps, schema_editor):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>try</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">OldModel</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">apps</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_model(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"old_app"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"OldModel"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>except</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>LookupError</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># The old app isn't installed.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">NewModel</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">apps</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_model(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"new_app"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"NewModel"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_797" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">NewModel</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">bulk_create(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">NewModel(new_attribute</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">old_object</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">old_attribute)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">old_object</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">OldModel</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">all()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Migration</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Migration):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">operations</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">RunPython(forwards, migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">RunPython</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">noop),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">dependencies</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"myapp"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"0123_the_previous_migration"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"new_app"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"0001_initial"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">global_apps</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">is_installed(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"old_app"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">dependencies</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">append((</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"old_app"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"0001_initial"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">))</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Also consider what you want to happen when the migration is unapplied. You could either do nothing (as in the example above) or remove some or all of the data from the new application. Adjust the second argument</p> <p>of the <a href="index.html#page_1609"><i>RunPython</i></a> operation accordingly.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Changing a ManyToManyField to use a through model</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you change a <a href="index.html#page_1649"><i>ManyToManyField</i></a> to use a through model, the default migration will delete the existing table</p> <p>and create a new one, losing the existing relations. To avoid this, you can use <a href="index.html#page_1611"><i>SeparateDatabaseAndState</i></a> to rename the existing table to the new table name while telling the migration autodetector that the new</p> <p>model has been created. You can check the existing table name through <a href="index.html#page_1452"><i>sqlmigrate</i></a> or <a href="index.html#page_1436"><i>dbshell</i></a><a href="index.html#page_1436">. </a>You can check the new table name with the through model’s _meta.db_table property. Your new through model should use the same names for the ForeignKeys as Django did. Also if it needs any extra fields, they should be added in operations after <a href="index.html#page_1611"><i>SeparateDatabaseAndState</i>.</a></p> <p>For example, if we had a Book model with a ManyToManyField linking to Author, we could add a through model AuthorBook with a new field is_primary, like so:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations, models</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db.models.deletion</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Migration</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Migration):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">dependencies</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"core"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"0001_initial"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_798"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">operations</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">SeparateDatabaseAndState(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Old table name from checking with sqlmigrate, new table</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># name from AuthorBook._meta.db_table.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">RunSQL(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:8em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">sql</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"ALTER TABLE core_book_authors RENAME TO core_authorbook"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">reverse_sql</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span <p style="margin-left:10em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"id"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:10em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">AutoField(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:12em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">auto_created</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=False</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:12em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">verbose_name</span><span <p style="margin-left:9em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:9em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:10em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:9em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:9em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:10em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"book"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:10em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ForeignKey(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:12em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">on_delete</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">django</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">db</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">deletion</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">DO_NOTHING,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:12em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">to</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"core.Book"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:10em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:9em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:8em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">AlterField(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:8em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">model_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span
