style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"authors"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_799" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:8em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">field</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ManyToManyField(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:9em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">to</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"core.Author"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:9em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">through</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"core.AuthorBook"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:8em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">migrations</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">AddField(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">model_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"authorbook"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"is_primary"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">field</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">BooleanField(default</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=False</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Changing an unmanaged model to managed</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you want to change an unmanaged model (<a href="index.html#page_1681"><i>managed=False</i>) </a>to managed, you must remove managed=False and generate a migration before making other schema-related changes to the model, since schema changes that appear in the migration that contains the operation to change Meta.managed may not be applied.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>4.1.5 How to write custom lookups</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django offers a wide variety of <a href="index.html#page_1762">built-in lookups</a> for filtering (for example, exact and icontains). This doc-umentation explains how to write custom lookups and how to alter the working of existing lookups. For the</p> <p>API references of lookups, see the <a href="index.html#page_1781">Lookup API reference</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>A lookup example</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Let’s start with a small custom lookup. We will write a custom lookup ne which works opposite to exact. Author.objects.filter(name__ne='Jack') will translate to the SQL:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">"author"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b><></b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'Jack'</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This SQL is backend independent, so we don’t need to worry about different databases.</p> <p>There are two steps to making this work. Firstly we need to implement the lookup, then we need to tell Django about it:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Lookup</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>NotEqual</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Lookup):</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_800"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">lookup_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"ne"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as_sql</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, compiler, connection):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">lhs, lhs_params</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">process_lhs(compiler, connection)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">rhs, rhs_params</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">process_rhs(compiler, connection)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">params</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">lhs_params</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>+</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">rhs_params</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"%s <> %s"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(lhs, rhs), params</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To register the NotEqual lookup we will need to call register_lookup on the field class we want the lookup to be available for. In this case, the lookup makes sense on all Field subclasses, so we register it with Field directly:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Field</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">Field</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">register_lookup(NotEqual)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Lookup registration can also be done using a decorator pattern:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Field</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@Field</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">register_lookup</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>NotEqualLookup</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Lookup):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>We can now use foo__ne for any field foo. You will need to ensure that this registration happens before you try to create any querysets using it. You could place the implementation in a models.py file, or register the lookup in the ready() method of an AppConfig.</p> <p>Taking a closer look at the implementation, the first required attribute is lookup_name. This allows the ORM to understand how to interpret name__ne and use NotEqual to generate the SQL. By convention, these names are always lowercase strings containing only letters, but the only hard requirement is that it must not contain the string __.</p> <p>We then need to define the as_sql method. This takes a SQLCompiler object, called compiler, and the active database connection. SQLCompiler objects are not documented, but the only thing we need to know about them is that they have a compile() method which returns a tuple containing an SQL string, and the parameters to be interpolated into that string. In most cases, you don’t need to use it directly and can pass it on to process_lhs() and process_rhs().</p> <p>A Lookup works against two values, lhs and rhs, standing for left-hand side and right-hand side. The left-</p> <p>hand side is usually a field reference, but it can be anything implementing the <a href="index.html#page_1783">query expression API. </a>The right-hand is the value given by the user. In the example Author.objects.filter(name__ne='Jack'), the left-hand side is a reference to the name field of the Author model, and 'Jack' is the right-hand side.</p> <p>We call process_lhs and process_rhs to convert them into the values we need for SQL using the compiler</p> <p id="page_801" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>object described before. These methods return tuples containing some SQL and the parameters to be interpo-lated into that SQL, just as we need to return from our as_sql method. In the above example, process_lhs returns ('"author"."name"', []) and process_rhs returns ('"%s"', ['Jack']). In this example there were no parameters for the left hand side, but this would depend on the object we have, so we still need to include them in the parameters we return.</p> <p>Finally we combine the parts into an SQL expression with <>, and supply all the parameters for the query. We then return a tuple containing the generated SQL string and the parameters.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>A transformer example</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The custom lookup above is great, but in some cases you may want to be able to chain lookups together. For example, let’s suppose we are building an application where we want to make use of the abs() op-erator. We have an Experiment model which records a start value, end value, and the change (start -end). We would like to find all experiments where the change was equal to a certain amount (Experiment. objects.filter(change__abs=27)), or where it did not exceed a certain amount (Experiment.objects. filter(change__abs__lt=27)).</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: This example is somewhat contrived, but it nicely demonstrates the range of functionality which is possible in a database backend independent manner, and without duplicating functionality already in Django.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>We will start by writing an AbsoluteValue transformer. This will use the SQL function ABS() to transform the value before comparison:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Transform</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AbsoluteValue</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Transform):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">lookup_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"abs"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">function</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"ABS"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Next, let’s register it for IntegerField:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">IntegerField</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">IntegerField</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">register_lookup(AbsoluteValue)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>We can now run the queries we had before. Experiment.objects.filter(change__abs=27) will generate the following SQL:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>SELECT</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>WHERE ABS</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"experiments"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"change"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">27</span></p> <p id="page_802"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>By using Transform instead of Lookup it means we are able to chain further lookups afterward. So Experiment.objects.filter(change__abs__lt=27) will generate the following SQL:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>SELECT</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>WHERE ABS</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"experiments"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"change"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b><</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">27</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note that in case there is no other lookup specified, Django interprets change__abs=27 as change__abs__exact=27.</p> <p>This also allows the result to be used in ORDER BY and DISTINCT ON clauses. For example Experiment. objects.order_by('change__abs') generates:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>SELECT</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ORDER BY ABS</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"experiments"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"change"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ASC</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>And on databases that support distinct on fields (such as PostgreSQL), Experiment.objects. distinct('change__abs') generates:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>SELECT</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>DISTINCT ON ABS</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"experiments"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"change"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When looking for which lookups are allowable after the Transform has been applied, Django uses the output_field attribute. We didn’t need to specify this here as it didn’t change, but supposing we were ap-plying AbsoluteValue to some field which represents a more complex type (for example a point relative to an origin, or a complex number) then we may have wanted to specify that the transform returns a FloatField type for further lookups. This can be done by adding an output_field attribute to the transform:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">FloatField, Transform</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AbsoluteValue</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Transform):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">lookup_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"abs"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">function</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"ABS"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@property</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>output_field</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">FloatField()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This ensures that further lookups like abs__lte behave as they would for a FloatField.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Writing an efficient abs__lt lookup</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When using the above written abs lookup, the SQL produced will not use indexes efficiently in some cases. In particular, when we use change__abs__lt=27, this is equivalent to change__gt=-27 AND change__lt=27. (For the lte case we could use the SQL BETWEEN).</p> <p>So we would like Experiment.objects.filter(change__abs__lt=27) to generate the following SQL:</p> <p id="page_803" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>SELECT</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">..</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>WHERE</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"experiments"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"change"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b><</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">27</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AND</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"experiments"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"change"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>> -</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">27</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The implementation is:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Lookup</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AbsoluteValueLessThan</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Lookup):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">lookup_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"lt"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as_sql</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, compiler, connection):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">lhs, lhs_params</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">compiler</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">compile(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">lhs</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">lhs)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">rhs, rhs_params</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">process_rhs(compiler, connection)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">params</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">lhs_params</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>+</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">rhs_params</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>+</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">lhs_params</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>+</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">rhs_params</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"%s < %s AND %s > -%s"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(lhs, rhs, lhs, rhs), params</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">AbsoluteValue</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">register_lookup(AbsoluteValueLessThan)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>There are a couple of notable things going on. First, AbsoluteValueLessThan isn’t calling process_lhs(). Instead it skips the transformation of the lhs done by AbsoluteValue and uses the original lhs. That is, we want to get "experiments"."change" not ABS("experiments"."change"). Referring directly to self. lhs.lhs is safe as AbsoluteValueLessThan can be accessed only from the AbsoluteValue lookup, that is the lhs is always an instance of AbsoluteValue.</p> <p>Notice also that as both sides are used multiple times in the query the params need to contain lhs_params and rhs_params multiple times.</p> <p>The final query does the inversion (27 to-27) directly in the database. The reason for doing this is that if the self.rhs is something else than a plain integer value (for example an F() reference) we can’t do the transformations in Python.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: In fact, most lookups with __abs could be implemented as range queries like this, and on most database backends it is likely to be more sensible to do so as you can make use of the indexes. However with PostgreSQL you may want to add an index on abs(change) which would allow these queries to be very efficient.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_804"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>A bilateral transformer example</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The AbsoluteValue example we discussed previously is a transformation which applies to the left-hand side of the lookup. There may be some cases where you want the transformation to be applied to both the left-hand side and the right-hand side. For instance, if you want to filter a queryset based on the equality of the left and right-hand side insensitively to some SQL function.</p> <p>Let’s examine case-insensitive transformations here. This transformation isn’t very useful in practice as Django already comes with a bunch of built-in case-insensitive lookups, but it will be a nice demonstration of bilateral transformations in a database-agnostic way.</p> <p>We define an UpperCase transformer which uses the SQL function UPPER() to transform the values before</p> <p>comparison. We define <a href="index.html#page_1784"><i>bilateral = True</i></a> to indicate that this transformation should apply to both lhs and rhs:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Transform</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>UpperCase</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Transform):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">lookup_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"upper"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">function</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"UPPER"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">bilateral</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>= True</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Next, let’s register it:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField, TextField</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">register_lookup(UpperCase)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">TextField</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">register_lookup(UpperCase)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Now, the queryset Author.objects.filter(name__upper="doe") will generate a case insensitive query like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>SELECT</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>WHERE UPPER</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"author"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>= UPPER</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">'doe'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Writing alternative implementations for existing lookups</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Sometimes different database vendors require different SQL for the same operation. For this example we will rewrite a custom implementation for MySQL for the NotEqual operator. Instead of <> we will be using != operator. (Note that in reality almost all databases support both, including all the official databases supported by Django).</p> <p>We can change the behavior on a specific backend by creating a subclass of NotEqual with an as_mysql method:</p> <p id="page_805" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MySQLNotEqual</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(NotEqual):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as_mysql</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, compiler, connection,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">extra_context):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">lhs, lhs_params</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">process_lhs(compiler, connection)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">rhs, rhs_params</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">process_rhs(compiler, connection)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">params</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">lhs_params</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>+</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">rhs_params</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"%s != %s"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(lhs, rhs), params</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">Field</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">register_lookup(MySQLNotEqual)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>We can then register it with Field. It takes the place of the original NotEqual class as it has the same lookup_name.</p> <p>When compiling a query, Django first looks for as_%s % connection.vendor methods, and then falls back to as_sql. The vendor names for the in-built backends are sqlite, postgresql, oracle and mysql.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>How Django determines the lookups and transforms which are used</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>In some cases you may wish to dynamically change which Transform or Lookup is returned based on the name passed in, rather than fixing it. As an example, you could have a field which stores coordinates or an arbitrary dimension, and wish to allow a syntax like .filter(coords__x7=4) to return the objects where the 7th coordinate has value 4. In order to do this, you would override get_lookup with something like:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>CoordinatesField</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Field):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get_lookup</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, lookup_name):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">lookup_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">startswith(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"x"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>try</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">dimension</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">int</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(lookup_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">removeprefix(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"x"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">))</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>except</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ValueError</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>pass</b></span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>else</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">get_coordinate_lookup(dimension)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_lookup(lookup_name)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You would then define get_coordinate_lookup appropriately to return a Lookup subclass which handles the relevant value of dimension.</p> <p>There is a similarly named method called get_transform(). get_lookup() should always return a Lookup subclass, and get_transform() a Transform subclass. It is important to remember that Transform objects can be further filtered on, and Lookup objects cannot.</p> <p>When filtering, if there is only one lookup name remaining to be resolved, we will look for a Lookup. If there are multiple names, it will look for a Transform. In the situation where there is only one name and a Lookup is not found, we look for a Transform and then the exact lookup on that Transform. All call sequences always end with a Lookup. To clarify:</p> <p id="page_806"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• .filter(myfield__mylookup) will call myfield.get_lookup('mylookup').</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• .filter(myfield__mytransform__mylookup) will call myfield.get_transform('mytransform'),</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">and then mytransform.get_lookup('mylookup').</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• .filter(myfield__mytransform) will first call myfield.get_lookup('mytransform'), which will</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">fail, so it will fall back to calling myfield.get_transform('mytransform') and then mytransform. get_lookup('exact').</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.47em"><b>4.2 Templates and output</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>4.2.1 How to create CSV output</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This document explains how to output CSV (Comma Separated Values) dynamically using Django views. To do this, you can either use the Python CSV library or the Django template system.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using the Python CSV library</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Python comes with a CSV library, <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/csv.html#module-csv">csv. </a>The key to using it with Django is that the <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/csv.html#module-csv">csv</a> module’s CSV-creation</p> <p>capability acts on file-like objects, and Django’s <a href="index.html#page_1871"><i>HttpResponse</i></a> objects are file-like objects.</p> <p>Here’s an example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">csv</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.http</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>some_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Create the HttpResponse object with the appropriate CSV header.</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">content_type</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"text/csv"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">headers</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Content-Disposition"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'attachment; filename="somefilename.csv"'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">writer</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">csv</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">writer(response)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">writer</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">writerow([</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"First row"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Foo"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Bar"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Baz"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">])</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">writer</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">writerow([</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Second row"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"A"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"B"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"C"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'"Testing"'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Here's a quote"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">])</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The code and comments should be self-explanatory, but a few things deserve a mention:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The response gets a special MIME type, <i>text/csv</i>. This tells browsers that the document is a CSV file,</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">rather than an HTML file. If you leave this off, browsers will probably interpret the output as HTML, which will result in ugly, scary gobbledygook in the browser window.</p> <p id="page_807" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The response gets an additional Content-Disposition header, which contains the name of the CSV</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">file. This filename is arbitrary; call it whatever you want. It’ll be used by browsers in the “Save as<i>. . .</i>” dialog, etc.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• You can hook into the CSV-generation API by passing response as the first argument to csv.writer.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The csv.writer function expects a file-like object, and <a href="index.html#page_1871"><i>HttpResponse</i></a> objects fit the bill.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• For each row in your CSV file, call writer.writerow, passing it an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-iterable">iterable</a>.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The CSV module takes care of quoting for you, so you don’t have to worry about escaping strings with</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">quotes or commas in them. Pass writerow() your raw strings, and it’ll do the right thing.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Streaming large CSV files</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When dealing with views that generate very large responses, you might want to consider using Django’s</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1879"><i>StreamingHttpResponse</i></a> instead. For example, by streaming a file that takes a long time to generate you can avoid a load balancer dropping a connection that might have otherwise timed out while the server was generating the response.</p> <p>In this example, we make full use of Python generators to efficiently handle the assembly and transmission of a large CSV file:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">csv</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.http</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">StreamingHttpResponse</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Echo</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"""An object that implements just the write method of the file-like</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">interface.</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"""</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>write</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, value):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"""Write the value by returning it, instead of storing in a buffer."""</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>some_streaming_csv_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"""A view that streams a large CSV file."""</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Generate a sequence of rows. The range is based on the maximum number of</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># rows that can be handled by a single sheet in most spreadsheet</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># applications.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">rows</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">([</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Row {}"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">format(idx),</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">str</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(idx)]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">idx</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">range</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">65536</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">))</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">pseudo_buffer</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Echo()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">writer</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">csv</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">writer(pseudo_buffer)</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_808"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">StreamingHttpResponse(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(writer</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">writerow(row)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">row</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">rows),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">content_type</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"text/csv"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">headers</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Content-Disposition"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'attachment; filename="somefilename.csv"'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using the template system</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Alternatively, you can use the <a href="index.html#page_398">Django template system</a> to generate CSV. This is lower-level than using the</p> <p>convenient Python <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/csv.html#module-csv">csv</a> module, but the solution is presented here for completeness.</p> <p>The idea here is to pass a list of items to your template, and have the template output the commas in a <a href="index.html#page_1985"><i>for</i></a> loop.</p> <p>Here’s an example, which generates the same CSV file as above:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.http</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.template</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">loader</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>some_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Create the HttpResponse object with the appropriate CSV header.</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">content_type</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"text/csv"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">headers</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Content-Disposition"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'attachment; filename="somefilename.csv"'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># The data is hard-coded here, but you could load it from a database or</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># some other source.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">csv_data</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"First row"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Foo"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Bar"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Baz"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Second row"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"A"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"B"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"C"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'"Testing"'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Here's a quote"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">t</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">loader</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_template(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"my_template_name.txt"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">c</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"data"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: csv_data}</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">write(t</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">render(c))</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The only difference between this example and the previous example is that this one uses template loading instead of the CSV module. The rest of the code – such as the content_type='text/csv' – is the same.</p> <p>Then, create the template my_template_name.txt, with this template code:</p> <p id="page_809" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">row</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">data</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">row.0</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>addslashes</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">", "</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">row.1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>addslashes</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">", "</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">row.2</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>addslashes</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">",</span> <span style="font-size:0.47em"><i>,</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.47em"><i>→</i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">row.3</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>addslashes</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">", "</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">row.4</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>addslashes</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endfor</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This short template iterates over the given data and displays a line of CSV for each row. It uses the</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_2005"><i>addslashes</i></a> template filter to ensure there aren’t any problems with quotes.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Other text-based formats</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Notice that there isn’t very much specific to CSV here – just the specific output format. You can use either of these techniques to output any text-based format you can dream of. You can also use a similar technique</p> <p>to generate arbitrary binary data; see <a href="index.html#page_809">How to create PDF files</a> for an example.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>4.2.2 How to create PDF files</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This document explains how to output PDF files dynamically using Django views. This is made possible by</p> <p>the excellent, open-source <a href="https://docs.reportlab.com/">ReportLab</a> Python PDF library.</p> <p>The advantage of generating PDF files dynamically is that you can create customized PDFs for different purposes – say, for different users or different pieces of content.</p> <p>For example, Django was used at <a href="https://www2.kusports.com/">kusports.com</a> to generate customized, printer-friendly NCAA tournament brackets, as PDF files, for people participating in a March Madness contest.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Install ReportLab</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The ReportLab library is <a href="https://pypi.org/project/reportlab/">available on PyPI. </a>A <a href="https://www.reportlab.com/docs/reportlab-userguide.pdf">user guide</a> (not coincidentally, a PDF file) is also available for download. You can install ReportLab with pip:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">$</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">python -m pip install reportlab</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Test your installation by importing it in the Python interactive interpreter:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">reportlab</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If that command doesn’t raise any errors, the installation worked.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_810"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Write your view</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The key to generating PDFs dynamically with Django is that the ReportLab API acts on file-like objects, and</p> <p>Django’s <a href="index.html#page_1882"><i>FileResponse</i></a> objects accept file-like objects.</p> <p>Here’s a “Hello World” example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">io</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.http</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">FileResponse</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">reportlab.pdfgen</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">canvas</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>some_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Create a file-like buffer to receive PDF data.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">buffer</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">io</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">BytesIO()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Create the PDF object, using the buffer as its "file."</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">p</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">canvas</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Canvas(buffer)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Draw things on the PDF. Here's where the PDF generation happens.</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># See the ReportLab documentation for the full list of functionality.</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">p</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">drawString(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">100</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">100</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Hello world."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Close the PDF object cleanly, and we're done.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">p</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">showPage()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">p</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># FileResponse sets the Content-Disposition header so that browsers</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># present the option to save the file.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">buffer</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">seek(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">0</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">FileResponse(buffer, as_attachment</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, filename</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"hello.pdf"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The code and comments should be self-explanatory, but a few things deserve a mention:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The response will automatically set the MIME type <i>application/pdf</i> based on the filename extension.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This tells browsers that the document is a PDF file, rather than an HTML file or a generic <i>application/ octet-stream</i> binary content.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• When as_attachment=True is passed to FileResponse, it sets the appropriate Content-Disposition</p> <p style="text-align:center">header and that tells web browsers to pop-up a dialog box prompting/confirming how to handle the document even if a default is set on the machine. If the as_attachment parameter is omitted, browsers will handle the PDF using whatever program/plugin they’ve been configured to use for PDFs.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• You can provide an arbitrary filename parameter. It’ll be used by browsers in the “Save as<i>. . .</i>” dialog.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• You can hook into the ReportLab API: The same buffer passed as the first argument to canvas.Canvas</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">can be fed to the <a href="index.html#page_1882"><i>FileResponse</i></a> class.</p> <p id="page_811" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Note that all subsequent PDF-generation methods are called on the PDF object (in this case, p) – not</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">on buffer.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Finally, it’s important to call showPage() and save() on the PDF file.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: <span style="float:right">ReportLab is not thread-safe. Some of our users have reported odd issues with building PDF-</span></p> <p>generating Django views that are accessed by many people at the same time.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Other formats</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Notice that there isn’t a lot in these examples that’s PDF-specific – just the bits using reportlab. You can use a similar technique to generate any arbitrary format that you can find a Python library for. Also see</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_806">How to create CSV output</a> for another example and some techniques you can use when generated text-based formats.</p> <p>See also:</p> <p>Django Packages provides a <a href="https://djangopackages.org/grids/g/pdf/">comparison of packages</a> that help generate PDF files from Django.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>4.2.3 How to override templates</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>In your project, you might want to override a template in another Django application, whether it be a third-party application or a contrib application such as django.contrib.admin. You can either put template overrides in your project’s templates directory or in an application’s templates directory.</p> <p>If you have app and project templates directories that both contain overrides, the default Django template</p> <p>loader will try to load the template from the project-level directory first. In other words, <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>DIRS</i></a> is searched</p> <p>before <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>APP_DIRS</i></a>.</p> <p>See also:</p> <p>Read <a href="index.html#page_1554">Overriding built-in widget templates</a> if you’re looking to do that.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Overriding from the project’s templates directory</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>First, we’ll explore overriding templates by creating replacement templates in your project’s templates di-rectory.</p> <p>Let’s say you’re trying to override the templates for a third-party application called blog, which provides the templates blog/post.html and blog/list.html. The relevant settings for your project would look like:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">pathlib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Path</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">BASE_DIR</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">__file__</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">resolve()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">parent</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">parent</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_812"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">INSTALLED_APPS</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"blog"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">TEMPLATES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"BACKEND"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.template.backends.django.DjangoTemplates"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"DIRS"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [BASE_DIR</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>/</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"templates"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"APP_DIRS"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_1932"><i>TEMPLATES</i></a> setting and BASE_DIR will already exist if you created your project using the default project</p> <p>template. The setting that needs to be modified is <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>DIRS</i></a> .</p> <p>These settings assume you have a templates directory in the root of your project. To override the templates for the blog app, create a folder in the templates directory, and add the template files to that folder:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">templates/</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">blog/</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">list.html</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">post.html</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The template loader first looks for templates in the DIRS directory. When the views in the blog app ask for the blog/post.html and blog/list.html templates, the loader will return the files you just created.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Overriding from an app’s template directory</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Since you’re overriding templates located outside of one of your project’s apps, it’s more common to use the first method and put template overrides in a project’s templates folder. If you prefer, however, it’s also possible to put the overrides in an app’s template directory.</p> <p>First, make sure your template settings are checking inside app directories:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">TEMPLATES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"APP_DIRS"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_813" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you want to put the template overrides in an app called myapp and the templates to override are named blog/list.html and blog/post.html, then your directory structure will look like:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp/</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">templates/</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">blog/</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">list.html</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">post.html</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>With <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>APP_DIRS</i></a> set to True, the template loader will look in the app’s templates directory and find the tem-plates.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Extending an overridden template</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>With your template loaders configured, you can extend a template using the <a href="index.html#page_1983"><i>{% extends %}</i></a> template tag whilst at the same time overriding it. This can allow you to make small customizations without needing to reimplement the entire template.</p> <p>For example, you can use this technique to add a custom logo to the admin/base_site.html template:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">Listing 6: templates/admin/base_site.html</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>extends</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"admin/base_site.html"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>block</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">branding</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">img</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">src</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"link/to/logo.png"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">alt</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"logo"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">block</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.super</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endblock</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Key points to note:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The example creates a file at templates/admin/base_site.html that uses the configured project-level</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">templates directory to override admin/base_site.html.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The new template extends admin/base_site.html, which is the same template as is being overridden.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The template replaces just the branding block, adding a custom logo, and using block.super to retain</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">the prior content.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The rest of the template is inherited unchanged from admin/base_site.html.</p> <p>This technique works because the template loader does not consider the already loaded override template (at templates/admin/base_site.html) when resolving the extends tag. Combined with block.super it is <b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p id="page_814">a powerful technique to make small customizations.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>4.2.4 How to implement a custom template backend</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Custom backends</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Here’s how to implement a custom template backend in order to use another template system. A tem-plate backend is a class that inherits django.template.backends.base.BaseEngine. It must implement get_template() and optionally from_string(). Here’s an example for a fictional foobar template library:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.template</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.template.backends.utils</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">foobar</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>FooBar</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># inside an installed application.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">app_dirname</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"foobar"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>__init__</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, params):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">params</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">engine</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">options)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from_string</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, template_code):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>try</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>except</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">foobar</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>raise</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">TemplateSyntaxError(exc</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">args)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get_template</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">exc:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>raise</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">TemplateDoesNotExist(exc</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">args, backend</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span
