<p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>raise</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">TemplateSyntaxError(exc</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">args)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_815" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Template</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>__init__</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, template):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>render</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, context</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=None</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=None</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">context</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>is None</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">context</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{}</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>is not None</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">context[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"request"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">context[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"csrf_input"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">csrf_input_lazy(request)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">context[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"csrf_token"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">csrf_token_lazy(request)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">render(context)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>See <a href="https://github.com/django/deps/blob/main/final/0182-multiple-template-engines.rst">DEP 182</a> for more information.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Debug integration for custom engines</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The Django debug page has hooks to provide detailed information when a template error arises. Custom tem-plate engines can use these hooks to enhance the traceback information that appears to users. The following hooks are available:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Template postmortem</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The postmortem appears when <a href="index.html#page_403"><i>TemplateDoesNotExist</i></a> is raised. It lists the template engines and loaders that were used when trying to find a given template. For example, if two Django engines are configured, the postmortem will appear like:</p> <p><img src="index-815_1.png" alt="" width="702px" height="182px"/></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Custom engines can populate the postmortem by passing the backend and tried arguments when raising</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_403"><i>TemplateDoesNotExist</i>. </a>Backends that use the postmortem <a href="index.html#page_817">should specify an origin</a> on the template object.</p> <p id="page_816"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Contextual line information</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If an error happens during template parsing or rendering, Django can display the line the error happened on. For example:</p> <p><img src="index-816_1.png" alt="" width="702px" height="254px"/></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Custom engines can populate this information by setting a template_debug attribute on exceptions raised</p> <p>during parsing and rendering. This attribute is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#dict">dict</a> with the following values:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'name': The name of the template in which the exception occurred.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'message': The exception message.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'source_lines': The lines before, after, and including the line the exception occurred on. This is for</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">context, so it shouldn’t contain more than 20 lines or so.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'line': The line number on which the exception occurred.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'before': The content on the error line before the token that raised the error.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'during': The token that raised the error.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'after': The content on the error line after the token that raised the error.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'total': The number of lines in source_lines.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'top': The line number where source_lines starts.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'bottom': The line number where source_lines ends.</p> <p>Given the above template error, template_debug would look like:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"/path/to/template.html"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"message"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Invalid block tag: 'syntax'"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"source_lines"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"some\n"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">2</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"lines\n"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">3</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"before\n"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_817" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">4</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Hello {% syntax error %} {{ world }}\n"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">5</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"some\n"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">6</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"lines\n"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">7</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"after\n"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">8</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">""</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"line"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">4</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"before"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Hello "</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"during"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"{% syntax error %}"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"after"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">" {{ world }}\n"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"total"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">9</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"bottom"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">9</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"top"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Origin API and 3rd-party integration</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django templates have an <a href="index.html#page_2051"><i>Origin</i></a> object available through the template.origin attribute. This enables</p> <p>debug information to be displayed in the <a href="index.html#page_815">template postmortem, </a>as well as in 3rd-party libraries, like the</p> <p><a href="https://pypi.org/project/django-debug-toolbar/">Django Debug Toolbar</a>.</p> <p>Custom engines can provide their own template.origin information by creating an object that specifies the following attributes:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'name': The full path to the template.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'template_name': The relative path to the template as passed into the template loading methods.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'loader_name': An optional string identifying the function or class used to load the template, e.g.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">django.template.loaders.filesystem.Loader.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>4.2.5 How to create custom template tags and filters</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django’s template language comes with a wide variety of <a href="index.html#page_1979">built-in tags and filters</a> designed to address the presentation logic needs of your application. Nevertheless, you may find yourself needing functionality that is not covered by the core set of template primitives. You can extend the template engine by defining custom</p> <p>tags and filters using Python, and then make them available to your templates using the <a href="index.html#page_1993"><i>{% load %}</i></a> tag.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_818"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Code layout</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The most common place to specify custom template tags and filters is inside a Django app. If they relate to an existing app, it makes sense to bundle them there; otherwise, they can be added to a new app. When a</p> <p>Django app is added to <a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a>, any tags it defines in the conventional location described below are automatically made available to load within templates.</p> <p>The app should contain a templatetags directory, at the same level as models.py, views.py, etc. If this doesn’t already exist, create it - don’t forget the __init__.py file to ensure the directory is treated as a Python package.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Development server won’t automatically restart</p> <p>After adding the templatetags module, you will need to restart your server before you can use the tags or filters in templates.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Your custom tags and filters will live in a module inside the templatetags directory. The name of the module file is the name you’ll use to load the tags later, so be careful to pick a name that won’t clash with custom tags and filters in another app.</p> <p>For example, if your custom tags/filters are in a file called poll_extras.py, your app layout might look like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">polls/</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">__init__.py</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">models.py</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">templatetags/</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">__init__.py</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">poll_extras.py</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">views.py</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>And in your template you would use the following:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">poll_extras</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The app that contains the custom tags must be in <a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a> in order for the <a href="index.html#page_1993"><i>{% load %}</i></a> tag to work. This is a security feature: It allows you to host Python code for many template libraries on a single host machine without enabling access to all of them for every Django installation.</p> <p>There’s no limit on how many modules you put in the templatetags package. Just keep in mind that a <a href="index.html#page_1993"><i>{%</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1993"><i>load %}</i></a> statement will load tags/filters for the given Python module name, not the name of the app.</p> <p>To be a valid tag library, the module must contain a module-level variable named register that is a template.Library instance, in which all the tags and filters are registered. So, near the top of your module, put the following:</p> <p id="page_819" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">register</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Library()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Alternatively, template tag modules can be registered through the 'libraries' argument to</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_407"><i>DjangoTemplates</i>. </a>This is useful if you want to use a different label from the template tag module name when loading template tags. It also enables you to register tags without installing an application.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Behind the scenes</p> <p>For a ton of examples, read the source code for Django’s default filters and tags. <span style="float:right">They’re in</span></p> <p><a href="https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/template/defaultfilters.py">django/template/defaultfilters.py</a> and <a href="https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/template/defaulttags.py">django/template/defaulttags.py</a><a href="https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/template/defaulttags.py">, </a>respectively.</p> <p>For more information on the <a href="index.html#page_1993"><i>load</i></a> tag, read its documentation.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Writing custom template filters</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Custom filters are Python functions that take one or two arguments:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The value of the variable (input) – not necessarily a string.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The value of the argument – this can have a default value, or be left out altogether.</p> <p>For example, in the filter {{ var|foo:"bar" }}, the filter foo would be passed the variable var and the argument "bar".</p> <p>Since the template language doesn’t provide exception handling, any exception raised from a template filter will be exposed as a server error. Thus, filter functions should avoid raising exceptions if there is a reasonable fallback value to return. In case of input that represents a clear bug in a template, raising an exception may still be better than silent failure which hides the bug.</p> <p>Here’s an example filter definition:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>cut</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(value, arg):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"""Removes all values of arg from the given string"""</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">replace(arg,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">""</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>And here’s an example of how that filter would be used:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">somevariable</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>cut</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:"0"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Most filters don’t take arguments. In this case, leave the argument out of your function:</p> <p id="page_820"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>lower</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(value):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Only one argument.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"""Converts a string into all lowercase"""</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">lower()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Registering custom filters</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>django.template.Library.<b>filter</b>()</p> <p>Once you’ve written your filter definition, you need to register it with your Library instance, to make it available to Django’s template language:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"cut"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, cut)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"lower"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, lower)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The Library.filter() method takes two arguments:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. The name of the filter – a string.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. The compilation function – a Python function (not the name of the function as a string).</p> <p>You can use register.filter() as a decorator instead:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"cut"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>cut</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(value, arg):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">replace(arg,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">""</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>lower</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(value):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">lower()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you leave off the name argument, as in the second example above, Django will use the function’s name as the filter name.</p> <p>Finally, register.filter() also accepts three keyword arguments, is_safe, needs_autoescape, and</p> <p>expects_localtime. These arguments are described in <a href="index.html#page_821">filters and auto-escaping</a> and <a href="index.html#page_824">filters and time zones</a> below.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_821" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Template filters that expect strings</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>django.template.defaultfilters.<b>stringfilter</b>()</p> <p>If you’re writing a template filter that only expects a string as the first argument, you should use the decorator stringfilter. This will convert an object to its string value before being passed to your function:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.template.defaultfilters</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">stringfilter</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">register</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Library()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@stringfilter</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>lower</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(value):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">lower()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This way, you’ll be able to pass, say, an integer to this filter, and it won’t cause an AttributeError (because integers don’t have lower() methods).</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Filters and auto-escaping</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When writing a custom filter, give some thought to how the filter will interact with Django’s auto-escaping behavior. Note that two types of strings can be passed around inside the template code:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Raw strings are the native Python strings. On output, they’re escaped if auto-escaping is in effect and</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">presented unchanged, otherwise.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Safe strings are strings that have been marked safe from further escaping at output time. Any necessary</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">escaping has already been done. They’re commonly used for output that contains raw HTML that is intended to be interpreted as-is on the client side.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Internally, these strings are of type <a href="index.html#page_2086"><i>SafeString</i></a>. You can test for them using code like:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.safestring</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">SafeString</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">isinstance</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(value, SafeString):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Do something with the "safe" string.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Template filter code falls into one of two situations:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. Your filter does not introduce any HTML-unsafe characters (<, >, ', " or &) into the result that were not</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">already present. In this case, you can let Django take care of all the auto-escaping handling for you. All you need to do is set the is_safe flag to True when you register your filter function, like so:</p> <p id="page_822"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(is_safe</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>myfilter</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(value):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This flag tells Django that if a “safe” string is passed into your filter, the result will still be “safe” and if a non-safe string is passed in, Django will automatically escape it, if necessary.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">You can think of this as meaning “this filter is safe – it doesn’t introduce any possibility of unsafe HTML.”</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The reason is_safe is necessary is because there are plenty of normal string operations that will turn a SafeData object back into a normal str object and, rather than try to catch them all, which would be very difficult, Django repairs the damage after the filter has completed.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For example, suppose you have a filter that adds the string xx to the end of any input. Since this introduces no dangerous HTML characters to the result (aside from any that were already present), you should mark your filter with is_safe:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(is_safe</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>add_xx</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(value):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"%sxx"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">When this filter is used in a template where auto-escaping is enabled, Django will escape the output whenever the input is not already marked as “safe”.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">By default, is_safe is False, and you can omit it from any filters where it isn’t required.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Be careful when deciding if your filter really does leave safe strings as safe. If you’re removing char-acters, you might inadvertently leave unbalanced HTML tags or entities in the result. For example, removing a > from the input might turn <a> into <a, which would need to be escaped on output to avoid causing problems. Similarly, removing a semicolon (;) can turn & into &, which is no longer a valid entity and thus needs further escaping. Most cases won’t be nearly this tricky, but keep an eye out for any problems like that when reviewing your code.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Marking a filter is_safe will coerce the filter’s return value to a string. If your filter should return a boolean or other non-string value, marking it is_safe will probably have unintended consequences (such as converting a boolean False to the string ‘False’).</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. Alternatively, your filter code can manually take care of any necessary escaping. This is necessary</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">when you’re introducing new HTML markup into the result. You want to mark the output as safe from further escaping so that your HTML markup isn’t escaped further, so you’ll need to handle the input yourself.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">To mark the output as a safe string, use <a href="index.html#page_2086"><i>django.utils.safestring.mark_safe()</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Be careful, though. You need to do more than just mark the output as safe. You need to ensure it really is safe, and what you do depends on whether auto-escaping is in effect. The idea is to write filters that</p> <p id="page_823" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">can operate in templates where auto-escaping is either on or off in order to make things easier for your template authors.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">In order for your filter to know the current auto-escaping state, set the needs_autoescape flag to True when you register your filter function. (If you don’t specify this flag, it defaults to False). This flag tells Django that your filter function wants to be passed an extra keyword argument, called autoescape, that is True if auto-escaping is in effect and False otherwise. It is recommended to set the default of the autoescape parameter to True, so that if you call the function from Python code it will have escaping enabled by default.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For example, let’s write a filter that emphasizes the first character of a string:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.html</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">conditional_escape</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.safestring</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">mark_safe</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">register</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Library()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(needs_autoescape</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>initial_letter_filter</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(text, autoescape</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">first, other</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">text[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">0</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">], text[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">autoescape:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">esc</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">conditional_escape</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>else</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">esc</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>= lambda</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">x: x</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">result</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"<strong>%s</strong>%s"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(esc(first), esc(other))</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">mark_safe(result)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The needs_autoescape flag and the autoescape keyword argument mean that our function will know whether automatic escaping is in effect when the filter is called. We use autoescape to decide whether the input data needs to be passed through django.utils.html.conditional_escape or not. (In the latter case, we use the identity function as the “escape” function.) The conditional_escape() function is like escape() except it only escapes input that is not a SafeData instance. If a SafeData instance is passed to conditional_escape(), the data is returned unchanged.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Finally, in the above example, we remember to mark the result as safe so that our HTML is inserted directly into the template without further escaping.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">There’s no need to worry about the is_safe flag in this case (although including it wouldn’t hurt any-thing). Whenever you manually handle the auto-escaping issues and return a safe string, the is_safe flag won’t change anything either way.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: Avoiding XSS vulnerabilities when reusing built-in filters <b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p id="page_824" style="margin-left:1em">Django’s built-in filters have autoescape=True by default in order to get the proper autoescaping be-</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">havior and avoid a cross-site script vulnerability.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">In older versions of Django, be careful when reusing Django’s built-in filters as autoescape defaults to</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">None. You’ll need to pass autoescape=True to get autoescaping.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">For example, if you wanted to write a custom filter called urlize_and_linebreaks that combined the</p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_2026"><i>urlize</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_2016"><i>linebreaksbr</i></a> filters, the filter would look like:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.template.defaultfilters</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">linebreaksbr, urlize</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(needs_autoescape</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>urlize_and_linebreaks</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(text, autoescape</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">linebreaksbr(urlize(text, autoescape</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">autoescape), autoescape</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">autoescape)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Then:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">comment</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>urlize_and_linebreaks</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:1em">would be equivalent to:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">comment</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>urlize</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>linebreaksbr</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Filters and time zones</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you write a custom filter that operates on <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime">datetime</a> objects, you’ll usually register it with the expects_localtime flag set to True:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(expects_localtime</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>businesshours</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(value):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>try</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">9</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b><=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">hour</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b><</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">17</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>except</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AttributeError</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">""</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When this flag is set, if the first argument to your filter is a time zone aware datetime, Django will convert it</p> <p>to the current time zone before passing it to your filter when appropriate, according to <a href="index.html#page_697">rules for time zones</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_697">conversions in templates.</a></p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_825" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Writing custom template tags</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Tags are more complex than filters, because tags can do anything. Django provides a number of shortcuts that make writing most types of tags easier. First we’ll explore those shortcuts, then explain how to write a tag from scratch for those cases when the shortcuts aren’t powerful enough.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Simple tags</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>django.template.Library.<b>simple_tag</b>()</p> <p>Many template tags take a number of arguments – strings or template variables – and return a result after doing some processing based solely on the input arguments and some external information. For example, a current_time tag might accept a format string and return the time as a string formatted accordingly.</p> <p>To ease the creation of these types of tags, Django provides a helper function, simple_tag. This function, which is a method of django.template.Library, takes a function that accepts any number of arguments, wraps it in a render function and the other necessary bits mentioned above and registers it with the template system.</p> <p>Our current_time function could thus be written like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">register</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Library()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">simple_tag</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>current_time</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(format_string):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">now()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">strftime(format_string)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A few things to note about the simple_tag helper function:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Checking for the required number of arguments, etc., has already been done by the time our function</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">is called, so we don’t need to do that.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The quotes around the argument (if any) have already been stripped away, so we receive a plain string.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• If the argument was a template variable, our function is passed the current value of the variable, not</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">the variable itself.</p> <p>Unlike other tag utilities, simple_tag passes its output through <a href="index.html#page_2082"><i>conditional_escape()</i></a> if the template con-text is in autoescape mode, to ensure correct HTML and protect you from XSS vulnerabilities.</p> <p>If additional escaping is not desired, you will need to use <a href="index.html#page_2086"><i>mark_safe()</i></a> if you are absolutely sure that your</p> <p>code does not contain XSS vulnerabilities. For building small HTML snippets, use of <a href="index.html#page_2082"><i>format_html()</i></a> instead of mark_safe() is strongly recommended.</p> <p id="page_826"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If your template tag needs to access the current context, you can use the takes_context argument when registering your tag:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">simple_tag(takes_context</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>current_time</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(context, format_string):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">timezone</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">context[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"timezone"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">your_get_current_time_method(timezone, format_string)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note that the first argument must be called context.</p> <p>For more information on how the takes_context option works, see the section on <a href="index.html#page_831">inclusion tags</a>.</p> <p>If you need to rename your tag, you can provide a custom name for it:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">simple_tag(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>lambda</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">x: x</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>-</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"minusone"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">simple_tag(name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"minustwo"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>some_function</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(value):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>-</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">2</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>simple_tag functions may accept any number of positional or keyword arguments. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">simple_tag</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_tag</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(a, b,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>*</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">args,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">warning</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"warning"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">profile</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"profile"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return ...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Then in the template any number of arguments, separated by spaces, may be passed to the template tag. Like in Python, the values for keyword arguments are set using the equal sign (”=”) and must be provided after the positional arguments. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_tag</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">123</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"abcd"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">book.title warning</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">message</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>lower</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">profile</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user.profile</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>It’s possible to store the tag results in a template variable rather than directly outputting it. This is done by using the as argument followed by the variable name. Doing so enables you to output the content yourself where you see fit:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>current_time</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"%Y-%m-%d %I:%M %p"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">the_time</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">p</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>The time is</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">the_time</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.</</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">p</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p id="page_827" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Simple block tags</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>django.template.Library.<b>simple_block_tag</b>()</p> <p>When a section of rendered template needs to be passed into a custom tag, Django provides the</p> <p>simple_block_tag helper function to accomplish this. Similar to <a href="index.html#page_825"><i>simple_tag()</i>, </a>this function accepts a custom tag function, but with the additional content argument, which contains the rendered content as defined inside the tag. This allows dynamic template sections to be easily incorporated into custom tags.</p> <p>For example, a custom block tag which creates a chart could look like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.charts</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">render_chart</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">register</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Library()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">simple_block_tag</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>chart</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(content):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">render_chart(source</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">content)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The content argument contains everything in between the {% chart %} and {% endchart %} tags:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>chart</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">digraph G {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">label = "Chart for</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request.user</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">A -> {B C}</span></p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endchart</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If there are other template tags or variables inside the content block, they will be rendered before being passed to the tag function. In the example above, request.user will be resolved by the time render_chart is called.</p> <p>Block tags are closed with end{name} (for example, endchart). This can be customized with the end_name parameter:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">simple_block_tag(end_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"endofchart"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>chart</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(content):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">render_chart(source</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">content)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Which would require a template definition like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>chart</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">digraph G {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">label = "Chart for</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request.user</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_828"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">A -> {B C}</span></p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endofchart</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A few things to note about simple_block_tag:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The first argument must be called content, and it will contain the contents of the template tag as a</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">rendered string.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Variables passed to the tag are not included in the rendering context of the content, as would be when</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">using the {% with %} tag.</p> <p>Just like <a href="index.html#page_825">simple_tag</a>, simple_block_tag:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Validates the quantity and quality of the arguments.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Strips quotes from arguments if necessary.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Escapes the output accordingly.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Supports passing takes_context=True at registration time to access context. Note that in this case,</p> <p style="text-align:center">the first argument to the custom function must be called context, and content must follow.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Supports renaming the tag by passing the name argument when registering.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Supports accepting any number of positional or keyword arguments.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Supports storing the result in a template variable using the as variant.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Content Escaping</p> <p>simple_block_tag behaves similarly to simple_tag regarding auto-escaping. For details on escaping and safety, refer to simple_tag. Because the content argument has already been rendered by Django, it is al-ready escaped.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>A complete example</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Consider a custom template tag that generates a message box that supports multiple message levels and content beyond a simple phrase. style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.html</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span level):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">format_kwargs</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endblock</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The following HTML is produced as the rendered output:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">div</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">class</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>Error</</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">strong</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>: Please read for <</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">i</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">summary</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">p</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">Please fix all errors. Further documentation can be found at</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">href</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">div</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">div</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">class</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"msgbox info"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">strong</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>Info</</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">strong</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>: Please read for <</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">i</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>Important Site</</span><span
