style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">More information at: <</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">href</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"http://othersite.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>Other Site</</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">p</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">details</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">div</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_831" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Inclusion tags</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>django.template.Library.<b>inclusion_tag</b>()</p> <p>Another common type of template tag is the type that displays some data by rendering another template. For example, Django’s admin interface uses custom template tags to display the buttons along the bottom of the “add/change” form pages. Those buttons always look the same, but the link targets change depending on the object being edited – so they’re a perfect case for using a small template that is filled with details from the current object. (In the admin’s case, this is the submit_row tag.) These sorts of tags are called “inclusion tags”.</p> <p>Writing inclusion tags is probably best demonstrated by example. Let’s write a tag that outputs a list of</p> <p>choices for a given Poll object, such as was created in the <a href="index.html#page_29">tutorials. </a>We’ll use the tag like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>show_results</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">poll</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><i>. . .</i>and the output will be something like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ul</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>First choice</</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>Second choice</</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>Third choice</</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ul</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>First, define the function that takes the argument and produces a dictionary of data for the result. The important point here is we only need to return a dictionary, not anything more complex. This will be used as a template context for the template fragment. Example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>show_results</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(poll):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">choices</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">poll</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">choice_set</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">all()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"choices"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: choices}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Next, create the template used to render the tag’s output. This template is a fixed feature of the tag: the tag writer specifies it, not the template designer. Following our example, the template is very short:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ul</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">choice</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">choices</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">choice</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endfor</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ul</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Now, create and register the inclusion tag by calling the inclusion_tag() method on a Library object. Following our example, if the above template is in a file called results.html in a directory that’s searched by the template loader, we’d register the tag like this:</p> <p id="page_832"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Here, register is a django.template.Library instance, as before</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">@register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">inclusion_tag(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"results.html"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>show_results</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(poll):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Alternatively it is possible to register the inclusion tag using a <a href="index.html#page_2033"><i>django.template.Template</i></a> instance:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.template.loader</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">get_template</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">t</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">get_template(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"results.html"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">inclusion_tag(t)(show_results)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><i>. . .</i>when first creating the function.</p> <p>Sometimes, your inclusion tags might require a large number of arguments, making it a pain for template au-thors to pass in all the arguments and remember their order. To solve this, Django provides a takes_context option for inclusion tags. If you specify takes_context in creating a template tag, the tag will have no re-quired arguments, and the underlying Python function will have one argument – the template context as of when the tag was called.</p> <p>For example, say you’re writing an inclusion tag that will always be used in a context that contains home_link and home_title variables that point back to the main page. Here’s what the Python function would look like:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">inclusion_tag(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"link.html"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, takes_context</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>jump_link</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(context):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"link"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: context[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"home_link"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: context[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"home_title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note that the first parameter to the function must be called context.</p> <p>In that register.inclusion_tag() line, we specified takes_context=True and the name of the template. Here’s what the template link.html might look like:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">Jump directly to <</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">href</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">link</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>.</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Then, any time you want to use that custom tag, load its library and call it without any arguments, like so:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>jump_link</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note that when you’re using takes_context=True, there’s no need to pass arguments to the template tag. It automatically gets access to the context.</p> <p>The takes_context parameter defaults to False. When it’s set to True, the tag is passed the context object, as in this example. That’s the only difference between this case and the previous inclusion_tag example.</p> <p id="page_833" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>inclusion_tag functions may accept any number of positional or keyword arguments. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">inclusion_tag(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"my_template.html"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_tag</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(a, b,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>*</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">args,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">warning</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"warning"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">profile</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"profile"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return ...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Then in the template any number of arguments, separated by spaces, may be passed to the template tag. Like in Python, the values for keyword arguments are set using the equal sign (”=”) and must be provided after the positional arguments. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_tag</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">123</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"abcd"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">book.title warning</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">message</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>lower</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">profile</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user.profile</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Advanced custom template tags</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Sometimes the basic features for custom template tag creation aren’t enough. Don’t worry, Django gives you complete access to the internals required to build a template tag from the ground up.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>A quick overview</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The template system works in a two-step process: compiling and rendering. To define a custom template tag, you specify how the compilation works and how the rendering works.</p> <p>When Django compiles a template, it splits the raw template text into ‘’nodes’’. Each node is an instance of django.template.Node and has a render() method. A compiled template is a list of Node objects. When you call render() on a compiled template object, the template calls render() on each Node in its node list, with the given context. The results are all concatenated together to form the output of the template.</p> <p>Thus, to define a custom template tag, you specify how the raw template tag is converted into a Node (the compilation function), and what the node’s render() method does.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Writing the compilation function</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>For each template tag the template parser encounters, it calls a Python function with the tag contents and the parser object itself. This function is responsible for returning a Node instance based on the contents of the tag.</p> <p>For example, let’s write a full implementation of our template tag, {% current_time %}, that displays the</p> <p>current date/time, formatted according to a parameter given in the tag, in <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/time.html#time.strftime">strftime()</a> syntax. It’s a good idea to decide the tag syntax before anything else. In our case, let’s say the tag should be used like this:</p> <p id="page_834"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">p</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>The time is</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>current_time</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"%Y-%m-%d %I:%M %p"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.</</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">p</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The parser for this function should grab the parameter and create a Node object:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>do_current_time</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(parser, token):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>try</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># split_contents() knows not to split quoted strings.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">tag_name, format_string</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">token</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">split_contents()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>except</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ValueError</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>raise</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">TemplateSyntaxError(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"%r tag requires a single argument"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">token</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">contents</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">split()[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">0</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if not</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(format_string[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">0</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">format_string[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>-</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>and</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">format_string[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">0</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">'"'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"'"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>raise</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">TemplateSyntaxError(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"%r tag's argument should be in quotes"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">tag_name</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">CurrentTimeNode(format_string[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>-</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">])</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Notes:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• parser is the template parser object. We don’t need it in this example.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• token.contents is a string of the raw contents of the tag. In our example, it’s 'current_time</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">"%Y-%m-%d %I:%M %p"'.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The token.split_contents() method separates the arguments on spaces while keeping quoted strings</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">together. The more straightforward token.contents.split() wouldn’t be as robust, as it would naively split on all spaces, including those within quoted strings. It’s a good idea to always use token. split_contents().</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• This function is responsible for raising django.template.TemplateSyntaxError, with helpful mes-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">sages, for any syntax error.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The TemplateSyntaxError exceptions use the tag_name variable. Don’t hard-code the tag’s name</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">in your error messages, because that couples the tag’s name to your function. token.contents. split()[0] will ‘’always’’ be the name of your tag – even when the tag has no arguments.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The function returns a CurrentTimeNode with everything the node needs to know about this tag. In</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">this case, it passes the argument – "%Y-%m-%d %I:%M %p". The leading and trailing quotes from the template tag are removed in format_string[1:-1].</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The parsing is very low-level. The Django developers have experimented with writing small frame-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">works on top of this parsing system, using techniques such as EBNF grammars, but those experiments made the template engine too slow. It’s low-level because that’s fastest.</p> <p id="page_835" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Writing the renderer</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The second step in writing custom tags is to define a Node subclass that has a render() method.</p> <p>Continuing the above example, we need to define CurrentTimeNode:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>CurrentTimeNode</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Node):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>__init__</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, format_string):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">format_string</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">format_string</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>render</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, context):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">now()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">strftime(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">format_string)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Notes:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• __init__() gets the format_string from do_current_time(). <span style="float:right">Always pass any op-</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">tions/parameters/arguments to a Node via its __init__().</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The render() method is where the work actually happens.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• render() should generally fail silently, particularly in a production environment. In some cases how-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">ever, particularly if context.template.engine.debug is True, this method may raise an exception to make debugging easier. For example, several core tags raise django.template.TemplateSyntaxError if they receive the wrong number or type of arguments.</p> <p>Ultimately, this decoupling of compilation and rendering results in an efficient template system, because a template can render multiple contexts without having to be parsed multiple times.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Auto-escaping considerations</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The output from template tags is not automatically run through the auto-escaping filters (with the exception</p> <p>of <a href="index.html#page_825"><i>simple_tag()</i></a> as described above). However, there are still a couple of things you should keep in mind when writing a template tag.</p> <p>If the render() method of your template tag stores the result in a context variable (rather than returning the result in a string), it should take care to call mark_safe() if appropriate. When the variable is ultimately rendered, it will be affected by the auto-escape setting in effect at the time, so content that should be safe from further escaping needs to be marked as such.</p> <p>Also, if your template tag creates a new context for performing some sub-rendering, set the auto-escape attribute to the current context’s value. The __init__ method for the Context class takes a parameter called autoescape that you can use for this purpose. For example:</p> <p id="page_836"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.template</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Context</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>render</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, context):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">new_context</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Context({</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"var"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: obj}, autoescape</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">context</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">autoescape)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ... Do something with new_context ...</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This is not a very common situation, but it’s useful if you’re rendering a template yourself. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>render</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, context):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">t</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">context</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">engine</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_template(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"small_fragment.html"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">t</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">render(Context({</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"var"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: obj}, autoescape</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">context</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">autoescape))</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If we had neglected to pass in the current context.autoescape value to our new Context in this example, the results would have always been automatically escaped, which may not be the desired behavior if the</p> <p>template tag is used inside a <a href="index.html#page_1979"><i>{% autoescape off %}</i></a> block.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Thread-safety considerations</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Once a node is parsed, its render method may be called any number of times. Since Django is sometimes run in multi-threaded environments, a single node may be simultaneously rendering with different contexts in response to two separate requests. Therefore, it’s important to make sure your template tags are thread safe.</p> <p>To make sure your template tags are thread safe, you should never store state information on the node itself.</p> <p>For example, Django provides a builtin <a href="index.html#page_1980"><i>cycle</i></a> template tag that cycles among a list of given strings each time it’s rendered:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">o</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">some_list</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">tr</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">class</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>cycle</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'row1' 'row2'</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">tr</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endfor</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A naive implementation of CycleNode might look something like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">itertools</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>CycleNode</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Node):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>__init__</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, cyclevars):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">cycle_iter</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">itertools</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">cycle(cyclevars)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_837" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>render</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, context):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">next</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">cycle_iter)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>But, suppose we have two templates rendering the template snippet from above at the same time:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. Thread 1 performs its first loop iteration, CycleNode.render() returns ‘row1’</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. Thread 2 performs its first loop iteration, CycleNode.render() returns ‘row2’</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">3. Thread 1 performs its second loop iteration, CycleNode.render() returns ‘row1’</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">4. Thread 2 performs its second loop iteration, CycleNode.render() returns ‘row2’</p> <p>The CycleNode is iterating, but it’s iterating globally. As far as Thread 1 and Thread 2 are concerned, it’s always returning the same value. This is not what we want!</p> <p>To address this problem, Django provides a render_context that’s associated with the context of the tem-plate that is currently being rendered. The render_context behaves like a Python dictionary, and should be used to store Node state between invocations of the render method.</p> <p>Let’s refactor our CycleNode implementation to use the render_context:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>CycleNode</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Node):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>__init__</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, cyclevars):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">cyclevars</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">cyclevars</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>render</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, context):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>not in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">context</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">render_context:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">context</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">render_context[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">itertools</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">cycle(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">cyclevars)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">cycle_iter</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">context</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">render_context[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">next</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(cycle_iter)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note that it’s perfectly safe to store global information that will not change throughout the life of the Node as an attribute. In the case of CycleNode, the cyclevars argument doesn’t change after the Node is instantiated, so we don’t need to put it in the render_context. But state information that is specific to the template that is currently being rendered, like the current iteration of the CycleNode, should be stored in the render_context.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: Notice how we used self to scope the CycleNode specific information within the render_context. There may be multiple CycleNodes in a given template, so we need to be careful not to clobber another node’s state information. The easiest way to do this is to always use self as the key into render_context. If you’re keeping track of several state variables, make render_context[self] a dictionary.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_838"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Registering the tag</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Finally, register the tag with your module’s Library instance, as explained in <a href="index.html#page_825">writing custom template tags</a> above. Example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">tag(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"current_time"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, do_current_time)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The tag() method takes two arguments:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. The name of the template tag – a string. If this is left out, the name of the compilation function will be</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">used.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. The compilation function – a Python function (not the name of the function as a string).</p> <p>As with filter registration, it is also possible to use this as a decorator:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">tag(name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"current_time"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>do_current_time</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(parser, token):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@register</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">tag</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>shout</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(parser, token):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you leave off the name argument, as in the second example above, Django will use the function’s name as the tag name.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Passing template variables to the tag</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Although you can pass any number of arguments to a template tag using token.split_contents(), the arguments are all unpacked as string literals. A little more work is required in order to pass dynamic content (a template variable) to a template tag as an argument.</p> <p>While the previous examples have formatted the current time into a string and returned the string, suppose</p> <p>you wanted to pass in a <a href="index.html#page_1630"><i>DateTimeField</i></a> from an object and have the template tag format that date-time:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">p</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>This post was last updated at</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>format_time</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">blog_entry.date_updated</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"%Y-%m-%d %I:%M %p"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.</</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">p</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Initially, token.split_contents() will return three values:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. The tag name format_time.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. The string 'blog_entry.date_updated' (without the surrounding quotes).</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">3. The formatting string '"%Y-%m-%d %I:%M %p"'. The return value from split_contents() will include</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">the leading and trailing quotes for string literals like this.</p> <p>Now your tag should begin to look like this:</p> <p id="page_839" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>do_format_time</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(parser, token):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>try</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># split_contents() knows not to split quoted strings.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">tag_name, date_to_be_formatted, format_string</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">token</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">split_contents()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>except</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ValueError</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>raise</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">TemplateSyntaxError(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"%r tag requires exactly two arguments"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">token</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">contents</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">split()[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">0</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if not</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(format_string[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">0</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">format_string[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>-</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>and</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">format_string[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">0</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">'"'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"'"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>raise</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">TemplateSyntaxError(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"%r tag's argument should be in quotes"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">tag_name</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">FormatTimeNode(date_to_be_formatted, format_string[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>-</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">])</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You also have to change the renderer to retrieve the actual contents of the date_updated property of the blog_entry object. This can be accomplished by using the Variable() class in django.template.</p> <p>To use the Variable class, instantiate it with the name of the variable to be resolved, and then call variable. resolve(context). So, for example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>FormatTimeNode</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Node):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>__init__</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, date_to_be_formatted, format_string):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">date_to_be_formatted</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Variable(date_to_be_formatted)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">format_string</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">format_string</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>render</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, context):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>try</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">actual_date</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">date_to_be_formatted</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">resolve(context)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">actual_date</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">strftime(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">format_string)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>except</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">VariableDoesNotExist:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">""</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Variable resolution will throw a VariableDoesNotExist exception if it cannot resolve the string passed to it in the current context of the page.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_840"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Setting a variable in the context</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The above examples output a value. Generally, it’s more flexible if your template tags set template variables instead of outputting values. That way, template authors can reuse the values that your template tags create.</p> <p>To set a variable in the context, use dictionary assignment on the context object in the render() method. Here’s an updated version of CurrentTimeNode that sets a template variable current_time instead of out-putting it:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>CurrentTimeNode2</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Node):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>__init__</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, format_string):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">format_string</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">format_string</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>render</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, context):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">context[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"current_time"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">now()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">strftime(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">format_string)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">""</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note that render() returns the empty string. render() should always return string output. If all the tem-plate tag does is set a variable, render() should return the empty string.</p> <p>Here’s how you’d use this new version of the tag:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>current_time</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"%Y-%m-%d %I:%M %p"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">p</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>The time is</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">current_time</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.</</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">p</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Variable scope in context</p> <p>Any variable set in the context will only be available in the same block of the template in which it was assigned. This behavior is intentional; it provides a scope for variables so that they don’t conflict with context in other blocks.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>But, there’s a problem with CurrentTimeNode2: The variable name current_time is hard-coded. This means you’ll need to make sure your template doesn’t use {{ current_time }} anywhere else, because the {% current_time %} will blindly overwrite that variable’s value. A cleaner solution is to make the template tag specify the name of the output variable, like so:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>current_time</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"%Y-%m-%d %I:%M %p"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">my_current_time</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">p</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>The current time is</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">my_current_time</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.</</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">p</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To do that, you’ll need to refactor both the compilation function and Node class, like so:</p> <p id="page_841" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">re</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>CurrentTimeNode3</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">""</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>do_current_time</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(parser, token):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># This version uses a regular expression to parse tag contents.</i></span> <span spaces.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">tag_name, arg</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">token</span><span <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"%r tag requires arguments"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">token</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">TemplateSyntaxError(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"%r tag had invalid arguments"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">tag_name)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">format_string, var_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">m</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">groups()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if not</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(format_string[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">0</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">format_string[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>-</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>and</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">format_string[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">0</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">'"'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"'"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>raise</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">TemplateSyntaxError(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"%r tag's argument should be in quotes"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">tag_name</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">CurrentTimeNode3(format_string[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>-</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">], var_name)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The difference here is that do_current_time() grabs the format string and the variable name, passing both to CurrentTimeNode3.</p> <p>Finally, if you only need to have a simple syntax for your custom context-updating template tag, consider</p> <p>using the <a href="index.html#page_825"><i>simple_tag()</i></a> shortcut, which supports assigning the tag results to a template variable.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_842"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Parsing until another block tag</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Template tags can work in tandem. For instance, the standard <a href="index.html#page_1980"><i>{% comment %}</i></a> tag hides everything until {% endcomment %}. To create a template tag such as this, use parser.parse() in your compilation function.</p> <p>Here’s how a simplified {% comment %} tag might be implemented:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>do_comment</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(parser, token):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">nodelist</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">parser</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">parse((</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"endcomment"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,))</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">parser</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">delete_first_token()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">CommentNode()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>CommentNode</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Node):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>render</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, context):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">""</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: The actual implementation of <a href="index.html#page_1980"><i>{% comment %}</i></a> is slightly different in that it allows bro-ken template tags to appear between {% comment %} and {% endcomment %}. It does so by calling parser.skip_past('endcomment') instead of parser.parse(('endcomment',)) followed by parser. delete_first_token(), thus avoiding the generation of a node list.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>parser.parse() takes a tuple of names of block tags ‘’to parse until’’. It returns an instance of django. template.NodeList, which is a list of all Node objects that the parser encountered ‘’before’’ it encountered any of the tags named in the tuple.</p> <p>In "nodelist = parser.parse(('endcomment',))" in the above example, nodelist is a list of all nodes between the {% comment %} and {% endcomment %}, not counting {% comment %} and {% endcomment %} themselves.</p> <p>After parser.parse() is called, the parser hasn’t yet “consumed” the {% endcomment %} tag, so the code needs to explicitly call parser.delete_first_token().</p> <p>CommentNode.render() returns an empty string. Anything between {% comment %} and {% endcomment %} is ignored.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_843" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Parsing until another block tag, and saving contents</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>In the previous example, do_comment() discarded everything between {% comment %} and {% endcomment %}. Instead of doing that, it’s possible to do something with the code between block tags.</p> <p>For example, here’s a custom template tag, {% upper %}, that capitalizes everything between itself and {% endupper %}.</p> <p>Usage:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>upper</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">This will appear in uppercase,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">your_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endupper</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>As in the previous example, we’ll use parser.parse(). But this time, we pass the resulting nodelist to the Node:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>do_upper</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(parser, token):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">nodelist</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">parser</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">parse((</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"endupper"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,))</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">parser</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">delete_first_token()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">UpperNode(nodelist)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>UpperNode</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(template</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Node):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>__init__</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, nodelist):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">nodelist</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">nodelist</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>render</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, context):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">output</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">nodelist</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">render(context)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">output</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">upper()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The only new concept here is the self.nodelist.render(context) in UpperNode.render().</p> <p>For more examples of complex rendering, see the source code of <a href="index.html#page_1985"><i>{% for %}</i></a> in</p> <p><a href="https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/template/defaulttags.py">django/template/defaulttags.py</a> and <a href="index.html#page_1986"><i>{% if %}</i></a> in <a href="https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/template/smartif.py">django/template/smartif.py</a><a href="https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/template/smartif.py">.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.47em"><b>4.3 Project configuration and management</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>4.3.1 How to manage static files (e.g. images, JavaScript, CSS)</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Websites generally need to serve additional files such as images, JavaScript, or CSS. In Django, we refer to</p> <p>these files as “static files”. Django provides <a href="index.html#page_1369"><i>django.contrib.staticfiles</i></a> to help you manage them.</p> <p>This page describes how you can serve these static files.</p> <p id="page_844"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Configuring static files</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. Make sure that django.contrib.staticfiles is included in your <a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. In your settings file, define <a href="index.html#page_1946"><i>STATIC_URL</i></a>, for example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">STATIC_URL</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"static/"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">3. In your templates, use the <a href="index.html#page_2029"><i>static</i></a> template tag to build the URL for the given relative path using the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">configured staticfiles <a href="index.html#page_1931"><i>STORAGES</i></a> alias.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">static</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">img</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">src</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>static</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'my_app/example.jpg'</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">alt</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"My image"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">4. Store your static files in a folder called static in your app. For example my_app/static/my_app/</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">example.jpg .</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Serving the files</p> <p>In addition to these configuration steps, you’ll also need to actually serve the static files.</p> <p>During development, if you use <a href="index.html#page_1369"><i>django.contrib.staticfiles</i></a>, this will be done automatically by</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1447"><i>runserver</i></a> when <a href="index.html#page_1907"><i>DEBUG</i></a> is set to True (see <a href="index.html#page_1377"><i>django.contrib.staticfiles.views.serve()</i></a>).</p> <p>This method is grossly inefficient and probably insecure, so it is unsuitable for production.</p> <p>See <a href="index.html#page_885">How to deploy static files</a> for proper strategies to serve static files in production environments.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Your project will probably also have static assets that aren’t tied to a particular app. In addition to using a</p> <p>static/ directory inside your apps, you can define a list of directories <a href="index.html#page_1946">(<i>STATICFILES_DIRS</i></a>) in your settings file where Django will also look for static files. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">STATICFILES_DIRS</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">BASE_DIR</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>/</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"static"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/var/www/static/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>See the documentation for the <a href="index.html#page_1947"><i>STATICFILES_FINDERS</i></a> setting for details on how staticfiles finds your files.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Static file namespacing</p> <p>Now we might be able to get away with putting our static files directly in my_app/static/ (rather than creating another my_app subdirectory), but it would actually be a bad idea. Django will use the first static file it finds whose name matches, and if you had a static file with the same name in a different application, Django would be unable to distinguish between them. We need to be able to point Django at the right one,</p> <p id="page_845" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>and the best way to ensure this is by namespacing them. That is, by putting those static files inside another directory named for the application itself.</p> <p>You can namespace static assets in <a href="index.html#page_1946"><i>STATICFILES_DIRS</i></a> by specifying <a href="index.html#page_1947">prefixes</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Serving static files during development</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you use <a href="index.html#page_1369"><i>django.contrib.staticfiles</i></a> as explained above, <a href="index.html#page_1447"><i>runserver</i></a> will do this automatically when</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1907"><i>DEBUG</i></a> is set to True. If you don’t have django.contrib.staticfiles in <a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a>, you can still</p> <p>manually serve static files using the <a href="index.html#page_2099"><i>django.views.static.serve()</i></a> view.</p> <p>This is not suitable for production use! For some common deployment strategies, see <a href="index.html#page_885">How to deploy static</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_885">files</a>.</p> <p>For example, if your <a href="index.html#page_1946"><i>STATIC_URL</i></a> is defined as static/, you can do this by adding the following snippet to your urls.py:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.conf</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">settings</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.conf.urls.static</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">static</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ... the rest of your URLconf goes here ...</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>+</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">static(settings</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">STATIC_URL, document_root</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">settings</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">STATIC_ROOT)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: This helper function works only in debug mode and only if the given prefix is local (e.g. static/) and not a URL (e.g. http://static.example.com/).</p> <p>Also this helper function only serves the actual <a href="index.html#page_1945"><i>STATIC_ROOT</i></a> folder; it doesn’t perform static files discovery</p> <p>like <a href="index.html#page_1369"><i>django.contrib.staticfiles</i></a>.</p> <p>Finally, static files are served via a wrapper at the WSGI application layer. As a consequence, static files</p> <p>requests do not pass through the normal <a href="index.html#page_303">middleware chain.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Serving files uploaded by a user during development</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>During development, you can serve user-uploaded media files from <a href="index.html#page_1922"><i>MEDIA_ROOT</i></a> using the <a href="index.html#page_2099"><i>django.views.</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_2099"><i>static.serve()</i></a> view.</p> <p>This is not suitable for production use! For some common deployment strategies, see <a href="index.html#page_885">How to deploy static</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_885">files</a>.</p> <p>For example, if your <a href="index.html#page_1922"><i>MEDIA_URL</i></a> is defined as media/, you can do this by adding the following snippet to your</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1925"><i>ROOT_URLCONF</i></a> :</p> <p id="page_846"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.conf</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">settings</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.conf.urls.static</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">static</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ... the rest of your URLconf goes here ...</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>+</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">static(settings</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">MEDIA_URL, document_root</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">settings</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">MEDIA_ROOT)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: This helper function works only in debug mode and only if the given prefix is local (e.g. media/) and not a URL (e.g. http://media.example.com/).</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Testing</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When running tests that use actual HTTP requests instead of the built-in testing client (i.e. when using the</p> <p>built-in <a href="index.html#page_493"><i>LiveServerTestCase</i>) </a>the static assets need to be served along the rest of the content so the test environment reproduces the real one as faithfully as possible, but LiveServerTestCase has only very basic static file-serving functionality: It doesn’t know about the finders feature of the staticfiles application</p> <p>and assumes the static content has already been collected under <a href="index.html#page_1945"><i>STATIC_ROOT</i></a> .</p> <p>Because of this, staticfiles ships its own <a href="index.html#page_1378"><i>django.contrib.staticfiles.testing.</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1378"><i>StaticLiveServerTestCase</i></a>, a subclass of the built-in one that has the ability to transparently serve all the assets during execution of these tests in a way very similar to what we get at development time with</p> <p>DEBUG = True, i.e. without having to collect them using <a href="index.html#page_1370"><i>collectstatic</i></a> first.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Deployment</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1369"><i>django.contrib.staticfiles</i></a> provides a convenience management command for gathering static files in a single directory so you can serve them easily.</p> <p style="text-align:center">1. Set the <a href="index.html#page_1945"><i>STATIC_ROOT</i></a> setting to the directory from which you’d like to serve these files, for example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">STATIC_ROOT</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"/var/www/example.com/static/"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. Run the <a href="index.html#page_1370"><i>collectstatic</i></a> management command:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">$ python manage.py collectstatic</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This will copy all files from your static folders into the <a href="index.html#page_1945"><i>STATIC_ROOT</i></a> directory.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">3. Use a web server of your choice to serve the files. <a href="index.html#page_885">How to deploy static files</a> covers some common</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">deployment strategies for static files.</p> <p id="page_847" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Learn more</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This document has covered the basics and some common usage patterns.
