Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• Populated (through <a href="index.html#page_978"><i>ContextMixin</i></a>) with the keyword arguments captured from the URL pattern</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">that served the view.</p> <p style="text-align:center">• You can also add context using the <a href="index.html#page_978"><i>extra_context</i></a> keyword argument for <a href="index.html#page_950"><i>as_view()</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>RedirectView</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> django.views.generic.base.<b>RedirectView</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Redirects to a given URL.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The given URL may contain dictionary-style string formatting, which will be interpolated against the parameters captured in the URL. Because keyword interpolation is always done (even if no arguments are passed in), any "%" characters in the URL must be written as "%%" so that Python will convert them to a single percent sign on output.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If the given URL is None, Django will return an HttpResponseGone (410).</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Ancestors (MRO)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This view style="font-size:0.87em">"go-to-django"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Attributes</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>url</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The URL to redirect to, as a string. Or None to raise a 410 (Gone) HTTP error.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>pattern_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The name of the URL pattern to redirect to. Reversing will be done using the same args and kwargs as are passed in for this view.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>permanent</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Whether the redirect should be permanent. The only difference here is the HTTP status code returned. If True, then the redirect will use status code 301. If False, then the redirect will use status code 302. By default, permanent is False.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>query_string</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Whether to pass along the GET query string to the new location. If True, then the query string is appended to the URL. If False, then the query string is discarded. By default, query_string is False.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Methods</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_redirect_url</b>(*args, **kwargs)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Constructs the target URL for redirection.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The args and kwargs arguments are positional and/or keyword arguments <a href="index.html#page_266">captured from the URL</a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_266">pattern</a>, respectively.</p> <p id="page_955" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The default implementation uses <a href="index.html#page_954"><i>url</i></a> as a starting string and performs expansion of % named parameters in that string using the named groups captured in the URL.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If <a href="index.html#page_954"><i>url</i></a> is not set, get_redirect_url() tries to reverse the <a href="index.html#page_954"><i>pattern_name</i></a> using what was captured in the URL (both named and unnamed groups are used).</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If requested by <a href="index.html#page_954"><i>query_string</i></a>, it will also append the query string to the generated URL. Sub-classes may implement any behavior they wish, as long as the method returns a redirect-ready URL string.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.3.2 Generic display views</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The two following generic class-based views are designed to display data. list of objects. It is not intended to be used directly, but rather as a parent</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">class of the <a href="index.html#page_957"><i>django.views.generic.list.ListView</i></a> or other views representing lists of objects.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Ancestors (MRO)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This view inherits methods and attributes from the following views:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_983"><i>django.views.generic.list.MultipleObjectMixin</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_950"><i>django.views.generic.base.View</i></a></p> <p id="page_959" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Methods</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get</b>(request, *args, **kwargs)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Adds object_list to the context. <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_950"><i>django.views.generic.base.View</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Context</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">In addition to the context provided by <a href="index.html#page_983"><i>django.views.generic.list.MultipleObjectMixin</i></a> (via</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a this can be altered to month or day using the at-</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">tribute date_list_period. This also applies to all subclass views.</p> <p id="page_967" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class YearArchiveView</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A yearly archive page showing all available months in a given year. If True, the list of objects will be made available to the context. If False, the None queryset will be used as the object list. By default, this is False.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_make_object_list</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Determine if an object list will be returned as part of the context. style="font-size:0.87em">p</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>WeekArchiveView</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class WeekArchiveView</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A weekly archive page showing all objects in a given week. Objects with a date in the future are not displayed unless you set allow_future to True.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Ancestors (MRO)</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_986"><i>django.views.generic.list.MultipleObjectTemplateResponseMixin</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_979"><i>django.views.generic.base.TemplateResponseMixin</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_978"><i>django.views.generic.dates.BaseWeekArchiveView</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_990"><i>django.views.generic.dates.YearMixin</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_993"><i>django.views.generic.dates.WeekMixin</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_994"><i>django.views.generic.dates.BaseDateListView</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_983"><i>django.views.generic.list.MultipleObjectMixin</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_994"><i>django.views.generic.dates.DateMixin</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_950"><i>django.views.generic.base.View</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Context</p> <p id="page_972"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">In addition to the context provided by <a href="index.html#page_983"><i>MultipleObjectMixin</i></a> (via <a href="index.html#page_994"><i>BaseDateListView</i></a>), the template’s context will be:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• week: A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.date">date</a> object representing the first day of the given week.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• next_week: A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.date">date</a> object representing the first day of the next week, according to <a href="index.html#page_995"><i>allow_empty</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">and <a href="index.html#page_994"><i>allow_future</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• previous_week: A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.date">date</a> object representing the first day of the previous week, according to</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_995"><i>allow_empty</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_994"><i>allow_future</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Notes</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• Uses a default template_name_suffix of _archive_week.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• The week_format attribute is a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/time.html#time.strptime">strptime()</a> format string used to parse the week number. The</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">following values are supported:</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">– '%U': Based on the United States week system where the week begins on Sunday. This is the</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">default value.</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">– '%W': Similar to '%U', except it assumes that the week begins on Monday. This is not the same</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">as the ISO 8601 week number.</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">– '%V': ISO 8601 week number where the week begins on Monday.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Example myapp/views.py:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.views.generic.dates</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">WeekArchiveView</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Article</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ArticleWeekArchiveView</b></span><span style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Example myapp/urls.py:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>date</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:"W"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">of year</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">next_week</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>date</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:"Y"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endif</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">p</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">In this example, you are outputting the week number. Keep in mind that week numbers computed by</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">the <a href="index.html#page_2006"><i>date</i></a> template filter with the 'W' format character are not always the same as those computed by</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/time.html#time.strftime">strftime()</a> and <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/time.html#time.strptime">strptime()</a> with the '%W' format string. For year 2015, for example, week numbers</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">output by <a href="index.html#page_2006"><i>date</i></a> are higher by one compared to those output by <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/time.html#time.strftime">strftime()</a><a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/time.html#time.strftime">. </a>There isn’t an equivalent</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">for the '%U' <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/time.html#time.strftime">strftime()</a> format string in <a href="index.html#page_2006"><i>date</i></a>. Therefore, you should avoid using <a href="index.html#page_2006"><i>date</i></a> to generate URLs for WeekArchiveView.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>DayArchiveView</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class DayArchiveView</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A day archive page showing all objects in a given day. Days in the future throw a 404 error, regardless of whether any objects exist for future days, unless you set allow_future to True.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Ancestors (MRO)</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_986"><i>django.views.generic.list.MultipleObjectTemplateResponseMixin</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_978"><i>django.views.generic.dates.BaseDayArchiveView</i></a> <b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p id="page_974" style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_990"><i>django.views.generic.dates.YearMixin</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_950"><i>django.views.generic.base.View</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Context</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">In addition to the context provided by <a href="index.html#page_983"><i>MultipleObjectMixin</i></a> (via <a href="index.html#page_994"><i>BaseDateListView</i></a>), the template’s context will be:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• day: A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.date">date</a> object representing the given day.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• next_day: A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.date">date</a> object representing the next day, according to <a href="index.html#page_995"><i>allow_empty</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_994"><i>allow_future</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• previous_day: A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.date">date</a> object representing the previous day, according to <a href="index.html#page_995"><i>allow_empty</i></a> and</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_994"><i>allow_future</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• next_month: A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.date">date</a> object representing the first day of the next month, according to <a href="index.html#page_995"><i>allow_empty</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">and <a href="index.html#page_994"><i>allow_future</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• previous_month: A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.date">date</a> object representing the first day of the previous month, according to</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_995"><i>allow_empty</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_994"><i>allow_future</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Notes</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• Uses a default template_name_suffix of _archive_day.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Example myapp/views.py:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span If the object has a date value in the future, the view will throw a 404 error by default, unless you set allow_future to True.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Ancestors (MRO)</p> <p style="font-size:0.87em">"<int:year>/<str:month>/<int:day>/<int:pk>/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">Article, date_field</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"pub_date"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"archive_date_detail"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Example myapp/article_detail.html:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">h1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">h1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p id="page_978"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: All of the generic views listed above have matching Base views that only differ in</p> <p>that they do not include the <a href="index.html#page_986"><i>MultipleObjectTemplateResponseMixin</i></a> (for the archive views) or</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_982"><i>SingleObjectTemplateResponseMixin</i></a> (for the <a href="index.html#page_1012"><i>DateDetailView</i></a>):</p> <p><b>class BaseArchiveIndexView</b></p> <p><b>class BaseYearArchiveView</b></p> <p><b>class BaseMonthArchiveView</b></p> <p><b>class BaseWeekArchiveView</b></p> <p><b>class BaseDayArchiveView</b></p> <p><b>class BaseTodayArchiveView</b></p> <p><b>class BaseDateDetailView</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.3.5 Class-based views mixins</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Class-based views API reference. For introductory material, see <a href="index.html#page_431">Using mixins with class-based views.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Simple mixins</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>ContextMixin</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> django.views.generic.base.<b>ContextMixin</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Attributes</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>extra_context</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A dictionary to include in the context. This is a convenient way of specifying some context in</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_950"><i>as_view()</i>. </a>Example usage:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.views.generic</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">TemplateView</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">TemplateView</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">as_view(extra_context</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Custom Title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">})</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Methods</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_context_data</b>(**kwargs)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns a dictionary representing the template context. The keyword arguments provided will make up the returned context. Example usage:</p> <p id="page_979" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get_context_data</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">context</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_context_data(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">context[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"number"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">random</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">randrange(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">100</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">context</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The template context of all class-based generic views include a view variable that points to the View instance.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Use <b>alters_data</b> where appropriate</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Note that having the view instance in the template context may expose potentially hazardous methods to template authors. To prevent methods like this from being called in the template, set</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">alters_data=True on those methods. For more information, read the documentation on <a href="index.html#page_2036">render-</a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_2036">ing a template context</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>TemplateResponseMixin</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> django.views.generic.base.<b>TemplateResponseMixin</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Provides a mechanism to construct a <a href="index.html#page_2054"><i>TemplateResponse</i>, </a>given suitable context. The template to use is configurable and can be further customized by subclasses.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Attributes</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>template_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The full name of a template to use as defined by a string. Not defining a template_name will raise</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">a <a href="index.html#page_1472"><i>django.core.exceptions.ImproperlyConfigured</i></a> exception.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>template_engine</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>NAME</i></a> of a template engine to use for loading the template. template_engine is passed as the using keyword argument to response_class. Default is None, which tells Django to search for the template in all configured engines.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>response_class</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The response class to be returned by render_to_response method. Default is <a href="index.html#page_2054"><i>TemplateResponse</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The template and context of TemplateResponse instances can be altered later (e.g. in <a href="index.html#page_307">template</a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_307">response middleware</a>).</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If you need custom template loading or custom context object instantiation, create a TemplateResponse subclass and assign it to response_class.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>content_type</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The content type to use for the response. content_type is passed as a keyword argument to response_class. Default is None – meaning that Django uses 'text/html'.</p> <p id="page_980"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Methods</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>render_to_response</b>( context, **response_kwargs)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns a self.response_class instance.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If any keyword arguments are provided, they will be passed to the constructor of the response class.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Calls <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>get_template_names()</i></a> to obtain the list of template names that will be searched looking for an existent template.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_template_names</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns a list of template names to search for when rendering the template. The first template that is found will be used.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The default implementation will return a list containing <a href="index.html#page_979"><i>template_name</i></a> (if it is specified).</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Single object mixins</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>SingleObjectMixin</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> django.views.generic.detail.<b>SingleObjectMixin</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Provides a mechanism for looking up an object associated with the current HTTP request.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Methods and Attributes</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>model</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The model that this view will display data for. Specifying model = Foo is effectively the same as</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">specifying queryset = Foo.objects.all(), where objects stands for Foo’s <a href="index.html#page_194">default manager</a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>queryset</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A QuerySet that represents the objects. If provided, the value of queryset supersedes the value</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">provided for <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>model</i>.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:5em">Warning: queryset is a class attribute with a mutable value so care must be taken when using</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">it directly. Before using it, either call its <a href="index.html#page_1723"><i>all()</i></a> method or retrieve it with <a href="index.html#page_981"><i>get_queryset()</i></a> which takes care of the cloning behind the scenes.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>slug_field</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The name of the field on the model that contains the slug. By default, slug_field is 'slug'.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>slug_url_kwarg</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The name of the URLConf keyword argument that contains the slug. By default, slug_url_kwarg is 'slug'.</p> <p id="page_981" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>pk_url_kwarg</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The name of the URLConf keyword argument that contains the primary key. By default, pk_url_kwarg is 'pk'.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>context_object_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Designates the name of the variable to use in the context.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>query_pk_and_slug</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If True, causes <a href="index.html#page_981"><i>get_object()</i></a> to perform its lookup using both the primary key and the slug. Defaults to False.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">This attribute can help mitigate <a href="https://wiki.owasp.org/index.php/Top_10_2013-A4-Insecure_Direct_Object_References">insecure direct object reference</a> attacks. When applications allow access to individual objects by a sequential primary key, an attacker could brute-force guess all URLs; thereby obtaining a list of all objects in the application. If users with access to individual objects should be prevented from obtaining this list, setting query_pk_and_slug to True will help prevent the guessing of URLs as each URL will require two correct, non-sequential arguments. Using a unique slug may serve the same purpose, but this scheme allows you to have non-unique slugs.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_object</b>(queryset=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns the single object that this view will display. If queryset is provided, that queryset will</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">be used as the source of objects; otherwise, <a href="index.html#page_981"><i>get_queryset()</i></a> will be used. get_object() looks for</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">a <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>pk_url_kwarg</i></a> argument in the arguments to the view; if this argument is found, this method performs a primary-key based lookup using that value. If this argument is not found, it looks for</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">a <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>slug_url_kwarg</i></a> argument, and performs a slug lookup using the <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>slug_field</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">When <a href="index.html#page_981"><i>query_pk_and_slug</i></a> is True, get_object() will perform its lookup using both the primary key and the slug.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_queryset</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns the queryset that will be used to retrieve the object that this view will display. By default,</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_981"><i>get_queryset()</i></a> returns the value of the <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>queryset</i></a> attribute if it is set, otherwise it constructs a</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_1709"><i>QuerySet</i></a> by calling the all() method on the <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>model</i></a> attribute’s default manager.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_context_object_name</b>(obj)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Return the context variable name that will be used to contain the data that this view is manipulat-</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">ing. If <a href="index.html#page_981"><i>context_object_name</i></a> is not set, the context name will be constructed from the model_name of the model that the queryset is composed from. For example, the model Article would have context object named 'article'.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_context_data</b>(**kwargs)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns context data for displaying the object.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The base implementation of this method requires that the self.object attribute be set by the view (even if None). Be sure to do this if you are using this mixin without one of the built-in views that does so.</p> <p id="page_982"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">It returns a dictionary with these contents:</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• object: The object that this view is displaying (self.object).</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• context_object_name: self.object will also be stored under the name returned by</p> <p style="text-align:right"><a href="index.html#page_981"><i>get_context_object_name()</i></a>, which defaults to the lowercased version of the model name.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Context variables override values from template context processors</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Any variables from <a href="index.html#page_981"><i>get_context_data()</i></a> take precedence over context variables from <a href="index.html#page_2042">con-</a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_2042">text processors. </a>For example, if your view sets the <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>model</i></a> attribute to <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>User</i></a>, the default con-</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">text object name of user would override the user variable from the <a href="index.html#page_2043"><i>django.contrib.auth.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_2043"><i>context_processors.auth()</i></a> context processor. Use <a href="index.html#page_981"><i>get_context_object_name()</i></a> to avoid a clash.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_slug_field</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns the name of a slug field to be used to look up by slug. By default this returns the value of</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_980"><i>slug_field</i></a> .</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>SingleObjectTemplateResponseMixin</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> django.views.generic.detail.<b>SingleObjectTemplateResponseMixin</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A mixin class that performs template-based response rendering for views that operate upon a single object instance. Requires that the view it is mixed with provides self.object, the object instance that the view is operating on. self.object will usually be, but is not required to be, an instance of a Django model. It may be None if the view is in the process of constructing a new instance.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Extends</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_979"><i>TemplateResponseMixin</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Methods and Attributes</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>template_name_field</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The field on the current object instance that can be used to determine the name of a candidate template. If either template_name_field itself or the value of the template_name_field on the current object instance is None, the object will not be used for a candidate template name.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>template_name_suffix</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The suffix to append to the auto-generated candidate template name. Default suffix is _detail.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_template_names</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns a list of candidate template names. Returns the following list:</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• the value of template_name on the view (if provided)</p> <p id="page_983" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• the contents of the template_name_field field on the object instance that the view is operat-</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">ing upon (if available)</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• <app_label>/<model_name><template_name_suffix>.html</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Multiple object mixins</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>MultipleObjectMixin</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> django.views.generic.list.<b>MultipleObjectMixin</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A mixin that can be used to display a list of objects.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If paginate_by is specified, Django will paginate the results returned by this. You can specify the page number in the URL in one of two ways:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• Use the page parameter in the URLconf. For example, this is what your URLconf might look like:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"objects/page<int:page>/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, PaginatedView</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">as_view()),</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• Pass the page number via the page query-string parameter. For example, a URL would look like</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">this:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">/objects/?page=3</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">These values and lists are 1-based, not 0-based, so the first page would be represented as page 1.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For more on pagination, read the <a href="index.html#page_715">pagination documentation</a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">As a special case, you are also permitted to use last as a value for page:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">/objects/?page=last</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This allows you to access the final page of results without first having to determine how many pages there are.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Note that page must be either a valid page number or the value last; any other value for page will result in a 404 error.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Extends</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_978"><i>django.views.generic.base.ContextMixin</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Methods and Attributes</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>allow_empty</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A boolean specifying whether to display the page if no objects are available. If this is False and no objects are available, the view will raise a 404 instead of displaying an empty page. By default, this is True.</p> <p id="page_984"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>model</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The model that this view will display data for. Specifying model = Foo is effectively the same as</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">specifying queryset = Foo.objects.all(), where objects stands for Foo’s <a href="index.html#page_194">default manager</a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>queryset</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A QuerySet that represents the objects. If provided, the value of queryset supersedes the value</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">provided for <a href="index.html#page_983"><i>model</i>.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:5em">Warning: queryset is a class attribute with a mutable value so care must be taken when using</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">it directly. Before using it, either call its <a href="index.html#page_1723"><i>all()</i></a> method or retrieve it with <a href="index.html#page_984"><i>get_queryset()</i></a> which takes care of the cloning behind the scenes.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>ordering</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A string or list of strings specifying the ordering to apply to the queryset. Valid values are the</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">same as those for <a href="index.html#page_1712"><i>order_by()</i>.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>paginate_by</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">An integer specifying how many objects should be displayed per page. If this is given, the view will paginate objects with paginate_by objects per page. The view will expect either a page query string parameter (via request.GET) or a page variable specified in the URLconf.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>paginate_orphans</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">An integer specifying the number of “overflow” objects the last page can contain. This extends</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">the <a href="index.html#page_984"><i>paginate_by</i></a> limit on the last page by up to paginate_orphans, in order to keep the last page from having a very small number of objects.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>page_kwarg</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A string specifying the name to use for the page parameter. The view will expect this parameter to be available either as a query string parameter (via request.GET) or as a kwarg variable specified in the URLconf. Defaults to page.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>paginator_class</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The paginator class to be used for pagination. By default, <a href="index.html#page_1855"><i>django.core.paginator.Paginator</i></a> is</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">used. If the custom paginator class doesn’t have the same constructor interface as <a href="index.html#page_1855"><i>django.core.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_1855"><i>paginator.Paginator</i></a> , you will also need to provide an implementation for <a href="index.html#page_985"><i>get_paginator()</i></a><a href="index.html#page_985">.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>context_object_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Designates the name of the variable to use in the context.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_queryset</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Get the list of items for this view. This must be an iterable and may be a queryset (in which queryset-specific behavior will be enabled).</p> <p id="page_985" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_ordering</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns a string (or iterable of strings) that defines the ordering that will be applied to the queryset.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns <a href="index.html#page_984"><i>ordering</i></a> by default.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>paginate_queryset</b>(queryset, page_size)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns a 4-tuple containing (paginator, page, object_list, is_paginated).</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Constructed by paginating queryset into pages of size page_size. If the request contains a page argument, either as a captured URL argument or as a GET argument, object_list will corre-spond to the objects from that page.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_paginate_by</b>(queryset)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns the number of items to paginate by, or None for no pagination. If this method returns False and no objects are available, the view will raise a 404 instead of displaying an empty page. By default, this is True.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_context_object_name</b>(object_list)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Return the context variable name that will be used to contain the list of data that this view is</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">manipulating. If object_list is a queryset of Django objects and <a href="index.html#page_984"><i>context_object_name</i></a> is not set, the context name will be the model_name of the model that the queryset is composed from, with postfix '_list' appended. For example, the model Article would have a context object named article_list.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_context_data</b>(**kwargs)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns context data for displaying the list of objects.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Context</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• object_list: The list of objects that this view is displaying. If context_object_name is specified,</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">that variable will also be set in the context, with the same value as object_list.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• is_paginated: A boolean representing whether the results are paginated. Specifically, this is set</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">to False if no page size has been specified, or if the available objects do not span multiple pages.</p> <p id="page_986"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• paginator: An instance of <a href="index.html#page_1855"><i>django.core.paginator.Paginator</i></a>. If the page is not paginated, this con-</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">text variable will be None.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>MultipleObjectTemplateResponseMixin</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> django.views.generic.list.<b>MultipleObjectTemplateResponseMixin</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A mixin class that performs template-based response rendering for views that operate upon a list of object instances. This function</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">can also return None or raise an <a href="index.html#page_285"><i>Http404</i></a> exception, depending on the values of <a href="index.html#page_995"><i>allow_empty</i></a> and</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_994"><i>allow_future</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>DayMixin</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class DayMixin</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A mixin that can be used to retrieve and provide parsing information for a day component of a date.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Methods and Attributes</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>day_format</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/time.html#time.strftime">strftime()</a> format to use when parsing the day. By default, this is '%d'.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>day</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional The value for the day, as a string. By default, set to None, which means the day will be determined using other means.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_day_format</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns the <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/time.html#time.strftime">strftime()</a> format to use when parsing the day. Returns <a href="index.html#page_992"><i>day_format</i></a> by default.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_day</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns the day for which this view will display data, as a string. Tries the following sources, in order:</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• The value of the <a href="index.html#page_992"><i>DayMixin.day</i></a> attribute.</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• The value of the day argument captured in the URL pattern.</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• The value of the day GET query argument.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Raises a 404 if no valid day specification can be found.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_next_day</b>( date)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns a date object containing the next valid day after the date provided. This function can</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">also return None or raise an <a href="index.html#page_285"><i>Http404</i></a> exception, depending on the values of <a href="index.html#page_995"><i>allow_empty</i></a> and</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_994"><i>allow_future</i></a>.</p> <p id="page_993" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_previous_day</b>(date)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns a date object containing the previous valid day. This function can also return None or</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">raise an <a href="index.html#page_285"><i>Http404</i></a> exception, depending on the values of <a href="index.html#page_995"><i>allow_empty</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_994"><i>allow_future</i></a><a href="index.html#page_994">.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>WeekMixin</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class WeekMixin</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A mixin that can be used to retrieve and provide parsing information for a week component of a date.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Methods and Attributes</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>week_format</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/time.html#time.strftime">strftime()</a> format to use when parsing the week. By default, this is '%U', which means the week starts on Sunday. Set it to '%W' or '%V' (ISO 8601 week) if your week starts on Monday.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>week</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional The value for the week, as a string. By default, set to None, which means the week will be determined using other means.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_week_format</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns the <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/time.html#time.strftime">strftime()</a> format to use when parsing the week. Returns <a href="index.html#page_993"><i>week_format</i></a> by default.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_week</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns the week for which this view will display data, as a string. Tries the following sources, in order:</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• The value of the <a href="index.html#page_993"><i>WeekMixin.week</i></a> attribute.</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• The value of the week argument captured in the URL pattern</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• The value of the week GET query argument.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Raises a 404 if no valid week specification can be found.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_next_week</b>(date)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns a date object containing the first day of the week after the date provided. This function</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">can also return None or raise an <a href="index.html#page_285"><i>Http404</i></a> exception, depending on the values of <a href="index.html#page_995"><i>allow_empty</i></a> and</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_994"><i>allow_future</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_prev_week</b>(date)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns a date object containing the first day of the week before the date provided. This function</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">can also return None or raise an <a href="index.html#page_285"><i>Http404</i></a> exception, depending on the values of <a href="index.html#page_995"><i>allow_empty</i></a> and</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_994"><i>allow_future</i></a>.</p> <p id="page_994"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>DateMixin</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class DateMixin</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A mixin class providing common behavior for all date-based views.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Methods and Attributes</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>date_field</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The name of the DateField or DateTimeField in the QuerySet’s model that the date-based archive should use to determine the list of objects to display on the page.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">When <a href="index.html#page_693">time zone support</a> is enabled and date_field is a DateTimeField, dates are assumed to be in the current time zone. Otherwise, the queryset could include objects from the previous or the next day in the end user’s time zone.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:5em">Warning: In this situation, if you have implemented per-user time zone selection, the same URL may show a different set of objects, depending on the end user’s time zone. To avoid this, you should use a DateField as the date_field attribute.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>allow_future</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A boolean specifying whether to include “future” objects on this page, where “future” means ob-jects in which the field specified in date_field is greater than the current date/time. By default, this is False.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_date_field</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns the name of the field that contains the date data that this view will operate on. Returns</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_994"><i>date_field</i></a> by default.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_allow_future</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Determine whether to include “future” objects on this page, where “future” means objects in which</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">the field specified in date_field is greater than the current date/time. Returns <a href="index.html#page_994"><i>allow_future</i></a> by default.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>BaseDateListView</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class BaseDateListView</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A base class that provides common behavior for all date-based views. There won’t normally be a reason</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">to instantiate <a href="index.html#page_994"><i>BaseDateListView</i></a>; instantiate one of the subclasses instead.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">While this view (and its subclasses) are executing, self.object_list will contain the list of objects that the view is operating upon, and self.date_list will contain the list of dates for which data is available.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Mixins</p> <p id="page_995" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_994"><i>DateMixin</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_983"><i>MultipleObjectMixin</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Methods and Attributes</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>allow_empty</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A boolean specifying whether to display the page if no objects are available. If this is True and no objects are available, the view will display an empty page instead of raising a 404.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">This is identical to <a href="index.html#page_983"><i>django.views.generic.list.MultipleObjectMixin.allow_empty</i></a>, except for the default value, which is False.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>date_list_period</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional A string defining the aggregation period for date_list. It must be one of 'year' (de-fault), 'month', or 'day'.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_dated_items</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns a 3-tuple containing (date_list, object_list, extra_context).</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">date_list is the list of dates for which data is available. object_list is the list of objects. extra_context is a dictionary of context data that will be added to any context data provided by</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">the <a href="index.html#page_983"><i>MultipleObjectMixin</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_dated_queryset</b> ( **lookup)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns a queryset, filtered using the query arguments defined by lookup. Enforces any restric-tions on the queryset, such as allow_empty and allow_future.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_date_list_period</b>()</p> <p style="text-align:center">Returns the aggregation period for date_list. Returns <a href="index.html#page_995"><i>date_list_period</i></a> by default.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_date_list</b>(queryset, date_type=None, ordering='ASC')</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns the list of dates of type date_type for which queryset contains entries. For example, get_date_list(qs, 'year') will return the list of years for which qs has entries. If date_type</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">isn’t provided, the result of <a href="index.html#page_995"><i>get_date_list_period()</i></a> is used. date_type and ordering are</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">passed to <a href="index.html#page_1721"><i>QuerySet.dates()</i>.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.3.6 Class-based generic views - flattened index</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This index provides an alternate organization of the reference documentation for class-based views. href="https://ccbv.co.uk/">Classy Class-Based Views</a> provides a nice interface to navigate the class hierarchy of the built-in class-based views.</p> <p id="page_996"><b>Django Documentation,
