[<i>get_year_format()</i>]</a></p> <p>Methods</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_950"><i>as_view()</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_951"><i>dispatch()</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• get()</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_981"><i>get_context_data()</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_992"><i>get_next_day()</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_992"><i>get_next_month()</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_981"><i>get_object()</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_992"><i>get_previous_day()</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_992"><i>get_previous_month()</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• head()</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_951"><i>http_method_not_allowed()</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_980"><i>render_to_response()</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_951"><i>setup()</i></a></p> <p id="page_1014"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.3.7 Specification</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Each request served by a class-based view has an independent state; therefore, it is safe to store state variables on the instance (i.e., self.foo = 3 is a thread-safe operation).</p> <p>A class-based view is deployed into a URL pattern using the <a href="index.html#page_950"><i>as_view()</i></a> classmethod:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"view/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, MyView</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">as_view(size</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">42</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Thread safety with view arguments</p> <p>Arguments passed to a view are shared between every instance of a view. This means that you shouldn’t use a list, dictionary, or any other mutable object as an argument to a view. If you do and the shared object is modified, the actions of one user visiting your view could have an effect on subsequent users visiting the same view.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Arguments passed into <a href="index.html#page_950"><i>as_view()</i></a> will be assigned onto the instance that is used to service a request. Using the previous example, this means that every request on MyView is able to use self.size. Arguments must correspond to attributes that already exist on the class (return True on a hasattr check).</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.3.8 Base vs Generic views</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Base class-based views can be thought of as parent views, which can be used by themselves or inherited from. They may not provide all the capabilities required for projects, in which case there are Mixins which extend what base views can do.</p> <p>Django’s generic views are built off of those base views, and were developed as a shortcut for common usage patterns such as displaying the details of an object. They take certain common idioms and patterns found in view development and abstract them so that you can quickly write common views of data without having to repeat yourself.</p> <p>Most generic views require the queryset key, which is a QuerySet instance; see <a href="index.html#page_143">Making queries</a> for more information about QuerySet objects.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1015" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.47em"><b>6.4 Clickjacking Protection</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The clickjacking middleware and decorators provide easy-to-use protection against <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clickjacking">clickjacking. </a>This type of attack occurs when a malicious site tricks a user into clicking on a concealed element of another site which they have loaded in a hidden frame or iframe.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.4.1 An example of clickjacking</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Suppose an online store has a page where a logged in user can click “Buy Now” to purchase an item. A user has chosen to stay logged into the store all the time for convenience. An attacker site might create an “I Like Ponies” button on one of their own pages, and load the store’s page in a transparent iframe such that the “Buy Now” button is invisibly overlaid on the “I Like Ponies” button. If the user visits the attacker’s site, clicking “I Like Ponies” will cause an inadvertent click on the “Buy Now” button and an unknowing purchase of the item.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.4.2 Preventing clickjacking</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Modern browsers honor the <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/X-Frame-Options">X-Frame-Options</a> HTTP header that indicates whether or not a resource is al-lowed to load within a frame or iframe. If the response contains the header with a value of SAMEORIGIN then the browser will only load the resource in a frame if the request originated from the same site. If the header is set to DENY then the browser will block the resource from loading in a frame no matter which site made the request.</p> <p>Django provides a few ways to include this header in responses from your site:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. A middleware that sets the header in all responses.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. A set of view decorators that can be used to override the middleware or to only set the header for certain</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">views.</p> <p>The X-Frame-Options HTTP header will only be set by the middleware or view decorators if it is not already present in the response.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.4.3 How to use it</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Setting X-Frame-Options for all responses</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To set the same X-Frame-Options value for all responses in your site, put 'django.middleware.</p> <p>clickjacking.XFrameOptionsMiddleware' to <a href="index.html#page_1923"><i>MIDDLEWARE</i></a> :</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">MIDDLEWARE</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.middleware.clickjacking.XFrameOptionsMiddleware"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_1016"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This middleware is enabled in the settings file generated by <a href="index.html#page_1456"><i>startproject</i></a>.</p> <p>By default, the middleware will set the X-Frame-Options header to DENY for every outgoing HttpResponse.</p> <p>If you want any other value for this header instead, set the <a href="index.html#page_1937"><i>X_FRAME_OPTIONS</i></a> setting:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">X_FRAME_OPTIONS</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"SAMEORIGIN"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When using the middleware there may be some views where you do not want the X-Frame-Options header set. For those cases, you can use a view decorator that tells the middleware not to set the header:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.http</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.views.decorators.clickjacking</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">xframe_options_exempt</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@xframe_options_exempt</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ok_to_load_in_a_frame</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"This page is safe to load in a frame on any site."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: If you want to submit a form or access a session cookie within a frame or iframe, you may need to</p> <p>modify the <a href="index.html#page_1894"><i>CSRF_COOKIE_SAMESITE</i></a> or <a href="index.html#page_1943"><i>SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE</i></a> settings.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Setting X-Frame-Options per view</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To set the X-Frame-Options header on a per view basis, Django provides these decorators:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.http</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.views.decorators.clickjacking</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">xframe_options_deny</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.views.decorators.clickjacking</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">xframe_options_sameorigin</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@xframe_options_deny</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>view_one</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"I won't display in any frame!"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@xframe_options_sameorigin</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>view_two</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Display in a frame if it's from the same origin as me."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p id="page_1017" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note that you can use the decorators in conjunction with the middleware. Use of a decorator overrides the middleware.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.4.4 Limitations</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The X-Frame-Options header will only protect against clickjacking in <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/X-Frame-Options#browser_compatibility">modern browsers</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.47em"><b>6.5</b></span> <span style="font-size:1.47em"><b>contrib</b></span> <span style="font-size:1.47em"><b>packages</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django aims to follow Python’s <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/stdlib.html#tut-batteries-included">“batteries included” philosophy</a>. It ships with a variety of extra, optional tools that solve common web development problems.</p> <p>This code lives in <a href="https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/contrib">django/contrib</a> in the Django distribution. This document gives a rundown of the packages in contrib, along with any dependencies those packages have.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Including <b>contrib</b> packages in <b>INSTALLED_APPS</b></p> <p>For most of these add-ons – specifically, the add-ons that include either models or template tags – you’ll need</p> <p>to add the package name (e.g., 'django.contrib.redirects') to your <a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a> setting and rerun manage.py migrate.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.5.1 The Django admin site</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>One of the most powerful parts of Django is the automatic admin interface. It reads metadata from your models to provide a quick, model-centric interface where trusted users can manage content on your site. The admin’s recommended use is limited to an organization’s internal management tool. It’s not intended for building your entire front end around.</p> <p>The admin has many hooks for customization, but beware of trying to use those hooks exclusively. If you need to provide a more process-centric interface that abstracts away the implementation details of database tables and fields, then it’s probably time to write your own views.</p> <p>In this document we discuss how to activate, use, and customize Django’s admin interface.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1018"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Overview</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The admin is enabled in the default project template used by <a href="index.html#page_1456"><i>startproject</i>.</a></p> <p>If you’re not using the default project template, here are the requirements:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. Add 'django.contrib.admin' and its dependencies - <a href="index.html#page_598"><i>django.contrib.auth</i></a>, <a href="index.html#page_1114"><i>django.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1114"><i>contrib.contenttypes</i></a>, <a href="index.html#page_1287"><i>django.contrib.messages</i></a>, and <a href="index.html#page_311"><i>django.contrib.sessions</i></a>- to your</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. Configure a <a href="index.html#page_407"><i>DjangoTemplates</i></a> backend in your <a href="index.html#page_1932"><i>TEMPLATES</i></a> setting with django.template.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">context_processors.request, django.contrib.auth.context_processors.auth, and django. contrib.messages.context_processors.messages in the 'context_processors' option of</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>OPTIONS</i></a> .</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">3. If you’ve customized the <a href="index.html#page_1923"><i>MIDDLEWARE</i></a> setting, <a href="index.html#page_1599"><i>django.contrib.sessions.middleware.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1599"><i>SessionMiddleware</i> , <i>django.contrib.auth.middleware.AuthenticationMiddleware</i></a>, and <a href="index.html#page_1594"><i>django.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1594"><i>contrib.messages.middleware.MessageMiddleware</i></a> must be included.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">4. <a href="index.html#page_1094">Hook the admin’s URLs into your URLconf.</a></p> <p>After you’ve taken these steps, you’ll be able to use the admin site by visiting the URL you hooked it into (/admin/, by default).</p> <p>If you need to create a user to login with, use the <a href="index.html#page_1461"><i>createsuperuser</i></a> command. By default, logging in to the</p> <p>admin requires that the user has the <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>is_staff</i></a> attribute set to True.</p> <p>Finally, determine which of your application’s models should be editable in the admin interface. For each of</p> <p>those models, register them with the admin as described in <a href="index.html#page_1038"><i>ModelAdmin</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Other topics</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Admin actions</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The basic workflow of Django’s admin is, in a nutshell, “select an object, then change it.” This works well for a majority of use cases. However, if you need to make the same change to many objects at once, this workflow can be quite tedious.</p> <p>In these cases, Django’s admin lets you write and register “actions” – functions that get called with a list of objects selected on the change list page.</p> <p>If you look at any change list in the admin, you’ll see this feature in action; Django ships with a “delete selected objects” action available to all models. For example, here’s the user module from Django’s built-in</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_598"><i>django.contrib.auth</i></a> app:</p> <p id="page_1019" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p><img src="index-1019_1.png" alt="" width="702px" height="314px"/></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: The “delete selected objects” action uses <a href="index.html#page_1760"><i>QuerySet.delete()</i></a> for efficiency reasons, which</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">has an important caveat: your model’s delete() method will not be called.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">If you wish to override this behavior, you can override <a href="index.html#page_1063"><i>ModelAdmin.delete_queryset()</i></a> or write a cus-</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">tom action which does deletion in your preferred manner – for example, by calling Model.delete() for</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">each of the selected items.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">For more background on bulk deletion, see the documentation on <a href="index.html#page_168">object deletion</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Read on to find out how to add your own actions to this list.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Writing actions</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The easiest way to explain actions is by example, so let’s dive in.</p> <p>A common use case for admin actions is the bulk updating of a model. Imagine a news application with an Article model:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">STATUS_CHOICES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"d"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Draft"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"p"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Published"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"w"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Withdrawn"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Article</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Model):</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_1020"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">100</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">body</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">TextField()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">status</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, choices</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">STATUS_CHOICES)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>__str__</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A common task we might perform with a model like this is to update an article’s status from “draft” to “published”. We could easily do this in the admin one article at a time, but if we wanted to bulk-publish a group of articles, it’d be tedious. So, let’s write an action that lets us change an article’s status to “published.”</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Writing action functions</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>First, we’ll need to write a function that gets called when the action is triggered from the admin. Action functions are regular functions that take three arguments:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The current <a href="index.html#page_1038"><i>ModelAdmin</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• An <a href="index.html#page_1859"><i>HttpRequest</i></a> representing the current request,</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• A <a href="index.html#page_1709"><i>QuerySet</i></a> containing the set of objects selected by the user.</p> <p>Our publish-these-articles function won’t need the <a href="index.html#page_1038"><i>ModelAdmin</i></a> or the request object, but we will use the queryset:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>make_published</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(modeladmin, request, queryset):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">queryset</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">update(status</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"p"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: For the best performance, we’re using the queryset’s <a href="index.html#page_170">update method. </a>Other types of actions might need to deal with each object individually; in these cases we’d iterate over the queryset:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">obj</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">queryset:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">do_something_with(obj)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>That’s actually all there is to writing an action! However, we’ll take one more optional-but-useful step and give the action a “nice” title in the admin. By default, this action would appear in the action list as “Make published” – the function name, with underscores replaced by spaces. That’s fine, but we can provide a</p> <p>better, more human-friendly name by using the <a href="index.html#page_1028"><i>action()</i></a> decorator on the make_published function:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_1021" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">action(description</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Mark selected stories as published"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>make_published</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(modeladmin, request, queryset):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">queryset</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">update(status</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"p"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: This might look familiar; the admin’s <a href="index.html#page_1048"><i>list_display</i></a> option uses a similar technique with the</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1100"><i>display()</i></a> decorator to provide human-readable descriptions for callback functions registered there, too.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Adding actions to the ModelAdmin</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Next, we’ll need to inform our <a href="index.html#page_1038"><i>ModelAdmin</i></a> of the action. This works just like any other configuration option. So, the complete admin.py with the action and its registration would look like:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Article</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">action(description</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Mark selected stories as published"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>make_published</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(modeladmin, request, queryset):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">queryset</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">update(status</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"p"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ArticleAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">list_display</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"status"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">ordering</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">actions</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[make_published]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">register(Article, ArticleAdmin)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>That code will give us an admin change list that looks something like this:</p> <p id="page_1022"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p><img src="index-1022_1.png" alt="" width="702px" height="333px"/></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>That’s really all there is to it! If you’re itching to write your own actions, you now know enough to get started. The rest of this document covers more advanced techniques.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Handling errors in actions</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If there are foreseeable error conditions that may occur while running your action, you should grace-</p> <p>fully inform the user of the problem. This means handling exceptions and using <a href="index.html#page_1073"><i>django.contrib.admin.</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1073"><i>ModelAdmin.message_user()</i></a> to display a user friendly description of the problem in the response.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Advanced action techniques</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>There’s a couple of extra options and possibilities you can exploit for more advanced options.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Actions as ModelAdmin methods</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The example above shows the make_published action defined as a function. That’s perfectly fine, but it’s not perfect from a code design point of view: since the action is tightly coupled to the Article object, it makes sense to hook the action to the ArticleAdmin object itself.</p> <p>You can do it like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ArticleAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">actions</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"make_published"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_1023" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">action(description</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Mark selected stories as published"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>make_published</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, request, queryset):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">queryset</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">update(status</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"p"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Notice first that we’ve moved make_published into a method and renamed the modeladmin parameter to self, and second that we’ve now put the string 'make_published' in actions instead of a direct function</p> <p>reference. This tells the <a href="index.html#page_1038"><i>ModelAdmin</i></a> to look up the action as a method.</p> <p>Defining actions as methods gives the action more idiomatic access to the <a href="index.html#page_1038"><i>ModelAdmin</i></a> itself, allowing the action to call any of the methods provided by the admin.</p> <p>For example, we can use self to flash a message to the user informing them that the action was successful:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ngettext</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ArticleAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>make_published</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, request, queryset):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">updated</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">queryset</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">update(status</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"p"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">message_user(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">request,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">ngettext(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"%d story was successfully marked as published."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"%d stories were successfully marked as published."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">updated,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">updated,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">SUCCESS,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This make the action match what the admin itself does after successfully performing an action:</p> <p id="page_1024"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p><img src="index-1024_1.png" alt="" width="702px" height="364px"/></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Actions that provide intermediate pages</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>By default, after an action is performed the user is redirected back to the original change list page. However, some actions, especially more complex ones, will need to return intermediate pages. For example, the built-in delete action asks for confirmation before deleting the selected objects.</p> <p>To provide an intermediary page, return an <a href="index.html#page_1871"><i>HttpResponse</i></a> (or subclass) from your action. For example, you</p> <p>might write an export function that uses Django’s <a href="index.html#page_731">serialization functions</a> to dump some selected objects as JSON:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.core</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">serializers</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.http</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>export_as_json</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(modeladmin, request, queryset):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse(content_type</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"application/json"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">serializers</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">serialize(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"json"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, queryset, stream</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">response)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">response</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Generally, something like the above isn’t considered a great idea. Most of the time, the best practice will be to</p> <p>return an <a href="index.html#page_1877"><i>HttpResponseRedirect</i></a> and redirect the user to a view you’ve written, passing the list of selected objects in the GET query string. This allows you to provide complex interaction logic on the intermediary pages. For example, if you wanted to provide a more complete export function, you’d want to let the user choose a format, and possibly a list of fields to include in the export. The best thing to do would be to write a small action that redirects to your custom export view:</p> <p id="page_1025" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.contenttypes.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ContentType</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.http</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponseRedirect</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>export_selected_objects</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(modeladmin, request, queryset):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">selected</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">queryset</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">values_list(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"pk"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, flat</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">ct</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ContentType</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_for_model(queryset</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">model)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponseRedirect(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/export/?ct=%s&ids=%s"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">ct</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">pk,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">","</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">join(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">str</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(pk)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">pk</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">selected),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>As you can see, the action is rather short; all the complex logic would belong in your export view. This would need to deal with objects of any type, hence the business with the ContentType.</p> <p>Writing this view is left as an exercise to the reader.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Making actions available site-wide</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>AdminSite.<b>add_action</b>(action, name=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Some actions are best if they’re made available to any object in the admin site – the export action</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">defined above would be a good candidate. You can make an action globally available using <a href="index.html#page_1025"><i>AdminSite.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1025"><i>add_action()</i> . </a>For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">add_action(export_selected_objects)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This makes the export_selected_objects action globally available as an action named “ex-port_selected_objects”. You can explicitly give the action a name – good if you later want to pro-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">grammatically <a href="index.html#page_1026">remove the action</a> – by passing a second argument to <a href="index.html#page_1025"><i>AdminSite.add_action()</i></a><a href="index.html#page_1025">:</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">add_action(export_selected_objects,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"export_selected"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1026"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Disabling actions</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Sometimes you need to disable certain actions – especially those <a href="index.html#page_1025">registered site-wide</a> – for particular objects. There’s a few ways you can disable actions:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Disabling a site-wide action</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>AdminSite.<b>disable_action</b>(name)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you need to disable a <a href="index.html#page_1025">site-wide action</a> you can call <a href="index.html#page_1026"><i>AdminSite.disable_action()</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For example, you can use this method to remove the built-in “delete selected objects” action:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">disable_action(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"delete_selected"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Once you’ve done the above, that action will no longer be available site-wide.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If, however, you need to reenable a globally-disabled action for one particular model, list it explicitly in your ModelAdmin.actions list:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Globally disable delete selected</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">disable_action(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"delete_selected"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># This ModelAdmin will not have delete_selected available</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>SomeModelAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">actions</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"some_other_action"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># This one will</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AnotherModelAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">actions</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"delete_selected"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"a_third_action"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Disabling all actions for a particular ModelAdmin</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you want no bulk actions available for a given <a href="index.html#page_1038"><i>ModelAdmin</i></a>, set <a href="index.html#page_1040"><i>ModelAdmin.actions</i></a> to None:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyModelAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">actions</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>= None</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This tells the <a href="index.html#page_1038"><i>ModelAdmin</i></a> to not display or allow any actions, including any <a href="index.html#page_1025">site-wide actions</a>.</p> <p id="page_1027" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Conditionally enabling or disabling actions</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>get_actions</b>( request)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Finally, you can conditionally enable or disable actions on a per-request (and hence per-user basis) by</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">overriding <a href="index.html#page_1027"><i>ModelAdmin.get_actions()</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This returns a dictionary of actions allowed. The keys are action names, and the values are (function, name, short_description) tuples.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For example, if you only want users whose names begin with ‘J’ to be able to delete objects in bulk:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyModelAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get_actions</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">actions</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_actions(request)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">username[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">0</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">upper()</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>!=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"J"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"delete_selected"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">actions:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:8em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>del</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">actions[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"delete_selected"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">actions</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Setting permissions for actions</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Actions may limit their availability to users with specific permissions by wrapping the action function with</p> <p>the <a href="index.html#page_1028"><i>action()</i></a> decorator and passing the permissions argument:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">action(permissions</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"change"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">])</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>make_published</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(modeladmin, request, queryset):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">queryset</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">update(status</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"p"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The make_published() action will only be available to users that pass the <a href="index.html#page_1072"><i>ModelAdmin.</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1072"><i>has_change_permission()</i></a> check.</p> <p>If permissions has more than one permission, the action will be available as long as the user passes at least one of the checks.</p> <p>Available values for permissions and the corresponding method checks are:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'add': <a href="index.html#page_1072"><i>ModelAdmin.has_add_permission()</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'change': <a href="index.html#page_1072"><i>ModelAdmin.has_change_permission()</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'delete': <a href="index.html#page_1072"><i>ModelAdmin.has_delete_permission()</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'view': <a href="index.html#page_1072"><i>ModelAdmin.has_view_permission()</i></a></p> <p>You can specify any other value as long as you implement a corresponding has_<value>_permission(self, request) method on the ModelAdmin.</p> <p id="page_1028"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.auth</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">get_permission_codename</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ArticleAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">actions</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"make_published"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">action(permissions</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"publish"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">])</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>make_published</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, request, queryset):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">queryset</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">update(status</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"p"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>has_publish_permission</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"""Does the user have the publish permission?"""</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">opts</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">opts</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">codename</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">get_permission_codename(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"publish"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, opts)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">has_perm(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"%s.%s"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(opts</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">app_label, codename))</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>The action decorator</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>action</b>(*, permissions=None, description=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This decorator can be used for setting specific attributes on custom action functions that can be used</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">with <a href="index.html#page_1040"><i>actions</i>:</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">action(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">permissions</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"publish"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">description</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Mark selected stories as published"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>make_published</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, request, queryset):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">queryset</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">update(status</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"p"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This is equivalent to setting some attributes (with the original, longer names) on the function directly:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>make_published</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, request, queryset):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">queryset</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">update(status</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"p"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">make_published</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">allowed_permissions</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"publish"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">make_published</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">short_description</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Mark selected stories as published"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Use of this decorator is not compulsory to make an action function, but it can be useful to use it without arguments as a marker in your source to identify the purpose of the function:</p> <p id="page_1029" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@admin</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">action</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>make_inactive</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, request, queryset):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">queryset</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">update(is_active</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=False</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">In this case it will add no attributes to the function.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Action descriptions are %-formatted and may contain '%(verbose_name)s' and '%(verbose_name_plural)s' placeholders, which are replaced, respectively, by the model’s</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1687"><i>verbose_name</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1687"><i>verbose_name_plural</i>.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>ModelAdmin List Filters</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin classes can define list filters that appear in the right sidebar of the change list page of the admin, as illustrated in the following screenshot:</p> <p><img src="index-1029_1.png" alt="" width="702px" height="360px"/></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To activate per-field filtering, set <a href="index.html#page_1055"><i>ModelAdmin.list_filter</i></a> to a list or tuple of elements, where each element is one of the following types:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• A field name.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• A subclass of django.contrib.admin.SimpleListFilter.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• A 2-tuple containing a field name and a subclass of django.contrib.admin.FieldListFilter.</p> <p>See the examples below for discussion of each of these options for defining list_filter.</p> <p id="page_1030"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using a field name</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The simplest option is to specify the required field names from your model.</p> <p>Each specified field should be either a BooleanField, CharField, DateField, DateTimeField, IntegerField, ForeignKey or ManyToManyField, for example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>PersonAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">list_filter</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"is_staff"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"company"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Field names in list_filter can also span relations using the __ lookup, for example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>PersonAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">UserAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">list_filter</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"company__name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using a SimpleListFilter</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>For custom filtering, you can define your own list filter by subclassing django.contrib.admin. SimpleListFilter. You need to provide the title and parameter_name attributes, and override the lookups and queryset methods, e.g.:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.translation</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span
