style="font-size:0.87em">qs</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">birthday__gte</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">date(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1990</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">birthday__lte</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">date(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1999</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">12</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">31</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">exists():</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>yield</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"90s"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, _(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"in the nineties"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">))</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using a field name and an explicit FieldListFilter</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Finally, if you wish to specify an explicit filter type to use with a field you may provide a list_filter item as a 2-tuple, where the first element is a field name and the second element is a class inheriting from django.contrib.admin.FieldListFilter, for example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>PersonAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">list_filter</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"is_staff"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">BooleanFieldListFilter),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Here the is_staff field will use the BooleanFieldListFilter. Specifying only the field name, fields will automatically use the appropriate filter for most cases, but this format allows you to control the filter used.</p> <p>The following examples show available filter classes that you need to opt-in to use.</p> <p>You can limit the choices of a related model to the objects involved in that relation using RelatedOnlyFieldListFilter:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>BookAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">list_filter</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"author"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">RelatedOnlyFieldListFilter),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Assuming author is a ForeignKey to a User model, this will limit the list_filter choices to the users who</p> <p id="page_1033" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>have written a book, instead of listing all users.</p> <p>You can filter empty values using EmptyFieldListFilter, which can filter on both empty strings and nulls, depending on what the field allows to store:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>BookAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">list_filter</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">EmptyFieldListFilter),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>By defining a filter using the __in lookup, it is possible to filter for any of a group of values. You need to override the expected_parameters method, and the specify the lookup_kwargs attribute with the appro-priate field name. By default, multiple values in the query string will be separated with commas, but this can be customized via the list_separator attribute. The following example shows such a filter using the vertical-pipe character as the separator:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>FilterWithCustomSeparator</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">FieldListFilter):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># custom list separator that should be used to separate values.</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">list_separator</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"|"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>__init__</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, field, request, params, model, model_admin, field_path):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">lookup_kwarg</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"%s__in"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">field_path</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>__init__</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(field, request, params, model, model_admin, field_path)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>expected_parameters</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">lookup_kwarg]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: The <a href="index.html#page_1118"><i>GenericForeignKey</i></a> field is not supported.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>List filters typically appear only if the filter has more than one choice. A filter’s has_output() method con-trols whether or not it appears.</p> <p>It is possible to specify a custom template for rendering a list filter:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>FilterWithCustomTemplate</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">SimpleListFilter):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">template</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"custom_template.html"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>See the default template provided by Django (admin/filter.html) for a concrete example.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1034"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Facets</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>By default, counts for each filter, known as facets, can be shown by toggling on via the admin UI. These</p> <p>counts will update according to the currently applied filters. See <a href="index.html#page_1056"><i>ModelAdmin.show_facets</i></a> for more details.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>The Django admin documentation generator</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django’s <a href="index.html#page_1034"><i>admindocs</i></a> app pulls documentation from the docstrings of models, views, template tags, and</p> <p>template filters for any app in <a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a> and makes that documentation available from the <a href="index.html#page_1017"><i>Django</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1017"><i>admin</i></a> .</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Overview</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To activate the <a href="index.html#page_1034"><i>admindocs</i>, </a>you will need to do the following:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Add <a href="index.html#page_1034"><i>django.contrib.admindocs</i></a> to your <a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Add path('admin/doc/', include('django.contrib.admindocs.urls')) to your urlpatterns.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Make sure it’s included before the 'admin/' entry, so that requests to /admin/doc/ don’t get handled by the latter entry.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Install the <a href="https://pypi.org/project/docutils/">docutils</a> 0.19+ package.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Optional: Using the admindocs bookmarklets requires django.contrib.admindocs.middleware.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">XViewMiddleware to be installed.</p> <p>Once those steps are complete, you can start browsing the documentation by going to your admin interface and clicking the “Documentation” link in the upper right of the page.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Documentation helpers</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The following special markup can be used in your docstrings to easily create hyperlinks to other components:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:8em">Django Component reStructuredText roles</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">Models :model:`app_label.ModelName`</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">Views :view:`app_label.view_name`</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">Template tags :tag:`tagname`</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">Template filters :filter:`filtername`</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">Templates :template:`path/to/template.html`</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Each of these support custom link text with the format :role:`link text <link>`. For example, :tag:`block <built_in-block>`.</p> <p>Support for custom link text was added.</p> <p id="page_1035" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Model reference</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The models section of the admindocs page describes each model that the user has access to along with all the fields, properties, and methods available on it. Relationships to other models appear as hyperlinks. Descrip-tions are pulled from help_text attributes on fields or from docstrings on model methods.</p> <p>A model with useful documentation might look like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>BlogEntry</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Model):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"""</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">Stores a single blog entry, related to :model:`blog.Blog` and</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">:model:`auth.User`.</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"""</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">slug</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">SlugField(help_text</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"A short label, generally used in URLs."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">author</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ForeignKey(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">User,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">SET_NULL,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">blank</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">null</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">blog</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ForeignKey(Blog, models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CASCADE)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>publish</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"""Makes the blog entry live on the site."""</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Access was restricted to only allow users with model view or change permissions.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>View reference</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Each URL in your site has a separate entry in the admindocs page, and clicking on a given URL will show you the corresponding view. Helpful things you can document in your view function docstrings include:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• A short description of what the view does.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The context, or a list of variables available in the view’s template.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The name of the template or templates that are used for that view.</p> <p>For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.shortcuts</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">render</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">MyModel</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_1036"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request, slug):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"""</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">Display an individual :model:`myapp.MyModel`.</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">**Context**</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">``mymodel``</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">An instance of :model:`myapp.MyModel`.</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">**Template:**</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">:template:`myapp/my_template.html`</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"""</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">context</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"mymodel"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: MyModel</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(slug</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">slug)}</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">render(request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"myapp/my_template.html"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, context)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Template tags and filters reference</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The tags and filters admindocs sections describe all the tags and filters that come with Django (in fact, the</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1979">built-in tag reference</a> and <a href="index.html#page_2004">built-in filter reference</a> documentation come directly from those pages). Any tags or filters that you create or are added by a third-party app will show up in these sections as well.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Template reference</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>While admindocs does not include a place to document templates by themselves, if you use the :template:`path/to/template.html` syntax in a docstring the resulting page will verify the path of that</p> <p>template with Django’s <a href="index.html#page_2047">template loaders</a>. This can be a handy way to check if the specified template exists and to show where on the filesystem that template is stored.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Included Bookmarklets</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>One bookmarklet is available from the admindocs page:</p> <p>Documentation for this page</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Jumps you from any page to the documentation for the view that generates that page.</p> <p>Using this bookmarklet requires that XViewMiddleware is installed and that you are logged into the <a href="index.html#page_1017"><i>Django</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1017"><i>admin</i></a> as a <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>User</i></a> with <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>is_staff</i></a> set to True.</p> <p id="page_1037" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>JavaScript customizations in the admin</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Inline form events</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You may want to execute some JavaScript when an inline form is added or removed in the admin change form. The formset:added and formset:removed events allow this. event.detail.formsetName is the form-set the row belongs to. For the formset:added event, event.target is the newly added row.</p> <p>In your custom change_form.html template, extend the admin_change_form_document_ready block and add the event listener code:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>extends</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'admin/change_form.html'</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">static</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>block</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin_change_form_document_ready</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">block</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.super</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">script</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">src</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>static</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'app/formset_handlers.js'</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">script</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endblock</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">Listing 1: app/static/app/formset_handlers.js</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">document</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.addEventListener(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">'formset:added'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, (event) => {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(event.detail.formsetName</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'author_set'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">) {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i>// Do something</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">});</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">document</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.addEventListener(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">'formset:removed'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, (event) => {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i>// Row removed</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">});</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Two points to keep in mind:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The JavaScript code must go in a template block if you are inheriting admin/change_form.html or it</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">won’t be rendered in the final HTML.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• {{ block.super }} is added because Django’s admin_change_form_document_ready block contains</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">JavaScript code to handle various operations in the change form and we need that to be rendered too.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1038"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Supporting versions of Django older than 4.1</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If your event listener still has to support older versions of Django you have to use jQuery to register your event listener. jQuery handles JavaScript events but the reverse isn’t true.</p> <p>You could check for the presence of event.detail.formsetName and fall back to the old listener signature as follows:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>function</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">handleFormsetAdded(row, formsetName) {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i>// Do something</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">$(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">document</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">).on(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">'formset:added'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, (event, $row, formsetName) => {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(event.detail</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>&&</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">event.detail.formsetName) {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i>// Django >= 4.1</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">handleFormsetAdded(event.target, event.detail.formsetName)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>else</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i>// Django < 4.1, use $row and formsetName</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">handleFormsetAdded($row.get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">0</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">), formsetName)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">})</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>See also:</p> <p>For information about serving the static files (images, JavaScript, and CSS) associated with the admin in</p> <p>production, see <a href="index.html#page_870">Serving files</a>.</p> <p>Having problems? Try <a href="index.html#page_915">FAQ: The admin.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>ModelAdmin objects</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class ModelAdmin</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The ModelAdmin class is the representation of a model in the admin interface. Usually, these are stored in a file named admin.py in your application. Let’s take a look at an example of the ModelAdmin:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AuthorAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>pass</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">register(Author, AuthorAdmin)</span></p> <p id="page_1039" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Do you need a <b>ModelAdmin</b> object at all?</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">In the preceding example, the ModelAdmin class doesn’t define any custom values (yet). As a result, the default admin interface will be provided. If you are happy with the default admin interface, you don’t need to define a ModelAdmin object at all – you can register the model class without providing a ModelAdmin description. The preceding example could be simplified to:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">register(Author)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>The register decorator</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>register</b>(*models, site=django.contrib.admin.sites.site)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">There is also a decorator for registering your ModelAdmin classes:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">register(Author)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AuthorAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>pass</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">It’s given one or more model classes to register with the ModelAdmin. If you’re using a custom</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1090"><i>AdminSite</i></a>, pass it using the site keyword argument:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author, Editor, Reader</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myproject.admin_site</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">custom_admin_site</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">register(Author, Reader, Editor, site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">custom_admin_site)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>PersonAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>pass</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">You can’t use this decorator if you have to reference your model admin class in its __init__() method, e.g. super(PersonAdmin, self).__init__(*args, **kwargs). You can use super(). __init__(*args, **kwargs).</p> <p id="page_1040"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Discovery of admin files</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When you put 'django.contrib.admin' in your <a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a> setting, Django automatically looks for an admin module in each application and imports it.</p> <p><b>class</b> apps.<b>AdminConfig</b></p> <p style="text-align:center">This is the default <a href="index.html#page_924"><i>AppConfig</i></a> class for the admin. It calls <a href="index.html#page_1040"><i>autodiscover()</i></a> when Django starts.</p> <p><b>class</b> apps.<b>SimpleAdminConfig</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This class works like <a href="index.html#page_1040"><i>AdminConfig</i>, </a>except it doesn’t call <a href="index.html#page_1040"><i>autodiscover()</i>.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>default_site</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A dotted import path to the default admin site’s class or to a callable that returns a site instance.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Defaults to 'django.contrib.admin.sites.AdminSite'. See <a href="index.html#page_1095">Overriding the default admin site</a> for usage.</p> <p><b>autodiscover</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This function attempts to import an admin module in each installed application. Such modules are expected to register models with the admin.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Typically you won’t need to call this function directly as <a href="index.html#page_1040"><i>AdminConfig</i></a> calls it when Django starts.</p> <p>If you are using a custom AdminSite, it is common to import all of the ModelAdmin subclasses into your code and register them to the custom AdminSite. In that case, in order to disable auto-discovery, you should put 'django.contrib.admin.apps.SimpleAdminConfig' instead of 'django.contrib.admin' in</p> <p>your <a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>ModelAdmin options</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The ModelAdmin is very flexible. It has several options for dealing with customizing the interface. All options are defined on the ModelAdmin subclass:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AuthorAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">date_hierarchy</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"pub_date"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>actions</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A list of actions to make available on the change list page. See <a href="index.html#page_1018">Admin actions</a> for details.</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>actions_on_top</b></p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>actions_on_bottom</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Controls where on the page the actions bar appears. By default, the admin changelist displays actions at the top of the page (actions_on_top = True; actions_on_bottom = False).</p> <p id="page_1041" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>actions_selection_counter</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Controls whether a selection counter is displayed next to the action dropdown. By default, the admin changelist will display it (actions_selection_counter = True).</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>date_hierarchy</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Set date_hierarchy to the name of a DateField or DateTimeField in your model, and the change list page will include a date-based drilldown navigation by that field.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">date_hierarchy</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"pub_date"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">You can also specify a field on a related model using the __ lookup, for example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">date_hierarchy</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"author__pub_date"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This will intelligently populate itself based on available data, e.g. if all the dates are in one month, it’ll show the day-level drill-down only.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Note: date_hierarchy uses <a href="index.html#page_1722"><i>QuerySet.datetimes()</i></a> internally. Please refer to its documentation for</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">some caveats when time zone support is enabled <a href="index.html#page_1936">(<i>USE_TZ = True</i></a>).</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>empty_value_display</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This attribute overrides the default display value for record’s fields that are empty (None, empty string, etc.). The default value is-(a dash). For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AuthorAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">empty_value_display</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"-empty-"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">You can also override empty_value_display for all admin pages with <span style="float:right"><a href="index.html#page_1091"><i>AdminSite.</i></a></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1091"><i>empty_value_display</i></a> , or for specific fields like this:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AuthorAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">list_display</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"view_birth_date"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">display(empty_value</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"???"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>view_birth_date</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, obj):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">obj</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">birth_date</span></p> <p id="page_1042"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>exclude</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This attribute, if given, should be a list of field names to exclude from the form.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For example, let’s consider the following model:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Author</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Model):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">100</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">3</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">birth_date</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">DateField(blank</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, null</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you want a form for the Author model that includes only the name and title fields, you would specify fields or exclude like this:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AuthorAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AuthorAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span Author model only has three fields, name, title, and birth_date, the forms resulting from the above declarations will contain exactly the same fields.</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>fields</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Use the fields option to make simple layout changes in the forms on the “add” and “change” pages such as showing only a subset of available fields, modifying their order, or grouping them into rows. For</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">example, you could define a simpler version of the admin form for the <a href="index.html#page_1128"><i>django.contrib.flatpages.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1128"><i>models.FlatPage</i></a> model as follows:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>FlatPageAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"url"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"content"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">In the above example, only the fields url, title and content will be displayed, sequentially, in the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">form. fields can contain values defined in <a href="index.html#page_1059"><i>ModelAdmin.readonly_fields</i></a> to be displayed as read-only.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For more complex layout needs, see the <a href="index.html#page_1043"><i>fieldsets</i></a> option.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The fields option accepts the same types of values as <a href="index.html#page_1048"><i>list_display</i>, </a>except that callables and __ lookups for related fields aren’t accepted. Names of model and model admin methods will only be used</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">if they’re listed in <a href="index.html#page_1059"><i>readonly_fields</i>.</a></p> <p id="page_1043" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">To display multiple fields on the same line, wrap those fields in their own tuple. In this example, the url and title fields will display on the same line and the content field will be displayed below them on its own line:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>FlatPageAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"url"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"content"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Possible confusion with the <b>ModelAdmin.fieldsets</b> option</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This fields option should not be confused with the fields dictionary key that is within the <a href="index.html#page_1043"><i>fieldsets</i></a> option, as described in the next section.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If neither fields nor <a href="index.html#page_1043"><i>fieldsets</i></a> options are present, Django will default to displaying each field that isn’t an AutoField and has editable=True, in a single fieldset, in the same order as the fields are defined</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">in the model, followed by any fields defined in <a href="index.html#page_1059"><i>readonly_fields</i>.</a></p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>fieldsets</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Set fieldsets to control the layout of admin “add” and “change” pages.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">fieldsets is a list of 2-tuples, in which each 2-tuple represents a <fieldset> on the admin form page. (A <fieldset> is a “section” of the form.)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The 2-tuples are in the format (name, field_options), where name is a string representing the title of the fieldset and field_options is a dictionary of information about the fieldset, including a list of fields to be displayed in it.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A full example, taken from the <a href="index.html#page_1128"><i>django.contrib.flatpages.models.FlatPage</i></a> model:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>FlatPageAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">fieldsets</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>None</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:8em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"fields"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"url"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"content"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"sites"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Advanced options"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:8em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"classes"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"collapse"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:8em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"fields"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"registration_required"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"template_name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_1044"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This results in an admin page that looks like:</p> <p><img src="index-1044_1.png" alt="" width="665px" height="603px"/></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If neither fieldsets nor <a href="index.html#page_1042"><i>fields</i></a> options are present, Django will default to displaying each field that isn’t an AutoField and has editable=True, in a single fieldset, in the same order as the fields are defined in the model.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The field_options dictionary can have the following keys:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <b>fields</b></p> <p style="margin-left:5em">A list or tuple of field names to display in this fieldset. This key is required.</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">Example:</p> <p id="page_1045" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"fields"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"first_name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"last_name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"address"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"city"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"state"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:5em">As with the <a href="index.html#page_1042"><i>fields</i></a> option, to display multiple fields on the same line, wrap those fields in their own tuple. In this example, the first_name and last_name fields will display on the same line:</p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"fields"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"first_name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"last_name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"address"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"city"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"state"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:5em">fields can contain values defined in <a href="index.html#page_1059"><i>readonly_fields</i></a> to be displayed as read-only.</p> <p style="text-align:right">If you add the name of a callable to fields, the same rule applies as with the <a href="index.html#page_1042"><i>fields</i></a> option:</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">the callable must be listed in <a href="index.html#page_1059"><i>readonly_fields</i>.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <b>classes</b></p> <p style="margin-left:5em">A list or tuple containing extra CSS classes to apply to the fieldset. This can include any custom CSS class defined in the project, as well as any of the CSS classes provided by Django. Within the default admin site CSS stylesheet, two particularly useful classes are defined: collapse and wide.</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">Example:</p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"classes"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"wide"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"collapse"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:5em">Fieldsets with the wide style will be given extra horizontal space in the admin interface. Field-sets with a name and the collapse style will be initially collapsed, using an expandable widget with a toggle for switching their visibility.</p> <p style="text-align:right">fieldsets using the collapse class now use <details> and <summary> elements, provided they define a name.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <b>description</b></p> <p style="text-align:right">A string of optional extra text to be displayed at the top of each fieldset, under the heading of the fieldset.</p> <p style="text-align:right">Note that this value is not HTML-escaped when it’s displayed in the admin interface. This lets</p> <p style="text-align:right">you include HTML if you so desire. Alternatively you can use plain text and <a href="index.html#page_2082"><i>django.utils.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><a href="index.html#page_2082"><i>html.escape()</i></a> to escape any HTML special characters.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>TabularInline</b> has limited support for <b>fieldsets Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p id="page_1046" style="margin-left:2em">Using fieldsets with <a href="index.html#page_1077"><i>TabularInline</i></a> has limited functionality. You can specify which fields will be displayed and their order within the TabularInline layout by defining fields in the field_options dictionary.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">All other features are not supported. This includes the use of name to define a title for a group of fields.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>filter_horizontal</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">By default, a <a href="index.html#page_1649"><i>ManyToManyField</i></a> is displayed in the admin site with a <select multiple>. However,</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">multiple-select boxes can be difficult to use when selecting many items. Adding a <a href="index.html#page_1649"><i>ManyToManyField</i></a> to this list will instead use a nifty unobtrusive JavaScript “filter” interface that allows searching within the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">options. The unselected and selected options appear in two boxes side by side. See <a href="index.html#page_1046"><i>filter_vertical</i></a> to use a vertical interface.</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>filter_vertical</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Same as <a href="index.html#page_1046"><i>filter_horizontal</i>, </a>but uses a vertical display of the filter interface with the box of unselected options appearing above the box of selected options.</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>form</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">By default a ModelForm is dynamically created for your model. It is used to create the form presented on both the add/change pages. You can easily provide your own ModelForm to override any default form behavior on the add/change pages. Alternatively, you can customize the default form rather</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">than specifying an entirely new one by using the <a href="index.html#page_1068"><i>ModelAdmin.get_form()</i></a> method.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For an example see the section <a href="index.html#page_1077">Adding custom validation to the admin.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Omit the <b>Meta.model</b> attribute</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you define the Meta.model attribute on a <a href="index.html#page_365"><i>ModelForm</i></a>, you must also define the Meta.fields attribute (or the Meta.exclude attribute). However, since the admin has its own way of defining fields, the Meta. fields attribute will be ignored.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If the ModelForm is only going to be used for the admin, the easiest solution is to omit the Meta.model attribute, since ModelAdmin will provide the correct model to use. Alternatively, you can set fields = [] in the Meta class to satisfy the validation on the ModelForm.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>ModelAdmin.exclude</b> takes precedence</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If your ModelForm and ModelAdmin both define an exclude option then ModelAdmin takes precedence:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">forms</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Person</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_1047" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>PersonForm</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(forms</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelForm):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Meta</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">exclude</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>PersonAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">exclude</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span <span style="font-size:0.87em">PersonForm</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">In the above example, the “age” field will be excluded but the “name” field will be included in the generated form.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>formfield_overrides</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This provides a quick-and-dirty way to override some of the <a href="index.html#page_1517"><i>Field</i></a> options for use in the admin. formfield_overrides is a dictionary mapping a field class to a dict of arguments to pass to the field at construction time.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Since that’s a bit abstract, let’s look at a concrete example. <span style="float:right">The most common use of</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">formfield_overrides is to add a custom widget for a certain type of field. So, imagine we’ve written a RichTextEditorWidget that we’d like to use for large text fields instead of the default <textarea>. Here’s how we’d do that:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Import our custom widget and our model from where they're defined</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">MyModel</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.widgets</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">RichTextEditorWidget</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyModelAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">formfield_overrides</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">TextField: {</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"widget"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: RichTextEditorWidget},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Note that the key in the dictionary is the actual field class, not a string. The value is another dictionary;</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">these arguments will be passed to the form field’s __init__() method. See <a href="index.html#page_1487">The Forms API</a> for details.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em">Warning: If you want to use a custom widget with a relation field (i.e. <a href="index.html#page_1643"><i>ForeignKey</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">or <a href="index.html#page_1649"><i>ManyToManyField</i></a>), make sure you haven’t included that field’s name in raw_id_fields, <b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p id="page_1048" style="margin-left:3em">radio_fields, or autocomplete_fields.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">formfield_overrides won’t let you change the widget on relation fields that have raw_id_fields, radio_fields, or autocomplete_fields set. That’s because raw_id_fields, radio_fields, and autocomplete_fields imply custom widgets of their own.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>inlines</b></p> <p style="text-align:center">See <a href="index.html#page_1077"><i>InlineModelAdmin</i></a> objects below as well as <a href="index.html#page_1069"><i>ModelAdmin.get_formsets_with_inlines()</i></a><a href="index.html#page_1069">.</a></p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>list_display</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Set list_display to control which fields are displayed on the change list page of the admin.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">list_display</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"first_name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"last_name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you don’t set list_display, the admin site will display a single column that displays the __str__() representation of each object.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">There are five types of values that can be used in list_display. All but the simplest may use the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1100"><i>display()</i></a> decorator, which is used to customize how the field is presented:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• The name of a model field. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>PersonAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">list_display</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"first_name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"last_name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• The name of a related field, using the __ notation. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>PersonAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">list_display</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"city__name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• A callable that accepts one argument, the model instance. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">display(description</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>upper_case_name</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(obj):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">f"{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">obj</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">first_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">} {</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">obj</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">last_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">}"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">upper()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>PersonAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">list_display</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[upper_case_name]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• A string representing a ModelAdmin method that accepts one argument, the model instance. For</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">example:</p> <p id="page_1049" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p If you want to do this nonetheless, give your model a custom method, and add that method’s name to list_display. (See below for more on custom methods in list_display.)</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• If the field is a BooleanField, Django will display a pretty “yes”, “no”, or “unknown” icon instead</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">of True, False, or None.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• If the string given is a method of the model, ModelAdmin or a callable, Django will HTML-</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">escape the output by default. model, ModelAdmin or a callable that returns True, False, or</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">None , Django will display a pretty “yes”, “no”, or “unknown” icon if you wrap the method with</p> <p
