style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Full name of the person"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">my_property</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">admin_order_field</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"last_name"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">my_property</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">boolean</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>= False</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">full_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">property</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(my_property)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• The field names in list_display will also appear as CSS classes in the HTML output, in the form</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">of column-<field_name> on each <th> element. This can be used to set column widths in a CSS file for example.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• Django will try to interpret every element of list_display in this order:</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">– A field of the model or from a related field.</p> <p id="page_1054"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:5em">– A callable.</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">– A string representing a ModelAdmin attribute.</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">– A string representing a model attribute.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">For example if you have first_name as a model field and as a ModelAdmin attribute, the model field will be used.</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>list_display_links</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Use list_display_links to control if and which fields in <a href="index.html#page_1048"><i>list_display</i></a> should be linked to the “change” page for an object.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">By default, the change list page will link the first column – the first field specified in list_display – to the change page for each item. But list_display_links lets you change this:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• Set it to None to get no links at all.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• Set it to a list or tuple of fields (in the same format as list_display) whose columns you want</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">converted to links.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">You can specify one or many fields. As long as the fields appear in list_display, Django doesn’t care how many (or how few) fields are linked. The only requirement is that if you want to use list_display_links in this fashion, you must define list_display.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">In this example, the first_name and last_name fields will be linked on the change list page:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>PersonAdmin</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">list_display</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"first_name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"last_name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"birthday"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">list_display_links</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"first_name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"last_name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">In this example, the change list page grid will have no links:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AuditEntryAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">list_display</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"timestamp"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"message"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">list_display_links</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>= None</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>list_editable</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Set list_editable to a list of field names on the model which will allow editing on the change list page. That is, fields listed in list_editable will be displayed as form widgets on the change list page, allowing users to edit and save multiple rows at once.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Note: list_editable interacts with a couple of other options in particular ways; you should note the following rules:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• Any field in list_editable must also be in list_display. You can’t edit a field that’s not dis-</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">played!</p> <p id="page_1055" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• The same field can’t be listed in both list_editable and list_display_links – a field can’t be</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">both a form and a link.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">You’ll get a validation error if either of these rules are broken.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>list_filter</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Set list_filter to activate filters in the right sidebar of the change list page of the admin.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">At it’s simplest list_filter takes a list or tuple of field names to activate filtering upon, but several</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">more advanced options as available. See <a href="index.html#page_1029">ModelAdmin List Filters</a> for the details.</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>list_max_show_all</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Set list_max_show_all to control how many items can appear on a “Show all” admin change list page. The admin will display a “Show all” link on the change list only if the total result count is less than or equal to this setting. By default, this is set to 200.</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>list_per_page</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Set list_per_page to control how many items appear on each paginated admin change list page. By default, this is set to 100.</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>list_select_related</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Set list_select_related to tell Django to use <a href="index.html#page_1724"><i>select_related()</i></a> in retrieving the list of objects on the admin change list page. This can save you a bunch of database queries.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The value should be either a boolean, a list or a tuple. Default is False.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">When value is True, select_related() will always be called. When value is set to False, Django will look at list_display and call select_related() if any ForeignKey is present.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you need more fine-grained control, use a tuple (or list) as value for list_select_related. Empty tuple will prevent Django from calling select_related at all. Any other tuple will be passed directly to select_related as parameters. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ArticleAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">list_select_related</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"author"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"category"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">will call select_related('author', 'category').</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you need to specify a dynamic value based on the request, you can implement a</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1066"><i>get_list_select_related()</i></a> method.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Note: ModelAdmin ignores this attribute when <a href="index.html#page_1724"><i>select_related()</i></a> was already called on the change-list’s QuerySet.</p> <p id="page_1056"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>ordering</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Set ordering to specify how lists of objects should be ordered in the Django admin views. This should</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">be a list or tuple in the same format as a model’s <a href="index.html#page_1683"><i>ordering</i></a> parameter.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If this isn’t provided, the Django admin will use the model’s default ordering.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you need to specify a dynamic order (for example depending on user or language) you can implement</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">a <a href="index.html#page_1064"><i>get_ordering()</i></a> method.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Performance considerations with ordering and sorting</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">To ensure a deterministic ordering of results, the changelist adds pk to the ordering if it can’t find a single or unique together set of fields that provide total ordering.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For example, if the default ordering is by a non-unique name field, then the changelist is sorted by name and pk. This could perform poorly if you have a lot of rows and don’t have an index on name and pk.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>paginator</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The paginator class to be used for pagination. By default, <a href="index.html#page_1855"><i>django.core.paginator.Paginator</i></a> is used.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If the custom paginator class doesn’t have the same constructor interface as <a href="index.html#page_1855"><i>django.core.paginator.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1855"><i>Paginator</i></a> , you will also need to provide an implementation for <a href="index.html#page_1073"><i>ModelAdmin.get_paginator()</i></a><a href="index.html#page_1073">.</a></p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>prepopulated_fields</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Set prepopulated_fields to a dictionary mapping field names to the fields it should prepopulate from:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ArticleAdmin</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">prepopulated_fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"slug"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">When set, the given fields will use a bit of JavaScript to populate from the fields assigned. The main use for this functionality is to automatically generate the value for SlugField fields from one or more other fields. The generated value is produced by concatenating the values of the source fields, and then by transforming that result into a valid slug (e.g. substituting dashes for spaces and lowercasing ASCII letters).</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Prepopulated fields aren’t modified by JavaScript after a value has been saved. It’s usually undesired that slugs change (which would cause an object’s URL to change if the slug is used in it).</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">prepopulated_fields doesn’t accept DateTimeField, ForeignKey, OneToOneField, and ManyToManyField fields.</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>preserve_filters</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">By default, applied filters are preserved on the list view after creating, editing, or deleting an object. You can have filters cleared by setting this attribute to False.</p> <p id="page_1057" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>show_facets</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Controls whether facet counts are displayed for filters in the admin changelist. Defaults to <a href="index.html#page_1057"><i>ShowFacets.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1057"><i>ALLOW</i></a> .</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">When displayed, facet counts update in line with currently applied filters.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>class ShowFacets</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Enum of allowed values for <a href="index.html#page_1056"><i>ModelAdmin.show_facets</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><b>ALWAYS</b></p> <p style="margin-left:5em">Always show facet counts.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><b>ALLOW</b></p> <p style="text-align:center">Show facet counts when the _facets query string parameter is provided.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><b>NEVER</b></p> <p style="margin-left:5em">Never show facet counts.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Set show_facets to the desired <a href="index.html#page_1057"><i>ShowFacets</i></a> value. For example, to always show facet counts without needing to provide the query parameter:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyModelAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Have facets always shown for this model admin.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">show_facets</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ShowFacets</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ALWAYS</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Performance considerations with facets</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Enabling facet filters will increase the number of queries on the admin changelist page in line with the number of filters. These queries may cause performance problems, especially for large datasets. In</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">these cases it may be appropriate to set show_facets to <a href="index.html#page_1057"><i>ShowFacets.NEVER</i></a> to disable faceting entirely.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>radio_fields</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">By default, Django’s admin uses a select-box interface (<select>) for fields that are ForeignKey or have choices set. If a field is present in radio_fields, Django will use a radio-button interface instead. Assuming group is a ForeignKey on the Person model:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>PersonAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">radio_fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"group"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">VERTICAL}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">You have the choice of using HORIZONTAL or VERTICAL from the django.contrib.admin module.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Don’t include a field in radio_fields unless it’s a ForeignKey or has choices set.</p> <p id="page_1058"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>autocomplete_fields</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">autocomplete_fields is a list of ForeignKey and/or ManyToManyField fields you would like to change</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">to <a href="https://select2.org/">Select2</a> autocomplete inputs.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">By default, the admin uses a select-box interface (<select>) for those fields. Sometimes you don’t want to incur the overhead of selecting all the related instances to display in the dropdown.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The Select2 input looks similar to the default input but comes with a search feature that loads the options asynchronously. This is faster and more user-friendly if the related model has many instances.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">You must define <a href="index.html#page_1060"><i>search_fields</i></a> on the related object’s ModelAdmin because the autocomplete search uses it.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">To avoid unauthorized data disclosure, users must have the view or change permission to the related object in order to use autocomplete.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Ordering and pagination of the results are controlled by the related ModelAdmin’s <a href="index.html#page_1064"><i>get_ordering()</i></a> and</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1073"><i>get_paginator()</i></a> methods.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">In the following example, ChoiceAdmin has an autocomplete field for the ForeignKey to the Question. The results are filtered by the question_text field and ordered by the date_created field:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>QuestionAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">ordering</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"date_created"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">search_fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"question_text"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ChoiceAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">autocomplete_fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"question"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Performance considerations for large datasets</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Ordering using <a href="index.html#page_1055"><i>ModelAdmin.ordering</i></a> may cause performance problems as sorting on a large queryset will be slow.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Also, if your search fields include fields that aren’t indexed by the database, you might encounter poor performance on extremely large tables.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For those cases, it’s a good idea to write your own <a href="index.html#page_1064"><i>ModelAdmin.get_search_results()</i></a> implementation using a full-text indexed search.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">You may also want to change the Paginator on very large tables as the default paginator always per-forms a count() query. For example, you could override the default implementation of the Paginator. count property.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>raw_id_fields</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">By default, Django’s admin uses a select-box interface (<select>) for fields that are ForeignKey. Some-</p> <p id="page_1059" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">times you don’t want to incur the overhead of having to select all the related instances to display in the drop-down.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">raw_id_fields is a list of fields you would like to change into an Input widget for either a ForeignKey or ManyToManyField:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ArticleAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">raw_id_fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"newspaper"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The raw_id_fields Input widget should contain a primary key if the field is a ForeignKey or a comma separated list of values if the field is a ManyToManyField. The raw_id_fields widget shows a magni-fying glass button next to the field which allows users to search for and select a value:</p> <p><img src="index-1059_1.png" alt="" width="597px" height="89px"/></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>readonly_fields</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">By default the admin shows all fields as editable. Any fields in this option (which should be a list or</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">tuple ) will display its data as-is and non-editable; they are also excluded from the <a href="index.html#page_365"><i>ModelForm</i></a> used for</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">creating and editing. Note that when specifying <a href="index.html#page_1042"><i>ModelAdmin.fields</i></a> or <a href="index.html#page_1043"><i>ModelAdmin.fieldsets</i></a> the read-only fields must be present to be shown (they are ignored otherwise).</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If readonly_fields is used without defining explicit ordering through <a href="index.html#page_1042"><i>ModelAdmin.fields</i></a> or</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1043"><i>ModelAdmin.fieldsets</i></a> they will be added last after all editable fields.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A read-only field can not only display data from a model’s field, it can also display the output of a</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">model’s method or a method of the ModelAdmin class itself. This is very similar to the way <a href="index.html#page_1048"><i>ModelAdmin.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1048"><i>list_display</i></a> behaves. This provides a way to use the admin interface to provide feedback on the status of the objects being edited, for example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span id="page_1060"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">format_html_join(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>save_as</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Set save_as to enable a “save as new” feature on admin change forms.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Normally, objects have three save options: “Save”, “Save and continue editing”, and “Save and add another”. If save_as is True, “Save and add another” will be replaced by a “Save as new” button that creates a new object (with a new ID) rather than updating the existing object.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">By default, save_as is set to False.</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>save_as_continue</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">When <a href="index.html#page_1060"><i>save_as=True</i>, </a>the default redirect after saving the new object is to the change view for that object. If you set save_as_continue=False, the redirect will be to the changelist view.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">By default, save_as_continue is set to True.</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>save_on_top</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Set save_on_top to add save buttons across the top of your admin change forms.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Normally, the save buttons appear only at the bottom of the forms. If you set save_on_top, the buttons will appear both on the top and the bottom.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">By default, save_on_top is set to False.</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>search_fields</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Set search_fields to enable a search box on the admin change list page. This should be set to a list of field names that will be searched whenever somebody submits a search query in that text box.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">These fields should be some kind of text field, such as CharField or TextField. You can also perform a related lookup on a ForeignKey or ManyToManyField with the lookup API “follow” notation:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">search_fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"foreign_key__related_fieldname"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For example, if you have a blog entry with an author, the following definition would enable searching blog entries by the email address of the author:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">search_fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"user__email"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">When somebody does a search in the admin search box, Django splits the search query into words</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">and returns all objects that contain each of the words, case-insensitive (using the <a href="index.html#page_1764"><i>icontains</i></a> lookup), where each word must be in at least one of search_fields. For example, if search_fields is set to</p> <p id="page_1061" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">['first_name', 'last_name'] and a user searches for john lennon, Django will do the equivalent of this SQL WHERE clause:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>WHERE</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(first_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ILIKE</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'%john%'</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>OR</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">last_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ILIKE</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'%john%'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AND</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(first_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ILIKE</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'%lennon%'</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>OR</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">last_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ILIKE</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'%lennon%'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The search query can contain quoted phrases with spaces. For example, if a user searches for "john winston" or 'john winston', Django will do the equivalent of this SQL WHERE clause:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>WHERE</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(first_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ILIKE</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'%john winston%'</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>OR</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">last_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ILIKE</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'%john winston%'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you don’t want to use icontains as the lookup, you can use any lookup by appending it the field.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For example, you could use <a href="index.html#page_1762"><i>exact</i></a> by setting search_fields to ['first_name__exact'].</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Some (older) shortcuts for specifying a field lookup are also available. You can prefix a field in search_fields with the following characters and it’s equivalent to adding __<lookup> to the field:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:15em">Prefix Lookup</p> <p style="margin-left:15em">^ <a href="index.html#page_1766"><i>istartswith</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:15em">= <a href="index.html#page_1763"><i>iexact</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:15em">@ <a href="index.html#page_1339"><i>search</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:15em">None <a href="index.html#page_1764"><i>icontains</i></a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you need to customize search you can use <a href="index.html#page_1064"><i>ModelAdmin.get_search_results()</i></a> to provide additional or alternate search behavior.</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>search_help_text</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Set search_help_text to specify a descriptive text for the search box which will be displayed below it.</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>show_full_result_count</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Set show_full_result_count to control whether the full count of objects should be displayed on a fil-tered admin page (e.g. 99 results (103 total)). If this option is set to False, a text like 99 results (Show all) is displayed instead.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The default of show_full_result_count=True generates a query to perform a full count on the table which can be expensive if the table contains a large number of rows.</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>sortable_by</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">By default, the change list page allows sorting by all model fields (and callables that use the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">ordering argument to the <a href="index.html#page_1100"><i>display()</i></a> decorator or have the admin_order_field attribute) specified</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">in <a href="index.html#page_1048"><i>list_display</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you want to disable sorting for some columns, set sortable_by to a collection (e.g. list, tuple, or</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">set) of the subset of <a href="index.html#page_1048"><i>list_display</i></a> that you want to be sortable. An empty collection disables sorting for all columns.</p> <p id="page_1062"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">If you need to specify this list dynamically, implement a <a href="index.html#page_1066"><i>get_sortable_by()</i></a> method instead.</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>view_on_site</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Set view_on_site to control whether or not to display the “View on site” link. This link should bring you to a URL where you can display the saved object.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This value can be either a boolean flag or a callable. If True (the default), the object’s</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1703"><i>get_absolute_url()</i></a> method will be used to generate the url.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If your model has a <a href="index.html#page_1703"><i>get_absolute_url()</i></a> method but you don’t want the “View on site” button to appear, you only need to set view_on_site to False:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>PersonAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">view_on_site</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>= False</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">In case it is a callable, it accepts the model instance as a parameter. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.urls</span> <span template options</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_1087">Overriding admin templates</a> section describes how to override or extend the default admin templates.</p> <p>Use the following options to override the default templates used by the <a href="index.html#page_1038"><i>ModelAdmin</i></a> views:</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>add_form_template</b></p> <p They aren’t meant for veto purposes, rather they allow you to perform extra</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">operations.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>save_model</b>(request, obj, form, change)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The save_model method is given the HttpRequest, a model instance, a ModelForm instance, and a boolean value based on whether it is adding or changing the object. Overriding this method allows</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">doing pre- or post-save operations. Call super().save_model() to save the object using <a href="index.html#page_1696"><i>Model.save()</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For example to attach request.user to the object prior to saving:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ArticleAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>save_model</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, request, obj, form, change):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">obj</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save_model(request, obj, form, change)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>delete_model</b>(request, obj)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The delete_model method is given the HttpRequest and a model instance. Overriding this method allows doing pre- or post-delete operations. Call super().delete_model() to delete the object using</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1700"><i>Model.delete()</i></a>.</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>delete_queryset</b>(request, ModelAdmin property return the property itself rather than a copy of</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">its value. Dynamically modifying the value can lead to surprising results.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Let’s take <a href="index.html#page_1065"><i>ModelAdmin.get_readonly_fields()</i></a> as an example:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>PersonAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">readonly</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_readonly_fields(request, obj)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="margin-left:1em">"age" is added each time non-superuser visits the page.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>get_ordering</b>(request)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The attribute. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>PersonAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get_ordering</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">request</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">is_superuser:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"rank"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>else</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>get_search_results</b>( request, queryset, search_term)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The get_search_results method modifies the list of objects displayed into those that match the pro-vided search term. It accepts the request, a queryset that applies the current filters, and the user-</p> <p id="page_1065" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">provided search term. It returns a tuple containing a queryset modified to implement the search, and a boolean indicating if the results may contain duplicates.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The default implementation searches the fields named in <a href="index.html#page_1060"><i>ModelAdmin.search_fields</i>.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This method may be overridden with your own custom search method. For example, you might wish</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">to search by an integer field, or use an external tool such as <a href="https://solr.apache.org">Solr</a> or <a href="https://haystacksearch.org">Haystack</a>. You must establish if the queryset changes implemented by your search method may introduce duplicates into the results, and return True in the second element of the return value.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For example, to search by name and age, you could use:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span search_term):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">queryset, may_have_duplicates</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span '=age') which results in a string comparison for the numeric field, for example ... OR UPPER("polls_choice". "votes"::text) = UPPER('4') on PostgreSQL.</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>save_related</b>(request, form, formsets, change)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The save_related method is given the HttpRequest, the parent ModelForm instance, the list of inline formsets and a boolean value based on whether the parent is being added or changed. <p>ModelAdmin.<b>get_inlines</b>( request, obj)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The get_inlines method is given the HttpRequest and the obj being edited (or None on an add form) and is expected to This is important, since it ensures two things:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">1. Permission checks are run, ensuring only active staff users can access the view.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">2. The <a href="index.html#page_289"><i>django.views.decorators.cache.never_cache()</i></a> decorator is applied to prevent caching,</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">ensuring the returned information is up-to-date.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Note: Notice that the custom patterns are included before the regular admin URLs: the admin URL patterns are very permissive and will match nearly anything, so you’ll usually want to prepend your custom URLs to the built-in ones.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">In this example, my_view will be accessed at /admin/myapp/mymodel/my_view/ (assuming the admin URLs are included at /admin/.)</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If the page is cacheable, but you still want the permission check to be performed, you can pass a cacheable=True argument to AdminSite.admin_view():</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"my_view/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">admin_site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">admin_view(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">my_view, cacheable</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">))</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">ModelAdmin views have model_admin attributes. style="margin-left:2em">The objects in the changelist page can be filtered with lookups from the URL’s query string. This is</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">how <a href="index.html#page_1055"><i>list_filter</i></a> works, for example. The lookups are similar to what’s used in <a href="index.html#page_1709"><i>QuerySet.filter()</i></a> (e.g. user__email=user@example.com). Since the lookups in the query string can be manipulated by the user, they must be sanitized to prevent unauthorized data exposure.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The lookup_allowed() method is given a lookup path from the query string (e.g. 'user__email'), the corresponding value (e.g. 'user@example.com'), and the request, and returns a boolean indicating whether filtering the changelist’s QuerySet using the parameters is permitted. If lookup_allowed()</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">returns False, DisallowedModelAdminLookup (subclass of <a href="index.html#page_1471"><i>SuspiciousOperation</i>) </a>is raised.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">By default, lookup_allowed() allows access to a model’s local fields, field paths used in <a href="index.html#page_1055"><i>list_filter</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">(but not paths from <a href="index.html#page_1066"><i>get_list_filter()</i>), </a>and lookups required for <a href="index.html#page_1646"><i>limit_choices_to</i></a> to function</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">correctly in <a href="index.html#page_1058"><i>raw_id_fields</i>.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Override this method to customize the lookups permitted for your <a href="index.html#page_1038"><i>ModelAdmin</i></a> subclass.</p> <p>ModelAdmin.<b>has_view_permission</b>(request, obj=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Should return True if viewing obj is permitted, False otherwise. If there are any related objects to be deleted, the list is nested and includes those related objects. The list is formatted</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">in the template using the <a href="index.html#page_2024"><i>unordered_list</i></a> filter.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">model_count is a dictionary mapping each model’s <a href="index.html#page_1687"><i>verbose_name_plural</i></a> to the number of objects that will be deleted.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">perms_needed is a set of <a href="index.html#page_1687"><i>verbose_name</i>s </a>of the models that the user doesn’t have permission to delete.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">protected is a list of strings representing of all the protected related objects that can’t be deleted. style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">change_form_template</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get_osm_info</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>pass</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>change_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, request, object_id, form_url</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">""</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, extra_context</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=None</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">extra_context</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">extra_context</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>or</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{}</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">extra_context[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"osm_data"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_osm_info()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">change_view(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">request,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">object_id,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">form_url,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">extra_context</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">extra_context,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>These views return <a href="index.html#page_2054"><i>TemplateResponse</i></a> instances which allow you to easily customize the response data before</p> <p>rendering. For more details, see the <a href="index.html#page_2052">TemplateResponse documentation.</a></p> <p id="page_1076"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>ModelAdmin asset definitions</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>There are times where you would like add a bit of CSS and/or JavaScript to the add/change views. This can be accomplished by using a Media inner class on your ModelAdmin:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ArticleAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Media</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">css</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"all"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"my_styles.css"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">js</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"my_code.js"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_1369">staticfiles app</a> prepends <a href="index.html#page_1946"><i>STATIC_URL</i></a> (or <a href="index.html#page_1922"><i>MEDIA_URL</i></a> if <a href="index.html#page_1946"><i>STATIC_URL</i></a> is None) to any asset paths. The same</p> <p>rules apply as <a href="index.html#page_394">regular asset definitions on forms</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>jQuery</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django admin JavaScript makes use of the <a href="https://jquery.com">jQuery</a> library.</p> <p>To avoid conflicts with user-supplied scripts or libraries, Django’s jQuery (version 3.7.1) is namespaced as django.jQuery. If you want to use jQuery in your own admin JavaScript without including a second copy, you can use the django.jQuery object on changelist and add/edit views. Also, your own admin forms or</p> <p>widgets depending on django.jQuery must specify js=['admin/js/jquery.init.js', <i>. . .</i>] when <a href="index.html#page_391">declaring</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_391">form media assets.</a></p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_1038"><i>ModelAdmin</i></a> class requires jQuery by default, so there is no need to add jQuery to your ModelAdmin’s list of media resources unless you have a specific need. For example, if you require the jQuery library to be in the global namespace (for example when using third-party jQuery plugins) or if you need a newer version of jQuery, you will have to include your own copy.</p> <p>Django provides both uncompressed and ‘minified’ versions of jQuery, as jquery.js and jquery.min.js respectively.</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1038"><i>ModelAdmin</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1077"><i>InlineModelAdmin</i></a> have a media property that returns a list of Media objects which store</p> <p>paths to the JavaScript files for the forms and/or formsets. If <a href="index.html#page_1907"><i>DEBUG</i></a> is True it will return the uncompressed versions of the various JavaScript files, including jquery.js; if not, it will return the ‘minified’ versions.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1077" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Adding custom validation to the admin</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can also add custom validation of data in the admin. The automatic admin interface reuses <a href="index.html#page_1487"><i>django.</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1487"><i>forms</i></a>, and the ModelAdmin class gives you the ability to define your own form:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ArticleAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">form</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">MyArticleAdminForm</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>MyArticleAdminForm can be defined anywhere as long as you import where needed. Now within your form you can add your own custom validation for any field:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyArticleAdminForm</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(forms</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelForm):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>clean_name</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># do something that validates your data</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">cleaned_data[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>It is important you use a ModelForm here otherwise things can break. See the <a href="index.html#page_1487">forms</a> documentation on <a href="index.html#page_1574">custom</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1574">validation</a> and, more specifically, the <a href="index.html#page_369">model form validation notes</a> for more information.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>InlineModelAdmin objects</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class InlineModelAdmin</b></p> <p><b>class TabularInline</b></p> <p><b>class StackedInline</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The admin interface has the ability to edit models on the same page as a parent model. These are called inlines. Suppose you have these two models:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Author</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Model):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">100</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Book</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Model):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">author</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ForeignKey(Author, on_delete</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CASCADE)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">100</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">You can edit the books authored by an author on the author page. You add inlines to a model by specifying them in a ModelAdmin.inlines:</p> <p id="page_1078"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author, Book</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>BookInline</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">TabularInline):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">model</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Book</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AuthorAdmin</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">inlines</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">BookInline,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">register(Author, AuthorAdmin)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Django provides two subclasses of InlineModelAdmin and they are:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_1077"><i>TabularInline</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• <a href="index.html#page_1077"><i>StackedInline</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The difference between these two is merely the template used to render them.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>InlineModelAdmin options</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>InlineModelAdmin shares many of the same features as ModelAdmin, and adds some of its own (the shared features are actually defined in the BaseModelAdmin superclass). The shared features are:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1079"><i>form</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1043"><i>fieldsets</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1042"><i>fields</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1047"><i>formfield_overrides</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1041"><i>exclude</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1046"><i>filter_horizontal</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1046"><i>filter_vertical</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1055"><i>ordering</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1056"><i>prepopulated_fields</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1066"><i>get_fieldsets()</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1073"><i>get_queryset()</i></a></p> <p id="page_1079" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1057"><i>radio_fields</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1059"><i>readonly_fields</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1080"><i>raw_id_fields</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1070"><i>formfield_for_choice_field()</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1069"><i>formfield_for_foreignkey()</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1070"><i>formfield_for_manytomany()</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1072"><i>has_module_permission()</i></a></p> <p>The InlineModelAdmin class adds or customizes:</p> <p>InlineModelAdmin.<b>model</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The model which the inline is using. This is required.</p> <p>InlineModelAdmin.<b>fk_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The name of the foreign key on the model. In most cases this will be dealt with automatically, but fk_name must be specified explicitly if there are more than one foreign key to the same parent model.</p> <p>InlineModelAdmin.<b>formset</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This defaults to <a href="index.html#page_387"><i>BaseInlineFormSet</i></a>. Using your own formset can give you many possibilities of cus-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">tomization. Inlines are built around <a href="index.html#page_379">model formsets.</a></p> <p>InlineModelAdmin.<b>form</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The value for form defaults to ModelForm. This is what is passed through to <a href="index.html#page_1550"><i>inlineformset_factory()</i></a> when creating the formset for this inline.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: When writing custom validation for InlineModelAdmin forms, be cautious of writing vali-</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">dation that relies on features of the parent model. If the parent model fails to validate, it may be left in</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">an inconsistent state as described in the warning in <a href="index.html#page_369">Validation on a ModelForm.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>InlineModelAdmin.<b>classes</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A list or tuple containing extra CSS classes to apply to the fieldset that is rendered for the inlines.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Defaults to None. As with classes configured in <a href="index.html#page_1043"><i>fieldsets</i>, </a>inlines with a collapse class will be initially collapsed using an expandable widget.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">fieldsets using the collapse class now use <details> and <summary> elements, provided they define a name.</p> <p>InlineModelAdmin.<b>extra</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This controls the number of extra forms the formset will display in addition to the initial forms. De-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">faults to 3. See the <a href="index.html#page_344">formsets documentation</a> for more information.</p> <p id="page_1080"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For users with JavaScript-enabled browsers, an “Add another” link is provided to enable any number of additional inlines to be added in addition to those provided as a result of the extra argument.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The dynamic link will not appear if the number of currently displayed forms exceeds max_num, or if the user does not have JavaScript enabled.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1081"><i>InlineModelAdmin.get_extra()</i></a> also allows you to customize the number of extra forms.</p> <p>InlineModelAdmin.<b>max_num</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This controls the maximum number of forms to show in the inline. This doesn’t directly correlate to</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">the number of objects, but can if the value is small enough. See <a href="index.html#page_383">Limiting the number of editable objects</a> for more information.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1081"><i>InlineModelAdmin.get_max_num()</i></a> also allows you to customize the maximum number of extra forms.</p> <p>InlineModelAdmin.<b>min_num</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This controls the minimum number of forms to show in the inline. See <a href="index.html#page_1549"><i>modelformset_factory()</i></a> for more information.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1081"><i>InlineModelAdmin.get_min_num()</i></a> also allows you to customize the minimum number of displayed forms.</p> <p>InlineModelAdmin.<b>raw_id_fields</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">By default, Django’s admin uses a select-box interface (<select>) for fields that are ForeignKey. Some-times you don’t want to incur the overhead of having to select all the related instances to display in the drop-down.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">raw_id_fields is a list of fields you would like to change into an Input widget for either a ForeignKey or ManyToManyField:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>BookInline</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">TabularInline):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">model</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Book</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">raw_id_fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"pages"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>InlineModelAdmin.<b>template</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The template used to render the inline on the page.</p> <p>InlineModelAdmin.<b>verbose_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">An override to the <a href="index.html#page_1687"><i>verbose_name</i></a> from the model’s inner Meta class.</p> <p>InlineModelAdmin.<b>verbose_name_plural</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">An override to the <a href="index.html#page_1687"><i>verbose_name_plural</i></a> from the model’s inner Meta class. If this isn’t given and</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">the <a href="index.html#page_1080"><i>InlineModelAdmin.verbose_name</i></a> is defined, Django will use <a href="index.html#page_1080"><i>InlineModelAdmin.verbose_name</i></a> + 's'.</p> <p>InlineModelAdmin.<b>can_delete</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Specifies whether or not inline objects can be deleted in the inline. Defaults to True.</p> <p id="page_1081" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>InlineModelAdmin.<b>show_change_link</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Specifies whether or not inline objects that can be changed in the admin have a link to the change form. style="font-size:0.87em">register(Person, PersonAdmin)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Working with many-to-many models</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>By default, admin widgets for many-to-many relations will be displayed on whichever model contains the</p> <p>actual reference to the <a href="index.html#page_1649"><i>ManyToManyField</i></a>. Depending on your ModelAdmin definition, each many-to-many field in your model will be represented by a standard HTML <select multiple>, a horizontal or vertical filter, or a raw_id_fields widget. However, it is also possible to replace these widgets with inlines.</p> <p>Suppose we have the following models:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Person</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">128</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">members</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ManyToManyField(Person, related_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"groups"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you want to display many-to-many relations using an inline, you can do so by defining an InlineModelAdmin object for the relationship:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span id="page_1084"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>GroupAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ModelAdmin):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"members"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">register(Group, GroupAdmin)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>There are two features worth noting in this example.</p> <p>Firstly - the MembershipInline class references Group.members.through. The through attribute is a refer-ence to the model that manages the many-to-many relation. This model is automatically created by Django when you define a many-to-many field.</p> <p>Secondly, the GroupAdmin must manually exclude the members field. Django displays an admin widget for a many-to-many field on the model that defines the relation (in this case, Group). If you want to use an inline model to represent the many-to-many relationship, you must tell Django’s admin to not display this widget- otherwise you will end up with two widgets on your admin page for managing the relation.</p> <p>Note that when using this technique the <a href="index.html#page_1957"><i>m2m_changed</i></a> signals aren’t triggered. This is because as far as the admin is concerned, through is just a model with two foreign key fields rather than a many-to-many relation.</p> <p>In all other respects, the InlineModelAdmin is exactly the same as any other. You can customize the appear-ance using any of the normal ModelAdmin properties.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Working with many-to-many intermediary models</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When you specify an intermediary model using the through argument to a <a href="index.html#page_1649"><i>ManyToManyField</i></a>, the admin will not display a widget by default. This is because each instance of that intermediary model requires more information than could be displayed in a single widget, and the layout required for multiple widgets will vary depending on the intermediate model.</p> <p>However, we still want to be able to edit that information inline. Fortunately, we can do this with inline admin models. Suppose we have the following models:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">128</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Group</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">128</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">members</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ManyToManyField(Person, through</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Membership"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">group</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ForeignKey(Group, on_delete</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">64</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The first step in displaying this intermediate model in the admin is to define an inline class for the Membership model:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MembershipInline</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Membership</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">extra</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This example uses the default InlineModelAdmin values for the Membership model, and limits the extra add forms to one. This could be customized using any of the options available to InlineModelAdmin classes.</p> <p>Now create admin views for the Person and Group models:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>PersonAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">register(Group, GroupAdmin)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Now your admin site is set up to edit Membership objects inline from either the Person or the Group detail pages.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1086"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using generic relations as an inline</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>It is possible to use an inline with generically related objects. Let’s say you have the following models:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.contenttypes.fields</span> <span <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Image</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Model):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">image</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ImageField(upload_to</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"images"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ForeignKey(ContentType, on_delete</span><span
