style="font-size:0.87em">object_id</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">PositiveIntegerField()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">content_object</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">GenericForeignKey(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"content_type"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"object_id"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Product</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Model):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">100</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you want to allow editing and creating an Image instance on the Product, add/change views you can</p> <p>use <a href="index.html#page_1123"><i>GenericTabularInline</i></a> or <a href="index.html#page_1123"><i>GenericStackedInline</i></a> (both subclasses of <a href="index.html#page_1123"><i>GenericInlineModelAdmin</i></a>) pro-</p> <p>vided by <a href="index.html#page_1123"><i>admin</i>. </a>They implement tabular and stacked visual layouts for the forms representing the inline objects, respectively, just like their non-generic counterparts. They behave just like any other inline. In your admin.py for this example app:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.contenttypes.admin</span> <span <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ImageInline</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(GenericTabularInline):</span></p> <p <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ProductAdmin</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">ImageInline,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span the <a href="index.html#page_1114">contenttypes documentation</a> for more specific information.</p> <p id="page_1087" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Overriding admin templates</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can override many of the templates which the admin module uses to generate the various pages of an admin site. You can even override a few of these templates for a specific app, or a specific model.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Set up your projects admin template directories</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The admin template files are located in the <a href="https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/contrib/admin/templates/admin">django/contrib/admin/templates/admin</a> directory.</p> <p>In order to override one or more of them, first create an admin directory in your project’s templates directory.</p> <p>This can be any of the directories you specified in the <a href="index.html#page_1933"><i>DIRS</i></a> option of the DjangoTemplates backend in the</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1932"><i>TEMPLATES</i></a> setting. If you have customized the 'loaders' option, be sure 'django.template.loaders. filesystem.Loader' appears before 'django.template.loaders.app_directories.Loader' so that your</p> <p>custom templates will be found by the template loading system before those that are included with <a href="index.html#page_1017"><i>django.</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1017"><i>contrib.admin</i></a>.</p> <p>Within this admin directory, create sub-directories named after your app. Within these app subdirectories create sub-directories named after your models. Note, that the admin app will lowercase the model name when looking for the directory, so make sure you name the directory in all lowercase if you are going to run your app on a case-sensitive filesystem.</p> <p>To override an admin template for a specific app, copy and edit the template from the</p> <p><a href="https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/contrib/admin/templates/admin">django/contrib/admin/templates/admin</a> directory, and save it to one of the directories you just created.</p> <p>For example, if we wanted to add a tool to the change list view for all the models in an app named my_app, we would copy contrib/admin/templates/admin/change_list.html to the templates/admin/my_app/ direc-tory of our project, and make any necessary changes.</p> <p>If we wanted to add a tool to the change list view for only a specific model named ‘Page’, we would copy that same file to the templates/admin/my_app/page directory of our project.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Overriding vs. replacing an admin template</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Because of the modular design of the admin templates, it is usually neither necessary nor advisable to replace an entire template. It is almost always better to override only the section of the template which you need to change.</p> <p>To continue the example above, we want to add a new link next to the History tool for the Page model. After looking at change_form.html we determine that we only need to override the object-tools-items block. Therefore here is our new change_form.html :</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>extends</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"admin/change_form.html"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">i18n admin_urls</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>block</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">object-tools-items</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_1088"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">href</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>url</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">opts</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>admin_urlname</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:'history'</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">original.pk</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>admin_urlquote</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">class</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span></p> <p><span style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">href</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"mylink/"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">class</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.47em"><i>,</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.47em"><i>→</i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"viewsitelink"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>translate</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"View on site"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endif</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endblock</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>And that’s it! If we placed this file in the templates/admin/my_app directory, our link would appear on the change form for all models within my_app.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Templates which may be overridden per app or model</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Not every template in contrib/admin/templates/admin may be overridden per app or per model. The following can:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• actions.html</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• app_index.html</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• change_form.html</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• change_form_object_tools.html</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• change_list.html</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• change_list_object_tools.html</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• change_list_results.html</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• date_hierarchy.html</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• delete_confirmation.html</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• object_history.html</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• pagination.html</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• popup_response.html</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• prepopulated_fields_js.html</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• search_form.html</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• submit_line.html</p> <p id="page_1089" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>For those templates that cannot be overridden in this way, you may still override them for your entire project by placing the new version in your templates/admin directory. This is particularly useful to create custom 404 and 500 pages.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: Some of the admin templates, such as change_list_results.html are used to render custom inclusion tags. These may be overridden, but in such cases you are probably better off creating your own version of the tag in question and giving it a different name. That way you can use it selectively.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Root and login templates</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you wish to change the index, login or logout templates, you are better off creating your own AdminSite</p> <p>instance (see below), and changing the <a href="index.html#page_1091"><i>AdminSite.index_template</i></a> , <a href="index.html#page_1091"><i>AdminSite.login_template</i></a> or</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1091"><i>AdminSite.logout_template</i></a> properties.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Theming support</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The admin uses CSS variables to define colors and fonts. This allows changing themes without having to override many individual CSS rules. For example, if you preferred purple instead of blue you could add a admin/base.html template override to your project:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>extends</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'admin/base.html'</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>block</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">extrastyle</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">block</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.super</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">style</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">html</span><span <p style="margin-left:1em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">--link-selected-fg</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">#8f5bb2</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endblock</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The list of CSS variables are defined at <a href="https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/contrib/admin/static/admin/css/base.css">django/contrib/admin/static/admin/css/base.css.</a></p> <p>Dark mode variables, respecting the <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/prefers-color-scheme">prefers-color-scheme</a> media query, are defined at</p> <p><a href="https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/contrib/admin/static/admin/css/dark_mode.css">django/contrib/admin/static/admin/css/dark_mode.css</a>. This is linked to the document in {% block dark-mode-vars %}.</p> <p id="page_1090"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>extrabody block</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can add custom HTML, JavaScript, or other content to appear just before the closing </body> tag of templates that extend admin/base.html by extending the extrabody block. For example, if you want an alert to appear on page load you could add a admin/base.html template override to your project:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>extends</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'admin/base.html'</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>block</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">extrabody</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">.super</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">script</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">document</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.addEventListener(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">'DOMContentLoaded'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>function</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">() {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">window</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">.alert(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">'Welcome!'</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">);</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endblock</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">extrabody</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>AdminSite objects</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class AdminSite</b>(name='admin')</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A Django administrative site is represented by an instance of django.contrib.admin.sites. AdminSite; by default, an instance of this class is created as django.contrib.admin.site and you can register your models and ModelAdmin instances with it.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you want to customize the default admin site, you can <a href="index.html#page_1095">override it</a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">When constructing an instance of an AdminSite, you can provide a unique instance name using the name argument to the constructor. This instance name is used to identify the instance, especially when</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1099">reversing admin URLs</a>. If no instance name is provided, a default instance name of admin will be used.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">See <a href="index.html#page_1094">Customizing the AdminSite class</a> for an example of customizing the <a href="index.html#page_1090"><i>AdminSite</i></a> class.</p> <p>django.contrib.admin.sites.<b>all_sites</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/weakref.html#weakref.WeakSet">WeakSet</a> contains all admin site instances.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>AdminSite attributes</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Templates can override or extend base admin templates as described in <a href="index.html#page_1087">Overriding admin templates.</a></p> <p>AdminSite.<b>site_header</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The text to put at the top of each admin page, as a <div> (a string). By default, this is “Django admin-istration”.</p> <p>AdminSite.<b>site_title</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The text to put at the end of each admin page’s <title> (a string). By default, this is “Django site admin”.</p> <p id="page_1091" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>AdminSite.<b>site_url</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The URL for the “View site” link at the top of each admin page. By default, site_url is /. Set it to None to remove the link.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For sites running on a subpath, the <a href="index.html#page_1092"><i>each_context()</i></a> method checks if the current request has request. META['SCRIPT_NAME'] set and uses that value if site_url isn’t set to something other than /.</p> <p>AdminSite.<b>index_title</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The text to put at the top of the admin index page (a string). By default, this is “Site administration”.</p> <p>AdminSite.<b>index_template</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Path to a custom template that will be used by the admin site main index view.</p> <p>AdminSite.<b>app_index_template</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Path to a custom template that will be used by the admin site app index view.</p> <p>AdminSite.<b>empty_value_display</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The string to use for displaying empty values in the admin site’s change list. Defaults to a dash. The value can also be overridden on a per ModelAdmin basis and on a custom field within a ModelAdmin</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">by setting an empty_value_display attribute on the field. See <a href="index.html#page_1041"><i>ModelAdmin.empty_value_display</i></a> for examples.</p> <p>AdminSite.<b>enable_nav_sidebar</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A boolean value that determines whether to show the navigation sidebar on larger screens. By default, it is set to True.</p> <p>AdminSite.<b>final_catch_all_view</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A boolean value that determines whether to add a final catch-all view to the admin that redirects unauthenticated users to the login page. By default, it is set to True.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em">Warning: Setting this to False is not recommended as the view protects against a potential model enumeration privacy issue.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>AdminSite.<b>login_template</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Path to a custom template that will be used by the admin site login view.</p> <p>AdminSite.<b>login_form</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Subclass of <a href="index.html#page_558"><i>AuthenticationForm</i></a> that will be used by the admin site login view.</p> <p>AdminSite.<b>logout_template</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Path to a custom template that will be used by the admin site logout view.</p> <p>AdminSite.<b>password_change_template</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Path to a custom template that will be used by the admin site password change view.</p> <p id="page_1092"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>AdminSite.<b>password_change_done_template</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Path to a custom template that will be used by the admin site password change done view.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>AdminSite methods</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>AdminSite.<b>each_context</b>( request)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns a dictionary of variables to put in the template context for every page in the admin site.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Includes the following variables and values by default:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• site_header: <a href="index.html#page_1090"><i>AdminSite.site_header</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• site_title: <a href="index.html#page_1090"><i>AdminSite.site_title</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• site_url: <a href="index.html#page_1091"><i>AdminSite.site_url</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• has_permission: <a href="index.html#page_1093"><i>AdminSite.has_permission()</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• available_apps: a list of applications from the <a href="index.html#page_921">application registry</a> available for the current user.</p> <p style="text-align:center">Each entry in the list is a dict representing an application with the following keys:</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">– app_label: the application label</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">– app_url: the URL of the application index in the admin</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">– has_module_perms: a boolean indicating if displaying and accessing of the module’s index</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">page is permitted for the current user</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">– models: a list of the models available in the application</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Each model is a dict with the following keys:</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">– model: the model class</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">– object_name: class name of the model</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">– name: plural name of the model</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">– perms: a dict tracking add, change, delete, and view permissions</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">– admin_url: admin changelist URL for the model</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">– add_url: admin URL to add a new model instance</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• is_popup: whether the current page is displayed in a popup window</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• is_nav_sidebar_enabled: <a href="index.html#page_1091"><i>AdminSite.enable_nav_sidebar</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• log_entries: <a href="index.html#page_1093"><i>AdminSite.get_log_entries()</i></a></p> <p>AdminSite.<b>get_app_list</b>( request, app_label=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns a list of applications from the <a href="index.html#page_921">application registry</a> available for the current user. You can op-tionally pass an app_label argument to get details for a single app. Each entry in the list is a dictionary representing an application with the following keys:</p> <p id="page_1093" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• app_label: the application label</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• app_url: the URL of the application index in the admin</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• has_module_perms: a boolean indicating if displaying and accessing of the module’s index page</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">is permitted for the current user</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• models: a list of the models available in the application</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• name: name of the application</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Each model is a dictionary with the following keys:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• model: the model class</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• object_name: class name of the model</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• name: plural name of the model</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• perms: a dict tracking add, change, delete, and view permissions</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• admin_url: admin changelist URL for the model</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• add_url: admin URL to add a new model instance</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Lists of applications and models are sorted alphabetically by their names. You can override this method to change the default order on the admin index page.</p> <p>AdminSite.<b>has_permission</b>(request)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns True if the user for the given HttpRequest has permission to view at least one page in the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">admin site. Defaults to requiring both <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>User.is_active</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>User.is_staff</i></a> to be True.</p> <p>AdminSite.<b>register</b>(model_or_iterable, admin_class=None, **options)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Registers the given model class (or iterable of classes) with the given admin_class. admin_class de-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">faults to <a href="index.html#page_1038"><i>ModelAdmin</i></a> (the default admin options). If keyword arguments are given – e.g. list_display – they’ll be applied as options to the admin class.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Raises <a href="index.html#page_1472"><i>ImproperlyConfigured</i></a> if a model is abstract. and django.contrib.admin.exceptions. AlreadyRegistered if a model is already registered.</p> <p>AdminSite.<b>unregister</b>(model_or_iterable)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Unregisters the given model class (or iterable of classes).</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Raises django.contrib.admin.exceptions.NotRegistered if a model isn’t already registered.</p> <p>AdminSite.<b>get_model_admin</b>(model)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns an admin class for the given model class. Raises django.contrib.admin.exceptions. NotRegistered if a model isn’t registered.</p> <p>AdminSite.<b>get_log_entries</b>(request)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns a queryset for the related <a href="index.html#page_1098"><i>LogEntry</i></a> instances, shown on the site index page. This method can be overridden to filter the log entries by other criteria.</p> <p id="page_1094"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Hooking AdminSite instances into your URLconf</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The last step in setting up the Django admin is to hook your AdminSite instance into your URLconf. Do this</p> <p>by pointing a given URL at the AdminSite.urls method. It is not necessary to use <a href="index.html#page_2070"><i>include()</i>.</a></p> <p>In this example, we register the default AdminSite instance django.contrib.admin.site at the URL / admin/</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># urls.py</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.urls</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">path</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"admin/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">urls),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Customizing the AdminSite class</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you’d like to set up your own admin site with custom behavior, you’re free to subclass AdminSite and override or add anything you like. Then, create an instance of your AdminSite subclass (the same way you’d instantiate any other Python class) and register your models and ModelAdmin subclasses with it instead of</p> <p>with the default site. Finally, update myproject/urls.py to reference your <a href="index.html#page_1090"><i>AdminSite</i></a> subclass.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">Listing 2: myapp/admin.py</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">MyModel</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyAdminSite</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">AdminSite):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">site_header</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Monty Python administration"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">admin_site</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">MyAdminSite(name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"myadmin"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">admin_site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">register(MyModel)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">Listing 3: myproject/urls.py</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.urls</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">path</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.admin</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin_site</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_1095" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"myadmin/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, admin_site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">urls),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note that you may not want autodiscovery of admin modules when using your own AdminSite instance since you will likely be importing all the per-app admin modules in your myproject.admin module. This means you need to put 'django.contrib.admin.apps.SimpleAdminConfig' instead of 'django.contrib.admin'</p> <p>in your <a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Overriding the default admin site</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can override the default django.contrib.admin.site by setting the <a href="index.html#page_1040"><i>default_site</i></a> attribute of a cus-tom AppConfig to the dotted import path of either a AdminSite subclass or a callable that returns a site instance.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">Listing 4: myproject/admin.py</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">Listing 5: myproject/apps.py</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.admin.apps</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">AdminConfig</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyAdminConfig</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(AdminConfig):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">default_site</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"myproject.admin.MyAdminSite"</span></p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1096"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">Listing 6: myproject/settings.py</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">INSTALLED_APPS</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"myproject.apps.MyAdminConfig"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Multiple admin sites in the same URLconf</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can create multiple instances of the admin site on the same Django-powered website. Create multiple instances of AdminSite and place each one at a different URL.</p> <p>In this example, the URLs /basic-admin/ and /advanced-admin/ feature separate versions of the admin site – using the AdminSite instances myproject.admin.basic_site and myproject.admin.advanced_site, respectively:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># urls.py</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.urls</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">path</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myproject.admin</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">advanced_site, basic_site</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"basic-admin/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, basic_site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">urls),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"advanced-admin/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, advanced_site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">urls),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>AdminSite instances take a single argument to their constructor, their name, which can be anything you</p> <p>like. This argument becomes the prefix to the URL names for the purposes of <a href="index.html#page_1099">reversing them</a>. This is only necessary if you are using more than one AdminSite.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Adding views to admin sites</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Just like <a href="index.html#page_1038"><i>ModelAdmin</i></a>, <a href="index.html#page_1090"><i>AdminSite</i></a> provides a <a href="index.html#page_1067"><i>get_urls()</i></a> method that can be overridden to define additional</p> <p>views for the site. To add a new view to your admin site, extend the base <a href="index.html#page_1067"><i>get_urls()</i></a> method to include a pattern for your new view.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: Any view you render that uses the admin templates, or extends the base admin template, should set request.current_app before rendering the template. It should be set to either self.name if your view is on an AdminSite or self.admin_site.name if your view is on a ModelAdmin.</p> <p id="page_1097" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Adding a password reset feature</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can add a password reset feature to the admin site by adding a few lines to your URLconf. Specifically, add these four patterns:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"reset/<uidb64>/<token>/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"password_reset_complete"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>(This assumes you’ve added the admin at admin/ and requires that you put the URLs starting with ^admin/ before the line that includes the admin app itself).</p> <p>The presence of the admin_password_reset named URL will cause a “forgotten your password?” link to appear on the default admin log-in page under the password box.</p> <p id="page_1098"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>LogEntry objects</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> models.<b>LogEntry</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The LogEntry class tracks additions, changes, and deletions of objects done through the admin inter-face.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>LogEntry attributes</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>LogEntry.<b>action_time</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The date and time of the action.</p> <p>LogEntry.<b>user</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The user (an <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>AUTH_USER_MODEL</i></a> instance) who performed the action.</p> <p>LogEntry.<b>content_type</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The <a href="index.html#page_1115"><i>ContentType</i></a> of the modified object.</p> <p>LogEntry.<b>object_id</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The textual representation of the modified object’s primary key.</p> <p>LogEntry.<b>object_repr</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The object`s repr() after the modification.</p> <p>LogEntry.<b>action_flag</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The type of action logged: ADDITION, CHANGE, DELETION.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">For example, to get a list of all additions done through the admin:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.admin.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ADDITION, LogEntry</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">LogEntry</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(action_flag</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ADDITION)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>LogEntry.<b>change_message</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The detailed description of the modification. In the case of an edit, for example, the message contains a list of the edited fields. The Django admin site formats this content as a JSON structure, so that</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1099"><i>get_change_message()</i></a> can recompose a message translated in the current user language. Custom code</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">might set this as a plain string though. You are advised to use the <a href="index.html#page_1099"><i>get_change_message()</i></a> method to retrieve this value instead of accessing it directly.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1099" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>LogEntry methods</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>LogEntry.<b>get_edited_object</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A shortcut that returns the referenced object.</p> <p>LogEntry.<b>get_change_message</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Formats and translates <a href="index.html#page_1098"><i>change_message</i></a> into the current user language. Messages created before Django 1.10 will always be displayed in the language in which they were logged.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Reversing admin URLs</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When an <a href="index.html#page_1090"><i>AdminSite</i></a> is deployed, the views provided by that site are accessible using Django’s <a href="index.html#page_278">URL reversing</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_278">system.</a></p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_1090"><i>AdminSite</i></a> provides the following named URL patterns:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Page URL name Parameters</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Index index</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Login login</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Logout logout</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Password change password_change</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Password change done password_change_done</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">i18n JavaScript jsi18n</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Application index page app_list app_label</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Redirect to object’s page view_on_site content_type_id, object_id</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Each <a href="index.html#page_1038"><i>ModelAdmin</i></a> instance provides an additional set of named URLs:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:5em">Page URL name Parameters</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">Changelist {{ app_label }}_{{ model_name }}_changelist</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">Add {{ app_label }}_{{ model_name }}_add</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">History {{ app_label }}_{{ model_name }}_history object_id Delete {{ app_label }}_{{ model_name }}_delete object_id Change {{ app_label }}_{{ model_name }}_change object_id</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The UserAdmin provides a named URL:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:8em">Page URL name Parameters</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">Password change auth_user_password_change user_id <b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p id="page_1100">These named URLs are registered with the application namespace admin, and with an instance namespace corresponding to the name of the Site instance.</p> <p>So - if you wanted to get a reference to the Change view for a particular Choice object (from the polls appli-cation) in the default admin, you would call:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.urls</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">reverse</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">c</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Choice</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">change_url</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">reverse(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"admin:polls_choice_change"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, args</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(c</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">id,))</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This will find the first registered instance of the admin application (whatever the instance name), and resolve to the view for changing poll.Choice instances in that instance.</p> <p>If you want to find a URL in a specific admin instance, provide the name of that instance as a current_app hint to the reverse call. For example, if you specifically wanted the admin view from the admin instance named custom, you would need to call:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">change_url</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">reverse(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"admin:polls_choice_change"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, args</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(c</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">id,), current_app</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"custom"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>For more details, see the documentation on <a href="index.html#page_279">reversing namespaced URLs</a>.</p> <p>To allow easier reversing of the admin urls in templates, Django provides an admin_urlname filter which takes an action as argument:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>load</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">admin_urls</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">href</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>url</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">opts</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>admin_urlname</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:'add'</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>Add user</</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">href</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>url</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">opts</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>|</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>admin_urlname</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:'delete'</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">user.pk</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">>Delete this user</</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The action in the examples above match the last part of the URL names for <a href="index.html#page_1038"><i>ModelAdmin</i></a> instances described above. The opts variable can be any object which has an app_label and model_name attributes and is usually supplied by the admin views for the current model.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>The display decorator</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>display</b>(*, boolean=None, ordering=None, description=None, empty_value=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This decorator can be used for setting specific attributes on custom display functions that can be used</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">with <a href="index.html#page_1048"><i>list_display</i></a> or <a attribute as-signed directly to the function. It cannot be used in conjunction with boolean – they are mutually exclusive.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Use of this decorator is not compulsory to make a display function, but it can be useful to use it without arguments as a marker in your source to identify the purpose of the function:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@admin</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">display</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>published_year</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, obj):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">obj</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">publish_date</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">year</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">In this case it will add no attributes to the function.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>The staff_member_required decorator</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>staff_member_required</b>(redirect_field_name='next', login_url='admin:login')</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This decorator is used on the admin views that require authorization. A view decorated with this func-tion will have the following behavior:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• If the user is logged in, is a staff member (User.is_staff=True), and is active (User.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">is_active=True), execute the view normally.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• Otherwise, the request will be redirected to the URL specified by the login_url parameter, with</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">the originally requested path in a query string variable specified by redirect_field_name. For example: /admin/login/?next=/admin/polls/question/3/.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Example usage:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.admin.views.decorators</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">staff_member_required</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">@staff_member_required</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p id="page_1102"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.5.2</b></span> <span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>django.contrib.auth</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This document provides API reference material for the components of Django’s authentication system. For more details on the usage of these components or how to customize authentication and authorization see the</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_530">authentication topic guide</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>User model</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> models.<b>User</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Fields</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> models.<b>User</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>User</i></a> objects have the following fields:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>username</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Required. 150 characters or fewer. Usernames may contain alphanumeric, _, @, +, . and-charac-ters.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The max_length should be sufficient for many use cases. If you need a longer length, please use a</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_586">custom user model.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>first_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional <a href="index.html#page_1616">(<i>blank=True</i>). </a>150 characters or fewer.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>last_name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional <a href="index.html#page_1616">(<i>blank=True</i>). </a>150 characters or fewer.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>email</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional <a href="index.html#page_1616">(<i>blank=True</i>). </a>Email address.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>password</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Required. A hash of, and metadata about, the password. (Django doesn’t store the raw password.) Raw passwords can be arbitrarily long and can contain any character. The metadata in this field</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">may mark the password as unusable. See the <a href="index.html#page_562">password documentation.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>groups</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Many-to-many relationship to <a href="index.html#page_1108"><i>Group</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>user_permissions</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Many-to-many relationship to <a href="index.html#page_1108"><i>Permission</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>is_staff</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Boolean. Allows this user to access the admin site.</p> <p id="page_1103" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>is_active</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Boolean. Marks this user account as active. We recommend that you set this flag to False instead of deleting accounts. That way, if your applications have any foreign keys to users, the foreign keys won’t break.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">This doesn’t necessarily control whether or not the user can log in. <span style="float:right">Authentication</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">backends aren’t required to check for the is_active flag but the default backend</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_1111">(<i>ModelBackend</i></a>) and the <a href="index.html#page_1113"><i>RemoteUserBackend</i></a> do. You can use <a href="index.html#page_1112"><i>AllowAllUsersModelBackend</i></a> or</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_1114"><i>AllowAllUsersRemoteUserBackend</i></a> if you want to allow inactive users to login. In this case,</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">you’ll also want to customize the <a href="index.html#page_558"><i>AuthenticationForm</i></a> used by the <a href="index.html#page_549"><i>LoginView</i></a> as it rejects</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">inactive users. Be aware that the permission-checking methods such as <a href="index.html#page_1105"><i>has_perm()</i></a> and the authentication in the Django admin all return False for inactive users.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>is_superuser</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Boolean. Treats this user as having all permissions without assigning any permission to it in par-ticular.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>last_login</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A datetime of the user’s last login.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>date_joined</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The date/time when the account was created.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Attributes</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> models.<b>User</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>is_authenticated</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Read-only attribute which is always True (as opposed to AnonymousUser.is_authenticated which is always False). This is a way to tell if the user has been authenticated. This does not imply any permissions and doesn’t check if the user is active or has a valid session. Even though normally you will check this attribute on request.user to find out whether it has been populated</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">by the <a href="index.html#page_1599"><i>AuthenticationMiddleware</i></a> (representing the currently logged-in user), you should know</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">this attribute is True for any <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>User</i></a> instance.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>is_anonymous</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Read-only attribute which is always False. This is a way of differentiating <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>User</i></a> and</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_1107"><i>AnonymousUser</i></a> objects. Generally, you should prefer using <a href="index.html#page_1103"><i>is_authenticated</i></a> to this attribute.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1104"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Methods</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> models.<b>User</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_username</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns the username for the user. Since the User model can be swapped out, you should use this method instead of referencing the username attribute directly.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_full_name</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns the <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>first_name</i></a> plus the <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>last_name</i></a>, with a space in between.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_short_name</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns the <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>first_name</i>.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>set_password</b>( raw_password)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Sets the user’s password to the given raw string, taking care of the password hashing. Doesn’t save</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">the <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>User</i></a> object.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">When the raw_password is None, the password will be set to an unusable password, as if</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_1104"><i>set_unusable_password()</i></a> were used.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>check_password</b>(raw_password)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>acheck_password</b>(raw_password)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Asynchronous version: acheck_password()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns True if the given raw string is the correct password for the user. (This takes care of the password hashing in making the comparison.)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>set_unusable_password</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Marks the user as having no password set by updating the metadata in the <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>password</i></a> field. This</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">isn’t the same as having a blank string for a password. <a href="index.html#page_1104"><i>check_password()</i></a> for this user will never</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">return True. Doesn’t save the <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>User</i></a> object.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">You may need this if authentication for your application takes place against an existing external source such as an LDAP directory.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Password reset restriction</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Users having an unusable password will not able to request a password reset email via</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_553"><i>PasswordResetView</i></a> .</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p user.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_user_permissions</b>(obj=None)</p> <p id="page_1105" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p The domain portion of <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>email</i></a> is automatically con-</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">verted to lowercase, and the returned <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>User</i></a> object will have <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>is_active</i></a> set to True.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If no password is provided, <a href="index.html#page_1104"><i>set_unusable_password()</i></a> will be called.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The extra_fields keyword arguments are passed through to the <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>User</i></a>’s __init__ method to</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">allow setting arbitrary fields on a <a href="index.html#page_583">custom user model</a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">See <a href="index.html#page_531">Creating users</a> for example usage.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">acreate_user() method was added.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>create_superuser</b>(username, email=None, password=None, **extra_fields)</p> <p id="page_1107" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>acreate_superuser</b>(username, email=None, password=None, **extra_fields)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Asynchronous version: acreate_superuser()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Same as <a href="index.html#page_1106"><i>create_user()</i></a>, but sets <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>is_staff</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1103"><i>is_superuser</i></a> to True.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">acreate_superuser() method was added.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>with_perm</b>(perm, is_active=True, include_superusers=True, backend=None, obj=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns users that have the given permission perm either in the "<app label>.<permission</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">codename>" format or as a <a href="index.html#page_1108"><i>Permission</i></a> instance. Returns an empty queryset if no users who have the perm found.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If is_active is True (default), returns only active users, or if False, returns only inactive users. Use None to return all users irrespective of active state.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If include_superusers is True (default), the result will include superusers.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If backend is passed in and it’s defined in <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS</i></a>, then this method will use</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">it. Otherwise, it will use the backend in <a href="index.html#page_1938"><i>AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS</i></a> , if there is only one, or raise an exception.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>AnonymousUser object</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> models.<b>AnonymousUser</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a The default validator for User.username.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Login and logout signals</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The auth framework uses the following <a href="index.html#page_751">signals</a> that can be used for notification when a user logs in or out.</p> <p><b>user_logged_in</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Sent when a user logs in successfully.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Arguments sent with this signal:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>sender</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The class of the user that just logged in.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>request</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The current <a href="index.html#page_1859"><i>HttpRequest</i></a> instance.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>user</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The user instance that just logged in.</p> <p><b>user_logged_out</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Sent when the logout method is called.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>sender</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">As above: the class of the user that just logged out or None if the user was not authenticated.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>request</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The current <a href="index.html#page_1859"><i>HttpRequest</i></a> instance.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>user</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The user instance that just logged out or None if the user was not authenticated.</p> <p><b>user_login_failed</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Sent when the user failed to login successfully</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>sender</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The name of the module used for authentication.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>credentials</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A dictionary of keyword arguments containing the user credentials that were passed to</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_532"><i>authenticate()</i></a> or your own custom authentication backend. Credentials matching a set of ‘sen-sitive’ patterns, (including password) will not be sent in the clear as part of the signal.</p> <p id="page_1110"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>request</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The <a href="index.html#page_1859"><i>HttpRequest</i></a> object, if one was provided to <a href="index.html#page_532"><i>authenticate()</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Authentication backends</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This section details the authentication backends that come with Django. For information on how to use them</p> <p>and how to write your own authentication backends, see the <a href="index.html#page_576">Other authentication sources section</a> of the <a href="index.html#page_530">User</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_530">authentication guide</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Available authentication backends</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The following backends are available in <a href="index.html#page_1110"><i>django.contrib.auth.backends</i>:</a></p> <p><b>class BaseBackend</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A base class that provides default implementations for all required methods. string perm.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">ahas_perm() function was added.</p> <p><b>class ModelBackend</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This is the default authentication backend used by Django. It authenticates using credentials consisting of a user identifier and password. For Django’s default user model, the user identifier is the username,</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">for custom user models it is the field specified by USERNAME_FIELD (see <a href="index.html#page_576">Customizing Users and au-</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_576">thentication</a>).</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">It also handles the default permissions model as defined for <a href="index.html#page_1102"><i>User</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_592"><i>PermissionsMixin</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1112"><i>has_perm()</i> , <i>get_all_permissions()</i></a>, <a href="index.html#page_1111"><i>get_user_permissions()</i></a><a href="index.html#page_1111">, </a>and <a href="index.html#page_1111"><i>get_group_permissions()</i></a> al-low an object to be passed as a parameter for object-specific permissions, but this backend does not implement them other than returning an empty set of permissions if obj is not None.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1112"><i>with_perm()</i></a> also allows an object to be passed as a parameter, but unlike others methods it returns an empty queryset if obj is not None.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>authenticate</b>( request, username=None, password=None, **kwargs)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>aauthenticate</b>(request, username=None, password=None, **kwargs)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Asynchronous version: aauthenticate()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Tries to authenticate username with password by calling <a href="index.html#page_1104"><i>User.check_password</i></a>. If no username</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">is provided, it tries to fetch a username from kwargs using the key <a href="index.html#page_586"><i>CustomUser.USERNAME_FIELD</i></a>. Returns an authenticated user or None.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">request is an <a href="index.html#page_1859"><i>HttpRequest</i></a> and may be None if it wasn’t provided to <a href="index.html#page_532"><i>authenticate()</i></a> (which passes it on to the backend).</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">aauthenticate() function was added.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_user_permissions</b>(user_obj, obj=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>aget_user_permissions</b>(user_obj, obj=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Asynchronous version: aget_user_permissions()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns the set of permission strings the user_obj has from their own user permissions. Returns</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">an empty set if <a href="index.html#page_588"><i>is_anonymous</i></a> or <a href="index.html#page_587"><i>is_active</i></a> is False.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">aget_user_permissions() function was added.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_group_permissions</b>(user_obj, obj=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>aget_group_permissions</b>(user_obj, obj=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Asynchronous version: aget_group_permissions()</p> <p id="page_1112"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns the set of permission strings the user_obj has from the permissions of the groups they</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">belong. Returns an empty set if <a href="index.html#page_588"><i>is_anonymous</i></a> or <a href="index.html#page_587"><i>is_active</i></a> is False.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">aget_group_permissions() function was added.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_all_permissions</b>(user_obj, obj=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>aget_all_permissions</b>(user_obj, obj=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Asynchronous version: aget_all_permissions()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Returns the set of permission strings the user_obj has, including both user permissions and group</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">permissions. Returns an empty set if <a href="index.html#page_588"><i>is_anonymous</i></a> or <a href="index.html#page_587"><i>is_active</i></a> is False.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">aget_all_permissions() function was added.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>has_perm</b>(user_obj, perm, obj=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>ahas_perm</b>(user_obj, perm, obj=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Asynchronous version: ahas_perm()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Uses <a href="index.html#page_1112"><i>get_all_permissions()</i></a> to check if user_obj has the permission string perm. Returns an empty queryset if no users who have the perm found.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If is_active is True (default), returns only active users, or if False, returns only inactive users. Use None to return all users irrespective of active state.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If include_superusers is True (default), the result will include superusers.</p> <p id="page_1113" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class AllowAllUsersModelBackend</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Same as <a href="index.html#page_1111"><i>ModelBackend</i></a> except that it doesn’t reject inactive users because <a href="index.html#page_1112"><i>user_can_authenticate()</i></a> always returns True.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">When using this backend, you’ll likely want to customize the <a href="index.html#page_558"><i>AuthenticationForm</i></a> used by the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_549"><i>LoginView</i></a> by overriding the <a href="index.html#page_558"><i>confirm_login_allowed()</i></a> method as it rejects inactive users.</p> <p><b>class RemoteUserBackend</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Use this backend to take advantage of external-to-Django-handled authentication. Determines whether or not a user object is created if not already in the database Defaults to True.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>authenticate</b>( request, remote_user)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>aauthenticate</b>(request, remote_user)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Asynchronous version: aauthenticate()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The username passed as remote_user is considered trusted. Returns the cleaned username.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>configure_user</b>(request, user, created=True)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>aconfigure_user</b>(request, user, created=True)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Asynchronous version: aconfigure_user()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Configures the user on each authentication attempt.
