style="font-size:0.87em">array([[0, 0, 0, 0],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">[1, 1, 1, 1],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">[2, 2, 2, 2],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:6em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">[3, 3, 3, 3]], dtype=uint8)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>metadata</b></p> <p style="text-align:center">The metadata of this band. The functionality is identical to <a href="index.html#page_1259"><i>GDALRaster.metadata</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Creating rasters from data</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This section describes how to create rasters from scratch using the ds_input parameter.</p> <p>A new raster is created when a dict is passed to the <a href="index.html#page_1253"><i>GDALRaster</i></a> constructor. The dictionary contains defining parameters of the new raster, such as the origin, size, or spatial reference system. The dictionary can also contain pixel data and information about the format of the new raster. The resulting raster can therefore be file-based or memory-based, depending on the driver specified.</p> <p>There’s no standard for describing raster data in a dictionary or JSON flavor. The definition of the dictionary</p> <p>input to the <a href="index.html#page_1253"><i>GDALRaster</i></a> class is therefore specific to Django. It’s inspired by the <a href="https://geojson.org/">geojson</a> format, but the geojson standard is currently limited to vector formats.</p> <p>Examples of using the different keys when creating rasters can be found in the documentation of the corre-</p> <p>sponding attributes and methods of the <a href="index.html#page_1253"><i>GDALRaster</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1260"><i>GDALBand</i></a> classes.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>The ds_input dictionary</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Only a few keys are required in the ds_input dictionary to create a raster: width, height, and srid. All other parameters have default values (see the table below). The list of keys that can be passed in the ds_input</p> <p>dictionary is closely related but not identical to the <a href="index.html#page_1253"><i>GDALRaster</i></a> properties. Many of the parameters are mapped directly to those properties; the others are described below.</p> <p>The following table describes all keys that can be set in the ds_input dictionary.</p> <p id="page_1264"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:8em">Key Default Usage</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">srid required Mapped to the <a href="index.html#page_1256"><i>srid</i></a> attribute</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">width required Mapped to the <a href="index.html#page_1255"><i>width</i></a> attribute</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">height required Mapped to the <a href="index.html#page_1255"><i>height</i></a> attribute</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">driver MEM Mapped to the <a href="index.html#page_1254"><i>driver</i></a> attribute</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">name '' See below</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">origin 0 Mapped to the <a href="index.html#page_1256"><i>origin</i></a> attribute</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">scale 0 Mapped to the <a href="index.html#page_1257"><i>scale</i></a> attribute</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">skew 0 Mapped to the <a href="index.html#page_1255"><i>width</i></a> attribute</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">bands [] See below</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">nr_of_bands 0 See below</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">datatype 6 See below</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">papsz_options {} See below</p> <p><b>name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">String representing the name of the raster. When creating a file-based raster, this parameter must be the file path for the new raster. If the name starts with /vsimem/, the raster is created in GDAL’s virtual filesystem.</p> <p><b>datatype</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Integer representing the data type for all the bands. Defaults to 6 (Float32). All bands of a new raster are required to have the same datatype. The value mapping is:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:9em">Value GDAL Pixel Type Description</p> <p style="margin-left:9em">1 GDT_Byte 8 bit unsigned integer</p> <p style="margin-left:9em">2 GDT_UInt16 16 bit unsigned integer</p> <p style="margin-left:9em">3 GDT_Int16 16 bit signed integer</p> <p style="margin-left:9em">4 GDT_UInt32 32 bit unsigned integer</p> <p style="margin-left:9em">5 GDT_Int32 32 bit signed integer</p> <p style="margin-left:9em">6 GDT_Float32 32 bit floating point</p> <p style="margin-left:9em">7 GDT_Float64 64 bit floating point</p> <p style="margin-left:9em">12 GDT_UInt64 64 bit unsigned integer (GDAL 3.5+)</p> <p style="margin-left:9em">13 GDT_Int64 64 bit signed integer (GDAL 3.5+)</p> <p style="margin-left:9em">14 GDT_Int8 8 bit signed integer (GDAL 3.7+)</p> <p><b>nr_of_bands</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Integer representing the number of bands of the raster. A raster can be created without passing band data upon creation. If the number of bands isn’t specified, it’s automatically calculated from the length of the bands input. The number of bands can’t be changed after creation.</p> <p><b>bands</b></p> <p id="page_1265" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:center">A list of band_input dictionaries with band input data. The resulting band indices are the same as in the list provided. The definition of the band input dictionary is given below. If band data isn’t provided, the raster bands values are instantiated as an array of zeros and the “no data” value is set to None.</p> <p><b>papsz_options</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A dictionary with raster creation options. The key-value pairs of the input dictionary are passed to the driver on creation of the raster.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The available options are driver-specific and are described in the documentation of each driver.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The values in the dictionary are not case-sensitive and are automatically converted to the correct string format upon creation.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The following example uses some of the options available for the <a href="https://gdal.org/drivers/raster/gtiff.html">GTiff driver</a>. The result is a com-pressed raster with an internal tiling scheme. The internal tiles have a block size of 23 by 23:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">GDALRaster(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"driver"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"GTiff"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"/path/to/new/file.tif"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"srid"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">4326</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"width"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">255</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"height"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">255</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"nr_of_bands"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"papsz_options"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"compress"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"packbits"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"tiled"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"yes"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"blockxsize"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">23</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"blockysize"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">23</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>The band_input dictionary</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The bands key in the ds_input dictionary is a list of band_input dictionaries. Each band_input dictionary can contain pixel values and the “no data” value to be set on the bands of the new raster. The data array can have the full size of the new raster or be smaller. For arrays that are smaller than the full raster, the size,</p> <p>shape, and offset keys control the pixel values. The corresponding keys are passed to the <a href="index.html#page_1262"><i>data()</i></a> method. Their functionality is the same as setting the band data with that method. The following table describes the keys that can be used.</p> <p id="page_1266"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Key Default Usage</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">nodata_value None Mapped to the <a href="index.html#page_1261"><i>nodata_value</i></a> attribute</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">data Same as nodata_value or 0 Passed to the <a href="index.html#page_1262"><i>data()</i></a> method</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">size (with, height) of raster Passed to the <a href="index.html#page_1262"><i>data()</i></a> method</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">shape Same as size Passed to the <a href="index.html#page_1262"><i>data()</i></a> method</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">offset (0, 0) Passed to the <a href="index.html#page_1262"><i>data()</i></a> method</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using GDAL’s Virtual Filesystem</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>GDAL can access files stored in the filesystem, but also supports virtual filesystems to abstract accessing other kind of files, such as compressed, encrypted, or remote files.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using memory-based Virtual Filesystem</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>GDAL has an internal memory-based filesystem, which allows treating blocks of memory as files. It can be</p> <p>used to read and write <a href="index.html#page_1253"><i>GDALRaster</i></a> objects to and from binary file buffers.</p> <p>This is useful in web contexts where rasters might be obtained as a buffer from a remote storage or returned from a view without being written to disk.</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1253"><i>GDALRaster</i></a> objects are created in the virtual filesystem when a bytes object is provided as input, or when the file path starts with /vsimem/.</p> <p>Input provided as bytes has to be a full binary representation of a file. For instance:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"># Read a raster as a file object from a remote source.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">urllib.request</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">urlopen</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">dat</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">urlopen(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"https://example.com/raster.tif"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">read()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"># Instantiate a raster from the bytes object.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">rst</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">GDALRaster(dat)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"># The name starts with /vsimem/, indicating that the raster lives in the</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"># virtual filesystem.</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">rst</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">'/vsimem/da300bdb-129d-49a8-b336-e410a9428dad'</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To create a new virtual file-based raster from scratch, use the ds_input dictionary representation and provide</p> <p>a name argument that starts with /vsimem/ (for detail of the dictionary representation, see <a href="index.html#page_1263">Creating rasters</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1263">from data</a>). For virtual file-based rasters, the <a href="index.html#page_1260"><i>vsi_buffer</i></a> attribute returns the bytes representation of the raster.</p> <p>Here’s how to create a raster and return it as a file in an <a href="index.html#page_1871"><i>HttpResponse</i></a>:</p> <p id="page_1267" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.http</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">rst</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">GDALRaster(</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"/vsimem/temporarymemfile"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"driver"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"tif"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"width"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">6</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"height"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">6</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"srid"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">3086</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"origin"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">500000</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">400000</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"scale"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">100</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>-</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">100</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"bands"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"data"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">range</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">36</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"nodata_value"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">99</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">}],</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">HttpResponse(rast</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">vsi_buffer,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"image/tiff"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using other Virtual Filesystems</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Depending on the local build of GDAL other virtual filesystems may be supported. You can use them by</p> <p>prepending the provided path with the appropriate /vsi*/ prefix. See the <a href="https://gdal.org/user/virtual_file_systems.html">GDAL Virtual Filesystems docu-</a></p> <p><a href="https://gdal.org/user/virtual_file_systems.html">mentation</a> for more details.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Compressed rasters</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Instead decompressing the file and instantiating the resulting raster, GDAL can directly access compressed files using the /vsizip/, /vsigzip/, or /vsitar/ virtual filesystems:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.gis.gdal</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">GDALRaster</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">rst</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">GDALRaster(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/vsizip/path/to/your/file.zip/path/to/raster.tif"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">rst</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">GDALRaster(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/vsigzip/path/to/your/file.gz"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">rst</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">GDALRaster(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/vsitar/path/to/your/file.tar/path/to/raster.tif"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Network rasters</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>GDAL can support online resources and storage providers transparently. As long as it’s built with such ca-pabilities.</p> <p>To access a public raster file with no authentication, you can use /vsicurl/:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.gis.gdal</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">GDALRaster</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">rst</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">GDALRaster(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/vsicurl/https://example.com/raster.tif"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">rst</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">'/vsicurl/https://example.com/raster.tif'</span></p> <p id="page_1268"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>For commercial storage providers (e.g. /vsis3/) the system should be previously configured for authentica-</p> <p>tion and possibly other settings (see the <a href="https://gdal.org/user/virtual_file_systems.html">GDAL Virtual Filesystems documentation</a> for available options).</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Settings</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>GDAL_LIBRARY_PATH</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A string specifying the location of the GDAL library. Typically, this setting is only used if the GDAL library is in a non-standard location (e.g., /home/john/lib/libgdal.so).</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Exceptions</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>exception GDALException</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The base GDAL exception, indicating a GDAL-related error.</p> <p><b>exception SRSException</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">An exception raised when an error occurs when constructing or using a spatial reference system object.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Geolocation with GeoIP2</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_1269"><i>GeoIP2</i></a> <span style="font-size:0.67em"><a href="index.html#page_1268">1</a></span> object is a wrapper for the <a href="https://pypi.org/project/geoip2/">MaxMind geoip2 Python library</a> <a href="index.html#page_1268">.</a></p> <p>In order to perform IP-based geolocation, the <a href="index.html#page_1269"><i>GeoIP2</i></a> object requires the <a href="https://pypi.org/project/geoip2/">geoip2</a> Python package and the GeoIP Country and/or City datasets in binary format (the CSV files will not work!), downloaded from e.g.</p> <p><a href="https://dev.maxmind.com/geoip/geolite2-free-geolocation-data">MaxMind</a> or <a href="https://db-ip.com/db/lite.php">DB-IP</a> websites. Grab the GeoLite2-Country.mmdb.gz and GeoLite2-City.mmdb.gz files and</p> <p>unzip them in a directory corresponding to the <a href="index.html#page_1271"><i>GEOIP_PATH</i></a> setting.</p> <p>Additionally, it is recommended to install the <a href="https://github.com/maxmind/libmaxminddb/">libmaxminddb C library, </a>so that geoip2 can leverage the C library’s faster speed.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Example</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Here is an example of its usage:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span 'NA',</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">'continent_name': 'North America',</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">'country_code': 'US',</span></p> <p><span Reference</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class GeoIP2</b>(path=None, cache=0, country=None, city=None)</p> <p>The GeoIP object does not require any parameters to use the default settings. However, at the very least</p> <p>the <a href="index.html#page_1271"><i>GEOIP_PATH</i></a> setting should be set with the path of the location of your GeoIP datasets. The following initialization keywords may be used to customize any of the defaults.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1270"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Key- Description</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">word</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Argu-</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">ments</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">path <span style="float:right">Base directory to where GeoIP data is located or the full path to where the city or country data</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">files (.mmdb) are located. Assumes that both the city and country datasets are located in this</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">directory; overrides the <a href="index.html#page_1271"><i>GEOIP_PATH</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">cache <span style="float:right">The cache settings when opening up the GeoIP datasets. May be an integer in (0, 1, 2, 4, 8) corre-</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">sponding to the MODE_AUTO, MODE_MMAP_EXT, MODE_MMAP, and GEOIP_INDEX_CACHE MODE_MEMORY C API settings, respectively. Defaults to 0 (MODE_AUTO).</p> <p style="text-align:center">country The name of the GeoIP country data file. Defaults to GeoLite2-Country.mmdb. Setting this</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">keyword overrides the <a href="index.html#page_1271"><i>GEOIP_COUNTRY</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="text-align:center">city The name of the GeoIP city data file. Defaults to GeoLite2-City.mmdb. Setting this keyword</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">overrides the <a href="index.html#page_1271"><i>GEOIP_CITY</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Methods</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Instantiating</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>classmethod</b> GeoIP2.<b>open</b>(path, cache)</p> <p>This classmethod instantiates the GeoIP object from the given database path and given cache setting.</p> <p>Deprecated since version 5.1: Use the <a href="index.html#page_1269"><i>GeoIP2()</i></a> constructor instead.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Querying</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>All the following querying routines may take an instance of <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/ipaddress.html#ipaddress.IPv4Address">IPv4Address</a> or <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/ipaddress.html#ipaddress.IPv6Address">IPv6Address</a><a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/ipaddress.html#ipaddress.IPv6Address">, </a>a string IP address, or a fully qualified domain name (FQDN). For example, IPv4Address("205.186.163.125"), "205.186.163. 125", and "djangoproject.com" would all be valid query parameters.</p> <p>GeoIP2.<b>city</b>(query)</p> <p>Returns a dictionary of city information for the given query. Some of the values in the dictionary may be undefined (None).</p> <p>GeoIP2.<b>country</b>(query)</p> <p>Returns a dictionary with the country code and country for the given query.</p> <p>GeoIP2.<b>country_code</b>(query)</p> <p>Returns the country code corresponding to the query.</p> <p id="page_1271" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>GeoIP2.<b>country_name</b>(query)</p> <p>Returns the country name corresponding to the query.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Coordinate Retrieval</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>GeoIP2.<b>coords</b>(query)</p> <p>Returns a coordinate tuple of (longitude, latitude).</p> <p>Deprecated since version 5.1: Use <a href="index.html#page_1271"><i>GeoIP2.lon_lat()</i></a> instead.</p> <p>GeoIP2.<b>lon_lat</b>(query)</p> <p>Returns a coordinate tuple of (longitude, latitude).</p> <p>GeoIP2.<b>lat_lon</b>(query)</p> <p>Returns a coordinate tuple of (latitude, longitude),</p> <p>GeoIP2.<b>geos</b>(query)</p> <p>Returns a <a href="index.html#page_1222"><i>Point</i></a> object corresponding to the query.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Settings</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>GEOIP_PATH</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A string or <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path">pathlib.Path</a> specifying the directory where the GeoIP data files are located. This setting is</p> <p>required unless manually specified with path keyword when initializing the <a href="index.html#page_1269"><i>GeoIP2</i></a> object.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>GEOIP_COUNTRY</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The basename to use for the GeoIP country data file. Defaults to 'GeoLite2-Country.mmdb'.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>GEOIP_CITY</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The basename to use for the GeoIP city data file. Defaults to 'GeoLite2-City.mmdb'.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1272"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Exceptions</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>exception GeoIP2Exception</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The exception raised when an error occurs in the <a href="index.html#page_1269"><i>GeoIP2</i></a> wrapper. Exceptions from the underlying geoip2 library are passed through unchanged.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>GeoDjango Utilities</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_1272"><i>django.contrib.gis.utils</i></a> module contains various utilities that are useful in creating geospatial web applications.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>LayerMapping data import utility</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_1274"><i>LayerMapping</i></a> class provides a way to map the contents of vector spatial data files (e.g. shapefiles) into GeoDjango models.</p> <p>This utility grew out of the author’s personal needs to eliminate the code repetition that went into pulling geometries and fields out of a vector layer, converting to another coordinate system (e.g. WGS84), and then inserting into a GeoDjango model.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: Use of <a href="index.html#page_1274"><i>LayerMapping</i></a> requires GDAL.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: GIS data sources, like shapefiles, may be very large. If you find that <a href="index.html#page_1274"><i>LayerMapping</i></a> is using</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">too much memory, set <a href="index.html#page_1907"><i>DEBUG</i></a> to False in your settings. When <a href="index.html#page_1907"><i>DEBUG</i></a> is set to True, Django <a href="index.html#page_913">automatically</a></p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><a href="index.html#page_913">logs</a> every SQL query – and when SQL statements contain geometries, this may consume more memory</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">than is typical.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Example</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. You need a GDAL-supported data source, like a shapefile (here we’re using a simple polygon shapefile,</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">test_poly.shp, with three features):</p> <p><span <span style="font-size:0.87em">DataSource</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ds</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p><span field.</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"poly"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"POLYGON"</span><span <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">LayerMapping(TestGeo,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"test_poly.shp"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, mapping)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">lm</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save(verbose</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Save the layermap, imports the data.</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Saved: Name: 1</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">Saved: Name: 2</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">Saved: Name: 3</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Here, <a href="index.html#page_1274"><i>LayerMapping</i></a> transformed the three geometries from the shapefile in their original spatial reference system (WGS84) to the spatial reference system of the GeoDjango model (NAD83). If no spatial reference</p> <p>system is defined for the layer, use the source_srs keyword with a <a href="index.html#page_1249"><i>SpatialReference</i></a> object to specify one.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1274"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>LayerMapping API</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class LayerMapping</b>(model, data_source, mapping, layer=0, source_srs=None, encoding=None,</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">transaction_mode='commit_on_success', transform=True, unique=True, using='default')</p> <p>The following are the arguments and keywords that may be used during instantiation of LayerMapping objects.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Ar- Description</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">gu-</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">ment</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">model The geographic model, not an instance.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">data_source The path to the OGR-supported data source file (e.g., a shapefile). Also accepts <a href="index.html#page_1232"><i>django.contrib.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><a href="index.html#page_1232"><i>gis.gdal.DataSource</i></a> instances.</p> <p style="text-align:center">mapping A dictionary: keys are strings corresponding to the model field, and values correspond to string</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">field names for the OGR feature, or if the model field is a geographic then it should correspond to the OGR geometry type, e.g., 'POINT', 'LINESTRING', 'POLYGON'.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Key-</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">word</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Argu-</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">ments</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">layer The index of the layer to use from the Data Source (defaults to 0)</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">source_srs Use this to specify the source SRS manually (for example, some shapefiles don’t come with</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">a '.prj' file). An integer SRID, WKT or PROJ strings, and <a href="index.html#page_1249"><i>django.contrib.gis.gdal.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_1249"><i>SpatialReference</i></a> objects are accepted.</p> <p style="text-align:center">encodingSpecifies the character set encoding of the strings in the OGR data source. For example,</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">'latin-1' , 'utf-8', and 'cp437' are all valid encoding parameters.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">transaction_mode May be 'commit_on_success' (default) or 'autocommit'.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">transform Setting this to False will disable coordinate transformations. In other words, geometries will be</p> <p style="text-align:center">inserted into the database unmodified from their original state in the data source.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">unique <span style="float:right">Setting this to the name, or a tuple of names, from the given model will create models unique only</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">to the given name(s). Geometries from each feature will be added into the collection associated with the unique model. Forces the transaction mode to be 'autocommit'.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">using Sets the database to use when importing spatial data. Default is 'default'.</p> <p id="page_1275" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>save() Keyword Arguments</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>LayerMapping.<b>save</b>(verbose=False, fid_range=False, step=False, progress=False, silent=False,</p> <p style="margin-left:8em">stream=sys.stdout, strict=False)</p> <p>The save() method also accepts keywords. These keywords are used for controlling output logging, error handling, and for importing specific feature ranges.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Save Description</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Key-</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">word</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Argu-</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">ments</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">fid_range May be set with a slice or tuple of (begin, end) feature ID’s to map from the data source. In</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">other words, this keyword enables the user to selectively import a subset range of features in the geographic data source.</p> <p style="text-align:center">progress When this keyword is set, status information will be printed giving the number of features</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">processed and successfully saved. By default, progress information will be printed every 1000 features processed, however, this default may be overridden by setting this keyword with an integer for the desired interval.</p> <p style="text-align:center">silent By default, non-fatal error notifications are printed to sys.stdout, but this keyword may be</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">set to disable these notifications.</p> <p style="text-align:center">step If set with an integer, transactions will occur at every step interval. For example, if step=1000,</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">a commit would occur after the 1,000th feature, the 2,000th feature etc.</p> <p style="text-align:center">stream Status information will be written to this file handle. Defaults to using sys.stdout, but any</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">object with a write method is supported.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">strict <span style="float:right">Execution of the model mapping will cease upon the first error encountered. The default value</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">(False) behavior is to attempt to continue.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">verbose If set, information will be printed subsequent to each model save executed on the database.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Troubleshooting</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Running out of memory</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>As noted in the warning at the top of this section, Django stores all SQL queries when DEBUG=True. Set DEBUG=False in your settings, and this should stop excessive memory use when running LayerMapping scripts.</p> <p id="page_1276"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>MySQL: max_allowed_packet error</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you encounter the following error when using LayerMapping and MySQL:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">OperationalError: (1153, "Got a packet bigger than 'max_allowed_packet' bytes")</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Then the solution is to increase the value of the max_allowed_packet setting in your MySQL configuration. For example, the default value may be something low like one megabyte – the setting may be modified in MySQL’s configuration file (my.cnf) in the [mysqld] section:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">max_allowed_packet</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">10M</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>OGR Inspection</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>ogrinspect</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>ogrinspect</b>(data_source, model_name, **kwargs)</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>mapping</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>mapping</b>(data_source, geom_name='geom', layer_key=0, multi_geom=False)</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>GeoJSON Serializer</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>GeoDjango provides a specific serializer for the <a href="https://geojson.org/">GeoJSON</a> format. See <a href="index.html#page_731">Serializing Django objects</a> for more information on serialization.</p> <p>The geojson serializer is not meant for round-tripping data, as it has no deserializer equivalent. For example,</p> <p>you cannot use <a href="index.html#page_1441"><i>loaddata</i></a> to reload the output produced by this serializer. If you plan to reload the outputted</p> <p>data, use the plain <a href="index.html#page_736">json serializer</a> instead.</p> <p>In addition to the options of the json serializer, the geojson serializer accepts the following additional option when it is called by serializers.serialize():</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• geometry_field: A string containing the name of a geometry field to use for the geometry key of the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">GeoJSON feature. This is only needed when you have a model with more than one geometry field and you don’t want to use the first defined geometry field (by default, the first geometry field is picked).</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• id_field: A string containing the name of a field to use for the id key of the GeoJSON feature. By</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">default, the primary key of objects is used.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• srid: The SRID to use for the geometry content. Defaults to 4326 (WGS 84).</p> <p id="page_1277" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_732">fields</a> option can be used to limit fields that will be present in the properties key, as it works with all other serializers.</p> <p>Example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.core.serializers</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">serialize</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">my_app.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">City</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">serialize(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"geojson"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, City</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">all(), geometry_field</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"point"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, fields</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">])</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Would output:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"type"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"FeatureCollection"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"crs"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"type"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"properties"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"EPSG:4326"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">}},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"features"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"type"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Feature"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"id"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"geometry"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"type"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Point"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"coordinates"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: [</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>-</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">87.650175</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">41.850385</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]},</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"properties"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Chicago"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When the fields parameter is not specified, the geojson serializer adds a pk key to the properties dictio-nary with the primary key of the object as the value.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>GeoDjango Management Commands</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>inspectdb</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>django-admin inspectdb</b></p> <p>When <a href="index.html#page_1130"><i>django.contrib.gis</i></a> is in your <a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a>, the <a href="index.html#page_1440"><i>inspectdb</i></a> management command is overridden with one from GeoDjango. The overridden command is spatially-aware, and places geometry fields in the auto-generated model definition, where appropriate.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1278"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>ogrinspect</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>django-admin ogrinspect data_source model_name</b></p> <p>The ogrinspect management command will inspect the given OGR-compatible <a href="index.html#page_1232"><i>DataSource</i></a> (e.g., a shape-file) and will output a GeoDjango model with the given model name. There’s a detailed example of using</p> <p>ogrinspect <a href="index.html#page_1140">in the tutorial</a>.</p> <p><b>--blank</b> BLANK</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Use a comma separated list of OGR field names to add the blank=True keyword option to the field definition. Set with true to apply to all applicable fields.</p> <p><b>--decimal</b> DECIMAL</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Use a comma separated list of OGR float fields to generate <a href="index.html#page_1630"><i>DecimalField</i></a> instead of the default</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1636"><i>FloatField</i></a> . Set to true to apply to all OGR float fields.</p> <p><b>--geom-name</b> GEOM_NAME</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Specifies the model attribute name to use for the geometry field. Defaults to 'geom'.</p> <p><b>--layer</b> LAYER_KEY</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The key for specifying which layer in the OGR <a href="index.html#page_1232"><i>DataSource</i></a> source to use. Defaults to 0 (the first layer).</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">May be an integer or a string identifier for the <a href="index.html#page_1233"><i>Layer</i></a>. When inspecting databases, layer is generally the table name you want to inspect.</p> <p><b>--mapping</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Automatically generate a mapping dictionary for use with <a href="index.html#page_1274"><i>LayerMapping</i>.</a></p> <p><b>--multi-geom</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">When generating the geometry field, treat it as a geometry collection. For example, if this setting is</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">enabled then a <a href="index.html#page_1162"><i>MultiPolygonField</i></a> will be placed in the generated model rather than <a href="index.html#page_1161"><i>PolygonField</i></a>.</p> <p><b>--name-field</b> NAME_FIELD</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Generates a __str__() method on the model that returns the given field name.</p> <p><b>--no-imports</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Suppresses the from django.contrib.gis.db import models import statement.</p> <p><b>--null</b> NULL</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Use a comma separated list of OGR field names to add the null=True keyword option to the field definition. Set with true to apply to all applicable fields.</p> <p><b>--srid</b> SRID</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The SRID to use for the geometry field. If not set, ogrinspect attempts to automatically determine of the SRID of the data source.</p> <p id="page_1279" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>GeoDjango’s admin site</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>GISModelAdmin</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class GISModelAdmin</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>gis_widget</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The widget class to be used for <a href="index.html#page_1161"><i>GeometryField</i></a>. Defaults to <a href="index.html#page_1176"><i>OSMWidget</i></a><a href="index.html#page_1176">.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>gis_widget_kwargs</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The keyword arguments that would be passed to the <a href="index.html#page_1279"><i>gis_widget</i></a>. Defaults to an empty dictio-nary.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Geographic Feeds</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>GeoDjango has its own <a href="index.html#page_1279"><i>Feed</i></a> subclass that may embed location information in RSS/Atom feeds formatted</p> <p>according to either the <a href="https://www.ogc.org/standard/georss/">Simple GeoRSS</a> or <a href="https://www.w3.org/2003/01/geo/">W3C Geo</a> standards. Because GeoDjango’s syndication API is a</p> <p>superset of Django’s, please consult <a href="index.html#page_1378">Django’s syndication documentation</a> for details on general usage.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Example</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>API Reference</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Feed Subclass</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class Feed</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">In addition to methods provided by the <a href="index.html#page_1385"><i>django.contrib.syndication.views.Feed</i></a> base class, GeoD-jango’s Feed class provides the following overrides. Note that these overrides may be done in multiple ways:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.gis.feeds</span> ...</b></span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">item_geometry</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>= ...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># And as a function with a single argument</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span get_object() and returns the feed’s geometry. Typically this is a GEOSGeometry instance, or can be a tuple to represent a point or a box. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ZipcodeFeed</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Feed):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>geometry</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, obj):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Can also return: `obj.poly`, and `obj.poly.centroid`.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">obj</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">poly</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">extent</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># tuple like: (X0, Y0, X1, Y1).</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>item_geometry</b>(item)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Set this to return the geometry for each item in the feed. This can be a GEOSGeometry instance, or a tuple that represents a point coordinate or bounding box. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ZipcodeFeed</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Feed):</span></p> style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">obj</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">poly</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>SyndicationFeed Subclasses</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The following <a
