W3CGeoFeed</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: <a href="https://www.w3.org/2003/01/geo/">W3C Geo</a> formatted feeds only support <a href="index.html#page_1161"><i>PointField</i></a> geometries.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1281" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Geographic Sitemaps</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>KML is an XML language focused on geographic <a href="index.html#page_1281">visualization<span style="font-size:0.67em">1</span></a> KMLSitemap . and its compressed counterpart KMZSitemap allow you to present geolocated data in a machine-readable format.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Example</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Reference</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>KMLSitemap</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>KMZSitemap</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Testing GeoDjango apps</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Included in this documentation are some additional notes and settings for <a href="index.html#page_1281">PostGIS</a> users.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>PostGIS</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Settings</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: The settings below have sensible defaults, and shouldn’t require manual setting.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>POSTGIS_VERSION</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When GeoDjango’s spatial backend initializes on PostGIS, it has to perform an SQL query to determine the version in order to figure out what features are available. Advanced users wishing to prevent this additional query may set the version manually using a 3-tuple of integers specifying the major, minor, and micro version numbers for PostGIS. For example, to configure for PostGIS X.Y.Z you would use:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">POSTGIS_VERSION</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(X, Y, Z)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><span style="font-size:0.6em">1</span> <span style="font-size:0.8em"><a href="https://www.ogc.org/standard/kml/">https://www.ogc.org/standard/kml/</a></span></p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1282"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Obtaining sufficient privileges</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Depending on your configuration, this section describes several methods to configure a database user with</p> <p>sufficient privileges to run tests for GeoDjango applications on PostgreSQL. If your <a href="index.html#page_1151">spatial database template</a> was created like in the instructions, then your testing database user only needs to have the ability to create databases. In other configurations, you may be required to use a database superuser.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Create database user</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To make a database user with the ability to create databases, use the following command:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">$ createuser --createdb -R -S <user_name></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The-R -S flags indicate that we do not want the user to have the ability to create additional users (roles) or to be a superuser, respectively.</p> <p>Alternatively, you may alter an existing user’s role from the SQL shell (assuming this is done from an existing superuser account):</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">postgres</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b># ALTER ROLE <</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>></b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">CREATEDB NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEROLE;</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Create database superuser</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This may be done at the time the user is created, for example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">$ createuser --superuser <user_name></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Or you may alter the user’s role from the SQL shell (assuming this is done from an existing superuser account):</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">postgres</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b># ALTER ROLE <</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">user_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>></b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">SUPERUSER;</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Windows</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>On Windows platforms you can use the pgAdmin III utility to add superuser privileges to your database user.</p> <p>By default, the PostGIS installer on Windows includes a template spatial database entitled template_postgis.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1283" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>GeoDjango tests</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To have the GeoDjango tests executed when <a href="index.html#page_2764">running the Django test suite</a> with runtests.py all of the</p> <p>databases in the settings file must be using one of the <a href="index.html#page_1165">spatial database backends.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Example</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The following is an example bare-bones settings file with spatial backends that can be used to run the entire</p> <p>Django test suite, including those in <a href="index.html#page_1130"><i>django.contrib.gis</i></a>:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">DATABASES</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"default"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"ENGINE"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.contrib.gis.db.backends.postgis"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"NAME"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"geodjango"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"USER"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"geodjango"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"other"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"ENGINE"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.contrib.gis.db.backends.postgis"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"NAME"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"other"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"USER"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"geodjango"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">SECRET_KEY</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django_tests_secret_key"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Assuming the settings above were in a postgis.py file in the same directory as runtests.py, then all Django and GeoDjango tests would be performed when executing the command:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">$ ./runtests.py --settings</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">postgis</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To run only the GeoDjango test suite, specify gis_tests:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">$ ./runtests.py --settings</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">postgis gis_tests</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Deploying GeoDjango</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Basically, the deployment of a GeoDjango application is not different from the deployment of a normal</p> <p>Django application. Please consult Django’s <a href="index.html#page_865">deployment documentation.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: GeoDjango uses the GDAL geospatial library which is not thread safe at this time. Thus,</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">it is highly recommended to not use threading when deploying – in other words, use an appropriate</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">configuration of Apache.</p> <p id="page_1284"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">For example, when configuring your application with mod_wsgi, set the WSGIDaemonProcess attribute</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">threads to 1, unless Apache may crash when running your GeoDjango application. Increase the number</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">of processes instead.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.5.6</b></span> <span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>django.contrib.humanize</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A set of Django template filters useful for adding a “human touch” to data.</p> <p>To activate these filters, add 'django.contrib.humanize' to your <a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a> setting. Once you’ve done that, use {% load humanize %} in a template, and you’ll have access to the following filters.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>apnumber</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>For numbers 1-9, returns the number spelled out. Otherwise, returns the number. This follows Associated Press style.</p> <p>Examples:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 1 becomes one.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 2 becomes two.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 10 becomes 10.</p> <p>You can pass in either an integer or a string representation of an integer.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>intcomma</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Converts an integer or float (or a string representation of either) to a string containing commas every three digits.</p> <p>Examples:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 4500 becomes 4,500.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 4500.2 becomes 4,500.2.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 45000 becomes 45,000.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 450000 becomes 450,000.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 4500000 becomes 4,500,000.</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_689">Format localization</a> will be respected if enabled, e.g. with the 'de' language:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 45000 becomes '45.000'.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 450000 becomes '450.000'.</p> <p id="page_1285" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>intword</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Converts a large integer (or a string representation of an integer) to a friendly text representation. Translates 1.0 as a singular phrase and all other numeric values as plural, this may be incorrect for some languages. Works best for numbers over 1 million.</p> <p>Examples:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 1000000 becomes 1.0 million.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 1200000 becomes 1.2 million.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 1200000000 becomes 1.2 billion.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">•-1200000000 becomes-1.2 billion.</p> <p>Values up to 10^100 (Googol) are supported.</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_689">Format localization</a> will be respected if enabled, e.g. with the 'de' language:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 1000000 becomes '1,0 Million'.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 1200000 becomes '1,2 Millionen'.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 1200000000 becomes '1,2 Milliarden'.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">•-1200000000 becomes '-1,2 Milliarden'.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>naturalday</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>For dates that are the current day or within one day, return “today”, “tomorrow” or “yesterday”, as appro-priate. Otherwise, format the date using the passed in format string.</p> <p>Argument: Date formatting string as described in the <a href="index.html#page_2006"><i>date</i></a> tag.</p> <p>Examples (when ‘today’ is 17 Feb 2007):</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 16 Feb 2007 becomes yesterday.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 17 Feb 2007 becomes today.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 18 Feb 2007 becomes tomorrow.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Any other day is formatted according to given argument or the <a href="index.html#page_1906"><i>DATE_FORMAT</i></a> setting if no argument is</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">given.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1286"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>naturaltime</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>For datetime values, returns a string representing how many seconds, minutes or hours ago it was – falling</p> <p>back to the <a href="index.html#page_2022"><i>timesince</i></a> format if the value is more than a day old. In case the datetime value is in the future the return value will automatically use an appropriate phrase.</p> <p>Examples (when ‘now’ is 17 Feb 2007 16:30:00):</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 17 Feb 2007 16:30:00 becomes now.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 17 Feb 2007 16:29:31 becomes 29 seconds ago.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 17 Feb 2007 16:29:00 becomes a minute ago.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 17 Feb 2007 16:25:35 becomes 4 minutes ago.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 17 Feb 2007 15:30:29 becomes 59 minutes ago.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 17 Feb 2007 15:30:01 becomes 59 minutes ago.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 17 Feb 2007 15:30:00 becomes an hour ago.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 17 Feb 2007 13:31:29 becomes 2 hours ago.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 16 Feb 2007 13:31:29 becomes 1 day, 2 hours ago.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 16 Feb 2007 13:30:01 becomes 1 day, 2 hours ago.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 16 Feb 2007 13:30:00 becomes 1 day, 3 hours ago.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 17 Feb 2007 16:30:30 becomes 30 seconds from now.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 17 Feb 2007 16:30:29 becomes 29 seconds from now.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 17 Feb 2007 16:31:00 becomes a minute from now.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 17 Feb 2007 16:34:35 becomes 4 minutes from now.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 17 Feb 2007 17:30:29 becomes an hour from now.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 17 Feb 2007 18:31:29 becomes 2 hours from now.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 18 Feb 2007 16:31:29 becomes 1 day from now.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 26 Feb 2007 18:31:29 becomes 1 week, 2 days from now.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>ordinal</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Converts an integer to its ordinal as a string.</p> <p>Examples:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 1 becomes 1st.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 2 becomes 2nd.</p> <p id="page_1287" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 3 becomes 3rd.</p> <p>You can pass in either an integer or a string representation of an integer. Negative integers are returned unchanged.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.5.7 The messages framework</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Quite commonly in web applications, you need to display a one-time notification message (also known as “flash message”) to the user after processing a form or some other types of user input.</p> <p>For this, Django provides full support for cookie- and session-based messaging, for both anonymous and authenticated users. The messages framework allows you to temporarily store messages in one request and retrieve them for display in a subsequent request (usually the next one). Every message is tagged with a specific level that determines its priority (e.g., info, warning, or error).</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Enabling messages</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Messages are implemented through a <a href="index.html#page_1591">middleware</a> class and corresponding <a href="index.html#page_2030">context processor</a><a href="index.html#page_2030">.</a></p> <p>The default settings.py created by django-admin startproject already contains all the settings required to enable message functionality:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• 'django.contrib.messages' is in <a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1923"><i>MIDDLEWARE</i></a> contains 'django.contrib.sessions.middleware.SessionMiddleware' and 'django.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">contrib.messages.middleware.MessageMiddleware'.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The default <a href="index.html#page_1287">storage backend</a> relies on <a href="index.html#page_311">sessions</a><a href="index.html#page_311">. </a>That’s why SessionMiddleware must be enabled and</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">appear before MessageMiddleware in <a href="index.html#page_1923"><i>MIDDLEWARE</i></a> .</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The 'context_processors' option of the DjangoTemplates backend defined in your <a href="index.html#page_1932"><i>TEMPLATES</i></a> set-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">ting contains 'django.contrib.messages.context_processors.messages'.</p> <p>If you don’t want to use messages, you can remove 'django.contrib.messages' from your</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a> , the MessageMiddleware line from <a href="index.html#page_1923"><i>MIDDLEWARE</i></a> , and the messages context processor from</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1932"><i>TEMPLATES</i></a> .</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Configuring the message engine</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Storage backends</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The messages framework can use different backends to store temporary messages.</p> <p>Django provides three built-in storage classes in <a href="index.html#page_1287"><i>django.contrib.messages</i></a>:</p> <p id="page_1288"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> storage.session.<b>SessionStorage</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This class stores all messages inside of the request’s session. Therefore it requires Django’s contrib. sessions application.</p> <p><b>class</b> storage.cookie.<b>CookieStorage</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This class stores the message data in a cookie (signed with a secret hash to prevent manipulation) to persist notifications across requests. Old messages are dropped if the cookie data size would exceed 2048 bytes.</p> <p><b>class</b> storage.fallback.<b>FallbackStorage</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This class first uses CookieStorage, and falls back to using SessionStorage for the messages that could not fit in a single cookie. It also requires Django’s contrib.sessions application.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This behavior avoids writing to the session whenever possible. It should provide the best performance in the general case.</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1288"><i>FallbackStorage</i></a> is the default storage class. If it isn’t suitable to your needs, you can select another storage</p> <p>class by setting <a href="index.html#page_1940"><i>MESSAGE_STORAGE</i></a> to its full import path, for example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">MESSAGE_STORAGE</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.contrib.messages.storage.cookie.CookieStorage"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> storage.base.<b>BaseStorage</b></p> <p>To write your own storage class, subclass the BaseStorage class in django.contrib.messages.storage. base and implement the _get and _store methods.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Message levels</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The messages framework is based on a configurable level architecture similar to that of the Python logging module. Message levels allow you to group messages by type so they can be filtered or displayed differently in views and templates.</p> <p>The built-in levels, which can be imported from django.contrib.messages directly, are:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Constant Purpose</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">DEBUG <span style="float:right">Development-related messages that will be ignored (or removed) in a production deployment</span></p> <p style="margin-left:1em">INFO Informational messages for the user</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">SUCCESS An action was successful, e.g. “Your profile was updated successfully”</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">WARNING A failure did not occur but may be imminent</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">ERROR An action was not successful or some other failure occurred</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_1940"><i>MESSAGE_LEVEL</i></a> setting can be used to change the minimum recorded level (or it can be <a href="index.html#page_1292">changed per</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1292">request</a>). Attempts to add messages of a level less than this will be ignored.</p> <p id="page_1289" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Message tags</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Message tags are a string representation of the message level plus any extra tags that were added directly in</p> <p>the view (see <a href="index.html#page_1293">Adding extra message tags</a> below for more details). Tags are stored in a string and are separated by spaces. Typically, message tags are used as CSS classes to customize message style based on message type. By default, each level has a single tag that’s a lowercase version of its own constant:</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:14em">Level Constant Tag</p> <p style="margin-left:14em">DEBUG debug</p> <p style="margin-left:14em">INFO info</p> <p style="margin-left:14em">SUCCESS success</p> <p style="margin-left:14em">WARNING warning</p> <p style="margin-left:14em">ERROR error</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To change the default tags for a message level (either built-in or custom), set the <a href="index.html#page_1941"><i>MESSAGE_TAGS</i></a> setting to a dictionary containing the levels you wish to change. As this extends the default tags, you only need to provide tags for the levels you wish to override:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.messages</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">constants</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>as</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">MESSAGE_TAGS</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">INFO:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">""</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">50</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"critical"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Using messages in views and templates</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>add_message</b>(request, level, message, extra_tags='', fail_silently=False)</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Adding a message</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To add a message, call:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">add_message(request, messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">INFO,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Hello world."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Some shortcut methods provide a standard way to add messages with commonly used tags (which are usually represented as HTML classes for the message):</p> <p id="page_1290"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">debug(request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"%s SQL statements were executed."</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">count)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">info(request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Three credits remain in your account."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">success(request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Profile details updated."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">warning(request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Your account expires in three days."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">error(request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Document deleted."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Displaying messages</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>get_messages</b>(request)</p> <p>In your template, use something like:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ul</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">class</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"messages"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">message</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">message.tags</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">class</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">message.tags</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endif</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">message</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endfor</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ul</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endif</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you’re using the context processor, your template should be rendered with a RequestContext. Otherwise, ensure messages is available to the template context.</p> <p>Even if you know there is only one message, you should still iterate over the messages sequence, because otherwise the message storage will not be cleared for the next request.</p> <p>The context processor also provides a DEFAULT_MESSAGE_LEVELS variable which is a mapping of the message level names to their numeric value:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ul</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">class</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"messages"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">message</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">message.tags</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">class</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">message.tags</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endif</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">message.level</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">DEFAULT_MESSAGE_LEVELS.ERROR</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Important:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endif</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">message</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">li</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endfor</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"></</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ul</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endif</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Outside of templates, you can use <a href="index.html#page_1290"><i>get_messages()</i>:</a></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.messages</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">get_messages</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_1291" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">storage</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">get_messages(request)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">message</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">storage:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">do_something_with_the_message(message)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>For instance, you can fetch all the messages to return them in a <a href="index.html#page_442">JSONResponseMixin</a> instead of a</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_979"><i>TemplateResponseMixin</i></a>.</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1290"><i>get_messages()</i></a> will return an instance of the configured storage backend.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>The Message class</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class Message</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">When you loop over the list of messages in a template, what you get are instances of the Message class. They have only a few attributes:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• message: The actual text of the message.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• level: An integer describing the type of the message (see the <a href="index.html#page_1288">message levels</a> section above).</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• tags: A string combining all the message’s tags (extra_tags and level_tag) separated by spaces.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• extra_tags: A string containing custom tags for this message, separated by spaces. It’s empty by</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">default.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• level_tag: The string representation of the level. By default, it’s the lowercase version of the</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">name of the associated constant, but this can be changed if you need by using the <a href="index.html#page_1941"><i>MESSAGE_TAGS</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Creating custom message levels</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Messages levels are nothing more than integers, so you can define your own level constants and use them to create more customized user feedback, e.g.:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">CRITICAL</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">50</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">add_message(request, CRITICAL,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"A serious error occurred."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When creating custom message levels you should be careful to avoid overloading existing levels. The values for the built-in levels are:</p> <p id="page_1292"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:14em">Level Constant Value</p> <p style="margin-left:14em">DEBUG 10</p> <p style="margin-left:14em">INFO 20</p> <p style="margin-left:14em">SUCCESS 25</p> <p style="margin-left:14em">WARNING 30</p> <p style="margin-left:14em">ERROR 40</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you need to identify the custom levels in your HTML or CSS, you need to provide a mapping via the</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1941"><i>MESSAGE_TAGS</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: If you are creating a reusable application, it is recommended to use only the built-in <a href="index.html#page_1288">message levels</a> and not rely on any custom levels.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Changing the minimum recorded level per-request</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The minimum recorded level can be set per request via the set_level method:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Change the messages level to ensure the debug message is added.</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">set_level(request, messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">DEBUG)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">debug(request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Test message..."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># In another request, record only messages with a level of WARNING and higher</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">set_level(request, messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">WARNING)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">success(request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Your profile was updated."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ignored</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">warning(request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Your account is about to expire."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># recorded</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Set the messages level back to default.</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">set_level(request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>None</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Similarly, the current effective level can be retrieved with get_level:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">current_level</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_level(request)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>For more information on how the minimum recorded level functions, see <a href="index.html#page_1288">Message levels</a> above.</p> <p id="page_1293" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Adding extra message tags</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>For more direct control over message tags, you can optionally provide a string containing extra tags to any of the add methods:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">add_message(request, messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">INFO,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Over 9000!"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, extra_tags</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"dragonball"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">error(request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Email box full"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, extra_tags</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"email"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Extra tags are added before the default tag for that level and are space separated.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Failing silently when the message framework is disabled</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you’re writing a reusable app (or other piece of code) and want to include messaging functionality, but don’t want to require your users to enable it if they don’t want to, you may pass an additional keyword argument fail_silently=True to any of the add_message family of methods. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">add_message(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">request,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">SUCCESS,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Profile details updated."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">fail_silently</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">info(request,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Hello world."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, fail_silently</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=True</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: Setting fail_silently=True only hides the MessageFailure that would otherwise occur when the messages framework disabled and one attempts to use one of the add_message family of methods. It does not hide failures that may occur for other reasons.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Adding messages in class-based views</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> views.<b>SuccessMessageMixin</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Adds a success message attribute to <a href="index.html#page_959"><i>FormView</i></a> based classes</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_success_message</b>(cleaned_data)</p> <p style="text-align:center">cleaned_data is the cleaned data from the form which is used for string formatting</p> <p>Example views.py:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.messages.views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">SuccessMessageMixin</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.views.generic.edit</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">CreateView</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_1294"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AuthorCreateView</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(SuccessMessageMixin, CreateView):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">model</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">success_url</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"/success/"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">success_message</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"%(name)s was created successfully"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The cleaned data from the form is available for string interpolation using the %(field_name)s syntax.</p> <p>For ModelForms, if you need access to fields from the saved object override the <a href="index.html#page_1293"><i>get_success_message()</i></a> method.</p> <p>Example views.py for ModelForms:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">CreateView</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myapp.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ComplicatedModel</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ComplicatedCreateView</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(SuccessMessageMixin, CreateView):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">model</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ComplicatedModel</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">success_message</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"%(calculated_field)s was created successfully"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get_success_message</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, cleaned_data):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">success_message</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">dict</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">cleaned_data,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">calculated_field</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">object</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">calculated_field,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Expiration of messages</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The messages are marked to be cleared when the storage instance is iterated (and cleared when the response is processed).</p> <p>To avoid the messages being cleared, you can set the messages storage to False after iterating:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">storage</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">messages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_messages(request)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>for</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">message</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>in</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">storage:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">do_something_with(message)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">storage</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">used</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>= False</b></span></p> <p id="page_1295" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Behavior of parallel requests</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Due to the way cookies (and hence sessions) work, the behavior of any backends that make use of cookies or sessions is undefined when the same client makes multiple requests that set or get messages in parallel. For example, if a client initiates a request that creates a message in one window (or tab) and then another that fetches any uniterated messages in another window, before the first window redirects, the message may appear in the second window instead of the first window where it may be expected.</p> <p>In short, when multiple simultaneous requests from the same client are involved, messages are not guaranteed to be delivered to the same window that created them nor, in some cases, at all. Note that this is typically not a problem in most applications and will become a non-issue in HTML5, where each window/tab will have its own browsing context.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Settings</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A few <a href="index.html#page_1940">settings</a> give you control over message behavior:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1940"><i>MESSAGE_LEVEL</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1940"><i>MESSAGE_STORAGE</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1941"><i>MESSAGE_TAGS</i></a></p> <p>For backends that use cookies, the settings for the cookie are taken from the session cookie settings:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1942"><i>SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1944"><i>SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1942"><i>SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY</i></a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Testing</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This module offers a tailored test assertion method, for testing messages attached to an <a href="index.html#page_1871"><i>HttpResponse</i>.</a></p> <p>To benefit from this assertion, add MessagesTestMixin to the class hierarchy:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.messages.test</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">MessagesTestMixin</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.test</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">TestCase</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MsgTestCase</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(MessagesTestMixin, TestCase):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>pass</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Then, inherit from the MsgTestCase in your tests.</p> <p id="page_1296"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>MessagesTestMixin.<b>assertMessages</b>(response, expected_messages, ordered=True)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Asserts that <a href="index.html#page_1287"><i>messages</i></a> added to the <a href="index.html#page_1871"><i>response</i></a> matches expected_messages.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">expected_messages is a list of <a href="index.html#page_1291"><i>Message</i></a> objects.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">By default, the comparison is ordering dependent. You can disable this by setting the ordered argu-ment to False.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.5.8</b></span> <span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>django.contrib.postgres</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>PostgreSQL has a number of features which are not shared by the other databases Django supports. This optional module contains model fields and form fields for a number of PostgreSQL specific data types.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: Django is, and will continue to be, a database-agnostic web framework. We would encourage those writing reusable applications for the Django community to write database-agnostic code where practical. However, we recognize that real world projects written using Django need not be database-agnostic. In fact, once a project reaches a given size changing the underlying data store is already a significant challenge and is likely to require changing the code base in some ways to handle differences between the data stores.</p> <p>Django provides support for a number of data types which will only work with PostgreSQL. There is no fundamental reason why (for example) a contrib.mysql module does not exist, except that PostgreSQL has the richest feature set of the supported databases so its users have the most to gain.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>PostgreSQL specific aggregation functions</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>These functions are available from the django.contrib.postgres.aggregates module. They are described</p> <p>in more detail in the <a href="https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-aggregate.html">PostgreSQL docs</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: All functions come without default aliases, so you must explicitly provide one. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">SomeModel</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">aggregate(arr</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ArrayAgg(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"somefield"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">))</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">{'arr': [0, 1, 2]}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Common aggregate options</p> <p>All aggregates have the <a href="index.html#page_1776">filter</a> keyword argument and most also have the <a href="index.html#page_1776">default</a> keyword argument.</p> <p id="page_1297" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>General-purpose aggregation functions</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>ArrayAgg</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class ArrayAgg</b>(expression, distinct=False, filter=None, default=None, ordering=(), **extra)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns a list of values, including nulls, concatenated into an array, or default if there are no values.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>distinct</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">An optional boolean argument that determines if array values will be distinct. style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Aggregate functions for statistics</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>y and x</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The arguments y and x for all these functions can be the name of a field or an expression returning a numeric data. Both are required.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Corr</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class Corr</b>(y, x, filter=None, default=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns the correlation coefficient as a float, or default if there aren’t any matching rows.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>CovarPop</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class CovarPop</b>(y, x, sample=False, filter=None, default=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns the population covariance as a float, or default if there aren’t any matching rows.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>sample</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional. By default CovarPop returns the general population covariance. However, if sample=True , the return value will be the sample population covariance.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>RegrAvgX</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class RegrAvgX</b>(y, x, filter=None, default=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns the average of the independent variable (sum(x)/N) as a float, or default if there aren’t any matching rows.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>RegrAvgY</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class RegrAvgY</b>(y, x, filter=None, default=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns the average of the dependent variable (sum(y)/N) as a float, or default if there aren’t any matching rows.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1302"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>RegrCount</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class RegrCount</b>(y, x, filter=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns an int of the number of input rows in which both expressions are not null.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Note: The default argument is not supported.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>RegrIntercept</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class RegrIntercept</b>(y, x, filter=None, default=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns the y-intercept of the least-squares-fit linear equation determined by the (x, y) pairs as a float , or default if there aren’t any matching rows.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>RegrR2</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class RegrR2</b>(y, x, filter=None, default=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns the square of the correlation coefficient as a float, or default if there aren’t any matching rows.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>RegrSlope</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class RegrSlope</b>(y, x, filter=None, default=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns the slope of the least-squares-fit linear equation determined by the (x, y) pairs as a float, or default if there aren’t any matching rows.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>RegrSXX</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class RegrSXX</b>(y, x, filter=None, default=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns sum(x^2) - sum(x)^2/N (“sum of squares” of the independent variable) as a float, or default if there aren’t any matching rows.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1303" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>RegrSXY</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class RegrSXY</b>(y, x, filter=None, default=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns sum(x*y) - sum(x) * sum(y)/N (“sum of products” of independent times dependent vari-able) as a float, or default if there aren’t any matching rows.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>RegrSYY</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class RegrSYY</b>(y, x, filter=None, default=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns sum(y^2) - sum(y)^2/N (“sum of squares” of the dependent variable) as a float, or default if there aren’t any matching rows.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Usage examples</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>We will use this example table:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">bar |</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">2 | (null) |</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">|</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">test |</span> <span <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">TestModel</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span statistical aggregate functions. The underlying math will be not de-</p> <p>scribed (you can read about this, for example, at <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regression_analysis">wikipedia</a>):</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">TestModel</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">aggregate(</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">avgx</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">RegrAvgX(y</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"field3"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, x</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"field2"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">), avgy</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">RegrAvgY(y</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"field3"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, x</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"field2"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">{'avgx': 2, 'avgy': 13}</span></p> <p id="page_1304"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>PostgreSQL specific database constraints</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>PostgreSQL supports additional data integrity constraints available from the django.contrib.postgres.</p> <p>constraints module. They are added in the model <a href="index.html#page_1687"><i>Meta.constraints</i></a> option.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>ExclusionConstraint</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class ExclusionConstraint</b>(*, name, expressions, index_type=None, condition=None, deferrable=None,</p> <p style="margin-left:11em">include=None, violation_error_code=None,</p> <p style="margin-left:11em">violation_error_message=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Creates an exclusion constraint in the database. Internally, PostgreSQL implements exclusion con-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">straints using indexes. The default index type is <a href="https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/gist.html">GiST</a>. To use them, you need to activate the <a href="https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/btree-gist.html">btree_gist</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/btree-gist.html">extension</a> on PostgreSQL. You can install it using the <a href="index.html#page_1336"><i>BtreeGistExtension</i></a> migration operation.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you attempt to insert a new row that conflicts with an existing row, an <a href="index.html#page_1474"><i>IntegrityError</i></a> is raised. Similarly, when update conflicts with an existing row.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Exclusion constraints are checked during the <a href="index.html#page_1692">model validation</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>name</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ExclusionConstraint.<b>name</b></p> <p>See <a href="index.html#page_1666"><i>BaseConstraint.name</i>.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>expressions</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ExclusionConstraint.<b>expressions</b></p> <p>An iterable of 2-tuples. The first element is an expression or string. The second element is an SQL operator</p> <p>represented as a string. To avoid typos, you may use <a href="index.html#page_1324"><i>RangeOperators</i></a> which maps the operators with strings. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">expressions</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"timespan"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, RangeOperators</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ADJACENT_TO),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(F(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"room"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">), RangeOperators</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">EQUAL),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Restrictions on operators.</p> <p>Only commutative operators can be used in exclusion constraints.</p> <p id="page_1305" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_1332"><i>OpClass()</i></a> expression can be used to specify a custom <a href="https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-opclass.html">operator class</a> for the constraint expressions. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">expressions</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(OpClass(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"circle"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"circle_ops"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">), RangeOperators</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">OVERLAPS),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>creates an exclusion constraint on circle using circle_ops.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>index_type</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ExclusionConstraint.<b>index_type</b></p> <p>The index type of the constraint. Accepted values are GIST or SPGIST. Matching is case insensitive. If not provided, the default index type is GIST.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>condition</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ExclusionConstraint.<b>condition</b></p> <p>A <a href="index.html#page_1779"><i>Q</i></a> object that specifies the condition to restrict a constraint to a subset of rows. For example, condition=Q(cancelled=False).</p> <p>These conditions have the same database restrictions as <a href="index.html#page_1663"><i>django.db.models.Index.condition</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>deferrable</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ExclusionConstraint.<b>deferrable</b></p> <p>Set this parameter to create a deferrable exclusion constraint. Accepted values are Deferrable.DEFERRED or Deferrable.IMMEDIATE. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.postgres.constraints</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ExclusionConstraint</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.postgres.fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">RangeOperators</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Deferrable</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">ExclusionConstraint(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"exclude_overlapping_deferred"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">expressions</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"timespan"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, RangeOperators</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">OVERLAPS),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">deferrable</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Deferrable</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">DEFERRED,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p id="page_1306"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>By default constraints are not deferred. A deferred constraint will not be enforced until the end of the trans-action. An immediate constraint will be enforced immediately after every command.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: Deferred exclusion constraints may lead to a <a href="https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createtable.html#id-1.9.3.85.9.4">performance penalty.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>include</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ExclusionConstraint.<b>include</b></p> <p>A list or tuple of the names of the fields to be included in the covering exclusion constraint as non-key columns.</p> <p>This allows index-only scans to be used for queries that select only included fields <a href="index.html#page_1306">(<i>include</i>) </a>and filter only</p> <p>by indexed fields (<a href="index.html#page_1304"><i>expressions</i></a>).</p> <p>include is supported for GiST indexes. PostgreSQL 14+ also supports include for SP-GiST indexes.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>violation_error_code</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>ExclusionConstraint.<b>violation_error_code</b></p> <p>The error code used when ValidationError is raised during <a href="index.html#page_1692">model validation. </a>Defaults to None.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>violation_error_message</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The error message used when ValidationError is raised during <a href="index.html#page_1692">model validation</a>. <span style="float:right">Defaults to</span></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1666"><i>BaseConstraint.violation_error_message</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>These expressions are available from the django.contrib.postgres.expressions module.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>ArraySubquery() expressions</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class ArraySubquery</b>(queryset)</p> <p>ArraySubquery is a <a href="index.html#page_1796"><i>Subquery</i></a> that uses the PostgreSQL ARRAY constructor to build a list of values from the</p> <p>queryset, which must use <a href="index.html#page_1716"><i>QuerySet.values()</i></a> to return only a single column.</p> <p>This class differs from <a href="index.html#page_1297"><i>ArrayAgg</i></a> in the way that it does not act as an aggregate function and does not require an SQL GROUP BY clause to build the list of values.</p> <p>For example, if you want to annotate all related books to an author as JSON objects:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">OuterRef</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db.models.functions</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">JSONObject</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.postgres.expressions</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ArraySubquery</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">books</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Book</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(author</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">OuterRef(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"pk"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">))</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">values(</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">json</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">JSONObject(title</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"title"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, pages</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"pages"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">author</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Author</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">annotate(books</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ArraySubquery(books))</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">first()</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">author</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">books</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">[{'title': 'Solaris', 'pages': 204}, {'title': 'The Cyberiad', 'pages': 295}]</span></p> <p id="page_1309" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>PostgreSQL specific model fields</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>All of these fields are available from the django.contrib.postgres.fields module.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Indexing these fields</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1661"><i>Index</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1623"><i>Field.db_index</i></a> both create a B-tree index, which isn’t particularly helpful when querying com-</p> <p>plex data types. Indexes such as <a href="index.html#page_1331"><i>GinIndex</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1331"><i>GistIndex</i></a> are better suited, though the index choice is</p> <p>dependent on the queries that you’re using. Generally, GiST may be a good choice for the <a href="index.html#page_1318">range fields</a> and</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1314"><i>HStoreField</i></a> , and GIN may be helpful for <a href="index.html#page_1309"><i>ArrayField</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>ArrayField</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class ArrayField</b>( base_field, size=None, **options)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A field for storing lists of data. Most field types can be used, and you pass another field instance as</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">the <a href="index.html#page_1309"><i>base_field</i></a>. You may also specify a <a href="index.html#page_1310"><i>size</i></a>. ArrayField can be nested to store multi-dimensional arrays.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you give the field a <a href="index.html#page_1623"><i>default</i></a>, ensure it’s a callable such as list (for an empty default) or a callable that returns a list (such as a function). Incorrectly using default=[] creates a mutable default that is shared between all instances of ArrayField.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>base_field</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">This is a required argument.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Specifies the underlying data type and behavior for the array. It should be an instance of a sub-</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">class of <a href="index.html#page_1656"><i>Field</i></a>. For example, it could be an <a href="index.html#page_1639"><i>IntegerField</i></a> or a <a href="index.html#page_1628"><i>CharField</i></a>. Most field types are</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">permitted, with the exception of those handling relational data (<a href="index.html#page_1643"><i>ForeignKey</i></a>, <a href="index.html#page_1652"><i>OneToOneField</i></a> and</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_1649"><i>ManyToManyField</i></a>) and file fields ( <a href="index.html#page_1631"><i>FileField</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1638"><i>ImageField</i></a>).</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">It is possible to nest array fields - you can specify an instance of ArrayField as the base_field. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.postgres.fields</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">ArrayField</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Post</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span
