<p><b>Weighting queries</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Every field may not have the same relevance in a query, so you can set weights of various vectors before you combine them:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.postgres.search</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">SearchQuery, SearchRank, SearchVector</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">vector</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">SearchVector(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"body_text"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, weight</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"A"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>+</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">SearchVector(</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"blog__tagline"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, weight</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"B"</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">query</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">SearchQuery(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"cheese"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Entry</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">annotate(rank</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">SearchRank(vector, query))</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(rank__gte</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">0.3</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">order_by(</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"rank"</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The weight should be one of the following letters: D, C, B, A. By default, these weights refer to the numbers 0.1, 0.2, 0.4, and 1.0, respectively. If you wish to weight them differently, pass a list of four floats to</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1341"><i>SearchRank</i></a> as weights in the same order above:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">rank</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">SearchRank(vector, query, weights</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">0.2</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">0.4</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">0.6</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">0.8</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">])</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Entry</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">annotate(rank</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">rank)</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(rank__gte</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">0.3</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">order_by(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"-rank"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Performance</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Special database configuration isn’t necessary to use any of these functions, however, if you’re searching more than a few hundred records, you’re likely to run into performance problems. Full text search is a more intensive process than comparing the size of an integer, for example.</p> <p>In the event that all the fields you’re querying on are contained within one particular model, you can create</p> <p>a functional <a href="index.html#page_1331"><i>GIN</i></a> or <a href="index.html#page_1331"><i>GiST</i></a> index which matches the search vector you wish to use. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">GinIndex(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">SearchVector(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"body_text"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"headline"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, config</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"english"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"search_vector_idx"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The PostgreSQL documentation has details on <a href="https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/textsearch-tables.html#TEXTSEARCH-TABLES-INDEX">creating indexes for full text search.</a></p> <p id="page_1344"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>SearchVectorField</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class SearchVectorField</b></p> <p>If this approach becomes too slow, you can add a SearchVectorField to your model. You’ll need to keep it</p> <p>populated with triggers, for example, as described in the <a href="https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/textsearch-features.html#TEXTSEARCH-UPDATE-TRIGGERS">PostgreSQL documentation. </a>You can then query the field as if it were an annotated SearchVector:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Entry</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">update(search_vector</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">SearchVector(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"body_text"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">))</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Entry</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(search_vector</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"cheese"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">[<Entry: Cheese on Toast recipes>, <Entry: Pizza recipes>]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Trigram similarity</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Another approach to searching is trigram similarity. A trigram is a group of three consecutive characters.</p> <p>In addition to the <a href="index.html#page_1333"><i>trigram_similar</i></a>, <a href="index.html#page_1333"><i>trigram_word_similar</i></a>, and <a href="index.html#page_1334"><i>trigram_strict_word_similar</i></a> lookups, you can use a couple of other expressions.</p> <p>To use them, you need to activate the <a href="https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/pgtrgm.html">pg_trgm extension</a> on PostgreSQL. You can install it using the</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1336"><i>TrigramExtension</i></a> migration operation.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>TrigramSimilarity</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class TrigramSimilarity</b>(expression, string, **extra)</p> <p>Accepts a field name or expression, and a string or expression. TrigramStrictWordDistance</b>(string, expression, **extra)</p> <p>Accepts a string or expression, and a field name or expression. Returns the trigram strict word distance between the two arguments.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Validators</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>These validators are available from the django.contrib.postgres.validators module.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1347" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>KeysValidator</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class KeysValidator</b>(keys, strict=False, messages=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Validates that the given keys are contained in the value. If strict is True, then it also checks that there are no other keys present.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The messages passed should be a dict containing the keys missing_keys and/or extra_keys.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Note: Note that this checks only for the existence of a given key, not that the value of a key is non-empty.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Range validators</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>RangeMaxValueValidator</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class RangeMaxValueValidator</b>(limit_value, message=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Validates that the upper bound of the range is not greater than limit_value.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>RangeMinValueValidator</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class RangeMinValueValidator</b>(limit_value, message=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Validates that the lower bound of the range is not less than the limit_value.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.5.9 The redirects app</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django comes with an optional redirects application. It lets you store redirects in a database and handles the redirecting for you. It uses the HTTP response status code 301 Moved Permanently by default.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Installation</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To install the redirects app, follow these steps:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. Ensure that the django.contrib.sites framework <a href="index.html#page_1365">is installed.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. Add 'django.contrib.redirects' to your <a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">3. Add 'django.contrib.redirects.middleware.RedirectFallbackMiddleware' to your <a href="index.html#page_1923"><i>MIDDLEWARE</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">setting.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">4. Run the command <a href="index.html#page_1446"><i>manage.py migrate</i></a>.</p> <p id="page_1348"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>How it works</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>manage.py migrate creates a django_redirect table in your database. This is a lookup table with site_id, old_path and new_path fields.</p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_1349"><i>RedirectFallbackMiddleware</i></a> does all of the work. Each time any Django application raises a 404 error, this middleware checks the redirects database for the requested URL as a last resort. Specifically, it checks</p> <p>for a redirect with the given old_path with a site ID that corresponds to the <a href="index.html#page_1945"><i>SITE_ID</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• If it finds a match, and new_path is not empty, it redirects to new_path using a 301 (“Moved Perma-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">nently”) redirect. You can subclass <a href="index.html#page_1349"><i>RedirectFallbackMiddleware</i></a> and set <a href="index.html#page_1349"><i>response_redirect_class</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">to <a href="index.html#page_1877"><i>django.http.HttpResponseRedirect</i></a> to use a 302 Moved Temporarily redirect instead.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• If it finds a match, and new_path is empty, it sends a 410 (“Gone”) HTTP header and empty (content-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">less) response.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• If it doesn’t find a match, the request continues to be processed as usual.</p> <p>The middleware only gets activated for 404s – not for 500s or responses of any other status code.</p> <p>Note that the order of <a href="index.html#page_1923"><i>MIDDLEWARE</i></a> matters. Generally, you can put <a href="index.html#page_1349"><i>RedirectFallbackMiddleware</i></a> at the end of the list, because it’s a last resort.</p> <p>For more on middleware, read the <a href="index.html#page_303">middleware docs.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>How to add, change and delete redirects</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Via the admin interface</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you’ve activated the automatic Django admin interface, you should see a “Redirects” section on the admin index page. Edit redirects as you edit any other object in the system.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Via the Python API</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> models.<b>Redirect</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Redirects are represented by a standard <a href="index.html#page_115">Django model,</a> which lives in</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/contrib/redirects/models.py">django/contrib/redirects/models.py. </a>You can access redirect objects via the <a href="index.html#page_143">Django database API</a>. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.conf</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">settings</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.redirects.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Redirect</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Add a new redirect.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">redirect</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Redirect</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">create(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">site_id</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">old_path</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/contact-us/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_1349" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">new_path</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/contact/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Change a redirect.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">redirect</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">new_path</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"/contact-details/"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">redirect</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">save()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">redirect</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><Redirect: /contact-us/ ---> /contact-details/></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Delete a redirect.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Redirect</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(site_id</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, old_path</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/contact-us/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">delete()</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(1, {'redirects.Redirect': 1})</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Middleware</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> middleware.<b>RedirectFallbackMiddleware</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">You can change the <a href="index.html#page_1871"><i>HttpResponse</i></a> classes used by the middleware by creating a sub-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">class of <a href="index.html#page_1349"><i>RedirectFallbackMiddleware</i></a> and overriding response_gone_class and/or response_redirect_class .</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>response_gone_class</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The <a href="index.html#page_1871"><i>HttpResponse</i></a> class used when a <a href="index.html#page_1348"><i>Redirect</i></a> is not found for the requested path or has a blank new_path value.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Defaults to <a href="index.html#page_1877"><i>HttpResponseGone</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>response_redirect_class</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The <a href="index.html#page_1871"><i>HttpResponse</i></a> class that handles the redirect.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Defaults to <a href="index.html#page_1877"><i>HttpResponsePermanentRedirect</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.5.10 The sitemap framework</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django comes with a high-level sitemap-generating framework to create <a href="https://www.sitemaps.org/">sitemap</a> XML files.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Overview</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A sitemap is an XML file on your website that tells search-engine indexers how frequently your pages change and how “important” certain pages are in relation to other pages on your site. This information helps search engines index your site.</p> <p>The Django sitemap framework automates the creation of this XML file by letting you express this informa-tion in Python code.</p> <p>It works much like Django’s <a href="index.html#page_1378">syndication framework</a>. To create a sitemap, write a <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>Sitemap</i></a> class and point to</p> <p>it in your <a href="index.html#page_266">URLconf.</a></p> <p id="page_1350"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Installation</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To install the sitemap app, follow these steps:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. Add 'django.contrib.sitemaps' to your <a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. Make sure your <a href="index.html#page_1932"><i>TEMPLATES</i></a> setting contains a DjangoTemplates backend whose APP_DIRS options is</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">set to True. It’s in there by default, so you’ll only need to change this if you’ve changed that setting.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">3. Make sure you’ve installed the <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>sites framework</i></a>.</p> <p>(Note: The sitemap application doesn’t install any database tables. The only reason it needs to go into</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a> is so that the <a href="index.html#page_2047"><i>Loader()</i></a> template loader can find the default templates.)</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Initialization</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>views.<b>sitemap</b>(request, sitemaps, section=None, template_name='sitemap.xml',</p> <p style="margin-left:6em">content_type='application/xml')</p> <p>To activate sitemap generation on your Django site, add this line to your <a href="index.html#page_266">URLconf:</a></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.sitemaps.views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">sitemap</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"sitemap.xml"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">sitemap,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"sitemaps"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: sitemaps},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.contrib.sitemaps.views.sitemap"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This tells Django to build a sitemap when a client accesses /sitemap.xml.</p> <p>The name of the sitemap file is not important, but the location is. Search engines will only index links in your sitemap for the current URL level and below. For instance, if sitemap.xml lives in your root directory, it may reference any URL in your site. However, if your sitemap lives at /content/sitemap.xml, it may only reference URLs that begin with /content/.</p> <p>The sitemap view takes an extra, required argument: {'sitemaps': sitemaps}. sitemaps should be a</p> <p>dictionary that maps a short section label (e.g., blog or news) to its <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>Sitemap</i></a> class (e.g., BlogSitemap or</p> <p>NewsSitemap). It may also map to an instance of a <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>Sitemap</i></a> class (e.g., BlogSitemap(some_var)).</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1351" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Sitemap classes</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>Sitemap</i></a> class is a Python class that represents a “section” of entries in your sitemap. For example, one</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>Sitemap</i></a> class could represent all the entries of your blog, while another could represent all of the events in your events calendar.</p> <p>In the simplest case, all these sections get lumped together into one sitemap.xml, but it’s also possible to use the framework to generate a sitemap index that references individual sitemap files, one per section. (See</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1356">Creating a sitemap index</a> below.)</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>Sitemap</i></a> classes must subclass django.contrib.sitemaps.Sitemap. They can live anywhere in your code-base.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>An example</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Let’s assume you have a blog system, with an Entry model, and you want your sitemap to include all the links to your individual blog entries. Here’s how your sitemap class might look:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.sitemaps</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Sitemap</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">blog.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Entry</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>BlogSitemap</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Sitemap):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">changefreq</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"never"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">priority</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">0.5</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>items</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Entry</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(is_draft</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=False</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>lastmod</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, obj):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">obj</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">pub_date</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1353"><i>changefreq</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1353"><i>priority</i></a> are class attributes corresponding to <changefreq> and <priority> ele-</p> <p style="text-align:center">ments, respectively. They can be made callable as functions, as <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>lastmod</i></a> was in the example.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>items()</i></a> is a method that returns a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-sequence">sequence</a> or QuerySet of objects. The objects returned will get</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">passed to any callable methods corresponding to a sitemap property (<a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>location</i>, <i>lastmod</i></a>, <a href="index.html#page_1353"><i>changefreq</i></a>,</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">and <a href="index.html#page_1353"><i>priority</i>).</a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>lastmod</i></a> should return a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime">datetime</a>.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• There is no <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>location</i></a> method in this example, but you can provide it in order to specify the URL for</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">your object. By default, <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>location()</i></a> calls get_absolute_url() on each object and returns the result.</p> <p id="page_1352"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Sitemap class reference</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class Sitemap</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A Sitemap class can define the following methods/attributes:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>items</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Required. A method that returns a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-sequence">sequence</a> or QuerySet of objects. The framework doesn’t care</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">what type of objects they are; all that matters is that these objects get passed to the <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>location()</i></a>,</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>lastmod()</i>,</a> <a href="index.html#page_1353"><i>changefreq()</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1353"><i>priority()</i></a> methods.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>location</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional. Either a method or attribute.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If it’s a method, it should return the absolute path for a given object as returned by <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>items()</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If it’s an attribute, its value should be a string representing an absolute path to use for every object</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">returned by <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>items()</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">In both cases, “absolute path” means a URL that doesn’t include the protocol or domain. Exam-ples:</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• Good: '/foo/bar/'</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• Bad: 'example.com/foo/bar/'</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• Bad: 'https://example.com/foo/bar/'</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>location</i></a> isn’t provided, the framework will call the get_absolute_url() method on each</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">object as returned by <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>items()</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">To specify a protocol other than 'http', use <a href="index.html#page_1353"><i>protocol</i>.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>lastmod</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional. Either a method or attribute.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If it’s a method, it should take one argument – an object as returned by <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>items()</i></a> – and return that</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">object’s last-modified date/time as a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime">datetime</a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If it’s an attribute, its value should be a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime">datetime</a> representing the last-modified date/time for</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">every object returned by <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>items()</i>.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If all items in a sitemap have a <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>lastmod</i></a>, the sitemap generated by <a href="index.html#page_1350"><i>views.sitemap()</i></a> will have a Last-Modified header equal to the latest lastmod. <span style="float:right">You can activate the</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_1593"><i>ConditionalGetMiddleware</i></a> to make Django respond appropriately to requests with an If-Modified-Since header which will prevent sending the sitemap if it hasn’t changed.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>paginator</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">This property returns a <a href="index.html#page_1855"><i>Paginator</i></a> for <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>items()</i></a><a href="index.html#page_1352">. </a>If you generate sitemaps in a batch you may want to override this as a cached property in order to avoid multiple items() calls.</p> <p id="page_1353" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>changefreq</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional. Either a method or attribute.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If it’s a method, it should take one argument – an object as returned by <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>items()</i></a> – and return that object’s change frequency as a string.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If it’s an attribute, its value should be a string representing the change frequency of every object</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">returned by <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>items()</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Possible values for <a href="index.html#page_1353"><i>changefreq</i>, </a>whether you use a method or attribute, are:</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• 'always'</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• 'hourly'</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• 'daily'</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• 'weekly'</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• 'monthly'</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• 'yearly'</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• 'never'</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>priority</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional. Either a method or attribute.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If it’s a method, it should take one argument – an object as returned by <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>items()</i></a> – and return that object’s priority as either a string or float.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">If it’s an attribute, its value should be either a string or float representing the priority of every</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">object returned by <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>items()</i>.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Example values for <a href="index.html#page_1353"><i>priority</i></a>: 0.4, 1.0. The default priority of a page is 0.5. See the <a href="https://www.sitemaps.org/protocol.html#prioritydef">sitemaps.org</a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="https://www.sitemaps.org/protocol.html#prioritydef">documentation</a> for more.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>protocol</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">This attribute defines the protocol ('http' or 'https') of the URLs in the sitemap. If it isn’t set, the protocol with which the sitemap was requested is used. If the sitemap is built outside the context of a request, the default is 'https'.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>limit</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">This attribute defines the maximum number of URLs included on each page of the sitemap. Its value should not exceed the default value of 50000, which is the upper limit allowed in the</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="https://www.sitemaps.org/protocol.html#index">Sitemaps protocol</a>.</p> <p id="page_1354"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>i18n</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A boolean attribute that defines if the URLs of this sitemap should be generated using all of your</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_1920"><i>LANGUAGES</i></a> . The default is False.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>languages</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-sequence">sequence</a> of <a href="index.html#page_706">language codes</a> to use for generating alternate links when <a href="index.html#page_1353"><i>i18n</i></a> is enabled. Defaults</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">to <a href="index.html#page_1920"><i>LANGUAGES</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>alternates</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A boolean attribute. When used in conjunction with <a href="index.html#page_1353"><i>i18n</i></a> generated URLs will each have a list</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">of alternate links pointing to other language versions using the <a href="https://developers.google.com/search/docs/advanced/crawling/localized-versions">hreflang attribute</a>. The default is False.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>x_default</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A boolean attribute. When True the alternate links generated by <a href="index.html#page_1354"><i>alternates</i></a> will contain a</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">hreflang="x-default" fallback entry with a value of <a href="index.html#page_1918"><i>LANGUAGE_CODE</i></a> . The default is False.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_latest_lastmod</b>()</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional. A method that returns the latest value returned by <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>lastmod</i>. </a>This function is used to</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">add the lastmod attribute to <a href="index.html#page_1359">Sitemap index context variables.</a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">By default <a href="index.html#page_1354"><i>get_latest_lastmod()</i></a> returns:</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• If <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>lastmod</i></a> is an attribute: <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>lastmod</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">• If <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>lastmod</i></a> is a method: The latest lastmod returned by calling the method with all items</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">returned by <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>Sitemap.items()</i></a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>get_languages_for_item</b>(item)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Optional. A method that returns the sequence of language codes for which the item is displayed.</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">By default <a href="index.html#page_1354"><i>get_languages_for_item()</i></a> returns <a href="index.html#page_1354"><i>languages</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Shortcuts</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The sitemap framework provides a convenience class for a common case:</p> <p><b>class GenericSitemap</b>(info_dict, priority=None, changefreq=None, protocol=None)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The <a href="index.html#page_1354"><i>django.contrib.sitemaps.GenericSitemap</i></a> class allows you to create a sitemap by passing it a dictionary which has to contain at least a queryset entry. This queryset will be used to generate the items of the sitemap. It may also have a date_field entry that specifies a date field for objects retrieved</p> <p id="page_1355" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">from the queryset. This will be used for the <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>lastmod</i></a> attribute and <a href="index.html#page_1354"><i>get_latest_lastmod()</i></a> methods in the in the generated sitemap.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The <a href="index.html#page_1353"><i>priority</i></a>, <a href="index.html#page_1353"><i>changefreq</i>, </a>and <a href="index.html#page_1353"><i>protocol</i></a> keyword arguments allow specifying these attributes for all URLs.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Example</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Here’s an example of a <a href="index.html#page_266">URLconf</a> using <a href="index.html#page_1354"><i>GenericSitemap</i></a>:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.sitemaps.views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">sitemap</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.urls</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">path</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">blog.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Entry</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">info_dict</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"queryset"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: Entry</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">all(),</span></p> <p style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># some generic view using info_dict</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># the sitemap</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"sitemap.xml"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">sitemap,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"sitemaps"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: {</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"blog"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: GenericSitemap(info_dict, priority</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">0.6</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)}},</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.contrib.sitemaps.views.sitemap"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Sitemap for static views</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Often you want the search engine crawlers to index views which are neither object detail pages nor flatpages.</p> <p>The solution is to explicitly list URL names for these views in items and call <a href="index.html#page_2063"><i>reverse()</i></a> in the location method of the sitemap. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># sitemaps.py</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib</span> <span <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">reverse</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_1356"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">priority</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">0.5</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">changefreq</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"daily"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>items</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">, item):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">reverse(item)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># urls.py</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.urls</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">path</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">.sitemaps</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span <span style="font-size:0.87em">views</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">sitemaps</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">}</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span views</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">about, name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span ...</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"sitemap.xml"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">sitemap,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Creating a sitemap index</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>views.<b>index</b>(request, sitemaps, template_name='sitemap_index.xml', content_type='application/xml',</p> <p style="margin-left:5em">sitemap_url_name='django.contrib.sitemaps.views.sitemap')</p> <p>The sitemap framework also has the ability to create a sitemap index that references individual sitemap files, one per each section defined in your sitemaps dictionary. The only differences in usage are:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• You use two views in your URLconf: <a href="index.html#page_1356"><i>django.contrib.sitemaps.views.index()</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1350"><i>django.</i></a></p> <p id="page_1357" style="text-align:right"><a href="index.html#page_1350"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1350"><i>contrib.sitemaps.views.sitemap()</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The <a href="index.html#page_1350"><i>django.contrib.sitemaps.views.sitemap()</i></a> view should take a section keyword argument.</p> <p>Here’s what the relevant URLconf lines would look like for the example above:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.sitemaps</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">views</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"sitemap.xml"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">views</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">index,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"sitemaps"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: sitemaps},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.contrib.sitemaps.views.index"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"sitemap-<section>.xml"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">views</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">sitemap,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"sitemaps"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: sitemaps},</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.contrib.sitemaps.views.sitemap"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This will automatically generate a sitemap.xml file that references both sitemap-flatpages.xml and</p> <p>sitemap-blog.xml. The <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>Sitemap</i></a> classes and the sitemaps dict don’t change at all.</p> <p>If all sitemaps have a lastmod returned by <a href="index.html#page_1354"><i>Sitemap.get_latest_lastmod()</i></a> the sitemap index will have a Last-Modified header equal to the latest lastmod.</p> <p>You should create an index file if one of your sitemaps has more than 50,000 URLs. In this case, Django will automatically paginate the sitemap, and the index will reflect that.</p> <p>If you’re not using the vanilla sitemap view – for example, if it’s wrapped with a caching decorator – you must name your sitemap view and pass sitemap_url_name to the index view:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span <span style="font-size:0.87em">sitemaps_views</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.views.decorators.cache</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">cache_page</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"sitemaps"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: sitemaps,</span> <span style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_1358"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p sitemap and index views via the URLconf:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.sitemaps</span> <span style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"custom-sitemap-<section>.xml"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">views</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">sitemap,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">{</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"sitemaps"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">: sitemaps,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"template_name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"custom_sitemap.html"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">},</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"django.contrib.sitemaps.views.sitemap"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p><span the response data before</p> <p>rendering. For more details, see the <a href="index.html#page_2052">TemplateResponse documentation.</a></p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1359" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Context variables</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>When customizing the templates for the <a href="index.html#page_1356"><i>index()</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1350"><i>sitemap()</i></a> views, you can rely on the following context variables.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Index</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The variable sitemaps is a list of objects containing the location and lastmod attribute for each of the sitemaps. Each URL exposes the following attributes:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• location: The location (url & page) of the sitemap.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• lastmod: Populated by the <a href="index.html#page_1354"><i>get_latest_lastmod()</i></a> method for each sitemap.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Sitemap</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The variable urlset is a list of URLs that should appear in the sitemap. Each URL exposes attributes as</p> <p>defined in the <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>Sitemap</i></a> class:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• alternates</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• changefreq</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• item</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• lastmod</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• location</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• priority</p> <p>The alternates attribute is available when <a href="index.html#page_1353"><i>i18n</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1354"><i>alternates</i></a> are enabled. It is a list of other lan-</p> <p>guage versions, including the optional <a href="index.html#page_1354"><i>x_default</i></a> fallback, for each URL. Each alternate is a dictionary with location and lang_code keys.</p> <p>The item attribute has been added for each URL to allow more flexible customization of the templates, such</p> <p>as <a href="https://support.google.com/news/publisher-center/answer/9606710">Google news sitemaps. </a>Assuming Sitemap’s <a href="index.html#page_1352"><i>items()</i></a> would return a list of items with publication_data and a tags field something like this would generate a Google News compatible sitemap:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b><?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?></b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><urlset</span></p> <p style="margin-left:1em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">xmlns=</span><span <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><lastmod></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"></news:publication_date></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endif</b></span> <span
