style="font-size:0.87em">url.item.tags</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><news:keywords></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">url.item.tags</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"></news:keywords></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endif</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"></news:news></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"></url></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endfor</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{%</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>endspaceless</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>%}</b></i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"></urlset></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.5.11 The “sites” framework</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django comes with an optional “sites” framework. It’s a hook for associating objects and functionality to particular websites, and it’s a holding place for the domain names and “verbose” names of your Django-powered sites.</p> <p>Use it if your single Django installation powers more than one site and you need to differentiate between those sites in some way.</p> <p>The sites framework is mainly based on this model:</p> <p><b>class</b> models.<b>Site</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A model for storing the domain and name attributes of a website.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>domain</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">The fully qualified domain name associated with the website. For example, www.example.com.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>name</b></p> <p style="margin-left:4em">A human-readable “verbose” name for the website.</p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_1945"><i>SITE_ID</i></a> setting specifies the database ID of the <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i></a> object associated with that particular settings file.</p> <p>If the setting is omitted, the <a href="index.html#page_1369"><i>get_current_site()</i></a> function will try to get the current site by comparing the</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>domain</i></a> with the host name from the <a href="index.html#page_1864"><i>request.get_host()</i></a> method.</p> <p>How you use this is up to you, but Django uses it in a couple of ways automatically via a couple of conventions.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1361" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Example usage</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Why would you use sites? It’s best explained through examples.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Associating content with multiple sites</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The <a href="https://www2.ljworld.com/">LJWorld.com</a> and Lawrence.com sites were operated by the same news organization – the Lawrence Journal-World newspaper in Lawrence, Kansas. LJWorld.com focused on news, while Lawrence.com focused on local entertainment. But sometimes editors wanted to publish an article on both sites.</p> <p>The naive way of solving the problem would be to require site producers to publish the same story twice: once for LJWorld.com and again for Lawrence.com. But that’s inefficient for site producers, and it’s redundant to store multiple copies of the same story in the database.</p> <p>A better solution removes the content duplication: Both sites use the same article database, and an article is</p> <p>associated with one or more sites. In Django model terminology, that’s represented by a <a href="index.html#page_1649"><i>ManyToManyField</i></a> in the Article model:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.sites.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Site</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Article</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Model):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">headline</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">200</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">sites</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ManyToManyField(Site)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This accomplishes several things quite nicely:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• It lets the site producers edit all content – on both sites – in a single interface (the Django admin).</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• It means the same story doesn’t have to be published twice in the database; it only has a single record</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">in the database.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• It lets the site developers use the same Django view code for both sites. The view code that displays a</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">given story checks to make sure the requested story is on the current site. It looks something like this:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.sites.shortcuts</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">get_current_site</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>article_detail</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request, article_id):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>try</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">a</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Article</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">id</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">article_id, sites__id</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_current_site(request)</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">id)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>except</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Article</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">DoesNotExist:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>raise</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Http404(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Article does not exist on this site"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p id="page_1362"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Associating content with a single site</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Similarly, you can associate a model to the <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i></a> model in a many-to-one relationship, using <a href="index.html#page_1643"><i>ForeignKey</i></a>.</p> <p>For example, if an article is only allowed on a single site, you’d use a model like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.sites.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Site</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Article</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Model):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">headline</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">200</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">site</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ForeignKey(Site, on_delete</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CASCADE)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This has the same benefits as described in the last section.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Hooking into the current site from views</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can use the sites framework in your Django views to do particular things based on the site in which the view is being called. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.conf</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">settings</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">settings</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">SITE_ID</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">3</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Do something.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>pass</b></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>else</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Do something else.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>pass</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>It’s fragile to hard-code the site IDs like that, in case they change. The cleaner way of accomplishing the same thing is to check the current site’s domain:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.sites.shortcuts</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">get_current_site</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">current_site</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">get_current_site(request)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">current_site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">domain</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"foo.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Do something</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>pass</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_1363" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>else</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Do something else.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>pass</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This has also the advantage of checking if the sites framework is installed, and return a <a href="index.html#page_1368"><i>RequestSite</i></a> instance if it is not.</p> <p>If you don’t have access to the request object, you can use the get_current() method of the <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i></a> model’s</p> <p>manager. You should then ensure that your settings file does contain the <a href="index.html#page_1945"><i>SITE_ID</i></a> setting. This example is equivalent to the previous one:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.sites.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Site</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_function_without_request</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">():</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">current_site</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_current()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">current_site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">domain</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>==</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"foo.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Do something</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>pass</b></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>else</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Do something else.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>pass</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Getting the current domain for display</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>LJWorld.com and Lawrence.com both have email alert functionality, which lets readers sign up to get no-tifications when news happens. It’s pretty basic: A reader signs up on a web form and immediately gets an email saying, “Thanks for your subscription.”</p> <p>It’d be inefficient and redundant to implement this sign up processing code twice, so the sites use the same code behind the scenes. But the “thank you for signing up” notice needs to be different for each site. By using</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i></a> objects, we can abstract the “thank you” notice to use the values of the current site’s <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>name</i></a> and <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>domain</i></a>.</p> <p>Here’s an example of what the form-handling view looks like:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.sites.shortcuts</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">get_current_site</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.core.mail</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">send_mail</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>register_for_newsletter</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Check form values, etc., and subscribe the user.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_1364"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">current_site</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">get_current_site(request)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">send_mail(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Thanks for subscribing to %s alerts"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">current_site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">name,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Thanks for your subscription. We appreciate it.\n\n-The %s team."</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(current_site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">name,),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"editor@%s"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">current_site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">domain,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">[user</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">email],</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>On Lawrence.com, this email has the subject line “Thanks for subscribing to lawrence.com alerts.” On LJ-World.com, the email has the subject “Thanks for subscribing to LJWorld.com alerts.” Same goes for the email’s message body.</p> <p>Note that an even more flexible (but more heavyweight) way of doing this would be to use Django’s template</p> <p>system. Assuming Lawrence.com and LJWorld.com have different template directories <a href="index.html#page_1933">(<i>DIRS</i></a> ), you could farm out to the template system like so:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.core.mail</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">send_mail</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.template</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">loader</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>register_for_newsletter</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Check form values, etc., and subscribe the user.</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">subject</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">loader</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_template(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"alerts/subject.txt"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">render({})</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">message</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">loader</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_template(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"alerts/message.txt"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">render({})</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">send_mail(subject, message,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"editor@ljworld.com"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, [user</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">email])</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>In this case, you’d have to create subject.txt and message.txt template files for both the LJWorld.com and Lawrence.com template directories. That gives you more flexibility, but it’s also more complex.</p> <p>It’s a good idea to exploit the <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i></a> objects as much as possible, to remove unneeded complexity and redun-dancy.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1365" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Getting the current domain for full URLs</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django’s get_absolute_url() convention is nice for getting your objects’ URL without the domain name, but in some cases you might want to display the full URL – with https:// and the domain and everything – for an object. To do this, you can use the sites framework. An example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.sites.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Site</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">obj</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">MyModel</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">id</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">3</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">obj</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_absolute_url()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">'/mymodel/objects/3/'</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_current()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">domain</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">'example.com'</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"https://%s%s"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(Site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_current()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">domain, obj</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_absolute_url())</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">'https://example.com/mymodel/objects/3/'</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Enabling the sites framework</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To enable the sites framework, follow these steps:</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">1. Add 'django.contrib.sites' to your <a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">2. Define a <a href="index.html#page_1945"><i>SITE_ID</i></a> setting:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">SITE_ID</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">1</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">3. Run <a href="index.html#page_1446"><i>migrate</i></a>.</p> <p>django.contrib.sites registers a <a href="index.html#page_1961"><i>post_migrate</i></a> signal handler which creates a default site named example.com with the domain example.com. This site will also be created after Django creates the test</p> <p>database. To set the correct name and domain for your project, you can use a <a href="index.html#page_457">data migration</a>.</p> <p>In order to serve different sites in production, you’d create a separate settings file with each SITE_ID (perhaps importing from a common settings file to avoid duplicating shared settings) and then specify the appropriate</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_746"><i>DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE</i></a> for each site.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Caching the current Site object</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>As the current site is stored in the database, each call to Site.objects.get_current() could result in a database query. But Django is a little cleverer than that: on the first request, the current site is cached, and any subsequent call returns the cached data instead of hitting the database.</p> <p>If for any reason you want to force a database query, you can tell Django to clear the cache using Site. objects.clear_cache():</p> <p id="page_1366"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># First call; current site fetched from database.</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">current_site</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_current()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Second call; current site fetched from cache.</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">current_site</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_current()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Force a database query for the third call.</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">Site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">clear_cache()</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">current_site</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_current()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>The CurrentSiteManager</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> managers.<b>CurrentSiteManager</b></p> <p>If <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i></a> plays a key role in your application, consider using the helpful <a href="index.html#page_1366"><i>CurrentSiteManager</i></a> in your model(s).</p> <p>It’s a model <a href="index.html#page_191">manager</a> that automatically filters its queries to include only objects associated with the current</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Mandatory <b>SITE_ID</b></p> <p>The CurrentSiteManager is only usable when the <a href="index.html#page_1945"><i>SITE_ID</i></a> setting is defined in your settings.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Use <a href="index.html#page_1366"><i>CurrentSiteManager</i></a> by adding it to your model explicitly. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.sites.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Site</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.sites.managers</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">CurrentSiteManager</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Photo</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Model):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">photo</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">FileField(upload_to</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"photos"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">photographer_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">100</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">pub_date</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">DateField()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">site</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ForeignKey(Site, on_delete</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CASCADE)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Manager()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">on_site</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">CurrentSiteManager()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>With this model, Photo.objects.all() will return all Photo objects in the database, but Photo.on_site.</p> <p>all() will return only the Photo objects associated with the current site, according to the <a href="index.html#page_1945"><i>SITE_ID</i></a> setting.</p> <p>Put another way, these two statements are equivalent:</p> <p id="page_1367" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">Photo</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">settings</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">SITE_ID)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">Photo</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">on_site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">all()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>How did <a href="index.html#page_1366"><i>CurrentSiteManager</i></a> know which field of Photo was the <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i></a>? By default, <a href="index.html#page_1366"><i>CurrentSiteManager</i></a></p> <p>looks for a either a <a href="index.html#page_1643"><i>ForeignKey</i></a> called site or a <a href="index.html#page_1649"><i>ManyToManyField</i></a> called sites to filter on. If you use a field</p> <p>named something other than site or sites to identify which <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i></a> objects your object is related to, then you</p> <p>need to explicitly pass the custom field name as a parameter to <a href="index.html#page_1366"><i>CurrentSiteManager</i></a> on your model. The following model, which has a field called publish_on, demonstrates this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.sites.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Site</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.sites.managers</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">CurrentSiteManager</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.db</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>Photo</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Model):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">photo</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">FileField(upload_to</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"photos"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">photographer_name</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CharField(max_length</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">100</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">pub_date</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">DateField()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">publish_on</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">ForeignKey(Site, on_delete</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">CASCADE)</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">models</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Manager()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">on_site</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">CurrentSiteManager(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"publish_on"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you attempt to use <a href="index.html#page_1366"><i>CurrentSiteManager</i></a> and pass a field name that doesn’t exist, Django will raise a ValueError.</p> <p>Finally, note that you’ll probably want to keep a normal (non-site-specific) Manager on your model, even if</p> <p>you use <a href="index.html#page_1366"><i>CurrentSiteManager</i></a>. As explained in the <a href="index.html#page_191">manager documentation</a><a href="index.html#page_191">, </a>if you define a manager man-ually, then Django won’t create the automatic objects = models.Manager() manager for you. Also note that certain parts of Django – namely, the Django admin site and generic views – use whichever manager is defined first in the model, so if you want your admin site to have access to all objects (not just site-specific ones), put objects = models.Manager() in your model, before you define <a href="index.html#page_1366"><i>CurrentSiteManager</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Site middleware</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you often use this pattern:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.sites.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Site</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>my_view</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(request):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">site</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Site</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_current()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>...</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To avoid repetitions, add <a href="index.html#page_1599"><i>django.contrib.sites.middleware.CurrentSiteMiddleware</i></a> to <a href="index.html#page_1923"><i>MIDDLEWARE</i></a> .</p> <p id="page_1368"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The middleware sets the site attribute on every request object, so you can use request.site to get the current site.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>How Django uses the sites framework</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Although it’s not required that you use the sites framework, it’s strongly encouraged, because Django takes advantage of it in a few places. Even if your Django installation is powering only a single site, you should</p> <p>take the two seconds to create the site object with your domain and name, and point to its ID in your <a href="index.html#page_1945"><i>SITE_ID</i></a> setting.</p> <p>Here’s how Django uses the sites framework:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• In the <a href="index.html#page_1347"><i>redirects framework</i></a>, each redirect object is associated with a particular site. When Django</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">searches for a redirect, it takes into account the current site.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• In the <a href="index.html#page_1124"><i>flatpages framework</i></a>, each flatpage is associated with a particular site. When a flatpage is cre-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">ated, you specify its <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i>, </a>and the <a href="index.html#page_1126"><i>FlatpageFallbackMiddleware</i></a> checks the current site in retrieving flatpages to display.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• In the <a href="index.html#page_1378"><i>syndication framework</i></a>, the templates for title and description automatically have access</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">to a variable {{ site }}, which is the <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i></a> object representing the current site. Also, the hook for</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">providing item URLs will use the domain from the current <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i></a> object if you don’t specify a fully-qualified domain.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• In the <a href="index.html#page_598"><i>authentication framework</i></a>, <a href="index.html#page_549"><i>django.contrib.auth.views.LoginView</i></a> passes the current <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">name to the template as {{ site_name }}.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The shortcut view (django.contrib.contenttypes.views.shortcut) uses the domain of the current</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i></a> object when calculating an object’s URL.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• In the admin framework, the “view on site” link uses the current <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i></a> to work out the domain for the</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">site that it will redirect to.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>RequestSite objects</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Some <a href="index.html#page_1017">django.contrib</a> applications take advantage of the sites framework but are architected in a way that doesn’t require the sites framework to be installed in your database. (Some people don’t want to, or just aren’t able to install the extra database table that the sites framework requires.) For those cases, the framework</p> <p>provides a <a href="index.html#page_1368"><i>django.contrib.sites.requests.RequestSite</i></a> class, which can be used as a fallback when the database-backed sites framework is not available.</p> <p><b>class</b> requests.<b>RequestSite</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A class that shares the primary interface of <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i></a> (i.e., it has domain and name attributes) but gets its</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">data from a Django <a href="index.html#page_1859"><i>HttpRequest</i></a> object rather than from a database.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><b>__init__</b>(request)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">Sets the name and domain attributes to the value of <a href="index.html#page_1864"><i>get_host()</i>.</a></p> <p id="page_1369" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A <a href="index.html#page_1368"><i>RequestSite</i></a> object has a similar interface to a normal <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i></a> object, except its <a href="index.html#page_1368"><i>__init__()</i></a> method takes</p> <p>an <a href="index.html#page_1859"><i>HttpRequest</i></a> object. It’s able to deduce the domain and name by looking at the request’s domain. It has</p> <p>save() and delete() methods to match the interface of <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i>, </a>but the methods raise <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#NotImplementedError">NotImplementedError</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>get_current_site shortcut</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Finally, to avoid repetitive fallback code, the framework provides a <a href="index.html#page_1369"><i>django.contrib.sites.shortcuts.</i></a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1369"><i>get_current_site()</i></a> function.</p> <p>shortcuts.<b>get_current_site</b>(request)</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">A function that checks if django.contrib.sites is installed and returns either the current <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>Site</i></a> ob-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">ject or a <a href="index.html#page_1368"><i>RequestSite</i></a> object based on the request. It looks up the current site based on <a href="index.html#page_1864"><i>request.</i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1864"><i>get_host()</i></a> if the <a href="index.html#page_1945"><i>SITE_ID</i></a> setting is not defined.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Both a domain and a port may be returned by <a href="index.html#page_1864"><i>request.get_host()</i></a> when the Host header has a port explicitly specified, e.g. example.com:80. In such cases, if the lookup fails because the host does not match a record in the database, the port is stripped and the lookup is retried with the domain part only.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This does not apply to <a href="index.html#page_1368"><i>RequestSite</i></a> which will always use the unmodified host.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.5.12 The</b></span> <span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>staticfiles</b></span> <span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>app</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>django.contrib.staticfiles collects static files from each of your applications (and any other places you specify) into a single location that can easily be served in production.</p> <p>See also:</p> <p>For an introduction to the static files app and some usage examples, see <a href="index.html#page_843">How to manage static files (e.g.</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_843">images, JavaScript, CSS)</a>. For guidelines on deploying static files, see <a href="index.html#page_885">How to deploy static files</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Settings</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>See <a href="index.html#page_1945">staticfiles settings</a> for details on the following settings:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1931"><i>STORAGES</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1945"><i>STATIC_ROOT</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1946"><i>STATIC_URL</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1946"><i>STATICFILES_DIRS</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_1947"><i>STATICFILES_FINDERS</i></a></p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1370"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Management Commands</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>django.contrib.staticfiles exposes three management commands.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>collectstatic</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>django-admin collectstatic</b></p> <p>Collects the static files into <a href="index.html#page_1945"><i>STATIC_ROOT</i></a> .</p> <p>Duplicate file names are by default resolved in a similar way to how template resolution works: the file that</p> <p>is first found in one of the specified locations will be used. If you’re confused, the <a href="index.html#page_1371"><i>findstatic</i></a> command can help show you which files are found.</p> <p>On subsequent collectstatic runs (if STATIC_ROOT isn’t empty), files are copied only if they have a modified timestamp greater than the timestamp of the file in STATIC_ROOT. Therefore if you remove an application</p> <p>from <a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a>, it’s a good idea to use the <a href="index.html#page_1371"><i>collectstatic --clear</i></a> option in order to remove stale static files.</p> <p>Files are searched by using the <a href="index.html#page_1947"><i>enabled finders</i></a>. The default is to look in all locations defined in</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1946"><i>STATICFILES_DIRS</i></a> and in the 'static' directory of apps specified by the <a href="index.html#page_1917"><i>INSTALLED_APPS</i></a> setting.</p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_1370"><i>collectstatic</i></a> management command calls the <a href="index.html#page_1373"><i>post_process()</i></a> method of the staticfiles stor-</p> <p>age backend from <a href="index.html#page_1931"><i>STORAGES</i></a> after each run and passes a list of paths that have been found by the man-</p> <p>agement command. It also receives all command line options of <a href="index.html#page_1370"><i>collectstatic</i></a>. This is used by the</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1374"><i>ManifestStaticFilesStorage</i></a> by default.</p> <p>By default, collected files receive permissions from <a href="index.html#page_1914"><i>FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS</i></a> and collected directories</p> <p>receive permissions from <a href="index.html#page_1914"><i>FILE_UPLOAD_DIRECTORY_PERMISSIONS</i></a>. If you would like different permissions</p> <p>for these files and/or directories, you can subclass either of the <a href="index.html#page_1373">static files storage classes</a> and specify the file_permissions_mode and/or directory_permissions_mode parameters, respectively. It yields tuples of three values: original_path, processed_path, processed. The path values are strings and processed is a boolean indicating whether or not the value was post-processed, or an exception if post-processing failed.</p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_1374"><i>ManifestStaticFilesStorage</i></a> uses this behind the scenes to replace the paths with their hashed coun-terparts and update the cache appropriately.</p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1374"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>ManifestStaticFilesStorage</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> storage.<b>ManifestStaticFilesStorage</b></p> <p>A subclass of the <a href="index.html#page_1373"><i>StaticFilesStorage</i></a> storage backend which stores the file names it handles by appending the MD5 hash of the file’s content to the filename. For example, the file css/styles.css would also be saved as css/styles.55e7cbb9ba48.css.</p> <p>The purpose of this storage is to keep serving the old files in case some pages still refer to those files, e.g. because they are cached by you or a 3rd party proxy server. Additionally, it’s very helpful if you want to</p> <p>apply <a href="https://developer.yahoo.com/performance/rules.html#expires">far future Expires headers</a> to the deployed files to speed up the load time for subsequent page visits.</p> <p>The storage backend automatically replaces the paths found in the saved files matching other saved files with</p> <p>the path of the cached copy (using the <a href="index.html#page_1373"><i>post_process()</i></a> method). The regular expressions used to find those paths (django.contrib.staticfiles.storage.HashedFilesMixin.patterns) cover:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS2/cascade.html#at-import">@import</a> rule and <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS2/syndata.html#uri">url()</a> statement of <a href="https://www.w3.org/Style/CSS/">Cascading Style Sheets</a><a href="https://www.w3.org/Style/CSS/">.</a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/devtools-user/debugger/how_to/use_a_source_map/">Source map</a> comments in CSS and JavaScript files.</p> <p>Subclass ManifestStaticFilesStorage and set the support_js_module_import_aggregation attribute to True, if you want to use the experimental regular expressions to cover:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Modules#importing_features_into_your_script">modules import</a> in JavaScript.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Modules#aggregating_modules">modules aggregation</a> in JavaScript.</p> <p>For example, the 'css/styles.css' file with this content:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">url</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>(</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"../admin/css/base.css"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>)</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">;</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><i>. . .</i>would be replaced by calling the <a href="index.html#page_1482"><i>url()</i></a> method of the ManifestStaticFilesStorage storage backend, ultimately saving a 'css/styles.55e7cbb9ba48.css' file with the following content:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">@</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">url</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>(</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"../admin/css/base.27e20196a850.css"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>)</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">;</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Usage of the <b>integrity</b> HTML attribute with local files</p> <p>When using the optional integrity attribute within tags like <script> or <link>, its value should be cal-culated based on the files as they are served, not as stored in the filesystem. This is particularly important because depending on how static files are collected, their checksum may have changed (for example when</p> <p>using <a href="index.html#page_1370"><i>collectstatic</i>). </a>At the moment, there is no out-of-the-box tooling available for this.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can change the location of the manifest file by using a custom ManifestStaticFilesStorage subclass that sets the manifest_storage argument. For example:</p> <p id="page_1375" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.conf</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">settings</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.staticfiles.storage</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">ManifestStaticFilesStorage,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">StaticFilesStorage,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyManifestStaticFilesStorage</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(ManifestStaticFilesStorage):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>__init__</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>*</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>References in comments</p> <p>ManifestStaticFilesStorage doesn’t ignore paths in statements that are commented out. This <a href="https://code.djangoproject.com/ticket/21080">may crash</a></p> <p><a href="https://code.djangoproject.com/ticket/21080">on the nonexistent paths</a>. You should check and eventually strip comments.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>storage.ManifestStaticFilesStorage.<b>manifest_hash</b></p> <p>This attribute provides a single hash that changes whenever a file in the manifest changes. This can be useful to communicate to SPAs that the assets on the server have changed (due to a new deployment).</p> <p>storage.ManifestStaticFilesStorage.<b>max_post_process_passes</b></p> <p>Since static files might reference other static files that need to have their paths replaced, multiple passes of replacing paths may be needed until the file hashes converge. To prevent an infinite loop due to hashes not converging (for example, if 'foo.css' references 'bar.css' which references 'foo.css') there is a maximum number of passes before post-processing is abandoned. In cases with a large number of refer-ences, a higher number of passes might be needed. Increase the maximum number of passes by subclassing ManifestStaticFilesStorage and setting the max_post_process_passes attribute. It defaults to 5.</p> <p>To enable the ManifestStaticFilesStorage you have to make sure the following requirements are met:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• the staticfiles storage backend in <a href="index.html#page_1931"><i>STORAGES</i></a> setting is set to 'django.contrib.staticfiles.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">storage.ManifestStaticFilesStorage'</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• the <a href="index.html#page_1907"><i>DEBUG</i></a> setting is set to False</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• you’ve collected all your static files by using the <a href="index.html#page_1370"><i>collectstatic</i></a> management command</p> <p>Since creating the MD5 hash can be a performance burden to your website during runtime, staticfiles will automatically store the mapping with hashed names for all processed files in a file called staticfiles.json.</p> <p>This happens once when you run the <a href="index.html#page_1370"><i>collectstatic</i></a> management command.</p> <p>storage.ManifestStaticFilesStorage.<b>manifest_strict Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p id="page_1376">If a file isn’t found in the staticfiles.json manifest at runtime, a ValueError is raised. This behavior can be disabled by subclassing ManifestStaticFilesStorage and setting the manifest_strict attribute to False – nonexistent paths will remain unchanged.</p> <p>Due to the requirement of running <a href="index.html#page_1370"><i>collectstatic</i>, </a>this storage typically shouldn’t be used when running tests as collectstatic isn’t run as part of the normal test setup. During testing, ensure that staticfiles</p> <p>storage backend in the <a href="index.html#page_1931"><i>STORAGES</i></a> setting is set to something else like 'django.contrib.staticfiles. storage.StaticFilesStorage' (the default).</p> <p>storage.ManifestStaticFilesStorage.<b>file_hash</b>(name, content=None)</p> <p>The method that is used when creating the hashed name of a file. Needs to return a hash for the given file name and content. By default it calculates a MD5 hash from the content’s chunks as mentioned above. Feel free to override this method to use your own hashing algorithm.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>ManifestFilesMixin</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> storage.<b>ManifestFilesMixin</b></p> <p>Use this mixin with a custom storage to append the MD5 hash of the file’s content to the filename as</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1374"><i>ManifestStaticFilesStorage</i></a> does.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Finders Module</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>staticfiles finders has a searched_locations attribute which is a list of directory paths in which the finders searched. Example usage:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.staticfiles</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span
