style="font-size:0.87em">finders</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">find(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"css/base.css"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">searched_locations</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">finders</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">searched_locations</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Other Helpers</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>There are a few other helpers outside of the <a href="index.html#page_1369"><i>staticfiles</i></a> app to work with static files:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The <a href="index.html#page_2045"><i>django.template.context_processors.static()</i></a> context processor which adds <a href="index.html#page_1946"><i>STATIC_URL</i></a> to</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">every template context rendered with <a href="index.html#page_2042"><i>RequestContext</i></a> contexts.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The builtin template tag <a href="index.html#page_2029"><i>static</i></a> which takes a path and urljoins it with the static prefix <a href="index.html#page_1946"><i>STATIC_URL</i></a><a href="index.html#page_1946">. </a>If</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">django.contrib.staticfiles is installed, the tag uses the url() method of the staticfiles storage</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">backend from <a href="index.html#page_1931"><i>STORAGES</i></a> instead.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The builtin template tag <a href="index.html#page_2030"><i>get_static_prefix</i></a> which populates a template variable with the static prefix</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1946"><i>STATIC_URL</i></a> to be used as a variable or directly.</p> <p id="page_1377" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The similar template tag <a href="index.html#page_2030"><i>get_media_prefix</i></a> which works like <a href="index.html#page_2030"><i>get_static_prefix</i></a> but uses <a href="index.html#page_1922"><i>MEDIA_URL</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The staticfiles key in <a href="index.html#page_1479"><i>django.core.files.storage.storages</i></a> contains a ready-to-use instance of</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">the staticfiles storage backend.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Static file development view</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The static files tools are mostly designed to help with getting static files successfully deployed into production. This usually means a separate, dedicated static file server, which is a lot of overhead to mess with when developing locally. Thus, the staticfiles app ships with a quick and dirty helper view that you can use to serve files locally in development.</p> <p>views.<b>serve</b>(request, path)</p> <p>This view function serves static files in development.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: This view will only work if <a href="index.html#page_1907"><i>DEBUG</i></a> is True.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">That’s because this view is grossly inefficient and probably insecure. This is only intended for local</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">development, and should never be used in production.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: To guess the served files’ content types, this view relies on the <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/mimetypes.html#module-mimetypes">mimetypes</a> module from the Python standard library, which itself relies on the underlying platform’s map files. If you find that this view doesn’t return proper content types for certain files, it is most likely that the platform’s map files are incorrect or need to be updated. This can be achieved, for example, by installing or updating the mailcap package on a Red Hat distribution, mime-support on a Debian distribution, or by editing the keys under HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT in the Windows registry.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This view is automatically enabled by <a href="index.html#page_1447"><i>runserver</i></a> (with a <a href="index.html#page_1907"><i>DEBUG</i></a> setting set to True). To use the view with a different local development server, add the following snippet to the end of your primary URL configuration:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.conf</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">settings</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.staticfiles</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">views</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.urls</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">re_path</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>if</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">settings</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">DEBUG:</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>+=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">re_path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">r"^static/(?P<path>.*)$"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, views</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">serve),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note, the beginning of the pattern (r'^static/') should be your <a href="index.html#page_1946"><i>STATIC_URL</i></a> setting.</p> <p>Since this is a bit finicky, there’s also a helper function that’ll do this for you:</p> <p id="page_1378"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>urls.<b>staticfiles_urlpatterns</b>()</p> <p>This will return the proper URL pattern for serving static files to your already defined pattern list. Use it like this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.staticfiles.urls</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">staticfiles_urlpatterns</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ... the rest of your URLconf here ...</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>+=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">staticfiles_urlpatterns()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This will inspect your <a href="index.html#page_1946"><i>STATIC_URL</i></a> setting and wire up the view to serve static files accordingly. Don’t forget</p> <p>to set the <a href="index.html#page_1946"><i>STATICFILES_DIRS</i></a> setting appropriately to let django.contrib.staticfiles know where to look for files in addition to files in app directories.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: This helper function will only work if <a href="index.html#page_1907"><i>DEBUG</i></a> is True and your <a href="index.html#page_1946"><i>STATIC_URL</i></a> setting is neither</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">empty nor a full URL such as http://static.example.com/.</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">That’s because this view is grossly inefficient and probably insecure. This is only intended for local</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">development, and should never be used in production.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Specialized test case to support ‘live testing’</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> testing.<b>StaticLiveServerTestCase</b></p> <p>This unittest TestCase subclass extends <a href="index.html#page_493"><i>django.test.LiveServerTestCase</i></a>.</p> <p>Just like its parent, you can use it to write tests that involve running the code under test and consuming it with testing tools through HTTP (e.g. Selenium, PhantomJS, etc.), because of which it’s needed that the static assets are also published.</p> <p>But given the fact that it makes use of the <a href="index.html#page_1377"><i>django.contrib.staticfiles.views.serve()</i></a> view described above, it can transparently overlay at test execution-time the assets provided by the staticfiles finders.</p> <p>This means you don’t need to run <a href="index.html#page_1370"><i>collectstatic</i></a> before or as a part of your tests setup.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.5.13 The syndication feed framework</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django comes with a high-level syndication-feed-generating framework for creating <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/RSS">RSS</a> and <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4287.html">Atom</a> feeds.</p> <p>To create any syndication feed, all you have to do is write a short Python class. You can create as many feeds as you want.</p> <p>Django also comes with a lower-level feed-generating API. Use this if you want to generate feeds outside of a web context, or in some other lower-level way.</p> <p id="page_1379" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>The high-level framework</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Overview</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The high-level feed-generating framework is supplied by the <a href="index.html#page_1385"><i>Feed</i></a> class. To create a feed, write a <a href="index.html#page_1385"><i>Feed</i></a> class</p> <p>and point to an instance of it in your <a href="index.html#page_266">URLconf</a>.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Feed classes</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>A <a href="index.html#page_1385"><i>Feed</i></a> class is a Python class that represents a syndication feed. A feed can be simple (e.g., a “site news” feed, or a basic feed displaying the latest entries of a blog) or more complex (e.g., a feed displaying all the blog entries in a particular category, where the category is variable).</p> <p>Feed classes subclass <a href="index.html#page_1385"><i>django.contrib.syndication.views.Feed</i></a>. They can live anywhere in your codebase.</p> <p>Instances of <a href="index.html#page_1385"><i>Feed</i></a> classes are views which can be used in your <a href="index.html#page_266">URLconf</a><a href="index.html#page_266">.</a></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>A simple example</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>This simple example, taken from a hypothetical police beat news site describes a feed of the latest five news items:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.syndication.views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Feed</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.urls</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">reverse</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">policebeat.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">NewsItem</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>LatestEntriesFeed</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Feed):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Police beat site news"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">link</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"/sitenews/"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">description</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Updates on changes and additions to police beat central."</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>items</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">NewsItem</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">order_by(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"-pub_date"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)[:</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">5</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>item_title</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, item):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">item</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>item_description</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, item):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">item</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">description</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># item_link is only needed if NewsItem has no get_absolute_url method.</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>item_link</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, item):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">reverse(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"news-item"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, args</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">[item</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">pk])</span></p> <p id="page_1380"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To connect a URL to this feed, put an instance of the Feed object in your <a href="index.html#page_266">URLconf</a>. For example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.urls</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">path</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myproject.feeds</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">LatestEntriesFeed</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"latest/feed/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, LatestEntriesFeed()),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• The Feed class subclasses <a href="index.html#page_1385"><i>django.contrib.syndication.views.Feed</i></a>.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• title, link and description correspond to the standard RSS <title>, <link> and <description></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">elements, respectively.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• items() is, a method that returns a list of objects that should be included in the feed as <item> el-</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">ements. Although this example returns NewsItem objects using Django’s <a href="index.html#page_1706">object-relational mapper</a>, items() doesn’t have to return model instances. Although you get a few bits of functionality “for free” by using Django models, items() can return any type of object you want.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• If you’re creating an Atom feed, rather than an RSS feed, set the subtitle attribute instead of the</p> <p style="text-align:center">description attribute. See <a href="index.html#page_1384">Publishing Atom and RSS feeds in tandem</a>, later, for an example.</p> <p>One thing is left to do. In an RSS feed, each <item> has a <title>, <link> and <description>. We need to tell the framework what data to put into those elements.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• For the contents of <title> and <description>, Django tries calling the methods item_title() and</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">item_description() on the <a href="index.html#page_1385"><i>Feed</i></a> class. They are passed a single parameter, item, which is the object itself. These are optional; by default, the string representation of the object is used for both.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">If you want to do any special formatting for either the title or description, <a href="index.html#page_1965">Django templates</a> can be used instead. Their paths can be specified with the title_template and description_template attributes</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">on the <a href="index.html#page_1385"><i>Feed</i></a> class. The templates are rendered for each item and are passed two template context variables:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– {{ obj }} – The current object (one of whichever objects you returned in items()).</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– {{ site }} – A <a href="index.html#page_1360"><i>django.contrib.sites.models.Site</i></a> object representing the current site. This</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">is useful for {{ site.domain }} or {{ site.name }}. If you do not have the Django sites frame-</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">work installed, this will be set to a <a href="index.html#page_1368"><i>RequestSite</i></a> object. See the <a href="index.html#page_1368">RequestSite section of the sites</a></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><a href="index.html#page_1368">framework documentation</a> for more.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">See <a href="index.html#page_1382">a complex example</a> below that uses a description template.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Feed.<b>get_context_data</b>(**kwargs)</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">There is also a way to pass additional information to title and description templates, if you need</p> <p id="page_1381" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em">to supply more than the two variables mentioned before. You can provide your implementation of get_context_data method in your Feed subclass. For example:</p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">mysite.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Article</span></p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.syndication.views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Feed</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:4em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ArticlesFeed</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Feed):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"My articles"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">description_template</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"feeds/articles.html"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>items</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Article</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">order_by(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"-pub_date"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)[:</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">5</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:5em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get_context_data</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">context</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_context_data(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>**</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">kwargs)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">context[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"foo"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"bar"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:7em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">context</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">And the template:</p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">Something about</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">foo</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">:</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">obj.description</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em">This method will be called once per each item in the list returned by items() with the following keyword arguments:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– item: the current item. For backward compatibility reasons, the name of this context variable is</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">{{ obj }}.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– obj: the object returned by get_object(). By default this is not exposed to the templates</p> <p style="margin-left:4em">to avoid confusion with {{ obj }} (see above), but you can use it in your implementation of get_context_data().</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– site: current site as described above.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">– request: current request.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The behavior of get_context_data() mimics that of <a href="index.html#page_420">generic views</a>- you’re supposed to call super() to retrieve context data from parent class, add your data and return the modified dictionary.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• To specify the contents of <link>, you have two options. For each item in items(), Django first</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">tries calling the item_link() method on the <a href="index.html#page_1385"><i>Feed</i></a> class. In a similar way to the title and descrip-tion, it is passed it a single parameter, item. If that method doesn’t exist, Django tries execut-ing a get_absolute_url() method on that object. Both get_absolute_url() and item_link() should return the item’s URL as a normal Python string. As with get_absolute_url(), the result of item_link() will be included directly in the URL, so you are responsible for doing all necessary URL quoting and conversion to ASCII inside the method itself.</p> <p id="page_1382"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>A complex example</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The framework also supports more complex feeds, via arguments.</p> <p>For example, a website could offer an RSS feed of recent crimes for every police beat in a city. It’d be silly</p> <p>to create a separate <a href="index.html#page_1385"><i>Feed</i></a> class for each police beat; that would violate the <a href="index.html#page_2105">DRY principle</a> and would couple data to programming logic. Instead, the syndication framework lets you access the arguments passed from</p> <p>your <a href="index.html#page_266">URLconf</a> so feeds can output items based on information in the feed’s URL.</p> <p>The police beat feeds could be accessible via URLs like this:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• /beats/613/rss/ – Returns recent crimes for beat 613.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• /beats/1424/rss/ – Returns recent crimes for beat 1424.</p> <p>These can be matched with a <a href="index.html#page_266">URLconf</a> line such as:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"beats/<int:beat_id>/rss/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, BeatFeed()),</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Like a view, the arguments in the URL are passed to the get_object() method along with the request object.</p> <p>Here’s the code for these beat-specific feeds:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.syndication.views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Feed</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>BeatFeed</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Feed):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">description_template</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"feeds/beat_description.html"</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>get_object</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, request, beat_id):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Beat</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get(pk</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">beat_id)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>title</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, obj):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Police beat central: Crimes for beat %s"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">obj</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">beat</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>link</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, obj):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">obj</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">get_absolute_url()</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>description</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, obj):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Crimes recently reported in police beat %s"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>%</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">obj</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">beat</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>items</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, obj):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Crime</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">filter(beat</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">obj)</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">order_by(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"-crime_date"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)[:</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">30</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To generate the feed’s <title>, <link> and <description>, Django uses the title(), link() and description() methods. In the previous example, they were string class attributes, but this example il-lustrates that they can be either strings or methods. For each of title, link and description, Django follows this algorithm:</p> <p id="page_1383" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• First, it tries to call a method, passing the obj argument, where obj is the object returned by</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">get_object() .</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Failing that, it tries to call a method with no arguments.</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• Failing that, it uses the class attribute.</p> <p>Also note that items() also follows the same algorithm – first, it tries items(obj), then items(), then finally an items class attribute (which should be a list).</p> <p>We are using a template for the item descriptions. It can be as minimal as this:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>{{</b></i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">obj.description</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i><b>}}</b></i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>However, you are free to add formatting as desired.</p> <p>The ExampleFeed class below gives full documentation on methods and attributes of <a href="index.html#page_1385"><i>Feed</i></a> classes.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Specifying the type of feed</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>By default, feeds produced in this framework use RSS 2.0.</p> <p>To change that, add a feed_type attribute to your <a href="index.html#page_1385"><i>Feed</i></a> class, like so:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.feedgenerator</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Atom1Feed</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MyFeed</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Feed):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">feed_type</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Atom1Feed</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note that you set feed_type to a class object, not an instance.</p> <p>Currently available feed types are:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_2079"><i>django.utils.feedgenerator.Rss201rev2Feed</i></a> (RSS 2.01. Default.)</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_2079"><i>django.utils.feedgenerator.RssUserland091Feed</i></a> (RSS 0.91.)</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_2079"><i>django.utils.feedgenerator.Atom1Feed</i></a> (Atom 1.0.)</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Enclosures</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>To specify enclosures, such as those used in creating podcast feeds, use the item_enclosures hook or, alterna-tively and if you only have a single enclosure per item, the item_enclosure_url, item_enclosure_length, and item_enclosure_mime_type hooks. See the ExampleFeed class below for usage examples.</p> <p id="page_1384"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Language</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Feeds created by the syndication framework automatically include the appropriate <language> tag (RSS 2.0)</p> <p>or xml:lang attribute (Atom). By default, this is <a href="index.html#page_2090"><i>django.utils.translation.get_language()</i></a>. You can change it by setting the language class attribute.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>URLs</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The link method/attribute can return either an absolute path (e.g. "/blog/") or a URL with the fully-qualified domain and protocol (e.g. "https://www.example.com/blog/"). If link doesn’t return the domain,</p> <p>the syndication framework will insert the domain of the current site, according to your <a href="index.html#page_1945"><i>SITE_ID setting</i></a>.</p> <p>Atom feeds require a <link rel="self"> that defines the feed’s current location. The syndication frame-</p> <p>work populates this automatically, using the domain of the current site according to the <a href="index.html#page_1945"><i>SITE_ID</i></a> setting.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Publishing Atom and RSS feeds in tandem</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Some developers like to make available both Atom and RSS versions of their feeds. To do that, you can create</p> <p>a subclass of your <a href="index.html#page_1385"><i>Feed</i></a> class and set the feed_type to something different. Then update your URLconf to add the extra versions.</p> <p>Here’s a full example:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.syndication.views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Feed</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">policebeat.models</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">NewsItem</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.feedgenerator</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Atom1Feed</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>RssSiteNewsFeed</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Feed):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Police beat site news"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">link</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"/sitenews/"</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">description</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"Updates on changes and additions to police beat central."</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>items</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">NewsItem</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">objects</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">order_by(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"-pub_date"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)[:</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">5</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>AtomSiteNewsFeed</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(RssSiteNewsFeed):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">feed_type</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Atom1Feed</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">subtitle</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">RssSiteNewsFeed</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">description</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Note: In this example, the RSS feed uses a description while the Atom feed uses a subtitle. That’s because Atom feeds don’t provide for a feed-level “description,” but they do provide for a “subtitle.”</p> <p id="page_1385" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you provide a description in your <a href="index.html#page_1385"><i>Feed</i></a> class, Django will not automatically put that into the subtitle element, because a subtitle and description are not necessarily the same thing. Instead, you should define a subtitle attribute.</p> <p>In the above example, we set the Atom feed’s subtitle to the RSS feed’s description, because it’s quite short already.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>And the accompanying URLconf:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.urls</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">path</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">myproject.feeds</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">AtomSiteNewsFeed, RssSiteNewsFeed</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">urlpatterns</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"sitenews/rss/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, RssSiteNewsFeed()),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">path(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"sitenews/atom/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, AtomSiteNewsFeed()),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># ...</i></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Feed class reference</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>class</b> views.<b>Feed</b></p> <p>This example illustrates all possible attributes and methods for a <a href="index.html#page_1385"><i>Feed</i></a> class:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.syndication.views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Feed</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">feedgenerator</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>ExampleFeed</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Feed):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># FEED TYPE -- Optional. This should be a class that subclasses</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># django.utils.feedgenerator.SyndicationFeed. This designates</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># which type of feed this should be: RSS 2.0, Atom 1.0, etc. If</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># you don't specify feed_type, your feed will be RSS 2.0. This</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># should be a class, not an instance of the class.</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">feed_type</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">feedgenerator</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Rss201rev2Feed</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># TEMPLATE NAMES -- Optional. These should be strings</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># representing names of Django templates that the system should</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># use in rendering the title and description of your feed items.</i></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># Both are optional. If a template is not specified, the</i></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># item_title() or item_description() methods are used instead.</i></span></p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_1386"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">title_template</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>= None</b></span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">description_template</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>= None</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><i># LANGUAGE -- Optional. low-level framework</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Behind the scenes, the high-level RSS framework uses a lower-level framework for generating feeds’ XML.</p> <p>This framework lives in a single module: <a href="https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/utils/feedgenerator.py">django/utils/feedgenerator.py.</a></p> <p>You use this framework on your own, for lower-level feed generation. You can also create custom feed generator subclasses for use with the feed_type Feed option.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>SyndicationFeed classes</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The <a href="index.html#page_2076"><i>feedgenerator</i></a> module contains a base class:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_2078"><i>django.utils.feedgenerator.SyndicationFeed</i></a></p> <p>and several subclasses:</p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_2079"><i>django.utils.feedgenerator.RssUserland091Feed</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_2079"><i>django.utils.feedgenerator.Rss201rev2Feed</i></a></p> <p style="text-indent:1em">• <a href="index.html#page_2079"><i>django.utils.feedgenerator.Atom1Feed</i></a></p> <p>Each of these three classes knows how to render a certain type of feed as XML. They share this interface:</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_2078"><i><b>SyndicationFeed.__init__()</b></i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Initialize the feed with the given dictionary of metadata, which applies to the entire feed. Required keyword arguments are:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• title</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• link</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• description</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">There’s also a bunch of other optional keywords:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• language</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• author_email</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• author_name</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• author_link</p> <p id="page_1399" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• subtitle</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• categories</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• feed_url</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• feed_copyright</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• feed_guid</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• ttl</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• stylesheets</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Any extra keyword arguments you pass to __init__ will be stored in self.feed for use with <a href="index.html#page_1401">custom</a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><a href="index.html#page_1401">feed generators</a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">All parameters should be strings, except for two:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• categories should be a sequence of strings.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• stylesheets should be a sequence of either strings or <a href="index.html#page_2077"><i>Stylesheet</i></a> instances.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Beware that some control characters are <a href="https://www.w3.org/International/questions/qa-controls">not allowed</a> in XML documents. If your content has some of</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">them, you might encounter a <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#ValueError">ValueError</a> when producing the feed.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">The stylesheets argument was added.</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_2078"><i><b>SyndicationFeed.add_item()</b></i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Add an item to the feed with the given parameters.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Required keyword arguments are:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• title</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• link</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• description</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Optional keyword arguments are:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• author_email</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• author_name</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• author_link</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• pubdate</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• comments</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• unique_id</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• enclosures</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• categories</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• item_copyright</p> <p id="page_1400"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• ttl</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• updateddate</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Extra keyword arguments will be stored for <a href="index.html#page_1401">custom feed generators</a>.</p> <p style="margin-left:2em">All parameters, if given, should be strings, except:</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• pubdate should be a Python <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime">datetime</a> object.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• updateddate should be a Python <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime">datetime</a> object.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• enclosures should be a list of <a href="index.html#page_2079"><i>django.utils.feedgenerator.Enclosure</i></a> instances.</p> <p style="margin-left:3em">• categories should be a sequence of strings.</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_2078"><i><b>SyndicationFeed.write()</b></i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Outputs the feed in the given encoding to outfile, which is a file-like object.</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_2078"><i><b>SyndicationFeed.writeString()</b></i></a></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Returns the feed as a string in the given encoding.</p> <p>For example, to create an Atom 1.0 feed and print it to standard output:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">feedgenerator</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">f</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">feedgenerator</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">Atom1Feed(</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"My Blog"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">link</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"https://www.example.com/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">description</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"In which I write about what I ate today."</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">language</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"en"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">author_name</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Myself"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">feed_url</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"https://example.com/atom.xml"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">f</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">add_item(</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">title</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"Hot dog today"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">link</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"https://www.example.com/entries/1/"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">pubdate</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">datetime</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">now(),</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">description</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"<p>Today I had a Vienna Beef hot dog. It was pink, plump and perfect.</p>"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">>>></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">print</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(f</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">writeString(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"UTF-8"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">))</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><feed xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xml:lang="en"></span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">...</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"></feed></span></p> <div style="page-break-after:always"></div> <p id="page_1401" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Custom feed generators</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you need to produce a custom feed format, you’ve got a couple of options.</p> <p>If the feed format is totally custom, you’ll want to subclass SyndicationFeed and completely replace the write() and writeString() methods.</p> <p>However, if the feed format is a spin-off of RSS or Atom (i.e. <a href="https://georss.org">GeoRSS</a>, Apple’s <a href="https://help.apple.com/itc/podcasts_connect/#/itcb54353390">iTunes podcast format</a><a href="https://help.apple.com/itc/podcasts_connect/#/itcb54353390">, </a>etc.), you’ve got a better choice. These types of feeds typically add extra elements and/or attributes to the un-derlying format, and there are a set of methods that SyndicationFeed calls to get these extra attributes. Thus, you can subclass the appropriate feed generator class (Atom1Feed or Rss201rev2Feed) and extend these callbacks. They are: <b>SyndicationFeed.root_attributes(self)</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Return a dict of attributes to add to the root feed element (feed/channel).</p> <p><b>SyndicationFeed.add_root_elements(self, handler)</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Callback to add elements inside the root feed element (feed/channel). handler is an <a href="https://docs.python.org/3/library/xml.sax.utils.html#xml.sax.saxutils.XMLGenerator">XMLGenerator</a> from Python’s built-in SAX library; you’ll call methods on it to add to the XML document in process.</p> <p><b>SyndicationFeed.item_attributes(self, item)</b></p> <p style="margin-left:2em">Return a dict of attributes to add to each item (item/entry) element. The argument, item, is a dictio-nary of all the data passed to SyndicationFeed.add_item().</p> <p><b>SyndicationFeed.add_item_elements(self, handler, item)</b></p> <p style="text-align:center">Callback to add elements to each item (item/entry) element. handler and item are as above.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:1em">Warning: If you override any of these methods, be sure to call the superclass methods since they add</p> <p style="margin-left:1em">the required elements for each feed format.</p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>For example, you might start implementing an iTunes RSS feed generator like so:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>iTunesFeed</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Rss201rev2Feed):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>root_attributes</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">attrs</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">root_attributes()</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">attrs[</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"xmlns:itunes"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"http://www.itunes.com/dtds/podcast-1.0.dtd"</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>return</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">attrs</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>def</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>add_root_elements</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">self</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">, handler):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">super</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">()</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">add_root_elements(handler)</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">handler</span><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>.</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">addQuickElement(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"itunes:explicit"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">"clean"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>There’s a lot more work to be done for a complete custom feed class, but the above example should demon-strate the basic idea.</p> <p id="page_1402"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><b>Feed stylesheets</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>If you wish to have your RSS feed render nicely in a browser, you will need to provide styling information</p> <p>for the XML file, typically in <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/XSLT/Transforming_XML_with_XSLT">XSLT</a> or CSS formats.</p> <p>You can add this to your RSS feed by setting the stylesheets attribute on the feed class.</p> <p>This can be a hardcoded URL:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.syndication.views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Feed</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>FeedWithHardcodedStylesheet</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Feed):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">stylesheets</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">"https://example.com/rss_stylesheet.xslt"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>You can also use Django’s static files system:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.syndication.views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Feed</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.templatetags.static</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">static</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>FeedWithStaticFileStylesheet</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Feed):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">stylesheets</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">static(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"rss_styles.xslt"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Another option is to have a view in your project that renders the XSLT document. You can then link it like so:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.syndication.views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Feed</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.urls</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">reverse_lazy</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>FeedWithStylesheetView</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Feed):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">stylesheets</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">[</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">reverse_lazy(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"your-custom-view-name"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Django will normally try to guess the MIME type of the given URL based on its extension, but if that fails</p> <p>you can specify it using the <a href="index.html#page_2077"><i>Stylesheet</i></a> class:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.syndication.views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Feed</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.feedgenerator</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Stylesheet</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continues on next page)</span></p> <p id="page_1403" style="text-align:right"><b>Django Documentation, Release 5.2.dev20241127161328</b></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p style="text-align:right"><span style="font-size:0.8em">(continued from previous page)</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Similarly, if you’d like to use a different media attribute than screen (Django’s default), you can use the</p> <p><a href="index.html#page_2077"><i>Stylesheet</i></a> class again:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.syndication.views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Feed</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>FeedWithHardcodedStylesheet</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Feed):</span></p> <p style="font-size:0.87em"><b>=</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"print"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>Any of these options can be combined when using multiple stylesheets:</p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.contrib.syndication.views</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Feed</span></p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>from</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">django.utils.feedgenerator</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>import</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">Stylesheet</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>class</b></span> <span style="font-size:0.87em"><b>MultiStylesheetFeed</b></span><span style="font-size:0.87em">(Feed):</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">stylesheets</span> <span style="font-size:0.87em">,</span></p> <p style="margin-left:3em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">Stylesheet(</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">"/stylesheet2.xsl"</span><span style="font-size:0.87em">),</span></p> <p style="margin-left:2em"><span style="font-size:0.87em">]</span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p><span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>6.5.14</b></span> <span style="font-size:1.2em"><b>admin</b></span></p> <p style="text-align:center"> </p> <p>The automatic Django administrative interface. For more information, see <a href="index.html#page_27">Tutorial 2</a> and the <a href="index.html#page_1017">admin docu-</a></p> <p><a href="index.html#page_1017">mentation.</a></p> <p>Requires the <a
